limit 20000)" under a Try again that could not help.

STEP 4. skribl/validation.py lets a Pad payload's frame spend the whole
document's budget: MAX_POINTS_PER_PAD, MAX_TOTAL_POINTS by default, and
MAX_GROUPS_PER_PAD, 50,000 strokes, the page's own ratio of four points a
stroke, so a drawing of short strokes does not meet a stroke cap nobody chose.
"Pad" is _payload_kind's answer, the same test every player uses. A Flip page
keeps 20,000 points and 5,000 strokes. Posts and account drafts share the rule,
so both move together.

THEIR OWN VARIABLES. The decision page said a Render setting of
SKRIBL_MAX_POINTS_PER_FRAME would win. Building it turned up that .env.example
sets exactly that variable to 20000, uncommented, so a deployment configured
from the example would have kept the Pad at 15 minutes whatever the code said.
The Pad's two ceilings are SKRIBL_MAX_POINTS_PER_PAD and
SKRIBL_MAX_GROUPS_PER_PAD instead, named in .env.example, and nothing on Render
needs changing.

STEP 2. lib/pointbudget.js mirrors the Pad's two ceilings (verify_sharedrules
pins them), the Pad loads it, and Post asks padFits() before building or
sending anything. Past the ceiling, the post sheet (lib/postsheet.js, both
editors) says the owner's words, "Couldn't post. Your drawing is still here.
It's longer than a post can hold, so save a backup to keep a copy as a file.",
and its button becomes Save a backup with the ⋯ menu's icon: pressing it puts
the sheet away and opens the menu's own drawer, which downloads the .skribl
file. Opening the sheet again puts Post back. Flip says the same words when its
pages add up past the budget, with the same button, and then what only it
knows ("Its 3 generated pages make up 27% of it; deleting one frees far more
room than deleting a drawing."). Its too-many-pages refusal moves under the
same first line ("It has 201 pages and a post holds 200; delete 1 to post
it."), and Post keeps its word there, since deleting pages is the remedy.

Measured through the real Pad: a drawing of exactly 200,000 points posts (201
in 2.7 s, every point on the server); 200,001 is answered in under a second
with nothing sent, and its backup is a 14 MB .skribl file with every point.

CALIBRATION

verify_posted TOO LONG TO POST drives both editors through Post: a Pad drawing
of exactly 200,000 points posts and the server holds every point; one point
more, on a phone in both themes, sends nothing, says the shared words, turns
Post into Save a backup with the menu's icon painted where the plane was, puts
the sheet away for the menu's drawer, downloads a .skribl file with every point,
and gives Post back when the sheet opens again; Flip past the budget says the
same words and its generated pages, with the same button, and saves every page.
verify_clouddrafts saves a 200,000-point Pad draft and has one point more
refused; verify_review asks each cap at its own edge (a Flip page, a Pad
frame, both stroke caps, the document); verify_sharedrules pins the Pad's two
numbers to the server's and asks the Pad to load the module; verify_flipmeta
pins the too-many-pages words.

Each was shown red on its own mutation, each in its own copy on its own server:
the Pad not asking before Post (the Pad's eight one-past checks; the server's
jargon came back); the button not turning into Save a backup (the button, the
drawer and the file, on both editors); the button not routed to the backup
(the drawer and the file only); the sheet not giving Post back (that check
only); the server's Pad cap back at 20,000 (the 200,000-point post, the
200,000-point draft, verify_review's two Pad checks); the Pad's copy of the cap
at 20,000 (the 200,000-point post, and verify_sharedrules' pin); Flip refusing
instead of offering the backup (Flip's button and file); and main, where all
fourteen new post checks, the draft, the two Pad caps, the Pad's module and the
pages words fail.

Two blind spots were found in the first round and fixed before the second. The
draft check read its limit from the server's own Pad constant, so it moved down
with the mutation that lowered it and stayed green; it, and the post checks,
now ask for the owner's number, the whole budget. And a red check that left the
sheet open made the next click wait out its timeout and stopped the suite, so
one failure hid the rest; the sheet is closed first now, and the drawer is asked
for its own open state rather than whether it is displayed, which it always is.

## After v322 -- the Pad plan, step 5: a note at 90% of what a post can hold, and at the limit

The owner's pick A. Until steps 2 and 4 nothing said anything until Post failed
at the end of the work; now, while drawing, the toast where "Draft restored" is
said (showToast's place under the header, taps passing through, never over a
button) says it twice at most: after a save that crossed 90% of what a post can
hold, how many minutes more fit at this drawing's own pace ("About 14 more
minutes will fit in a post."); after one that reached the limit, "That's as
long as a post can hold. It's all still saved here." The second sentence only
when that save landed: a failed save says the first alone.

lib/pointbudget.js holds the rule for both editors. padShare() and docShare()
say how much of a post is spent by whichever ceiling runs out first (a Pad
drawing's points or strokes, a Flip's points or pages); note() makes one
teller per editor, which answers each level the first time it is reached and
again only after the drawing has fallen back under it (an undo, a deleted
page); prime() takes the level of a drawing restored at boot without a word,
since it was told before the reload; noteWords() says it, the minutes or pages
left being what is left of the share at the rate it was spent. Each editor
calls it from the one place its saves report, showAutosaveStatus().

Flip: shared. The same note in Flip's chip, counting pages: "About 20 more
pages will fit in a post."

CALIBRATION

verify_drafts NEARLY TOO LONG loads the two-hour generator's drawing just under
90% and draws one stroke across it on a phone, then asks for the exact sentence
(the minutes worked out again in Python from the drawing's points and time),
that taps go through the toast and that no button drawn under it is covered
(asked by elementFromPoint, which sees through it as taps do); then that the
next save says nothing, the limit is said once, said again after an undo and a
redo, not said as a drawing restored at the limit boots or on its next save,
and said without "still saved here" when the save failed (localStorage made to
refuse). Flip at 180 of 200 pages says "About 20 more pages".

Each was shown red on its own mutation, each in its own copy on its own server:
the Pad's save never asking (the Pad's five note checks); the teller answering
every save (the next save, the undo and redo, the restore and Flip's); no
re-arming after falling back (the undo and redo); no prime at restore (the
restore); "saved" taken as given (the failed save); the minutes counted ten
times over (the sentence); Flip's save never asking (Flip's); and the tree
before this change (all six note checks).

Three things were wrong in the first round. The placement check read boxes: a
closed drawer's Done and a hidden grid button keep theirs under the toast, so
it called them covered; it asks what is painted now. The restore check
installed its recorder after the page had booted, and the boot's own save is
where a missing prime speaks, so that mutation stayed green; the toast is
watched from the first paint now. And the copy meant to be the tree before this
change was taken from the wrong commit and passed everything; taken from the
right one, it fails all six.

## After v322 -- the first far jump races there: fast-forward instead of a freeze

The owner's pick A, from the mock ("yes, A"). Step 3's copies made every jump
after the first short, but the first jump to a far part of a long drawing
still drew everything up to it at once, and the page stood still: the bar
stuck where it was, then the picture jumped. Now that jump is drawn a slice a
frame, about 24 ms of drawing each, so the page keeps moving: the bar and the
clock are where it was pointed at once, the drawing races there, and the pen
dot rides along on the Pad's preview and the shared link. In all three
players: the Pad's preview, the shared link's player, and the in-post player
(a feed, the Gallery, the Library).

`lib/seekcache.js` holds the rule and the slices, so the three cannot race
differently. far() says a jump races when it would draw more than 8,000 points
(a minute or two of drawing) through a stretch with no copy yet -- the first
visit there; a jump through stretches that have their copies lands at once, as
it did, however long, and so does any short one. race() draws the points a
slice a frame through the caller's own drawing call; the slices grow or shrink
to take about 24 ms each, never more than doubling from one frame to the
next. The slices draw the same points in the same order as the one long draw,
and presenting between them repaints nothing a later present does not, so a
race lands on exactly the picture the jump drawn at once paints.

What waits on it, and what stops it:

- The caller is told where the race stands after every slice, so a newer seek
  mid-race takes over from where the canvas really is (forward, it carries on
  from there; back, it starts from a copy).
- The Pad's replay loop holds still while it races, and its clock is held at
  the place pointed, so a pause, a new speed or a drag on the drawing mid-race
  all read that place, and the replay carries on from it when it lands.
- Play pressed mid-race waits for the landing (the first frame would otherwise
  draw the rest of the way at once, which is the freeze again). The button
  says Pause meanwhile, as it will then; a second press, a tap on the drawing,
  or a drag takes the Play back, as each would pause playing. On the shared
  link the sound is unlocked and the iPhone's session claimed in the tap
  itself, before it waits, and released if the Play is taken back; Restart
  spends a waiting Play. A drag to the very end while playing stays on the
  finished drawing, as it always did. The in-post player's waiting Play from
  rest (the Library seeks a post nobody has played) is paused where it was
  pointed if taken back.
- Anything that repaints from the base stops a race: Stop on the Pad (the
  finished drawing comes back), Restart on the shared link, and in the in-post
  player any repaint at all (settled, a new post, a resize).

Measured on the shared link, a 120,000-point post at 2x, a tap at 80% while
playing: main stood still 1.5 to 1.6 s in one task (8.6 to 8.7 s on a CPU
slowed 4x); now it lands after 1.6 s with no frame over 63 ms and 55 painted
meanwhile (9.7 to 9.9 s slowed, no frame over 177 ms).

Flip: not for Flip. Flip scrubs page by page, and its heavy pages are already
kept as pictures (lib/framebitmap.js), so it never draws thousands of points
to jump.

CALIBRATION

verify_replayspeed THE FIRST FAR JUMP RACES THERE (sixteen checks) taps the
bar at 80% on a 120,000-point drawing, the Pad on a phone the owner's width at
2x and the shared link on a 2x desk -- 2x so a stretch between copies is wider
than the threshold, and "has its copies" and "is short" are different
questions. It reads the bar and the clock at once, frames and long tasks while
it races, every byte at the landing against a replay from the first point, a
newer seek mid-race, a pause mid-race, Play mid-race and each way of taking it
back, Stop and Restart mid-race, a drag to the end, a drag holding a waiting
Play, and a short jump into new ground and a long one back through copies.
verify_inline has the same for the in-post player on a feed (eight checks,
the reference a page that refuses lib/seekcache.js, so it seeks from zero),
and verify_audiosession one: a Play taken back mid-race lets the session go.
The existing long-drawing checks in both suites wait for a landing.

Thirty-three mutations, each in its own copy on its own server, every one red:
the race never starting (twelve checks on the Pad and the link, seven in the
in-post player); a race claiming its landing a slice early (the pixel checks,
old and new); far() ignoring copies, or the threshold (only the short-jump
check); the caller not told after each slice (the Pad's supersede and clock,
the link's supersede); the link's own place not kept (its supersede); the
Pad's loop not waiting, its clock not held, a repaint from the base not
stopping a race; each bar set only at the landing; eleven pieces of the link's
waiting Play, its session release among them; and eleven in the in-post
player, its race and what stops it among them -- each red on its own check.
The tree before this change fails seven of the eight in-post checks; the
eighth is exactness, which it has.

Two things were wrong in the first round. The Pad's supersede came a quarter
of a second into the race, by when the race had passed a stretch and taken a
copy, so the newer seek restored from it and healed a race that never said
where it had got to; the link's check went red and the Pad's stayed green. It
comes two frames in now, before any copy (and says none is held), and goes red
too. And "keeps moving" was a 200 ms bar: with four suites sharing the machine,
one frame of an unrelated mutation's race took 220 ms; 300 ms is still five
times under the freeze.

The shared player's JavaScript grows by 1,758 B and the in-post player's by
1,416 B (both ledgers name it), after spending 195 B and 278 B of what the
change itself added.

NOT TESTED HERE: whether a Play that waits still gets sound on an iPhone. The
unlock and the claim happen in the tap, which is what iOS asks, but this box
has no WebKit, and its Chromium starts audio unlocked, so the locked case
cannot be made to happen.

## After v322 -- the Pad keeps every pen sample a frame batches, as Flip has since v230

The owner's yes, after making Bloom showed it: the Pad never got v230's fix for
"when I draw circles fast we get a lot of straight line segments". v230 wired
lib/inputsamples.js into Flip alone -- its commit touched flip.js and no Pad
file -- and lib/brushes.js has said since that both editors capture with the
coalesced points, which was true of one. A pointermove comes once a frame while
a phone samples the finger at 120-240Hz, so the Pad stored a fast circle at the
frame rate, as a polygon, where Flip stored the same circle smooth.

continueDraw (editor_draw.js) now does what Flip's handler does, through the
same lib: extract() the batch the browser kept, map each sample through the
Pad's own getPos, thin() it from the last point stored, and store what is left,
each sample through the stabilizer, Shift's axis and the brush, each with its
OWN pressure -- pressureSize reads the sample, not the event, or a taper
flattens across the batch. The batch shares one `t`, as on Flip: it arrived
together, and a replay draws it in one step, as the live line did. A move that
carries one event -- every move an engine without the batch makes, and every
one the harness's mouse makes -- stores exactly what it did before. The wet
layer is presented once a batch.

Flip: shared. One lib, both editors; Flip's handler is unchanged.

What changes on the canvas: a fast stroke stores more points, so it bends where
the pen bent, and the thinning keeps a slow one at about what it cost. The
pencil brush tapers by the distance between stored points (shape() in
lib/brushes.js), so on the Pad it now tapers less on a fast flick than it did
-- exactly as Flip's pencil already did. If the pencil should taper more on
both, that is the one number in shape(). Likewise the stabilizer, when it is
on, eases toward each stored point as Flip's does, so a fast stroke is eased
over a shorter distance than before; at its default, Off, nothing changes.

CALIBRATION

verify_input.py could not see a batch arrive through Playwright's mouse, which
sends one event per move, and said so; it tested the thinning rule alone.
Chromium honours `coalescedEvents` in the PointerEvent constructor, so the
suite now hands each editor one pointermove carrying its samples, as a phone
does, and reads what was stored before the pen lifts: eight samples twenty
pixels apart become eight points where the pen went, their widths rising as the
pressure does; forty samples a third of a pixel apart thin to under a third,
the last where the pen is; a move without a batch stores its one point; and the
two editors keep the same points from the same batch. Against the tree before
this change, four go red -- the Pad's lib not loaded, one point of eight, one
width, and the Pad keeping 1 where Flip keeps 8 -- and Flip's stay green. Seven
mutations, each in its own copy on its own server, each red on its own check:
the Pad ignoring the batch, taking the event's pressure, not thinning, and its
page not loading the lib; Flip the first three ways. So Flip's v230 handler is
pinned for the first time by what it stores, not only by its thinning rule.

NOT TESTED HERE: Safari's batches. This box has no WebKit. Wherever
getCoalescedEvents is missing or empty, the Pad stores one point a move, as
before, and the no-batch check holds that.

## After v322 -- an open drawer rests while a drawing plays, and Play shows the whole drawing

The owner, at the desk with Bloom open and the Draw drawer up: "it disappears
the drawer contents to draw it but leaves all the empty space. is that good?"
It was not. Both editors faded an open drawer to nothing while a drawing played
and held its space, so the drawing played above a hole -- on the desk, 456px of
empty page under it. Mocked against "now": the drawer closed and the drawing
re-centred (the owner: "I don't necessarily like the options of spreading the
space out"), and the owner's own idea, which they asked for: keep it open, "it
might be a pain to open it again".

- An open drawer RESTS while a drawing plays, in both editors: open where it
  was, its contents dimmed to --drawer-rest (one token in styles.css for both),
  taking no taps, and Stop wakes it. By its CONTENTS, never its own opacity --
  it is frosted glass, the header's v315 rule -- and the Media card keeps its
  glass too, where it used to drop it.
- Flip's tap-away rule closed the drawer on Play's own tap, and would have
  closed a resting one on any tap mid-play, since taps pass through it. Now
  Play and Stop are not a tap away, and nothing is while a Flip plays.
- Play shows the whole drawing (lib/drawerdetent.js revealTop, both editors).
  With a drawer open the page can sit scrolled down to it while Play is still
  in reach -- the phone's header is sticky -- and the drawing played with its
  top under the header: 26-45px of the Pad's on a 375x667 phone with any drawer
  open, 53px of a Flip's on the owner's 402x874, and Space on a desk played a
  Flip with only its bottom 64px on screen. The owner found Play reachable only
  from the top on their own phone and desk, which holds for the Pad there; the
  reveal is a no-op whenever the drawing is already whole. It calls off a
  drawer's pending re-asserts (revealPanelEnd's, at 300, 700 and 1200ms), which
  carried the page straight back down when Play followed a drawer's opening.

Flip: shared. One token, one reveal, the same rest. Flip's play swaps its page
strip for its speed row, which lifts what is below by 24px, as it always did.

CALIBRATION

verify_parity's new section, on both editors at the owner's 402x874 and a
375x667 phone, and Flip at 1280x900 with Space: the drawer still open, its

The owner, on a desk, with Bloom open in the Pad: "looks weird on reload. this
happens (the offset) sometimes." Bloom sat low and to the left of its frame,

on another 4:3, which is why it came and went. A post made after such a
reload would have carried the wrong size too. Flip's autosave has always held

- editor_draft.js: the autosave holds the drawing's canvasSize, as a post

  carries no size and keeps the window's choice, so Bloom wants opening once
  more from its file; from then on its shape comes back with it.
- Flip: already right, and now pinned beside the Pad.

## After v322 -- full screen while it plays, in the Pad and Flip

The owner, at the measured mock of full screen for the editors: "I like your
picks". The picks: the way in at the end of the line under the drawing --
Flip's at the end of its speed row -- and, in full screen, the controls
stepping back a moment after the drawing starts, so the drawing takes the
whole height and the controls lie over its foot when they come back. Asked
whether faded controls come back to change the speed: they do, and the owner
added, "make the first tap on a faded phone just reveal the controls without
pausing, matching how video apps work".

- lib/watchfull.js, one module for both editors. Each hands over its frame,
  its button, what travels into the band (the Pad's scrubber and line; Flip's
  progress line and speed row), how to lay its canvas out, and its own play,
  pause and resume. The way in is the link page's four corners, there only
  while a drawing plays and never on the drawing. Going full screen is
  lib/immersive.js: the real API on a desk, the pinned stand-in on an iPhone,
  which has none for an element. Escape leaves either.
- The drawing is as big as the screen allows, centred, in its own shape, and
  uncapped as on the link page: past the size it was drawn at the lines soften
  a little, and the mock said so. Measured: the Pad on the owner's 402x874
  from 378 to 402 wide, and on a 1333x906 desk from 694 to 906 tall; Flip from
  378x284 to 402x302, and from 673x505 to 1208x906. Never magnified: a Pad
  zoomed in on a detail (Flip fits its magnifier on Play; the Pad keeps it)
  goes full screen as the whole drawing and comes back to the page as it was.
- The frame, the band and the x are the link page's own rules, widened to
  `:is(.canvas-wrap, .watch-full)` at the same specificity, so the three full
  screens are one look and cannot drift. The controls are MOVED into the band,
  not copied, and put back on the way out: one of every control, every
  handler still bound. Focus goes with the way in, and the way out hands it
  back to it, as a dialog does.
- lib/chromefade.js says WHEN they step back: after 2.5s of quiet while it
  plays. A mouse that moves 3px, a press, a key or focus brings them back; a
  paused or finished drawing, or the Pad's open speed menu, keeps them up.
  styles.css says WHAT steps back, so the link page and the Gallery can take
  the same rule next.

## After v322 -- a drawing deleted in the Library is gone from the Gallery you come Back to

The owner asked whether a drawing deleted from the Library should leave the
Gallery too. It does, and always did: Delete takes the post down for everyone,
and every listing after it leaves the drawing out. Driven on a local server:
two public drawings and one link only, Delete on the first, and the server
answers 404 for it and its link page while a fresh Gallery lists the second.

One path brought it back. The Gallery, then the Library in the same tab,
Delete, then Back: the Gallery showed the deleted drawing again, looking
playable until it was tapped (the tap said "This drawing isn't here
anymore."). The listing sent no Cache-Control, and a history load prefers a
stored response whether or not it is fresh: Chromium read GET /api/skribls
from disk (fromDiskCache, measured) and never asked the server.

* The listing sends `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, the one directive a
  history load cannot reuse. It is also the payload GET's rule since PF-017:
  the listing is read through visibility (an author's own listing carries
  their private posts, and a host's feed_filter decides per viewer), so no
  shared cache may keep it either.
* A Gallery restored from memory (the back-forward cache Safari and Chrome
  keep for Back) runs none of its script again, so no-store cannot reach it.
  On `pageshow` with `persisted` it asks the listing again and takes off the
  tiles the answer no longer names. Nothing is added and nothing else is
  rebuilt, so the place in the grid is kept. An absence counts only where the
  answer covers the tile: the whole list came back, or, newest first, the tile
  sits above one the answer names. Hot reorders by plays, so there only the
  whole list can say.

What stays as it was, on purpose: the eye switch (In gallery, or link only)
takes a drawing out of the Gallery and keeps its link working; Clear list
forgets this browser's list and takes nothing down; and the Library offers
Delete only for a drawing this browser holds the key for. A Gallery open on
another device keeps a deleted drawing until it reloads, and a tap on it says
it isn't here anymore.

NOT TESTED HERE: a real back-forward restore. Headless Chromium refuses one
(BackForwardCacheDisabledForDelegate) and there is no WebKit, so the restore
is driven with the event a browser fires for one.

Flip: shared. The Gallery and the Library list Pad and Flip drawings alike.

CALIBRATION: verify_gallery, "a drawing taken down", nine rows. On main, four
are red: the header, the Back row, the restore row and the short answer. Each
part of the fix broken on its own: no-store off (the header and Back rows red),
no restore handler (restore, short answer), every absence believed (short
answer, Hot), any pageshow (the ordinary pageshow row), the grid reloaded
instead of pruned (restore, same tiles, short answer, Hot), Hot read like New
(Hot). Each red on its own rows, and all nine green with the fix.

## After v322 -- every Play arrow sits in the middle of its disc

The owner's yes to the two steps offered after #466: the same arrow fix for the
Library's, the Gallery's and Flip's Play, and the Play inside a post measured.
Read by its ink at the owner's 402x874, 3x (the Gallery card on a desk too),
each was off to the right:

    the Library's Play                          0.46
    the full-screen bar (Library and Gallery)   0.95, and 0.51 low
    the Gallery card's Play                     0.81, and 0.6 high
    the Play inside a post                      1.51
    the paused Play (tap to pause)              2.56

The post's is the one every Gallery tile and every skribls.net post shows, and
the paused Play is the one the Pad, Flip and the link page show on their canvas.
Neither is a control, so the centring tool never reached them.

Three causes, three fixes:

* The one play glyph puts its box in the middle, and its middle, to the eye, is
  halfway between its box and its mass: 0.583 of its 24 units right, 2.43% of
  its width. The Library's, the card's and the bar's Play move it back with
  `translate: -2.43%`, matched by the glyph's path so Pause, which is
  symmetric, stays put: #466's rule for the link player, as a share of the
  glyph so one rule serves every size.
* Both discs carried a nudge the other way: the post's a 2px margin-left, the
  paused one 3px. Both give way to the same translate.
* The bar and the card drew the mark on a half pixel: (48 - 19) / 2 and
  (40 - 15) / 2. A renderer rounds a half pixel one way or the other (this one

## After v322 -- a drawing's picture keeps the card's round corner at every shape

Found while mocking the Gallery without its black bars. Before a drawing plays,
the in-post player shows its share card clipped down to the drawing, with the
card's own rounded corner (fitPoster in inlineplayer.js). The corner's radius
was worked out as a share of the DRAWING, and CSS resolves inset()'s radius
against the IMAGE, which is the whole card, the same as its four edges. So the
corner stretched by the card's width over the drawing's, worst on a tall
drawing: 28.8 x 8.4 px in a Gallery tile and 86.9 x 25.6 px in a post, where
the card's corner at that size is 6.6 and 19.8 round, drawn as a long curve
with the box's ground showing in it. It is a share of the card now, both ways.

image's own box at all four canvas shapes, in a box with no line (a Gallery
tile) and one with it (a post), and wants each corner round and the card's
size. Red on main (all eight bent, the square too), green with the fix.

## After v322 -- what three release runs toward v323 found, and notes for the next session

Asked "Should we seal?" before starting a new session, three release runs toward
v323 each stopped on something different. Each was found rather than run again,
and the fixes land here without the version bump: the seal is the next thing to
do, from this tree.

**`verify_parity` had outgrown the 600-second budget every suite runs under**
(`harness/run_harness.sh`). The first run stopped it with all 469 checks it had
reached passing and its last section unfinished: 514 s on CI (run 1210, 477
checks), past 600 s on the box. That section, full screen while it plays in the
Pad and Flip (`lib/watchfull.js`), is `verify_watchfull.py` now, moved whole,
its assertions word for word, with the three helpers it borrowed (`ED`,
`_fresh`, `_drawn`). Run alone on the box, `verify_parity` took 500 s for 409
checks and `verify_watchfull` 113 s for 68; on CI 407 s and 99 s. With the Pad's
way in taken away, the new suite goes red on the Pad's first row; with Flip's,
on Flip's first row, and all 36 of the Pad's pass.

**The Gallery ignored words typed before it listened** (`verify_hot`, second
run). The search box is in the page's own HTML and `gallery.js` is deferred, so
on a slow phone a person can type before anything listens, and a browser that
restores fields on Back fills the box itself: the box said "beta fish" over a
grid of everything. `gallery.js` now reads the box's words for its first
listing. HOT 5c holds `gallery.js` at the route until the words are in, so the
race is driven every time: red on its two rows with the old `gallery.js`, green
with the fix. HOT 5b now acts only once the page is listening (its boot flag),
so it tests the in-flight race it names.

**`verify_compose` drew before the framed Pad was listening** (second run). A
fixed four seconds stood in for the editor in the composer's frame being ready,
and the stroke drawn after it landed first, so Record stayed hidden through the
click's whole 30 s. `frame_booted()` waits for the framed editor's own boot flag
(`__skriblBoot.pad`, `.flip`) at all five editor opens. With the Pad's script
held six seconds, the old wait fails as the run did and the new one passes,
86/86.

**A frozen sample read as a jump** (`verify_motion`, third run, the only red in
11,721 assertions across all 125 suites, both CI lanes attested). Flip's tool
row read "526 -> 768, 0 frames between" as the last drawer closed. Twenty
closes on the quiet box read 8 or 9 frames each, and Flip's close costs no long
task at all at full speed and at most 108 ms on a CPU slowed 4x (the Pad's 81):
nothing in the editor swallows a glide. The sampler reads on the page's own
thread, once a frame, so a stall there lets the compositor carry the glide
through while nothing is read. It now records the longest wait between frames,
and a glide sample in which a frame waited past 250 ms is taken again, at most
twice. Calibrated three ways: a 700 ms freeze after the first close fails the
old check in the run's own words and passes the new one ("taken again after
frames of [683] ms"); Flip made to jump home (`behavior: 'auto'`) fails the new
check with its frames still 17 ms apart, the Pad's row green; untouched, 20/20.

Also here, none of it app code: `harness/tools/make_grow.py`, which draws the
seven growing-Blooby takes put to the owner the night of the cheer (FUTURE.md
6m), kept in the tree because it lived only in a session's scratch space;
FUTURE.md 6l marked BUILT, its dark ground answered by the badge the owner chose
over the sticker; and START-HERE's device check given Blooby's places to look
at, in place of "Blooby cheering after a post", which was parked then and is
built now.

**For the seal.** CI's full battery was green on every tree the runs froze
(runs 1210, 1211, 1212). The third run's record (FAIL on the glide only) was
kept out of the tree. Of v322's still-open list, the two-hour piece (#438 to

**One fix inside this seal**, found by its own first release run: 11,655
assertions across all 125 suites, and one red, `verify_watchfull`'s "/skribl-pad
on a desk: ...and the x hands focus back to the way in", with focus on
`<body>`. CI had passed the same tree. A log of every focus change on the way
out showed why it could happen: the browser drops focus from the x to nothing
as it leaves its full screen, before `fullscreenchange` reaches
`lib/watchfull.js`, which gave focus back only from inside full screen. It
won the race on this box eight times of eight, at full speed and with the CPU
slowed 6x, so the new row drives it on purpose: the x focused, focus dropped,
then the browser's own exit. Without the fix it reads `<body>` on both editors
on a desk (the Pad's in the run's own words); with focus on nothing counted as
in full screen, as a dialog gives focus back however it closes, 70/70. That
run's record was not kept; the record below is the next one, on the fixed tree.

## After v323 -- a replay glides

The owner's iPhone: "Why is it jumpy when drawing? ... The playback. It does
it at 1x too." A pointermove hands over every sample since the last one, and
both editors stamp the whole bundle with one time (editor_draw.js: "The batch
shares one `t`"). Replay draws whole segments once their time has come and
never part of one, so it put each bundle down at once, held still, and
jumped; at 1/4x each hold lasted four times as long, and the nib hopped with
it while the scrub bar glided. The owner's scrub bar showed it: one smooth
stroke drawn as evenly spaced clumps of ink.

lib/holdtiming.js untie(), one rule for every replay (the Pad's timeline in
app.js, the posted and in-post players in inlineplayer.js, and a Flip page
that draws itself): a bundle of equal times is spread evenly over the moment
before it, at most 34 ms so a pause still reads as a pause, its last point
kept where it was. Played times only: no drawing changes, no replay's length
changes, and every drawing ever made plays smoothly. A stroke's first bundle
has no moment before it and still comes together. Recording each sample's
own time (a coalesced event's timeStamp) would be more exact for new
drawings; not done here, since untie() already covers them and the old ones.

verify_glide watches the nib on every animation frame: on the shared player
at 1/4x (bundles of 4, 16 ms apart) and at 1x (12, 48 ms apart), and on the
Pad at 1/4x it moves on nearly every frame, never still for more than two;
every row red with untie() turned off (nib moving on a quarter to a third of
the frames). Not tested here: iPhone Safari itself.

## After v323 -- the Pad | Flip switch moves before it goes

The owner's iPhone: "when I click flip, starts loading flip and never shows
the button move, then boom you're in flip. It takes a while to flip back and
forth and it never shows the pill move." The menu's other editor is a plain
link, so the browser left at once and the pill never moved; the screen sat
still while the next editor loaded. lib/editorswitch.js, one module for both
menus: a tap glides the pill under the other editor and lights its name,
and the page goes when it has arrived (280 ms, the pill's .26s glide; at
once with reduced motion; never for a tap that means a new tab). It moves
the pill itself, because lib/segslider.js follows a selected button and
would put it back, and it marks the switch data-going, which segslider does
not watch. Each editor's leave guard hears the tap first (the module loads
last) and still stops it when work is at risk. The other editor's page is
fetched ahead once this one has settled, so the trip is quicker; Back from
it puts the pill home.

verify_menu taps the other editor on both and reads the pill under it while
the page is still up, then the arrival, and the fetch ahead; each red with
its part taken out (with no glide the page left at once).

## After v323 -- kind transitions

The owner: "The transition should be smooth. No transitions should be
jumpy. Kind transitions right." Written into WORKING-AGREEMENTS as a rule
that holds everywhere, with how to check it (every animation frame, red on
the jumpy version first). Applied first where the owner saw it: between
Skribl's own pages (both editors, the Library, the Gallery, the player) a
soft cross-fade instead of a cut, styles.css @view-transition, .28s; a
browser without it keeps the plain cut, and so does reduced motion. The Pad |
Flip switch now glides its pill, then the next editor fades in over this
one. verify_menu reads pagereveal's viewTransition on the arriving editor,
both ways; red with the rule off. The player's CSS ratchet rises +107 B for
it, a named cost. Not tested here: iPhone Safari, which has it from 18.2.

## After v325 -- the mp4 job keeps the files it checks

The v325 auditor asked for the real-Chrome exports themselves, not only the
suite's word for them. `verify_mp4.py` now also writes each export it
inspects to the directory `SKRIBL_KEEP_EXPORTS` names (unset, it writes
nothing), and the mp4 job reads them back with ffprobe and ffmpeg's
volumedetect into an `mp4-exports` artifact: streams, codecs, decoded frame
count, how loud the audio is, a contact sheet of each Flip, each file's
SHA-256 and the tree hash. A standard runner and an artifact: free. A
manual run also prints the files into its log, the attestations' fallback,
because the build container gets a 403 from the artifact store.

Two traps, both caught before CI saw them. The files first went inside the
checkout, where `release_run.tree_files` (it walks the disk, not git) would
have counted them and turned a true MP4 attestation STALE; they live in the
runner's temp directory. And a dry run of the step here read the report's own
file back as a video (ffmpeg reads text with its tty demuxer), so the file
list is now taken before the report exists. Keeping was shown both ways on a
trimmed copy of the suite: four files with the variable set, none without.

## After v325 -- a video with no frame in it is not a success (a bug fix)

The evidence run for the v325 auditor ran `verify_videoexport` beside two
other suites and an install, on a loaded machine, and it went red: Flip's
silent WebM walked as no tracks and no frames, and the chip said "Animation
exported". SK-AUD-003's fix had made a recording a success when it had bytes
and the container's signature at its start, and a header with nothing behind
it has both. Reproduced on v325 with a stand-in recorder that hands back a
header-only WebM: both editors downloaded it and said it worked ("Animation
exported", "Video exported"). The real recorder made such a file once; in 76
more exports (12 on a quiet machine, 24 with the CPU starved, 40 beside other
browsers) it did not, so it is rare. A false success all the same. (This
entry first said 84; the run logs hold 76, and the count was corrected with
the Copy link fix.)

`lib/videorecord.js`, one module for both editors, now also asks the file for
a frame: a block on a WebM's video track, or an MP4 `mdat` with bytes in it,
looked for in its first 4 MB (a header alone is a few hundred bytes, so a
larger file is not one). Without one it is 'empty', and the editor says what
both already say for an empty recording: "The video came out empty, so
nothing was saved. Try again." Still not a decoder. The frame finder was
checked on 13 files: real WebMs from both editors, the same files cut back to
their headers, and plain, fast-start and fragmented MP4s with and without
samples. An MP4 holding only audio samples would still pass; nothing here
makes one.

`verify_videoexport` gains the header-only recorder on both editors and a
check that the stand-in file really is a WebM with a video track and no frame:
17/19 on the old recorder (exactly the two new checks red), 19/19 with the
fix. The MP4 route is untouched: it encodes every frame itself.

Pad and Flip: shared, one module.

## After v325 -- a finger that lifted unheard no longer costs the next stroke (a bug fix)

The owner, on an iPhone, checklist P1: "I made several fast strokes and
eventually it won't draw one. It might be when I draw fast and it goes
offscreen. Sometimes next one draws and then soon fails."

A stroke belongs to one pointer: both editors refuse a second pointer while
one is drawing, so a palm cannot steer it. When a finger lifts and the page's
handlers never hear it (no pointerup, pointercancel, lostpointercapture,
touchend or touchcancel), the editor still holds a stroke for a finger that is
gone. It refuses the next finger as if it were a second one, and only that
finger's own lift clears the state: one stroke lost, the next drawn, then lost
again, exactly the pattern on the owner's phone. Simulated in Chromium with
real touch input, the browser ending the touch and a listener installed
before the page's own swallowing the end events: both editors did it.

Why the lift went unheard on the owner's phone is not known here; there is no
WebKit in this box. What the editors can know is the screen: a refused
finger's touchstart lists every touch on the glass, and if it lists only that
finger, the stroke's own finger is gone. `lib/lostlift.js`, one module for
both editors, then ends the stuck stroke, kept as it stands, and runs the
editor's own pointerdown again for the new finger. A real second finger or a
palm is a second touch, so it is refused as before, and two fingers on the
canvas are still a pinch. Touch only, and only for a refusal that arrived with
that same press (read off the page's clock: a browser need not measure event
timeStamps from one origin).

`verify_pointerpad` gains the lost lift on both editors, with the pinch as its
edge: 29/31 before, exactly the two lost-lift rows red (the stuck stroke was
kept when the refused finger lifted, and that finger's own stroke was lost: 1
group to 2, wanting 3), 31/31 after. (This entry, and the squash commit,
first said 25/31; the red run's log says 29/31, and the entry was corrected
after the merge.)
Not tested on an iPhone; the owner's next checklist run is the test.

Pad and Flip: shared, one module.

## After v325 -- an iPhone video's music plays everywhere, not only on Apple's player (a bug fix)

The owner's iPhone exports from the device checklist (E1, E2) played with
their music on the phone. Read here with ffprobe, the music track would not
open: "Audio object type 0 is not implemented", 0 channels. The samples were
all there (pulled out and given the right config, they decode as AAC-LC,
48 kHz, stereo, at the music's own level), but the file's esds held a whole
MPEG-4 ES_Descriptor where the two-byte AudioSpecificConfig belongs. Safari's
AudioEncoder gives that descriptor as `decoderConfig.description` (Chrome
gives the config itself), and the muxer wrapped what it was given. Apple's
player copes; ffmpeg reads the wrapper's first byte as the config, and so does
everything built on it: many upload sites, Android, most players off Apple's.

`lib/mp4export.js` now digs the config out of such a descriptor before the
muxer sees it (`aacConfig`). A description that is already a config passes
through untouched, and so does one it cannot read. `verify_muxer` drives the
export's own `encode()` with stand-in encoders that describe their audio the
way Safari's did on the owner's phone (the bytes read out of that file) and
the way Chrome's does: the file's config was the 39-byte descriptor before
the fix and is `11 90` (AAC-LC, 48 kHz, stereo) with it. Played end to end
here with real AAC frames through the vendored muxer: before, ffmpeg opened no
audio; after, it decodes. Not tested on an iPhone here; the owner's next
export is the test.

Pad and Flip: shared (`lib/mp4export.js` is both editors' MP4 route).

## After v325 -- WAVE reads no errors on any page (a bug fix)

The owner ran WAVE (WebAIM's checker) on the live Pad from their phone: 76
errors, 0 contrast errors, 23 alerts, an AIM score of 3.3 out of 10. Read
here with WAVE's own rules, the Pad gave the same 69, 3, 2, 1 and 1, and the
other pages had their share: Flip 89, the player 13, the Library 12, the feed

the red run's log had been written over by the re-run, and survived only
because it was copied off the terminal.

`harness/run_parallel.py` still re-runs a red suite that measures alone,
because load makes those checks fail. What changed is what it says after:
the red run keeps its log, the re-run writes its own
(`<suite>.alone.log`), and a suite red beside others and green alone is
INTERMITTENT, with both counts on its line, listed apart, not counted as ok,
its red failures said again, and the run's exit is 3 (1 when anything simply
failed). Whether the red was load or a defect is now a judgement the person
quoting it has to write down.

The reviewer also asked whether any release gate used the permissive logic.
None does: the seal (`release_run.py`) and CI (`run_harness.sh`) run each
suite once and report what it said; the re-run alone exists only in this
development runner.

`verify_runreport`, a source suite on the PR gate (no browser, no server),
drives the runner's re-run step with a stand-in suite and its report with
results built in the suite: 13/13, and 7/13 with the old rule put back (a
green alone counted as ok).

## After v326 -- Firefox, after every merge

The outside review of the v325 packet asked for a wider browser list, and the
owner said yes to a Firefox check on the run GitHub makes after each merge, so
a pull request stays quiet ("all yes"). Nothing here had driven Gecko before:
every suite launches Chromium, and real Chrome for the MP4s.

`harness/firefox_smoke.py` is a smoke, not a port of the battery, which is
written to Chromium (real touches through CDP, its pixels for goldens,
Chrome's encoders); a port would be a second harness to keep in step. It asks
what someone opening Skribl in Firefox meets first, and reads each answer from
the thing itself: the five pages boot and nothing throws; a stroke on each
editor is drawing data and ink on its canvas; each editor posts through its
own sheet, ticked public; the Pad's link plays and shows ink; the Gallery shows
both posts and the Library, in the browser that posted them, lists both; and
each editor's video is counted in the file (WebM blocks, or an MP4's video
samples, whichever Firefox makes). Flip draws two pages first: a one-page Flip
is a picture, and its Video is off.

It is not a `verify_` suite: the build container has no Firefox, so a bare run
or a seal could only skip it, and a skip proves nothing. CI's new `firefox`
job installs Firefox, runs it through `run_harness.sh`, and fails on a skip,
as the mp4 lane does. `main-watch` now reads its result with the battery's
three, so a red Firefox on main opens the same issue a red battery does
(`verify_docs` reads the job, its needs and the result it hands on).

Checked here on Chromium (`SKRIBL_SMOKE_ENGINE=chromium`): 12/12, and 7/11
with Flip's script broken on purpose, naming the error. Its counters read 342
frames in an MP4 the repository ships, as ffprobe does, and none in a WebM
header with no frame behind it.

**What Firefox found on its first runs** (Firefox 142, 18 October). Neither
editor's video came: the export sat at "Recording…" with its bar full, for
good. That Firefox has no H.264 encoder, so the video goes
to the recorder, and with no music the recorder was asked for
`video/webm;codecs=vp8,opus`. Gecko's recorder, asked for an audio codec with
no audio track, waits for one: its start event came only at stop(), then no
data and no stop. Six trials in Firefox told it apart: both types naming opus
stalled, however the canvas was captured; the four without it recorded.
Chromium records either way, which is why nothing in the battery saw it.

`lib/videorecord.js` now asks for a type with sound only when the stream has
an audio track (THE TYPE FOLLOWS THE TRACKS), one change for both editors.
`verify_videoexport` puts in a stand-in recorder that waits as Gecko's did, on
each editor with no music: red on the old recorder (no video in 15 s; it asked
for `vp9,opus`), green on the new. The smoke now fails a missing video on its
own and still posts behind it: every red Firefox has shown so far was this one.

Still Firefox's own: it captures by sampling here, because its requestFrame is
on the stream and the recorder looks on the track. In the trials, sampling
kept 8 or 9 of 16 painted frames and the stream's requestFrame kept them all,
so Firefox's videos are choppier than Chromium's. That is on the list, not in
this change. A video with music has not been made in Firefox yet.

The first green run (Firefox 142.0.1, run 1343 on GitHub): 12/12. The Pad's
video held 47 frames and Flip's two pages 3, where Chromium makes about 83
and 4 from the same steps: that is the sampling.

## After v326 -- Firefox's frames, pushed; and a stop that never comes

Two follow-ups from Firefox's first runs, both in `lib/videorecord.js`, the
one recorder both editors use. Bug fixes, from the list #530 left.

**Frames, pushed.** Gecko keeps requestFrame on the canvas stream, not on its
track. The recorder looked on the track, found nothing, and fell back to
sampling the canvas: in Firefox the Pad's video held 48 of the 82 frames its
export planned, and Flip's two pages 3 of 4 (run 1350, red on the old
recorder). It now pushes through whichever has the method. The smoke counts
each video against the export's own plan, read from the page; Chromium lands
on it exactly (82 of 82, 83 of 83, 4 of 4). `verify_videoexport` moves
requestFrame onto the stream in Chromium: three pages must be three pushes
and three frames. The old recorder made no pushes, and Chromium's sampling
happened to give three frames, which is why the check counts the pushes.

In Firefox after the fix (runs 1351 and 1352): Flip's 4 of 4 both times,
where sampling had dropped a page. The Pad's 30 a second came out 63 of 82,
then 47 of 78: on CI, Gecko takes about 18 frames a second however they are
asked for (a pushed frame is taken at its next screen refresh, when it has
the time), so the Pad's video there stays choppier than Chromium's, with its
timing kept. Whether a desktop Firefox keeps up is not tested here. Not
chased further: making the recorder wait for each refresh would stretch the
replay's time instead, and the replay's timing is the performance. The smoke
holds Flip (12 a second, five refreshes apart) to exactly its beats, and the
Pad to never more than its beats.

**A stop that never comes.** Once every frame was in, nothing was left to
notice a cancel, so a recorder that never answered its stop (Gecko's did,
before the type fix) held the progress up for good. The stop is now waited
for with a limit, the video's own length and 15 s at least, after which it
fails as 'stalled' and the editor says the video came out empty, nothing
saved; Cancel ends the wait at once. `verify_videoexport` puts in a stand-in
that never answers: given up on at 16 and 17 s on Flip and the Pad, and
Cancel during the wait closes the export in under 0.2 s. All four red on the
old recorder.

over work on the canvas it still asks first ("Tap again — this replaces what
is on your canvas"), and a draft of the other kind still opens in its own
editor.

The list scrolls, and a menu inside it would be cut off at its edge. So the
open menu floats: it is fixed, placed under its ⋯ by the script, in the
sheet's box (the sheet is transformed, which makes it the box a fixed element
is placed in), and above the ⋯ where the screen ends first. It shuts when the
list scrolls or the window resizes, as a tap elsewhere and Escape shut it.

Delete wears the Library's deeper red, `--row-danger-ink` (#7a0a2d in light,
#ffb3c6 in dark): the same row's Delete, 9.8:1 and 10.7:1 on the menu's paper,
where the editors' own --danger would read 5.4:1 and 4.7:1. The token is set
on the sheet's row, not the root: the player wears styles.css's root tokens,

player's CSS by a token only this sheet reads. The asking red stays red under
a pointer through a hover rule behind the hover guard, where A11Y 17b caught a
first draft that had it outside.

The sheet's old bin, and its own copy of the bin's paths (`BIN` in
lib/savedrafts.js), are gone; every draft row's bin is drawn by rowEnd.

## After v326 -- one full screen: the Gallery's and the Library's are the link page's

The owner: "why can't the gallery player look like the others? with the same
scrubber and all?" They could not because the Gallery and the Library play
in the in-post player, and its full-screen bar (lib/fullbar.js) was built
before the link page had its line of speeds and its scrubber in the
drawing's shape. It never moved over. Measured on one drawing at one moment,
the Gallery showed a 6px line, three speeds a tap each, 0:50 of 2:00 where
the link page said 8:26 of 20:09 (the artist's time, as "Drawn in 20 min"
says), and the page's colour round the drawing.

The owner's picks from the mock ("All yes"):

- The Gallery's and the Library's full screen is the link page's, with who
  drew it in the top corner across from the x (A).
- The cards in the grid keep their small bar.
- One PR, checked on the Gallery and the Library, phone and desk, light and
  dark, with a check that their full screen measures the same as the link
  page's.

And the two defaults given when the owner asked whether anything needed a
choice: the name in the corner is words only (no avatar), and a tap on the
drawing pauses, as it already did.

WHAT IT IS. lib/fullbar.js band() builds the link page's band inside the
stage: the scrubber, the clock, the line with every speed, the five buttons,
the x, and the name in the corner (.fb-who, in the glass for the ground it
sits on, stepping back with the controls). attach() is the card's alone now.
The scrubber and the words are the player's own: the in-post player lends
the line a post wears under it (me.band), wired to its own clock, and tells
the band the artist's time (me.clock) and the drawing's ground (me.ground),
which the frame wears to the screen's edges. A new player (the Library puts
one on its stage for each row) gets fresh ones.

THE RULES ARE THE LINK PAGE'S, NOT A COPY OF THEM. fullband.css is made from
styles.css by harness/tools/cssgraph.py, as player.css is, and verify_seam
holds it to the regeneration byte for byte on the PR gate. A browser census
keeps every rule that matches inside the full-screen frame's band parts and
nothing outside them; styles.css's tokens (the dark :root and the light
data-theme) are emitted scoped to the frame, with the body's inherited type
and ink, so the band reads the same words in the same face. Splitting the
sheet by hand failed before (verify_cssplit's docstring says how).

FOUND ON THE WAY, each by a row that went red:

- The census first called every card's hidden band "outside" the frame,
  because every tile carries one. Inside is the open frame's parts; a part
  on another card is not outside.
- The name in the corner was white on white and the ground stopped short of
  the edges: the in-post box kept its own border, round and background in
  full screen. In immersive it has none (inlineplayer.css).
- The Library's page did not load lib/replayline.js, lib/scrubkeys.js or
  lib/seekcache.js, so its player had no line to lend. It loads them now.
- The Gallery's old bar had touch-action: manipulation, the fix for the
  owner's "the button is not very responsive, it takes pushing it many
  times, there is a lag". The link page's band never had it. One rule in
  styles.css gives it to the band's buttons and speeds, so every full screen
  has it: the link page and the Pad's band too. Flip had it already
  (flip.css).
- The old bar's one speed button stepped from the player's rate, which was
  the cause of "goes to 2x and sticks". The line has no step: a press asks
  for its own speed. verify_gallery now presses three speeds with the
  player's rate lying and reads three speeds. The throw on the way (a pick
  sets the rate, then rebuilds the sound) moved to verify_inline's post with
  sound, because only a drawing with sound reaches the sound. That row pins
  applyRate's catch, which nothing pinned before: without it the player runs
  at 2x and the line says 1x.

LEFT AS IT IS: the link page's own full screen keeps its canvas frame's
inset vignette (.canvas-wrap's inset shadow), which the Gallery and the
Library do not have. verify_onefull's edges rows ask the two of them only.
Put to the owner as an optional choice; the default is to leave it.

verify_onefull asks the Gallery and the Library beside the link page, one
drawing paused at one place, on the owner's phone and a desk, in both
themes: the same parts in the same order, each measuring the same by its
computed size, spacing, type, colour and glass; the same clock; every speed;
the ground at the screen's edges, read off painted pixels; the name in the
corner; the way out. Every row is red on main's code. Taken away one at a
time, each piece turns its own rows red: the band's sheet, its tokens, the
body's type, the player's band hook, its clock, its ground, the box's own
background in full screen, the name, the name stepping back, and the
Library's line scripts.

The in-post player's line costs a host 449 B more (verify_inline, named);
the player's stylesheet 73 B more for the no-double-tap rule (verify_jsstrip
and verify_player_isolation, named).

## After v326 -- a lost lift with a thumb on the glass no longer stops the Pad (a bug fix)

The owner, on an iPhone, the v326 re-test (T1, the Pad): "When I go really
fast it stops accepting strokes at a certain point, but after a little wait
it will accept them again. Not sure it has anything to do with edge." And T2,
Flip: "Seems like flip works but not pad".

The lost-lift fix above rescues a finger the Pad refused by reading the touch
list: if the new finger was the only touch on the glass, the stroke's own
finger was gone. Anything else touching the glass, a thumb resting at its
foot while the other hand draws fast, made the count two. Then the Pad
refused every finger after a lost lift, and only the last touch lifting
cleared it: strokes stop, then come back after a pause, as the owner saw.
Flip ends a stroke on any lift, so it lost only the stroke after it. Driven
here with real touch input, a thumb resting off the drawing and one lift
swallowed before the page's handlers: the Pad drew none of the next four
strokes and Flip drew three. Why lifts go unheard on the owner's phone is
still not known here (there is no WebKit in this box). This is the pattern
reproduced; the next re-test is the test.

`lib/lostlift.js`, shared by both editors, now remembers the stroke's own
touch from the touchstart that came with its pointerdown. A refused finger
draws when that touch is no longer on the glass, whatever else is. A real
second finger leaves it there, so it is refused as before, and two fingers on
the drawing are still a pinch. A stroke whose touch it never saw is judged by
the count, as before. And any touch ending anywhere that leaves the stroke's
touch off the glass ends the stroke, so a stuck stroke can no longer keep the
chrome faded until the next press on the drawing.

Checks. verify_pointerpad gains the resting thumb on both editors: after the
lost lift, the next four strokes give 2, 3, 4 and 5 groups (the stuck one
kept). On the Pad alone, a tap beside the drawing ends a second stuck stroke,
kept, with the take's Done back at full strength. Flip ends a stroke on any
lift, so it cannot fail that row. Each piece, taken away on its own, turns
its own rows red. The old module: the Pad 0, 0, 0, 0, Flip 1, 2, 3, 4, and the
tap leaves the Pad drawing, chrome faded. The rescue by count alone: the same
three rows. No lift rule: only the tap row. The fix: 11/11 on that part of the
suite.

Pad and Flip: shared, one module.

## After v326 -- the server review: what a hand-built request, a smaller host and a big photo meet (bug fixes)

A read-only review of the server and its documents, before the next seal,
found six things a request or a host could reach. Each was reproduced with
the test client; each now has a row that is red on the code before it.

- A point's time `t` was never bounded. An infinite one (1e400 in the JSON),
  a 400-digit one, or a gap too wide for a float answered 500 when the line
  under the post was summed; a NaN was stored as a bare NaN token, which no
  browser can read back, so the post could never play. A 400-digit x
  answered 500 too, through math.isfinite. `t` is now finite and within a
  million million milliseconds, an int of any length counts as finite, a NaN
  anywhere else in the payload is refused (json.dumps with allow_nan=False,
  where the remainder is measured), and the line refuses to sum what it cannot.
  The editors never send these; a hand-built request can.
- A host with no SECRET_KEY, on the memory rate limiter it gets by default,
  answered 500 to every play and every report: the limiter's identity hash
  demanded a key only the db backend stores. Memory forgets on a restart, so
  it now uses a key that lasts the process. The db backend still refuses.
- A photo or a song too big to post told the person a field path: "Couldn't
  post. 'frames[0].photo.data' is too large (8200 kB; limit 8000 kB)." It now
  says "The photo is too big to post (8.2 MB; up to 8 MB). Try a smaller
  one.", and "save" for a draft. The field's version moved to a `detail` key
  for an API caller to match on.
- A DELETE's body (its delete key) escaped the request cap that bounds POST,
  PUT and PATCH: 50 KB of it answered 204 where the same on a PATCH was 413.
  It is bounded on the read now, chunked included, and a DELETE that sends no
  body still needs no length.
- The cards' meta, which can carry a private post's title, and the two
  drafts reads went out with no Cache-Control. They say private, no-store,
  as the listing and the payload already did.
- The demo with SKRIBL_DEMO_IDENTITY set, no login key and CSRF off logged
  that nobody was signed in and the demo would run anonymous, then refused to
  boot for want of CSRF. The refusal is the design verify_hostseams pins (an
  identity without CSRF fails closed, naming the switch); the warning now
  comes only when the demo does boot, with CSRF on.

And the documents it found out of date: SESSION-CONTEXT's standing
preferences contradicted WORKING-AGREEMENTS on the PR ending, the branch and

## After v326 -- the Pad review: seven edges a person could walk (bug fixes)

A read-only review of the Pad, before the next seal, walked it the way a
person does and found seven places it was left in a state it should not be
in. Each was reproduced in a browser; each now has a row in the new
verify_padedges that is red on the code before it (5/17 there, the five that
pass being the no-page-error rows).

- The photo and the music lost their bytes to Clear drawing and to every
  post, while they stayed on screen: the pill said Saved, and a reload said
  "Media missing". Clear drawing now rewrites the autosave (the drawing goes,
  the media stays), and dropping a posted draft keeps the bytes while the
  media is on the page; New Skribl removes the media first, so its bytes
  still go.
- Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y reached Undo and Redo during a replay, past the toolbar
  that takes no pointer then: the canvas jumped while the replay painted on,
  and undoing a one-stroke drawing took Play/Stop away with the replay still
  running and left its ink. Both end the replay first, as Record does.
- An Oval or Poly tap with no drag on a blank canvas started an empty take,
  so the next drawing after Done was never recorded. A shape that makes no
  points is unwound now, exactly as a pinch unwinds the stroke its first
  finger began.
- A reload lost the drawing's name, its Pauses and the speed its viewers
  start at. The autosave carries all three (the typed name only, so a blank
  one still takes a fresh date name), as a post and Flip's autosave do.
- New Skribl with only a photo, a track or a picked ground said "Already a
  fresh one" and left them. They count as work now, as the drafts count them
  and How it works promises.
- Export opened during a replay saved the replay so far as "The final
  drawing as a still image". Opening Export ends the replay first, as Post and
  Video do; the Video option's tooltip says "with its music" only when there
  is some.
- A draft opened over a drawing never played had its see-through strokes
  painted twice (alpha 192 for 128): the old drawing's base, still decoding,
  painted the new strokes, then the new drawing's own decode did. Clearing
  the canvas supersedes a restore in flight, and a decoded base is cached
  under its own source.

And four messages said "Stop recording" for the button that says Done.

Checks: verify_padedges, one section per edge. The two halves of the media
fix each redden their own row (the autosave Clear drawing rewrites; the bytes
a posted draft keeps).

Pad and Flip: the Pad's. Flip draws its exported page and its card on its own
canvas, and its own review is separate.

## After v326 -- the Flip review: undo, the page bar, the strip and the paste (bug fixes)

A read-only review of Flip, before the next seal, drove it with a real mouse
and real touch and found seven ways it acted on the wrong thing, or on
nothing. Each now has a row in the new verify_flipedges, red on the code
before it (2/14 there, the two that pass being the no-page-error rows).

- "Undo clear" never worked by mouse or finger. Every pointerup on the page
  ran endStroke, which spent the clear's backup before the button's click
  arrived; only Enter on the focused button reached it. It is spent by a
  stroke now, and by an undo or redo that acts, not by a Ctrl+Z on the empty
  page a clear leaves.
- The undo history outlived the document. After New Skribl, Clear all pages
  or opening a file or a draft, Undo pulled a deleted page into the new
  drawing, or threw and left every stroke after it throwing until a reload.
  A replaced document starts with none.
- An undo named its page by position, and Duplicate, Blank, a page move and
  a paste shift pages without an entry of their own. A selection's Flip
  undone after a Duplicate rewrote the page beside it; a tween's undo deleted
  the artist's page and its redo put one page object in twice. Every entry
  carries the page it acted on, found again at undo time (dropped when it is
  gone), and a tween's carved holds go back by page.
- On a desk the page bar stayed live during playback, and its Delete took
  whichever page was flashing by. play() now disables it as its own rule
  always said, and the page actions refuse while playing.
- "Select through here" was always disabled on a phone, where the ⋯ shows
  only on the current page: the test was "this is the current page". It
  starts from the page you were on before.
- After Cut, the chip says "paste it on any page", and on a blank page there
  was no Paste: the selection bar showed only with a selection. With the
  Select tool held and something cut or copied, it shows Paste and Done; and
  Ctrl+V pastes a cut selection when no pages are copied.
- With a page copied, the paste ghost in the strip put the playback outline,
  the loop's bracket, a drag's drop and Move mode's scope a tile off. Every
  lookup counts pages (_tiles), as the thumbnails already did.

And the tile's x names its page and says its first press out loud, as every
other arm here does (SK-AUD-018); four notes lost their capitals and
"In-between" for the button's own "Tween", the onion skin's "stacked-sheets
button" and the photo's "Media"; a group tooltip that said "Pen / Eraser"
and two comments describing things that are gone are gone.

Pad and Flip: Flip's. The Pad's own review is above; Flip's New Skribl
still undoes through Undo clear, where the Pad shows an Undo chip (a choice
for the owner).

And the Gallery says "Tap one to watch it come alive" (a Flip does not draw

## After v326 -- one music editor: the Pad and Flip share the music drawer (bug fixes)

The owner, with Flip's Fine-tune on screen: "flip has crossfade ... it needs
to be the same music editor on both pad and flip." (The words review had said
Flip had no Crossfade, from a search that stopped short; it was wrong, and
the help was put right in that PR.) The drawer's markup was already one file
and its arithmetic was shared, but every control's wiring was written twice,
in editor_music.js, editor_photo.js and app.js for the Pad and in flip.js for
Flip, and the copies had drifted. lib/musicdrawer.js is the one copy now:
Trim | Fine-tune, the loop detail's zoom and Scroll, the edges' drags and
nudges, Crossfade, Match Drawing Time, Preview Loop, Test Seam and the
switch. Each editor hands it its own state through hooks; the state stays
where it was (the Pad's player reads it through app.js). Where the two
differed, each now does what the better side did:

- Crossfade carried a playing preview over to the new join on Flip; the Pad's
  kept the old join until it was stopped. Both carry it now, Play's music too.
- Test Seam played the join on the Pad (the loop's last 1.25 s, the join, its
  first 1.25 s) and the loop from its top, twice, on Flip; with a crossfade
  set, the Pad played the whole clip three times instead. Both play the join,
  on the baked clip, the posted loop itself, so the crossfade is in it. It
  stays an <audio> element played inside the tap, the path that is heard on
  an iPhone set to silent (not tested here: no WebKit).
- Preview Loop's fallback, when Web Audio cannot start, was the baked clip
  looping on the Pad and the raw track wrapped by a timer on Flip, where no
  crossfade is heard. Both loop the baked clip.
- The Pad's Preview Loop played at the replay's speed, pitch and all, because
  the gapless engine follows the replay for Play. A preview is the loop as
  posted: 1x.
- The Pad saved a trim only on a mouseup or touchend ON the strip, so an edge
  let go past it was never saved. Every change to the loop saves itself when
  it lands, as Flip's did.
- Match Drawing Time counted Flip's pages at one frame each: no holds, no
  drawing pages, no loops (lib/holdtiming.js plan has the length as it
  plays). And on a Flip with nothing drawn it set a 0.5 s loop; it leaves the
  loop alone, as the Pad's does. Flip does not fit a new track to the drawing
  on its own, as the Pad does: a Flip loops, and a one-second song would
  stutter under it (not for Flip, by its nature).
- The switch, off, silenced Flip's Play; on the Pad it paused the <audio>
  element only, while the gapless loop and any preview played on. On again
  mid-Play, Flip's music came back and the Pad's did not. Off is silence now,
  Play's music and any preview, and on brings Play's music back where the
  drawing is. A preview is its own request, so it still plays while the
  switch is off.
- The Pad dropped a switched-off track from its draft, its autosave and the
  New Skribl undo: the song was lost. Flip kept it. The Pad keeps it now,
  marked off, and opens it off; a post (and the composer's) leaves it out,
  as Flip's does, so what the author last heard is what a viewer hears.
- A new track kept the Pad's last zoom, focus and scroll, the last song's
  view. Both start a new track, or a new document, on the whole loop at 1x.
- Flip took a photo named song.mp3 as far as a failed decode; it is refused
  by its type now, in the Pad's words (lib/media_validation.js).
- Flip's Play left a preview playing under it; Play stops a preview first, as
  the Pad's always has.

Loose ends, gone: the Scroll and Crossfade rows were built by script in each
editor and are the drawer's markup now; Flip's music file input was a second
copy outside the drawer, visually hidden and still reached by Tab (one input
now, the drawer's, out of the Tab order, and Flip's photo and backup inputs
too); the step size's buttons were named differently on each; the Pad's
"Plays for" label never showed, because the loop's summary wrote over it on
the first trim; and Flip's mute flag was never set.

Pad and Flip: shared, one module both load. Kept apart by nature: how each
Play plays music (the Pad's follows the replay's speed, Flip's keeps its own
pace and loops, the owner's F1), and the fit on adding a track (Pad only).

The player's scripts are 3,134 B lighter (151,670 -> 148,536), and the names
the two editors both define fell from 62 to 53 (verify_surfaces). The new
verify_music drives every row on both editors; each was red on one of them
before.

Found on the way, by the affected suites. The Pad's video export still called
the Test Seam stop this change took away, so an export threw before its
download: fixed, and a search for every removed name found no other caller.
verify_tools kept two exemptions for the music strip's old save triggers,
which the drawer replaced; its stale-entry check said so, and they are gone.
And the next seal could not have started: release_run.py refuses while a
suite on disk is in no batch, and five had reached main in none over five
pull requests (verify_padedges, verify_flipedges, verify_viewedges and
verify_words from the whole-app review, and verify_music here), which only
the seal's own dry run would have said. Each is placed now and tagged by what
it does, and verify_docs asks the same question on every pull request, so the
next unplaced suite is red where it is added (red on main, green here).

## After v326 -- the owner's seven yeses: one name each, the Post title from the name, New Skribl's way back on both, no shadow on any full screen, four tips

The owner said yes to all seven choices on the resubmission page.

  your file" when one opens, on both editors; the Post sheet's too-long words

  editors): a name a person gave, not the date name a blank drawing saves

  And found on the way, on the Pad: a drawing that opened (New's Undo, a
