## After v326 -- T1: asking the phone, with an input log (tooling)

The owner's iPhone, re-testing after v326 (T1): "When I go really fast it
stops drawing. It seems like it's processing because if you wait a second it
will accept your strokes", Flip fine. Then, of the next fix's test steps: "Not
off edge. That was coincidence" and "No rest your thumb". One finger, in the
middle of the drawing, and the Pad stops taking strokes for about a second.

So the reading that #528 and #553 were built on -- a lift the page never
hears, then a thumb resting on the glass -- is not what the phone does, and the
third version of it (where a touch began, not the count) stays off main. It
was never seen on the phone; it was inferred, and twice the inference was
wrong.

Chromium here does not do it. Sixty quick one-finger strokes on each editor,
then 120 with the processor slowed six times, real touch through CDP at 402
by 874: every stroke kept, on both. The pop-ups that sit over the drawing (the
saving pill, the tips) already let a finger through. No timer refuses a press.
The answer is on the phone, and a phone has no console without a Mac.

lib/inputlog.js asks it. Opened with ?inputlog in the address, either editor
records what the screen said: every press, lift and cancel, pointer and touch
alike, where it landed, how many fingers the screen listed and where each
began, what the editor was doing just before (drawing, whose stroke, pinching,
playing, the tool, how many strokes it holds), a press that began no stroke
marked NO STROKE, a frame that came late, and the page losing focus or going
out of sight. Copy log puts it on the clipboard, as Report a problem does; it
sends nothing. Its listeners are passive, on the window, in the capture
phase: it hears everything first and can cancel nothing. Without ?inputlog it
adds no listener and no element. Its bar sits in the top corner, over the
logo, never the drawing.

verify_pointerpad drives it on both editors: off, nothing; on, the bar off the
drawing, a press refused while pinching marked with why, and Copy log's text
headed by the editor and its build. Each was red with its part broken: always
on (both off rows), the mark never written (both NO STROKE rows), either
editor not watched (that editor's rows), the bar moved over the drawing.

Pad and Flip: shared -- one module, each editor passes its own state.

Not tested here: WebKit, which is the point of it.

## After v326 -- T1: nothing heavy while the pen is down (bug fix)

The owner, on the iPhone, after the input log went up: "If I draw back and
fast on iPhone it stops and waits to catch up. Flip is fine. Saving pop?"

The save was the thing. Both editors save a draft a moment after a change:
the Pad 1.2s after a lift, Flip 0.8s after a change. The timer was never told
about the next stroke, so when that stroke began inside the wait -- every
stroke, drawing fast -- the draft was written and the Saved pill popped up in
the middle of it, and the line stood still until both were done. Driven here
with real touch, a stroke begun just after a lift and drawn on past the timer
got one draft write with the pen down, on each editor.

Now the debounced save waits for the finger: if a stroke is down when the
timer goes off, it looks again a quarter second later (editor_draft.js
autosaveWhenLifted, flip.js saveWhenLifted). A flush -- pagehide, leaving for
the other editor -- still writes at once, because that path is about not
losing work and nothing is being drawn then.

Two smaller costs went with it. While the pen is down the saved pill is at a
tenth of its strength, and now its frosted glass steps away too, as the
header's always has: a blur nobody can see, redone for every frame of a
changing screen, is work an iPhone does for nothing. And the Pad's take clock
wrote the same "0:06" five times a second, each a layout; it is written when
its words change.

Measured first, on the way: the Pad restyles about seventeen times as often as
Flip during the same scribble (Chromium's counters, processor slowed four
times: 1,225 against 73), four in five of them the take's waveform, whose bars
dance while the pen is down. That
is the design (the owner's "the wave") and it stays; Chromium may not be what
the iPhone does with it, and the input log is how to find out.

verify_pointerpad: a stroke drawn past the timer gets no draft write with the
pen down and one after the lift, on both editors; the pill has no glass while
drawing; the clock is written at most once a second. Each red with its part
undone: the Pad's old timer, Flip's old timer, the pill's rule removed, the
clock written every tick.

And one thing the old timing hid. A music write the store refused once is
retried by the next save. On main that retry came from the save that landed
mid-stroke, and the save after the lift found the bytes stored and said Saved.
With one save after the lift, the retry's own landing has to say it, and it
did not: the pill refreshed only while showing, and an amber you dismissed is
hidden. Now a landing that turns a dismissed amber green says so
(editor_draft.js _refreshMediaPill). verify_amber's retry row was red with the
save fix alone, 109/110, and is green with this, 110/110.

verify_strokegroups' snapshot taken mid-stroke is now a flush's
(flushFlipDraft while the pen is down): the debounced save no longer writes
mid-stroke, and a flush, the page hidden or left while drawing, still can.

The player carries +74 B of script (the clock written on change, in app.js),
raised in writing in verify_jsstrip and verify_player_isolation.

Pad and Flip: the same rule in each editor's own save, and one shared pill rule.

Not tested here: WebKit. The input log (?inputlog) on the owner's phone is the
test that matters.

## After v326 -- L3 at 150%: the drawing re-fits when the zoom changes, and every ⋯ stays in reach (bug fixes, and the owner's yes to a round +)

The owner's L3 screenshots, at Safari's Page Zoom of 150% on a 402pt iPhone
(268 CSS px wide, under the 320 safety net). The first two came back at 115%,
measured from four controls of known size, so the check was taken again with a
tell: at 150% the Pad's Post button is a round paper plane with no word. Then
the owner: "When I switch back to 100% I get 3rd screen shot. Also check the
... menu at 150%".

The third screenshot was the Pad at 100% with its drawing still the size it
had at 150%, in a band of empty page. The Pad re-fit its canvas only on the
window's resize event, and a zoom changed in Settings while Safari sat in the
background reached the page without one. Flip re-fit when its chrome changed
size (the header, the strip, the dock: a ResizeObserver since #289), so it
followed. That watch is lib/chromefit.js now, and both editors use it: only
the chrome is observed, never the stage, so a fit cannot feed back into
itself, and a fit that moved the canvas says so with a resize event, as
Flip's always did. Measured with the event held back: the Pad stayed 244px
wide at 100%; Flip went to 378, and now the Pad does too.

Thirty-two merges since the v326 seal (#530 to #563) carry no sealed record

The owner's last checks, as they stand at this seal: on the phone the

The first release run of this seal came back red in one suite, and the fix is

## After v327 -- The first hello, as M1: the mark writes itself, its dot bounces in over the i, and the ink lifts away into the canvas (the owner's pick)

THE ASK, after the seal: "his background looks super low resolution. and it
just doesn't grab me. since it's the first thing and first time - it has to
be awesome and kind. it is neither yet." Then "shouldn't he be on laptops too
- any first time?", "weird nubs on the edge of star tips" and "I was hoping
for a super crisp look, but it looks kind of blurry". Four takes on Blooby's
star were mocked and the owner chose C ("C looks good"). C was built and
checked, and before it merged the owner asked: "Should it start with skribl
drawing the brand ... then it evaporates ... Better than blooby star?" The
brand was mocked twice: first written with a brush ("Does yours look like?
No, and the weird wave at the end? Plus blooby is not over the i"), then as
the app draws its mark, as M1 (the dot bounces in) and M2 (Blooby lands on the
i). Then: "I like m1 but look at the dot on the i. It's to the right?", and
"all yes". C never shipped. FUTURE.md 6m has the round.

WHAT M1 IS. The header's own mark (_skribl_brand_mark.html: one stroke, 2.3
of its 30 units wide, slanted 8 degrees, sweeping from Skribl purple to the
accent blue), written by the real pen through the real Flip editor.
harness/tools/make_hello.py reads both of the mark's paths from that template,
so the hello and the header cannot drift. The pen lays the line down in 64
short pieces, each in the sweep's colour where it sits, a lift and a touch at
the same point so it runs on unbroken, fitted into 1.6 s as one movement of
the hand. Then the dot drops in over nine pages at 12 a second: stretched as
it falls, squashed as it lands, a bounce, and three at rest. Then the ink
lifts away in the order it was written: a soft edge sweeps across left to
right while the line rises a little and blurs, and from 0.6 s the ground fades
too, so the canvas shows through as the last of it goes. About 3.4 s in all,
on the page's own ground in either theme (the sweep is 4.5 to 6.2:1 on the
dark, 4.2 to 3.1:1 on the light), and 9 KB as served where Blooby's star was
299.

THE DOT WAS THE MARK'S OWN. The hello traced the header exactly, and the
header's dot sat 1.3 of its units right of the i, toward the b: lost at the
header's size, plain once the mark filled a screen. Before the skew, over the
i is straight up, so the dot's middle is now directly above the i's top (37.9,
15.7), in the header too. The Blooby card's tool (blooby.py) reads the dot from
the template now; the two help demos that draw the card keep the old spot until
they are drawn again.

THE BLUR WAS THE SHRINK (found for C, and kept). The player drew the hello at
three pixels a point: 1593 pixels across a box the iPhone showed 1147.5 wide,
1.39 of its pixels to each of the screen's, off the grid, and the phone's
shrink softened every edge. Now the box is a whole number of the drawing's 9 x
16 steps in screen pixels, placed on whole screen pixels, and the drawing fills
it a whole number of its pixels to each, placed by no transform (the player's
own centring is a translate by half, which an engine may land between pixels).
Twice the screen's pixels where the drawing stays within 8 million, one for one
past that: twice on a 402-point iPhone's full screen would be 10.3 million, and
in Chrome here a canvas of 9 million left the fast path (8.1 million did not),
from half a millisecond a frame to nine. The attach option is `dpr` (it was
`maxDpr`, the hello's alone), 9 bytes lighter as served.

THE WAY OUT IS TRANSITIONS, NOT KEYFRAMES. cssgraph keeps every @keyframes in
player.css, as it keeps every Reduce Motion rule (its superset gate), so a
keyframes for the hello would be paid for by every shared link. lib/hello.js
sets the soft edge in place first, all of the ink still showing, a frame before
it moves; and the transitions belong to the moving rule alone. On the edge's
own rule, putting the edge in place glided in from hidden, and the first look
at the way out was a blank screen. Under Reduce Motion lib/hello.js leaves the
lifting off and the whole hello just fades.

A FLIP'S LAST MOMENT IS ONE BEFORE ITS END. At its very end the player's clock
comes round to the first page (holdtiming's wrap), which for the hello is the
word before it starts: a blank canvas. The still under Reduce Motion showed
exactly that until it asked for the last moment instead, as the player's
scrubber already does, and the way out asks for it too if the drawing reached
its end first. The same wrap ends a Flip whose loop a viewer turns off (the
full-screen bar, the Library) on its first page rather than its last: named in
FUTURE.md 6m for its own fix.

ANY SCREEN, ANY KEY, ONE WELCOME. It comes on the first visit on a desk as on a
phone; never in a composer's frame. A tap, a click or any key skips it, and the
key does nothing else. Seen is per hello (skribl.hello.v2), so someone who met
Blooby meets the mark once. When it will not come, the hello takes its element
away at once, and the button cards' first note (lib/learncard.js) looks for it:

## After v327 -- The hello asks for its files first and draws once the page is ready, so a slow first visit still gets it, smoothly (bug fix)

The owner: "Why does it not show every time in incognito". Two reasons, one of
them a bug.

Once it has played, a private window remembers it: the hello comes once, and
Chrome and Edge keep one memory for every incognito window until the last one
closes. That is by design.

The bug: an empty cache, as every private window has, on a slow line. The
hello waited LATE (4 s) for its three files (the player, the hold timing, the
drawing) and otherwise did not come that time. They are small, but they were
asked for after the editor's own 104 scripts (384 KB here) and came with them.
Measured here on an empty cache, with Chrome's network presets: Slow 4G had
them at 3.3 s of its 4, and 3G at 6.5 s, so on 3G it never came, and on a
phone's real line Slow 4G sits at the edge.

The first fix asked for the three at high priority (fetchPriority on the two
scripts, priority on the drawing's fetch): Slow 4G had them at 0.45 s, 3G at
0.92 s. But then the hello began long before the page's own scripts were done
and drew while they ran, and on a phone (the processor slowed four times,
Slow 4G) it froze for up to 0.65 s at a time as each one did. A hop is a bug
here as much as a miss.

So the files are asked for first, and the hello draws once the page's own
scripts are done (DOMContentLoaded), as it always did on a fast line; LATE
counts from then. Measured the same way: on a fast line it starts just after
the page is ready, as before, worst gap 0.15 s; on Slow 4G it came three runs
in three, worst gap 0.13 s, where the old hello missed one run in three; and
on an empty cache it comes on every line tried, 3G too. Nothing more is
fetched.

The two slow-line rows read the hello the same way now. The one for the page's
own scripts (after v327) asks that it never plays as plain pages, while those
are held and once they come: with the hello waiting for the page, there is no
player at all while they are held.

CHECKED (verify_hello, an empty cache on DevTools' 3G): the hello comes, its
files here before the page's own scripts, and it draws once those are done.
Red on the hello before this (taken away at 4.4 s, its files at 6.8 s), red on
the first fix (it drew at 2.6 s, the page ready at 8 s), green with this; the
page-scripts row red on the hello before #569 (plain pages, 833 ms). The
measuring tool was itself shown both ways first: it read "not this time" on
every run until its watch was pointed at the document rather than a root that
did not exist yet.

Not tested here: WebKit, and the live site, whose server may share the line
differently from this box's (HTTP/1.1 here); the priority is the same ask of
the browser either way. The frame gaps are this box's software drawing with
the processor slowed; their size against each other is what they show.

## After v327 -- Main red after #573: the hello's touchend, named and allowlisted

#573 gave the hello a touchend (a tap that skips it presses nothing under it)

would leave stuck. The hello's holds none: it only cancels the click a tap

## After v327 -- Recolor: a line already drawn takes a new colour (the owner: "I love the recolor too")

The mock of recolouring lines (choices 1-6, each defaulting to yes) and the
owner's "I love the recolor too", taken as yes to all six. This entry is the
editors' half: the button, the mode, the run of colour, undo, Flip's Select bar.
The replay showing a change when it was made, and the Blooby card's demos with
the new dot, follow.

ONE MODULE FOR BOTH EDITORS (lib/recolor.js): the hit-test, the colour rule,
the run along the line and the bar. What a change does to a drawing stays each
editor's: the Pad's undo stack and its record of the moment (editor_tools.js),
Flip's page entry in its action log (flip.js).

THE BUTTON sits beside the eyedropper, its mirror (that takes a colour from the
drawing, this gives one to it). In the colour row the pair made eleven items,
which at a phone's 24px dots shut the gaps to 7px at 402 and overlapped them at
320 -- the crowding the owner sent back once ("the pink is too close to
white"). So the eyedropper and Recolor sit together at the end of the Pen |
Background row, at every size, and the colour row is nine colours again (15px
apart at 402). That is the one change from the mock, where the pair closed the
colour row: said in the report, and one CSS grid to put back. The two stay 30px
with the eyedropper's own 8px of touch round each (46 to a finger), 16px apart
so the touch areas meet without crossing; the phone rule that grew the
eyedropper's to 10px was for the 24px button the colour row needed, and with
the row to themselves they need neither.

THE MODE. Tapping Recolor closes the drawer, and its bar takes the dock's row
(the dock keeps its size and glass, so nothing moves; its own controls fade out
of sight and out of reach): the pen's colour, "Tap a line to recolor", Undo and
Done. The mock's bubble on the canvas hid the lines you would tap, so the words
are in the bar. The colour opens the drawer to change it, and a pick there
closes it again. Done, Escape, a replay and the eraser key end the mode. Flip's
Select and Move bars take the page bar's row; this bar takes the dock's on both
editors, so the two behave the same, and Undo is in the bar because the dock's
is under it.

A LINE is one movement of the pen (a group). A Flip fill is many groups laid in
one tap, read as one line (consecutive level bands, each starting a millisecond
after the last ended, one colour), or a tap on a fill would recolour a stripe.
An eraser's stroke is never hit. A tap takes the topmost line under it, else the
nearest within a finger's slack; a drag takes each line it crosses, once; a
press changes nothing until it lifts or travels, so the first finger of a pinch
recolours nothing. The colour keeps the line's opacity, in whichever form its
colour was written (hex, rgba, a Smear's hex-8).

THE COLOUR RUNS ALONG THE LINE from the finger, both ends at once, 380 ms,
eased. The editor repaints once with the new colour; a canvas laid over the
drawing shows the drawing as it was (the artwork stage, backdrop and photo and
ink) across the part the colour has not reached, shrinking to nothing, and goes.
The editor's canvas is never painted by the run, so nothing it paints meanwhile
can be painted over. Under Reduce Motion the colour simply changes.

UNDO is one step a gesture: the Pad pushes its history state and REPLACES the
recoloured points (a state holds the point objects themselves -- Select's lesson
in editor_draw.js); Flip records one before/after page entry ('selframe', named
Recolor), as the Select bar's actions do.

THE PAD KEEPS THE MOMENT (app.js `recolors`): the line, its old and new colour,
the drawing's length then, which gesture it was (`k`: the lines one drag
crossed share one, so a replay runs them together, and two taps with nothing
drawn between them do not), the point the colour ran from, and, while a take
records, the take's clock. The points carry the colour they ended with, so every
still picture and any player that never reads the list shows the drawing as it
was left; the list is what will let the replay show the change when it was made
(the owner's R2). v219 took Select off the Pad because it moved recorded points
and the replay drew them in their new place at their old time; this is the same
kind of edit, with its time kept. A post, a .skribl file and the draft carry
it, the history states hold it, and the server keeps it as it keeps any frame
key, inside the payload's extra-bytes budget. A recolour among the undone steps
leaves the draft's redo out (the restore rebuilds history as the applied strokes
plus later strokes, and an undone recolour changed lines already drawn), so a
reload never brings an undone colour back. And the undo a reload rebuilds, a
line at a time, keeps in each state only the recolours made by then: a line
undone there takes the later recolours with it, where they would have waited
for the next line drawn to reach their moment and played in the middle of it.

WHAT IT COST: the player's JavaScript +364 B, all app.js (the list kept with
the undo states, the clear, the post's frame and the load, which is the part
the player needs), raised in verify_player_isolation and verify_jsstrip
together. verify_surfaces counts one more name both editors define,
paintPenSwoosh: the Pad's pen-colour funnel is a function now, like Flip's,
since Recolor's bar follows the pen colour from there on both.

FLIP: one page entry of undo a gesture; the page thumbnail's signature reads
colour now (it read only shape, so a recoloured page kept its old tile); and a
generated page that was recoloured, or the pages either side of one made from a
recoloured page, is saved as it now looks, not as the recipe that would rebuild
it in the old colours (the recipe's print reads positions, never colours). The
Select bar gains Color: every selected line takes the pen's colour, keeping its
opacity, as one step of undo; its glyph is the pen's colour; on a phone the
count is the bare number, so the row's seven buttons fit.

CHECKED (verify_recolor, new, on both editors): each row was shown red
by its own break -- the tools back in the colour row (the row's gaps, the
pair's place), the tools left showing with Background, the dock's controls
reachable, the drawer left open, a colour pick leaving it open, an undo step for
a tap on nothing, an undo step per line of a drag, the first of overlapping
lines taken, a solid colour for a see-through line, an eraser's stroke hit, a
pinch's first finger recolouring, no run, a run under Reduce Motion, no clock
during a take, no recolours in a post or a draft, the undone recolour's redo
written, no moment number, the rebuilt undo keeping a later recolour, the
tools' touch areas crossing on a phone, a thumbnail blind to colour, a fill taken a band at a time, a tween
page saved as its recipe, the bare count, and a replay or the eraser key leaving
the mode on. verify_parity lists Recolor among the controls both editors carry.

Pad and Flip: shared (lib/recolor.js, the drawer partial, the dock's bar);
Flip alone has the Select bar's Color, as it alone has Select. Not tested here:
WebKit, and the owner's fonts.

## After v327 -- the replay shows a recolour when it was made (the owner's pick R2)

Choice 2 of the recolour mock, "the Pad's replay shows the change when you
made it", yes with the other five. Every replay of a Pad drawing -- the Pad's
Play, the link page, the in-post player (Gallery, Library, a host's feed), and
the GIF, WebM and MP4 exports -- now plays a recoloured line in the colour it
was drawn in; at the moment it was recoloured, the new colour runs along it
from where it was tapped, as it did in the editor; and the replay carries on.

ONE MODULE FOR EVERY REPLAY (lib/recolorplay.js), so they cannot show it
differently. place() puts each moment into the timeline as two entries, where
it was made and RUN (380 ms of replay) after, and everything after waits RUN;
the replay is that much longer, at any speed in proportion. The replay cores
hand those entries to the timeline's player instead of drawing them.

THE CHANGE IS A REPAINT, never a line drawn over the old one: a line drawn
later across it, an eraser through it and a see-through colour come out as the
finished drawing has them only if the drawing so far is painted again in its
colours as of then. Each engine keeps its own paint (its base, its compositor,
which reseeds from the repaint); the module says what to paint.

THE RUN is a canvas laid exactly over the drawing (its box, its transform, its
fit, fractions and all: half a pixel off would hop back as it ends) showing the
drawing as it now is, with the part of each line the colour has not reached as
it was. The drawing's own canvas is hidden under it and never painted by it, so
a seek's copy can never hold half a run. A scrub inside the run keeps it; one
that repaints from before the moment starts it again when it reaches it.
Under Reduce Motion the colour simply changes, and the moment is a still RUN:
the replay is one length for everyone. An export has no screen to lay a canvas
over and draws the run into its frames.

A MOMENT COUNTS by one rule: an entry whose `k` is a whole number from 0 and
whose `n` is a whole number from 1 to the points there are; entries sharing a
`k` (one drag) are one moment. The server keeps the same rule
(validation._payload_line), so the line under a post says the replay's length
and its shape with the run in them -- checked against the JS on 400 drawings
with junk entries in, and on a real post. What a moment paints never changes
its timing.

WHAT IT COSTS, AND WHO PAYS: the module is 10,114 B and is fetched by the link
page and the in-post player ONLY for a drawing that has recolours; nearly all
drawings have none, and pay for the hooks alone: the link page +1,487 B
(app.js), a page of posts +1,735 B (inlineplayer.js). The editors load it with
lib/recolor.js, which now takes its colour rule and the run's shape from it.
verify_jsstrip counts the page's script tags, not every asset its config names,
and pins the module on its own; verify_player_isolation and verify_inline raise
with the hooks' names.

ALSO: a GIF lost a base drawn before the first take whenever see-through
layering was on -- its compositor was made before the base and the first
present() wiped it. It is made after the base now, as the two video exports
always had it.

Pad and Flip: the replay is the Pad's (Flip's recolours edit the page in place,
and a Flip plays pages). CHECKED (verify_recolorplay, new, each row shown red
by its own break: the timeline not placed, the cores drawing a moment as a dot,
a scrub stopping the run, Reduce Motion ignored, the link page never fetching or
always fetching the module, the server not counting the run, the GIF's
compositor before its base, the run laid on whole pixels, the in-post player
not placing, the exports drawing on the editor's canvas). Not tested here:
WebKit, and the MP4 export, which needs real Chrome (the same code as the GIF
and WebM paths; CI's MP4 job makes one but does not read its colours).

MAIN WENT RED AFTER #576, on both of the player's byte lines (verify_jsstrip,
verify_player_isolation): 149,458 B against 149,448. Recolor's line was set
from 149,443, measured before its last 15 B -- a fresh take clearing the
recolours, the fix for a take that kept the last one's -- and never measured
again. Its cost was +379 B, not +364. This change's lines are measured on
main's tree plus this change (150,945, +1,487 B), and the two notes say so.
The lesson is the old one: a ratchet is measured on the commit it ships in.

ALSO: verify_surfaces read a script's assets with a greedy match, so the
in-post player's tag, which names lib/recolorplay.js in a data attribute, read
as that module in place of inlineplayer.js, and every module the player reads
looked unread. It reads the SRC now (shown red on the old match, and on a page
given a module nothing reads).

AND verify_replayspeed's "a second tap carries it on" read the fill once,
300 ms after the tap. At 8x what is left of its replay runs about 310 ms and a
post loops, so beside two other suites the read caught the next lap at 0%: the
replay had carried on, finished and begun again. It reads the fill on every

when a sheet over the drawing keeps the tap from carrying anything on).

## After v327 -- Recolor keeps its pointer on Flip after a colour change (the owner's desktop check R3)

The owner, checking Recolor on a desk: "on flip the pointer dissapears when I
select a different color to recolor the lines ... as soon as I change the
color, the pointer dissapears over the canvas." The mode puts the pen's ring
away and wants the system's crosshair, which lib/recolor.js wrote inline on
the canvas from sync(), the one call every colour change passes. A colour pick
also sets the pen's own cursor inline: 'none' on Flip, for the ring. The Pad
set the pen's first and then synced, so the crosshair came back; Flip's
setColor() synced first and then ran setTool('pen'), so the pen's 'none' came
last and nothing at all showed over the canvas.

The mode's crosshair is now a rule over any inline cursor while it is on,
body.recoloring on each editor's canvas (flip.css #pad, styles.css #canvas),
and lib/recolor.js writes no cursor at all: the order an editor calls things
in cannot lose it again, nor can Flip's zoom, which writes '' (Flip's canvas
is 'none' under it). On the Pad the rule also covers a finished take, whose
lock writes 'not-allowed' where recolouring is allowed.

verify_recolor, THE POINTER (new, on a desk, both editors): the pointer over
the canvas is a crosshair in the mode, and still is after a colour picked from
the bar. On the tree before the fix, Flip's second row was red ('none') and
the Pad's were green. Each rule taken out alone turns its own editor's rows
red: Flip's to 'none', the Pad's to 'not-allowed' on a loaded drawing.

lost it.

## After v327 -- The hello's ground is the first paint (the owner's desktop checks, H1 and H3)

The owner, of the hello on a desk: "on a reload it goes to the canvas first,
then goes to the skribl cursive with i's dot dropping in." lib/hello.js shows
the hello once the page's own scripts are done and its files are here, and by
then the page had painted the canvas: on a reload of the replay link here, 15
frames of the Pad's header, canvas and dock came before the hello (about 0.6 s).

Whether it comes is now decided in the page's head, before the first paint, as
the theme is: _skribl_hello_boot.html (both editors include it after the theme
boot) stamps data-hello-comes on the page and lays the hello's ground over it
(styles.css, THE HELLO'S GROUND: body::after, just under the hello). The hello
comes in over that ground, which goes from under it as it leaves, so the canvas
is first seen as the ink lifts. lib/hello.js reads the stamp and decides
nothing of its own; the key it marks seen with is the one the head reads.

The ground never holds up a page that is ready. It stays while the page's own
scripts come, as an app's launch screen does, since the canvas does nothing
before they run; once they are done lib/hello.js waits 0.3 s more for its files
and then fades it, and a hello whose files come later still comes in over the
canvas, as it did (on a slow line that is where it differs from a plain 2.5 s
cap, which would have shown a page that did nothing and then covered it). If
lib/hello.js never runs, or the page never gets that far, the head fades it at
8 s. Under Reduce Motion its fade is near-instant, as every fade is.

A reload keeps showing the page it leaves until the new one paints; that is
the browser's, and it is the page that was there. From the new page's first
frame on, it is the ground and then the hello.

verify_hello, read off every frame the screen made (Page.startScreencast) on a
reload of the replay link, the page being left painted a colour no Skribl page
is (only the frames after the first of that colour count) and one of the
editor's scripts held 0.8 s: the first thing painted is the hello's ground and
no frame of the page comes before the hello, on the Pad and on Flip. Red on the
tree before (6 frames of the page, first, on each editor). Each part shown red
on its own: the ground's rule gone (7 frames of the page); the 0.3 s gone (the ground waited for the hello to
give up, lifting at 4.7 s with the page ready at 0.7); the backstop gone (still
up at 9.5 s with lib/hello.js refused); lib/hello.js leaving the ground in
place (the existing row "then it is gone, the canvas there again"); and the key
drifting or a second decision in lib/hello.js (a static row). Beside two other
suites the row first went red on Flip with one frame of the page before the
ground: the screen's first frame was the page being left as it was before its
colour was painted, read as the new page. It now waits two frames for that
colour and counts only what comes after it; four runs on Flip with the machine
loaded past its cores were clean before that change too, so it was the
instrument, not a flash.

Pad and Flip: shared, one partial and one module for both.

columns were empty while colours ran. Each colour's moment is now a dot of the

reads every script, not the files it names. The card is not built twice, so the

THE PAGE THAT WENT. Main's full battery on the seal's commit (run 39702105179) was green in fifteen
of its sixteen jobs. In PostgreSQL's fourth shard, verify_help's "Flip: the page
stays where it was opened, all through the sheet" was red: "Execution context
was destroyed" at the first evaluate after the page's load, and "it loaded
again: nothing seen". It is that row's second red, both times Flip on a phone
and both on CI (the first, after #575, on sqlite 5/6); the same tree passed it
in the seal and on every other job.

What the record says, and what it does not: Playwright words any lost context
that is not a crash or a closed page that way (its crExecutionContext.js
rewriteError; a crash is reported as a crash), and no load of the page was
heard. A hundred and twenty runs of the row's own opening here, three at once,
one with the CPU slowed four times, each recording DevTools' own events, lost no
context. So the cause is not known, and what the row asks is not changed.

What changes is what it keeps: the browser's own account of the page after its
load (DevTools' events for a context destroyed or cleared, a navigation in the
document or out of it, a crash), each with its time from the load, said in the
row when the page goes. As it is, both editors' rows are green (verify_help
87/87). With the page made to reload itself 1.25 s after its load, both are red
and name it twice over, Playwright's load and the browser's own (a reload asked
for at +1.25 s, the contexts cleared and the frame navigated at +1.43 s). A
renderer crashed on purpose took the test driver down with it, so it shows
nothing about the row and is not counted. The app is unchanged.

## After v328 -- bootstrap.sh finishes an install it was cut off in

The session after the handoff, checking the ground: the first
`harness/bootstrap.sh` was reaped at a turn boundary part way through its pip
installs. The second run found the venv's python3, skipped installing, and
stopped at the tables with "No module named 'flask'"; so would every run after
it, until the venv was deleted or the installs were run by hand. The owner:
"yes, put up the bootstrap fix".

A venv the script makes now carries a mark, `.bootstrap-installing`, from before
the venv exists until both installs have finished. While the mark is there,
the next run installs again into the venv it finds. A venv with no mark is used
as it is: README-OFFLINE's, made from the wheels with no package network, must
not send pip to a network it does not have, and a venv an earlier bootstrap
finished has no mark either.

verify_bootstrap runs the script against a stand-in python3.12 whose venv's
python3 and pip only write down what they were asked, and whose pip fails on
request; every run stops at the tables, so no server starts and nothing is
fetched. Red on the script as it was (4/7: no mark after the failed run, and
no install on the next), and red with the mark never taken off (5/7: a
finished venv installed into on every run). Green as built (7/7). The owner's
case ran for real too: a fresh venv, a bootstrap stopped at 20 seconds (the
mark left), then a second run that installed, booted, and imported Flask and
Playwright, with the mark gone. It needs no browser, server or network, so it
joins the pull-request gate beside verify_runreport, and the release batch
that suite is in.

Pad and Flip: not for either; this is the harness's environment, not the app.

## After v328 -- Two saves of one account draft at once: one saved, the other told, never a 500 (AUD-002, bug fix)

The auditor's second answer, `skribl-v328-audit-developer-package-AZ.zip`
(SHA-256 cd6dbf261420..., about 155 KB), kept as received in
`docs/audit/v328/returned-a-to-z/` with its three reports beside it as `.txt`
(as the first answer's are, so verify_docs does not read their quoted totals as
ours). Its own SHA256SUMS checks. The release decision: NOT READY for
unconditional launch sign-off, and nothing scored; the browser was still
refused, so nothing on screen was seen. AUD-001: the patch verified on a copy
(145/145) and to be sealed in the next release. HIST-001: as before. And the
first product finding, AUD-002, HIGH: two saves of one account draft made
together, on SQLite, answered one 200 and one 500 (three of three, with both
held after each had read the draft; scripts/draft_race.py).

WHAT HAPPENS. Skribl makes every SQLite request a real transaction
(models.py's BEGIN recipe), so a save's reads hold the file's read lock until
the request ends. Two saves that have both read, then both write, deadlock,
and SQLite makes one fail with "database is locked". The comparison's row
lock (with_for_update) is PostgreSQL's alone. The failing write was the ORM's
flush, which also marks the host's session for rollback, so even a caught
error would have come back as a 500 from the host's commit.

WHAT CHANGES (skribl/drafts.py save_draft). The overwrite of a saved draft is
one UPDATE statement, not the ORM's flush, and a "database is locked" there is
DraftBusy: a 409 with busy:true, "Another save is being made right now. Try
again in a moment." Not a conflict: the lock is the whole file's, so what a
save met may be any write, and a conflict would have the editor say this
draft changed on another device and save a copy that was never needed. The
editor shows the message and keeps the drawing; a Save after it meets the
stored draft as it then is, and a real conflict is answered as one, which the
editor already keeps as a copy (lib/savedrafts.js). On PostgreSQL the row lock
already made the second save a conflict, and still does.

The auditor's other suggestion, the comparison carried into the UPDATE
itself, was built and taken out again: on SQLite a save that has compared
holds the read lock, so the other cannot commit before it writes, and on
PostgreSQL the row is locked; no order of two saves reaches it, so nothing
could show it red, and it stays out.

verify_draftrace, new, in-process through docs/INTEGRATION.md's own host on two
threads, held together at the comparison as the auditor's probe was: twenty
pairs, and a save that meets a write to another draft. On SQLite every pair is
one save and one busy, and the busy one's next Save is the conflict (so the
editor keeps both); the save that meets another draft's write is busy and
then goes through, never a conflict. On PostgreSQL, where DATABASE_URL names
one (CI's postgres jobs), every pair is a save and a conflict. Shown red each
by its own break: main as it was, every pair one 200 and one 500, and the
other draft's write a 500; the ORM's flush put back with the lock still
caught, the same; busy answered as a conflict, false conflicts on both rows;
on PostgreSQL, with_for_update taken out, every pair two 200s, the first save
replaced without a word. As built, 4/4 here and 8/8 with a PostgreSQL 16 run
for the purpose (stopped after; no seal was running). The auditor's own probe
on this tree: (200, 500) three times before, a save and a busy three times
after. It needs neither browser nor server, so it joins the PR gate.

Beside it: verify_clouddrafts 94/94, verify_hostseams 69/69, verify_txcontract
95/95, verify_integration 29/29, verify_csrf 27/27, verify_docs 142/142,
verify_bootstrap 7/7.

Pad and Flip: shared; both save account drafts through lib/savedrafts.js and
this route. Not here: the same SQLite lock on other writes (a post, a draft's
first save), which ratelimit.py already turns into refusals for its own; named,
not chased.

## After v328 -- A WebKit smoke on an iPhone's screen, after every merge (the owner's yes)

The owner passed on a suggestion from another assistant: an npm Playwright
suite in WebKit on an emulated iPhone, catching script errors, console errors
and failed requests, with a screenshot on failure and load times. Asked
whether Skribl already did that: it did not. Every browser suite is Chromium,
plus the Firefox smoke after a merge; this container cannot download WebKit.
Proposed instead in the harness's own shape, not a second npm stack beside a
Python one, and said plainly what it is not: Playwright's WebKit is the engine
Safari is built on, for Linux, not an iPhone. The owner: "let's keep it native
to our Python/Flask stack ... add it to the main branch pipeline".

harness/webkit_smoke.py, built like harness/firefox_smoke.py, on Playwright's
"iPhone 15" (393x659 at 3x, touch, its user agent): the Pad, Flip, the
Gallery, the Library and a share link boot; a stroke on each editor is data
and ink; the Pad's replay plays; each editor posts through its own sheet,
ticked public; the link plays with ink; the Gallery shows both posts and the
Library lists both. On every page: nothing thrown, nothing logged as an error,
no request to Skribl failed or answered 400 or more (warnings printed, not
failed), and a full-page screenshot of any page that broke one of those or
stopped a step, kept as the job's artifact. Each page's first byte,
DOMContentLoaded and load are printed from its own navigation timing, a
baseline rather than a gate. No video: that build records through a media
stack an iPhone does not have, and its answer would describe neither.

CI's new `webkit` job runs it after a merge only, installs WebKit with its
system packages, and fails on a skip, as Firefox's does; main-watch waits for
it too, so a red WebKit smoke opens the "main is red" issue. verify_docs pins
all three (the lane, its skip guard, main-watch's five needs and results).

Checked here on Chromium with the same phone (SKRIBL_SMOKE_ENGINE=chromium):
12/12, with the load times printed. Shown red: on a port Chrome refuses
(5061), every page's steps and the failed-request row; with an error logged
and an error thrown planted on every page, those two rows, and a screenshot of
each of the five pages. Its first real WebKit run is CI's, after this merges.

## After v329 -- Seal only when there is a reason; a preflight before a seal; WebKit opens no red-main issue (the owner's yeses)

The owner, after the v329 seal took half the day: "is there a way to make this
more efficient?", then "yes, do 1, 2 and 4 after the seal", and "we don't need
to seal so frequently."

SEAL ONLY WHEN THERE IS A REASON. WORKING-AGREEMENTS.md's "Sealing a release"
and SESSION-CONTEXT.md §4 now open with it: an outside audit, a release someone
is handed, or the owner's ask. Nothing written said how often to seal, so each
session read the section and sealed; that is why this had been talked about
before and kept coming back.

A PREFLIGHT (release_run.preflight(), on every start and on --dry-run): the
python3 on PATH must import Flask and launch a Chromium, since each batch is
run_harness.sh and runs that python3; no browser, PostgreSQL, Flask server,
run_harness.sh, run_parallel.py, release_run.py or suite may be running
already; and port 5001 must be free. Processes are read by what they are (the
command, the script python runs), never by words in their arguments, and this
run's own ancestors and finished processes are not neighbours; a first draft
that grepped the command lines flagged its own shell and its own probe's
browser. Refused with exit 2 and a line each: the system python3 (no Flask),
a Flask server on 5001 (twice: the process and the port), and a Chromium left
open (each of its processes); green on an idle box with the venv first.

WEBKIT OPENS NO RED-MAIN ISSUE. Its install pulls some 190 system packages
from the Ubuntu mirror, which crawled twice after v328 (about 3 MB every 37
seconds) and timed the job out before the smoke began, at 20 minutes and
then at 40. The job still runs after every merge and shows its own result;
main-watch needs sqlite, postgres, mp4 and firefox. verify_docs pins the four,
and is red with webkit put back in needs.

NOT DONE, item 1 (the seal's non-timing batches side by side): measured from
the v329 run's batch logs, about 106 of its minutes are in batches that must
run alone (they measure, or share a store) and about 51 in the rest, so three
at a time saves some 35 minutes, not the two hours first said, and needs
run_harness.sh made safe to run twice at once (its port, database, log and
LAST-RUN.txt). With seals rare, not worth it; told to the owner.

## After v329 -- HIST-001 found: a promise Chrome collected, not a page that went

Five reds on CI since #575 (main after #575, #583, #594, #595 and the v329
dispatch), each verify_help's Flip-on-a-phone row: "Execution context was
destroyed, most likely because of a navigation", about 1.4s after the load, at
the step that opens every section of How it works; no navigation heard, and,
once the row kept the browser's account, no context destroyed or created, no
crash and no change to the tab.

Reproduced here on that step alone, in a loop: red 15 times in 200 runs at
normal speed, never with the CPU slowed. After each red the page was the same
document (the same performance.timeOrigin, navigation type "navigate") and
answered the next call; the step's timer had run and its promise had resolved
about 80ms after it was set. Playwright's own protocol log said what happened:
the reply to that evaluate was `Promise was collected`, which Playwright words
as the navigation message. The step was one evaluate awaiting a promise the
page resolved from a 60ms timer, and opening the sheet loads its demos
(images, sound, a 690 KB file); in that burst Chrome sometimes collected the
awaited promise. The app was never involved.

The step is now two calls with the wait between them in the suite: open the
sheet, wait 60ms, open its sections. 0 reds in 60 runs of the loop; verify_help
87/87 three times; and red on both editors with a reload put into the opening
("it loaded again" naming the page), so the row still catches a page that
really goes. The browser's account the row keeps stays: it is what ruled out
everything else.

Other suites await promises their pages resolve; none has been seen red this
way, and they are left as they are.

## After v329 -- The draw drawer's four tiles (the owner: "go ahead, build it. Keep it kind")

Under the colour, the drawer was six rows of labelled pills on the Pad and
seven on Flip, behind a "Brush, smoothing & more" button on a phone. The owner
asked for it to be as visual and kind as the ⋯ menu had become, and picked from
four mocked shapes "In place", Joined: four picture tiles -- Brush, Size, Feel,
Eraser -- each painted in the pen's colour with what it holds now; a tap opens
its choices in place, joined to the tile as one shape, and the same tile closes
them. No chevron and no back button (the owner: easy to forget, and cheap).
Colours are the menu's tokens role for role: a tile and its card are the
menu's card, an unchosen choice the paper, the chosen one the one tint.

lib/drawtiles.js owns which tile is open, the pictures and the tiles' words,
and four quick sizes. Every control inside keeps its id and its module, so
nothing behind them changed. Size holds the slider, the quick sizes and
opacity; Feel holds smoothing, pressure ("with a stylus; a finger draws one
width") and Flip's Draw-on; Clear and its Undo stay at the drawer's end. On a
phone the half detent shows Color and the tiles; opening a tile goes to full,
its choices on screen and Clear with them. Closing folds the choices away over
frames; Reduce Motion keeps them still.

Two things the build found. Pad still handed the four groups to the pill
slider, whose pill, with no track to sit in, hung from a far ancestor and
painted a column of tint down the whole page under the chosen choice
(lib/segslider.js now gives .dp-choices the aria-pressed, the one Tab stop and
the arrows, but no pill). And a choice's name ran its two lines together for a
screen reader ("OffAs you drew it").

verify_drawtiles (243 rows) was shown red per component, Pad or Flip, one
theme per device: the pill put back (nothing paints outside the drawer), no
fold (the fold row), not joined and an off-token tile (one shape, the menu's
colours), the pictures ignoring the pen, the detent ignoring tiles (the
phone's full), the choices taken out of the pick groups (one Tab stop, and the
quick size's pressed state), the JS ignoring Reduce Motion, a quick size not
firing the slider's input (the editor's readout), and the tiles' words left
stale. A CSS-only Reduce Motion mutation stayed green -- a global rule already
stills animations -- so the row is pinned by its JS branch instead.

Pad and Flip: shared, one partial and one module.

## After v329 -- The music drawer's three levels (the owner: "I want it all, but from super simple to super powerful")

Step 1 of the music plan the owner approved in the mock ("All yes", then
"Yes" to start): the three levels, with today's controls in their new homes.
The owner's words were the brief: "like 3 levels of controls. The more control
you want, the deeper into the controls you go... most people don't want to get
super detailed, they want it to just work automatically while others like me
want to get super detailed and perfect with the loops... no getting rid of
anything either... Keep it kind too. The 4 pillars."

The drawer's head is one pill of three, each its name over what it is for:
Simple (Skribl does it), Adjust (shape it yourself), Fine-tune (make it
perfect). A level only shows and hides -- `data-levels` on each block, so a
hidden control is `hidden` and out of the Tab order -- and the strip, its times
and the pick line are on every level in the same place, so switching never
moves the loop under the finger. "Switching keeps your loop." says so over the
strip for a moment, taking no tap and no room. The level is remembered, one
key for both editors.

- Simple: Skribl's pick, Fit my drawing, Whole song, Play with my drawing.
- Adjust: the loop's length against the drawing and both ends typed (to the
  hundredth), Smooth restart and Hear the restart.
- Fine-tune: today's Fine-tune re-homed -- the loop detail with Loop / Start /
  End, zoom and Scroll, and Hear the whole loop; Each tap (0.01s, 1 frame,
  0.1s, 1s); Start of loop and End of loop typed (to the thousandth) or
  stepped; the sync line ("Comes round every 8.000s · 240 frames at 30 a
  second · fits your drawing"); Lock the length; Smooth restart and its
  length.

Today's names, kept as ids so nothing behind them moved: Trim is Adjust
(#fineTuneTrim), Match Drawing Time is Fit my drawing (#matchDrawingBtn), Test
Seam is Hear the restart (#testSeamBtn), Preview Loop is Hear the whole loop
(#previewLoopBtn), Crossfade is Smooth restart's length (#crossfadeSlider).
Step size's - and + became Each tap's four. Today's 0.02s and 0.05s steps are
not among them, as the owner chose: "All yes but lose .02 and .05."

SKRIBL'S PICK is what a new song starts on: its first 20 seconds, or all of a
shorter one, with a smooth restart (0.25s, never more than a quarter of the
loop). On the Pad a drawing already there sets the length instead, what is
heard as long as the drawing, as the Pad's add always did. Not on Flip (the
owner said yes): an animation goes round in a second or two, and a loop that
short stutters; Fit my animation is one tap. Phase 1 of the pick, with no ears
yet: "the part that loops best, on the beat" is step 3, and the pick line says
only what is true ("Skribl picked the first 8 seconds, as long as your
drawing, with a smooth restart."). A change says "You've made your own loop."
with Back to Skribl's pick, whose Undo lasts eight seconds. When it was the
drawing that changed -- an Undo with the drawer open, or more drawing after
the song -- the line says "Your drawing has changed since Skribl picked this
loop." instead, and the way back fits the drawing as it is now. A song a draft
brings back keeps the draft's loop: the pick is for a song just chosen (Flip
marks that with `musicFresh`; the Pad's add already skipped a restore).

A SMOOTH RESTART MAKES THE LOOP SHORTER, which the drawer now counts. The
crossfade folds the loop's end over its start (lib/audioloop.js), so what is
heard comes round sooner than the stretch selected, by the crossfade's length.
Match Drawing Time set the selection to the drawing and, with a crossfade on,
fell short of it by that much; Fit my drawing makes what is HEARD as long as
the drawing, and "fits your drawing" and every length the drawer says are what
is heard. With the pick turning the smooth restart on for every new song (the
owner said yes to that too), this went from a corner to the common case.

PLAY WITH MY DRAWING is the editor's own Play (it shows the whole drawing, as
Play does), and follows it however it is pressed; with nothing to replay it
plays the loop on its own and says "Play the loop". The Pad's replay rests the
drawer while it plays, as it always has, so Stop is the header's.

Four things the build found, each fixed where it lived:

- The drawer did not hear about the drawing. Fit stayed off after the first
  stroke, and the lines went stale after an Undo with the drawer open. Each
  editor's duration label already ran on every drawing change (the Pad's
  updateDrawingTimeLabels, Flip's syncFlipDuration); it now refreshes the
  drawer too, measuring the drawing once per refresh.
- A level picked soon after a song landed, or soon after the drawer opened,
  chased the page down: the reveal's late re-asserts (300, 700 and 1200ms)
  saw a taller drawer and carried the page to its new end, the switch just
  tapped under the header. lib/drawerdetent.js: a level change moves
  followGrowth's baseline and calls its re-asserts off, and a press inside a
  drawer calls off revealPanelEnd's (once the person acts, the page is
  theirs). Fine-tune's own reveal shows the loop detail but never scrolls the
  switch out of sight.
- A length said two ways: a 4.448s drawing was "the first 4.4 seconds" over
  an Adjust line saying 4.45s. The seconds are rounded from the hundredths
  the lines show, as a person rounds what they read: 4.5.
- A two-line label read as one word ("SimpleSkribl does it"), the bug the
  draw drawer's tiles had: a space between the two spans, which the flex
  layout ignores.

The loop detail's header says "smooth 0.25s" where it said "xfade 250ms".
How it works says the new words: Three levels, Skribl's pick, Fit my drawing
(or animation), Smooth restart, Hear the restart, Play with my drawing, Loop
Detail with Hear the whole loop, Start and end with Adjust's typed ends, Each
tap and Lock the length. verify_helpclaims claims each, and its census of
named controls knows the new ones (the level switch by its group, How much
control).

verify_musiclevels was shown red per component: a broken copy of one file
served to the browser (the files on disk untouched), one part of the suite
run. The levels not hiding turned the three "what each level shows" rows and
"hidden, so out of the Tab order" red on both editors; the level not stored,
"remembered"; no note, "says so"; a switch that moved the loop, "keeps the
loop". The pick without its smooth restart, both editors' pick rows; Flip's
pick not applied, its pick and its way back; Flip's pick applied on every
decode, its re-add and its draft rows; no Undo, the way back and the eight
seconds; a minute's Undo, the eight seconds; the pick not remembered, "an
Undo says the drawing changed", which the Pad's refresh hook removed also
turned; the old rounding, the 4.448s row. Match Drawing Time's old sum, Fit
and the one tint; Whole song keeping its start, or never "Longest loop", its
row; Flip's refresh hook removed, Flip's "Fit wakes"; Fit never off, both.
The switch always coming back at 0.25s, both; the lines counting the
selection, both. No comma, no put-back, a frame fixed at the Pad's 1/30 (Flip's
frame and sync line), no size order (Flip's frame), no lock, no frames in the

The glide rows read the switch on every animation frame, and beside two other

Four more reds beside the others were the suites' own, each fixed where it

## After v329 -- Hear the loop, and Tap the beat (the owner: "so I'm not at 7 or 9 when I want 8")

The owner, with the three levels live: "How do I test the loop without having
it show me drawing? It's cumbersome, plus to know how many beats are in the
loop, so I'm not at 7 or 9 when I want 8." The mock laid the answers into the
real drawer and photographed them beside today's; "All yes" to its five
defaults.

THE PAIR THAT PLAYS. Play with my drawing and Hear the loop sit side by side,
the same size, under the strip and the pick line on every level, so an end
dragged is an end heard. Each is its verb over what it plays (Play / with my
drawing, Hear / the loop), and Stop while it plays. Hear the loop is today's
Preview Loop, the music alone, round and round; the loop detail's own Hear the
whole loop went, since the pair sits just above it (the owner's second yes).
An end moved while the loop plays is heard from its next time round: the
gapless engine starts the new loop where the old one comes round, never a cut
mid-loop. With nothing drawn, Play with my drawing waits, faded, as Fit my
drawing does; step 1 had it play the loop instead, which is Hear the loop's
job now. Under 360px half the row is 127px and "with my animation" needs 160,
so there the two go one to a row.

TAP THE BEAT, on Adjust and Fine-tune. It is tapped along with Hear the loop,
which the first tap starts (that tap is not counted: it is the start, not a
beat), so every tap is timed against the loop as it will be posted. Two
seconds after the last tap it settles. The tempo is the middle gap, so one
stray tap cannot move it, refined by the mean of the gaps near it and rounded
to a whole beat a minute. Where the beat falls is the taps' own, read off the
song's clock (the circular mean of each tap's place in its beat, over the taps
since the loop last came round), less the time the sound takes to reach the
ear. A person taps to what they hear, which is the audio clock less the
context's and the device's latency (lib/audioloop.js latency(): 42ms in this
box's Chromium, 10 base and 32 output; a phone's speaker is about as much,
Bluetooth 150-250ms). Read raw, the marks, and every end that snaps to them,
would sit that much late. Fewer than four taps leave the tempo as it was, and
say so. Every line the tap shows is two lines at most on a phone, as tall as
the tap: the first draft's idle line wrapped to three, and the first tap moved
the button 4.3px under the finger.

THEN EVERY COUNT IS OF WHAT IS HEARD, smooth restart included. The length line
and the sync line say the beats. Make it offers the three whole counts nearest
what is heard and sets the end so the loop is that many: with a 0.25s smooth
restart the handle sits 0.25s past the eighth beat, and a dashed line on the
strip shows where the loop comes round, on the beat. A count the song or the
20s cap is too short for is faded. Each tap gains One beat, in size order. The
strip marks every beat that stands 6px from the next (else every fourth, else
every sixteenth), taller every four counted from the loop's start, and the
loop detail marks its own window. An end let go within 8px of a beat settles
on it (for the end, the place the loop comes round), and typed or stepped ends
never snap. The tempo is the editor's own state, as the crossfade is: saved
with the song in the drafts and the re-add card, never posted, and gone with a
new song.

Pad and Flip: shared. The template and lib/musicdrawer.js are one copy; each
editor added only its state (`musicTempo`), its two hooks, the engine's
duration and latency, and the tempo where its drafts already wrote the
crossfade.

How it works has a tip for each (Hear the loop, Tap the beat), and Play with my
drawing, Loop Detail and Start and end say the new arrangement.

verify_musicbeat is new: 44 rows, each on the Pad and on Flip. Each part was
shown red with that part broken, served to the browser from a mutated copy
with the files on disk untouched: 32 mutations, each red on the rows it
breaks. Some runs did not count the first time and were run again: one
crashed on a click Flip's drawers covered (the suite's clicks now go through
press(), which says so in red), one served only the second of its two edits
to one file (the calibration's router answered the last route only; now one
handler a file), and the tap part's ran again after its probes changed.

Calibrating found two faults in the instrument itself. Beside another suite,
the stray gap read 119 once: a tap held up past its mark by a busy machine.
The taps now wake 15ms early and wait out the rest on the clock, and a try
whose taps strayed more than 4ms is tapped again on a fresh page, three tries
at most. 4ms is the most the rows can stand: half a beat a minute at 120 is
2.1ms in the mean of the stray gap's four gaps. A page held up 40ms just
before a mark read 12ms; quiet, the taps land within 1ms. And the phase row
read the song's clock after each click, while the tap's handler reads it
first thing: the handler's own work let the audio clock take one of its
8-21ms steps on some taps, and twice the two means sat 7ms apart. It reads
just before the click now, and they agree to the ten-thousandth.

Not tested here: tapping with a finger on an iPhone, the sound, whether Safari
reports a Bluetooth headset's latency (where it reports none, the beat sits
that much late), Segoe UI and SF.

## After v329 -- The music drawer, streamlined: one view and More (the owner: "we'll need to streamline it")

The owner, with the three levels and the beat live: "The music drawer is so
complicated. I think I liked it better before you did so much to it," then
"Leave it for now but we'll need to streamline it." The step 2 mock
photographed the drawer two ways, as planned and streamlined, and "I guess you
should finish" took its five defaults: streamlined; loops in whole bars (4, 8,
16, 32 beats); Smooth restart in More; Cut on silence on by default; and the
streamline first, with today's strip, before step 2's timeline. Cut on silence
comes with step 2. The owner asked whether we could go back to before any
changes: yes, by reverting #613 and #611 in one PR (to check before such a
merge: that drafts keep their songs and loops). Not done; it stays an offer.

ONE VIEW, AND MORE. The drawer opens on the strip, the one line, the pair that
plays (Play with my drawing, Hear the loop), Fit my drawing and Whole song,
and More. More is a menu card the drawer's width, its name and what it holds
on one line (More · The restart, the beat, exact times) and a drawn + at its
end (a - while open). Its words are one block, which lib/labels.js trims to
cap height over the baseline as it does every button's label (.lbl-own), so
the + sits on the letters in any font; the first build's words were a flex
row, which cannot be trimmed, and the + sat 1-2px low and the tile was 56px
for 48. Asserted on the ink in nine faces, the ones that split ascent and
descent unlike the app's among them. It opens in place, joined to its tile as the draw
drawer's tiles are, and unfolds and folds away the way they do (Web
Animations, at once under Reduce Motion); the drawer gets shorter only once
the fold is done, and gently (lib/drawerdetent.js). It holds four parts, each
under its name: The restart (Smooth restart, its length, Hear the restart),
The beat (Tap the beat), Exact times (the loop detail, and Start and End of
loop typed or stepped) and How it loops (Lock the length). Inside More's card
the loop detail has no box of its own, which would be a card in a card, and
every choice keeps the menu's white card, as every choice in a drawer does:
the first build put them on the paper (paper, card, paper, as the draw
drawer's choices sit in its card), and verify_contrast's census, the owner's
sheets rule, said so.
Whether More is open is remembered under the levels' key, one for both
editors: 'fine' (Fine-tune) is open, anything else, the old Adjust too,
closed. The ids stay: #fineTuneToggle is More's tile, #fineTuneBody what it
opens, and #musicDetail's data-level still says which, set before More shows
or hides, so lib/drawerdetent.js takes it as a move of its baseline and not
as a song landing.

THE ONE LINE: "4.00s · 8 beats · fits your drawing", then Skribl's pick, or
Back to Skribl's pick, and for eight seconds after that, its Undo. It was
three lines: the pick line ("Skribl picked the first 20 seconds, with a smooth
restart."), Adjust's length line, and Fine-tune's sync line ("Comes round
every 4.000s · 120 frames at 30 a second ..."). The length is what is heard,
to the hundredth, in bold; the beats come once there is a tempo; the drawing,
once there is one. A loop that was the pick and is not now, because the
drawing changed, says only that it is shorter or longer than the drawing, and
offers the way back: nobody is told they did something ("You've made your own
loop" went with the rest of the old words). The strip's middle label ("0:04.25
selected") went too, a second length beside the line's; the song's two ends
stay under the strip, and a handle's bubble says its time while it moves.

ITS HEIGHT NEVER CHANGES. Sized to what it said, the line wrapped on the
owner's phone the moment the way back appeared ("Back to Skribl's pick" is
169px of a 344px line), and everything under it dropped 24px with the finger
still on the strip. Its words and its end now have fixed widths to share,
340px and 190px, so below 540px the end always takes a second row and above
it never does: 55.5px on the phone and 32px on a desk, whatever it says.

WHOLE BARS (the owner: "we only ever want 4,8,16,... beats. Probably never
going to odd numbers. Like 1 2 3 4.. 1 2 3 4 etc"). With a tempo, an end let
go on the strip settles where the loop is 4, 8, 16 or 32 beats, the count
nearest what the finger left, smooth restart and all, with the other end
kept; a count the song or the 20s cap has no room for is passed over. The
start settles as the end does. The settle glides there in 200ms, frame by
frame, so the strip, its handles and the line move as one (a CSS transition
on the handles alone would have left the strip's tint and the line to jump),
at once under Reduce Motion; any other change to the loop stops it. Dragging
the start no longer puts it on a beat, so the loop slid along the strip does:
let go, its start settles on the nearest beat, its length kept. In the loop
detail, a close-up, an end let go within 8px of a beat still settles on it,
as before. Typed and stepped ends never settle, nor a locked loop's. - and +
move 0.1s, or a bar once there is a tempo (so 12 beats is there, by asking
for it), and their names and a line under them say which. Make it 7 8 9 went,
as the mock said, and so did Each tap (0.01s, 1 frame, 0.1s, 1 beat, 1s), its
frame, and the editors' frameSeconds hook that gave it.

MEASURED as the mock measured (the controls you can see and press, and the
drawer's height), on the Pad on the owner's phone with the cat drawn, a song
and a tempo: the drawer as it opens has 7 controls and is 514px tall, where
today's Simple had 9 (502px) and Adjust, where the beat's words were, 18
(814px). With More open, 28 at 1243px; Fine-tune had 39 at 1320px.

Pad and Flip: shared. The template, lib/musicdrawer.js and the CSS are one
copy; each editor lost the strip's middle label and the frame hook.

How it works: More takes Three levels' place; Skribl's pick says the line;
Move the loop, Smooth restart, Tap the beat, Loop Detail, and Start and end
say where they live now and which ends settle.

TESTS. verify_musiclevels.py is verify_musicmore.py, the one view and More.
verify_musicbeat.py lost Make it and Each tap's beat and gained whole bars
(both ends, the room the song and the cap leave, the glide, Reduce Motion, the
slide) and the loop detail's settle, with typed and locked ends that never
settle. The suites that clicked a level now open More: verify_music,
verify_sheetswipe, verify_contrast (Music, and Music with More open),
verify_tools, verify_onepill, verify_theme, verify_ux and verify_parity, by
aria-expanded (the tile is a disclosure; a row asking for aria-pressed would

  and 375) where they did from 348, and stack below, as they always did where

- In dark, the card's inset highlight (1px of white at 4%) shows as a faint
  line under an open tile, under More's as under the draw drawer's. Left as
  the draw drawer has it: one shape for both, and a fix for both together.

- verify_surfaces reads class names as tokens across the repo, and the marks'
  classes are made by the macro (mk-{{ name }}), so a rule styling .mk-plus

- verify_helpclaims's control aliases named the old controls ("How much

CALIBRATION. Each part was shown red with that part broken, served to the
browser from a mutated copy with the files on disk untouched: 35 mutations
of lib/musicdrawer.js, styles.css and labels.css, 34 of them red on the rows
they break (More never hiding, no fold, no unfold, motion
under Reduce Motion, More forgotten, the old Adjust opening it, the tile
under its card, the tile not joined, the loop lost on opening; the pick
always shown, "fits" always said, no beats, the selection's length, the line
sized to its words, the old blaming words; - and + always 0.1s, a beat, or
unnamed; no shrink, an uncapped scroll; whole bars off, any count, the

## After v329 -- A tall drawer opens at its top; a Flip draft's smooth restart shows on its switch

The owner, from an iPhone, with two screenshots: "When you click the media
button and click music it open all the way to the bottom? Second is loading a
new music file?" The first: the music drawer opened through Media and Music
with its top, the tabs, the song and the strip, under the header, and Lock the
length on screen. The second: a song just added, the drawer from its top.

WHY THE TWO DIFFER. Adding a song grows the drawer, and that growth was
already followed only so far: the bar above the drawer stays under the pinned
header (lib/drawerdetent.js followGrowth, "controls on top of controls"). The
open had no such stop. It scrolled the drawer's end to the foot of the screen
(the Pad's revealPanelEnd, Flip's scrollIntoView with block 'end'), and since
#616 remembers More open, the music drawer is taller than a phone: 1236px on
the owner's 874px screen, so its end at the foot put its top 350 to 600px
above the screen.

NOW THE OPEN STOPS WHERE THE GROWTH DOES. revealPanelEnd takes the bar above
the drawer and never scrolls it under the header; a drawer that fits still
opens with its end on screen, as before. Flip moves from scrollIntoView to the
same computed scroll, which the Pad moved to because scrollIntoView proved
unreliable on the owner's iPhone, and it now jumps under Reduce Motion as the
Pad's does. The re-asserts that settle the iPhone's own scrolls put the page
back on that place whichever way it was carried (what is above the drawer can
still be settling as it opens; aimed once, the bar ended 4 to 78px under the
header), and a wheel or a trackpad anywhere now calls them off, as a press or a
key in the drawer already did, so a person who scrolls on is left there.

THE SECOND SCREENSHOT HAD ITS OWN BUG. "19.75s" under the first 20 seconds is
a 0.25s smooth restart, and the switch beside it said Off: a Flip draft opened
from Your drafts or a .skribl file set the loop's smooth restart and repainted
everything in the drawer but the switch's row. Reproduced on main and on the
step 2 branch: a draft saved with 0.25s, opened over a song whose smooth
restart was switched off. The drawer's own repaint (lib/musicdrawer.js sync,
which every editor's updateTrimUI ends with) now says the switch, its words
and its length too, so no path can set the one without the other. The Pad
already synced it on its own loads.

Pad and Flip: shared. lib/drawerdetent.js is one copy, each editor passes its
own bar (the Pad's #toolBar, Flip's .flip-tools), and the drawer's repaint is
lib/musicdrawer.js's.

verify_musicmore, in its kind part, on the Pad and Flip: opened with More open
the drawer starts at its top, the bar just under the header, on the owner's
phone and a 390x640 one, and Photo, which fits, still shows its end; a person
who scrolls on as it opens is left where they scrolled to; a draft opened says
its own smooth restart, the switch, its words and its length agreeing with the
line. On main the first two rows are red on both editors (the tabs 344 to 606px
above the screen) and the third on Flip. Shown red per part of the fix, each
broken copy served to the browser with the file on disk untouched: the stop
taken out of revealPanelEnd, the Pad's bar not passed, Flip back on

## After v329 -- Step 2 of the music plan: the timeline, the Restart view, Cut on silence

The owner, to the list after the streamline: "Yes on all," and choice 8 was
"step 2: the timeline, the Restart view and Cut on silence, mocked as built
before anything merges." The mock (the stream variant) is what was built; this
is the build, photographed beside today's drawer, waiting on the owner's OK.

THE TIMELINE (lib/musictimeline.js) took over from the strip (the whole song,
two handles, a window to slide) and from the loop detail in More (a close-up
of an end at 1x to 32x, Loop | Start | End and Scroll). YOUR DRAWING STAYS PUT
AND THE SONG SLIDES UNDER IT. Above, the drawing's own lane: each stroke when
it replays on the Pad, each page as long as it shows on Flip, numbered, its
next turns fainter until the loop has come round, and a dashed line wherever
the loop comes round under it; over it, its name and how long it plays ("Your
drawing · 7.6s", or "nothing drawn yet"). Below, the song: its waveform, the
loop lit, a dot on each beat once there is a tempo (bigger on each bar from the
loop's start), a smooth restart's fold coming in at the loop's end, and what
lies past either end of the song dimmed. The loop's two ends are handles, each
with its time in a bubble while it is held. Under it all, the whole song as
one thin line, and where the loop is in it.

THE FRAMING: 1.28 times the longer of the loop and the drawing, the drawing
counted up to three loops (a two-hour piece would make the loop a sliver),
with the loop's start 9% in. The view eases toward it every frame (70ms to
most of the way, so a settle and the reframing after it read as one glide) and
holds still while a finger is down; under Reduce Motion it is where it belongs
at once.

WHAT A FINGER DOES. On the song it slides the song under the drawing: both
ends move, the loop keeps its length, and the handles stay where they are on
screen. On an end it moves that end, and held within 28px of the edge it is
dragged toward, the view widens smoothly, the far side kept, so a loop can
grow past what is on screen. On the whole song's line a tap glides the loop
there, its middle under the finger and its start on a beat once there is a
tempo; a drag slides it with the finger. On the drawing's lane nothing: it is
the drawing, and a finger there scrolls the page. A finger on the song that
moves up or down first scrolls the page too (touch-action: pan-y and a 6px
lock), which the strip never let it: the timeline is two and a half strips
tall. Let go, the drawer settles what was moved once there is a tempo, as
before: an end on whole bars, a slid loop's start on a beat.

THE RESTART VIEW (lib/musicrestart.js), in More under The restart: the loop's
end beside its start. On the left its last 0.6 seconds up to where it comes
round, on the right its first 0.6, and the line between them is the restart;
with a smooth restart the end's last moments fade out under the start, as
lib/audioloop.js folds them, and what is drawn is what plays, Cut on silence's
move included. A finger on the left moves the end and on the right the start,
the music following the finger, so the beats can be lined up across the join
by eye; let go near a beat (8px) and it settles on it, the loop detail's rule,
whose close-up job this took. The dot at its foot is the smooth restart's
length: pulled out it blends the two, in 5ms steps, as far as half a second or
half the loop; back to the line, a clean cut. Its hint says so, with the beat
("Line the beats up across the middle: drag either side.") and without.

CUT ON SILENCE (lib/audioloop.js cutFrames), under How it loops, beside Lock
the length. A clean cut clicks where the loop's last sample jumps to its first.
With it on, both ends move together, by the same number of frames, 5ms at most
either way, to where the loop's first samples come nearest the song's own next
ones after its last. On for a new song; off for a song from a draft or card
that never said, so nothing already made changes; kept in the drafts and the
re-add cards. Its words say how far ("Both ends move 0.001s later, to where the
end runs into the start without a click", "under a thousandth of a second" for
less). With a smooth restart there is nothing to cut, and it says so. The
posted clip is the cut loop, and the player plays it as it is (the post's music
carries no cut, so it is not cut twice).

DEPARTURES FROM THE MOCK, each for a reason:
- ONE MOVE FOR BOTH ENDS. The mock moved each end to its own quiet moment,
  which changed the loop's length by up to ten thousandths; Fit my drawing and
  whole bars are exact lengths, and a loop that goes round for minutes hears
  ten thousandths as drift.
- THE NEAREST CLEAN JOIN, NOT THE CLEANEST (found by the new suite). A note
  comes round to the same place every half of its period, so joins nearly as
  clean as each other lie all through the reach. Taking the cleanest by a hair
  moved a 220Hz tone's loop the whole 5ms when one 0.5ms away was within a
  sixth of it; now the smallest move within a quarter of the cleanest wins, and
  that one was cleaner on the join too (0.011 off the song's next sample
  against 0.019).
- The end held at the edge widens the view; the mock did not say how a loop
  grows past the screen.
- Exact times lost its rule, the line above Start and End of loop: it parted
  them from the loop detail, and alone it parted the fields from their own
  name.

Pad and Flip: shared. One template partial, lib/musicdrawer.js, the two new
modules and the CSS are one copy each; each editor's half is its hooks: the
lane (the Pad's playback timeline, Flip's lib/holdtiming.js plan) and Cut on
silence's state in the drafts and the post. Six function names left both
editors with the strip and the loop detail (drawWaveform, drawZoomWaveform,
formatTimeH, getZoomWindow, requestZoomWaveformDraw, updateZoomHandles), so
verify_surfaces' ratchet is 49 from 55. lib/loopwave.js and lib/zoomstep.js
are gone.

How it works: The timeline, Loop ends, The Restart view and Cut on silence are
new; Move the loop, Smooth restart, Skribl's pick, Play and Tap the beat say
where things live now; Loop markers and Loop Detail went with what they named.

TESTS. New suite verify_musictimeline.py: the one view, the framing, the
fingers (mouse and a real touch sequence), an end and the edge read on every
