## After v329 -- Tap the beat's row reads the song beside the tap's own handler (main green again)

Main went red after step 2 in one shard: verify_musicbeat's "where the beat
falls is the taps' own" on Flip, the tempo's beat 10ms from the taps' own
(the row allows 5). Nothing in the drawer was wrong. The row read where the
song had got to just before each click, and the tap's handler reads it again
as it runs; the audio clock moves in steps (2.9 or 11.6ms here), and a busy
page let it step between the two reads. Replayed on this box with the
processor slowed sixfold, the handler read 11.6ms later than the row on four
taps of six, and the row went red one time in six, the same way.

The row now reads the song beside the handler: a listener on the button that
goes first (capture, at the target) and one that goes after it, so the
handler's own reading is between the two, equal to both unless the clock
stepped in that moment. The tempo's beat has to lie between the two means,
half a millisecond either side (it keeps four places), which is tighter than
the 5ms it had and holds on a busy page.

CALIBRATION, the processor slowed sixfold on Flip, a fresh page each: the old
reading red one time in six, the new one green six of six (the clock stepped
within a tap on two of them, and the handler's beat was between the two
readings). The drawer broken in a copy served to the browser: the time to the
ear left out (the beat 42ms late), and the beat not the taps' own (fixed at
0): red on the Pad and Flip, two runs each. The same file served unchanged:
green.

## After v329 -- More starts closed every time; Each press picks how far - and + move; Snap to the beat

Three of the owner's questions from the phone, and the picks. "More starts
open": it remembered an old Fine-tune, and with More open the music drawer is
taller than a phone. Of always closed, closed today then remembered, or left
remembering, the pick was always closed. Then "How to adjust step?", of Exact
times' "- and + move 0.1s.": the streamline had made the step automatic (0.1s,
or a bar once there is a tempo; before it, Each tap had five steps). Of
leaving it, a small choice under the times, or holding for finer, the pick
was the choice. Then, of the whole bars: "It's cool how it snaps to a beat
but if a song has a bunch of empty space at the beginning it ends up putting
the beat in the middle rather than in the right spot. Can I no longer freely
adjust start and end? It seems like it snaps no matter what." The start was
never put on a beat, only the loop's length on whole bars, so a start in a
quiet intro left every bar after it off the music. Of a let-go end landing on
the beat marks, and a switch to turn snapping off, the pick was both, "if
they let me set the starting point. I need a free set so it's not all
automatic".

MORE STARTS CLOSED, EVERY TIME (lib/musicdrawer.js): on a load, the old
remembered key on file too, and whenever the music panel is put away (the
drawer closed, or Photo picked), when it closes at once, with nothing of it
on the screen to fold. Nothing remembers it, so the drawer opens on its one
view, which fits the owner's phone.

EACH PRESS, under the times: one pill (lib/segslider.js), 0.01s, 0.1s, and a
bar once there is a tempo. Untouched it is a bar while Snap to the beat is
on, and the step it was, 0.1s, otherwise; a step picked is kept, a tempo or
not; a new song starts untouched. The buttons' names say the step ("End of
loop, 0.01s later"); the line that said it went. The bar was first dimmed
until there was a tempo, as a dimmed button is, and read 2.5:1 on the dark
desk card (verify_onepill: every label of a pill 4.5:1), with a title to say
why that a phone never shows. It is not there until there is a tempo now.

SNAP TO THE BEAT, under the tap once there is a tempo, on to start. On, a
start let go on the timeline lands on the nearest beat and the end follows
to whole bars (of 4, 8, 16 and 32 beats, the count nearest what is heard from
there that the song and the 20s cap have room for); an end let go counts its
whole bars from the start wherever it is, so a start set off the beat, typed
or placed with the switch off, is never moved. The slid loop and a tap on the
whole song start on a beat, and in the Restart view an end let go near a
beat settles on it, as before. Off, nothing settles. Typed and pressed times
never did and still do not. The switch is kept in the tempo, as snap: false,
so it goes with the song into the drafts and the .skribl file and nothing
else had to learn it; tapped again, the tempo keeps it; a new song has no
tempo, so it starts on. The switch and the bar open out when the tempo lands,
the row down and the pill across, frame by frame, so what is under them
glides rather than jumps; at once under Reduce Motion.

Pad and Flip: shared, the template, lib/musicdrawer.js and the CSS; neither
editor changed.

The tall-drawer fix's rows opened the drawer with More open to make it taller

## After v329 -- Magnify on the timeline, 1x to 64x, around the end last touched

The owner, from the phone: "Where did magnify go?", and then "I was looking
for the magnify on fine tune". The loop detail in More had one (an end close
up, 1x to 16x, with Loop, Start, End and Scroll); the timeline took over from
the loop detail in step 2 and the magnifier went with it. Mocked beside
today, on the timeline, around the end last touched, the answer was "All yes
but maybe go to x64?", and of the zoom going back to 1x when the drawer is
put away or staying, "stay".

MAGNIFY (lib/musictimeline.js, the template, the CSS): a magnifier's - and +
either side of the rung, Exact times' look, at the end of the timeline's name
line, its middle on the name's. Each rung is the framing over 1, 2, 4, 8, 16,
32 or 64, with the end last touched in the middle: the start, until a tap or
a drag on the end's handle, the end's own - and +, a typed end or the Restart
view's end makes it the end (lib/musicdrawer.js's setEdge tells the timeline
which). The loop never moves for it. A step glides there as any reframing
does, at once under Reduce Motion; each button stops at its end of the
ladder. Zoomed in, a held end follows the finger while the view holds still,
and held near either edge (not only its own, so the loop can shorten past
what is in view as well as grow) the view slides along at the zoom, PAN views
a second at the edge itself, rather than widening; let go, it glides back
with the end in the middle. It slides only as far as the end can follow:
where the end stops (the song's start or end, the other end, the 20s cap) the
view stops with it, the end under the finger, and an end held at the edge
that was already as far as it goes leaves the view still rather than jumping
it there. The mock slid on into the dimmed part past the song, the end
drifting off from under the finger: nothing stopped it, which reading the
slide's code again for its calibration found. A slide at the zoom carries the
view with the end zoomed around, so the song moves under the finger and the
ends stay where they are on screen. The zoom stays when the drawer is put
away and opened again; a new song starts at 1x on its start. At 64x a column
of the song can hold less than the 128 samples of its finest block, so there
the song is drawn from the samples themselves, and a single loud sample shows
in its own column and no other.

Pad and Flip: shared, the template, lib/musictimeline.js, lib/musicdrawer.js
and the CSS; neither editor changed.

TESTS. verify_musictimeline, a new part (magnify), each on both editors: the
ladder and its readout, each button stopping at its end; each rung's framing
around the start, the loop unmoved; a step's glide, frame by frame, and at
once under Reduce Motion; a tap on the end's handle making it the end zoomed
around; at 8x, a held end following the finger while the view holds, held at
the left edge and then the right the view sliding along with the end under
the finger, held at the song's start the view stopping with the start under
the finger and held there again holding still, let go gliding back with it in
the middle, a slide with the ends put, and the end's own + making it the end;
the zoom kept when the drawer is put away and opened again, and a new song at
1x on its framing; a loud sample in its own column; the magnifier's place,
and its words and glyphs against what is behind them, light and dark on the
owner's phone. verify_helpclaims reads the new tip, "Magnify the timeline".

CALIBRATION, each part broken in a copy served to the browser, the files on
disk untouched, and the magnify part run: the ladder stopping at 32x, and the
buttons never disabled (the ladder's row; never disabled, a new song's row
too, whose - is disabled at 1x); a rung framed from the start, 9% in (most

step in one frame (the glide's row); Reduce Motion gliding (its row); a held

## After v329 -- A person who scrolls back up as a song lands is left there

Found while step 2's rows were being read, and fixed on the owner's word
("Fix the bug too"). When a song lands, the drawer grows and
lib/drawerdetent.js followGrowth glides the page to the drawer's new end,
then holds it there with re-asserts at 300, 700 and 1200ms. The hold only
ever pushes down, so a person who scrolled back up in that time, to look at
the drawing, came straight back to the drawer's end at the next re-assert: on
a desk, a wheel 300px up 330ms after the song landed was taken back 296px in
one frame at 700ms, on the Pad and Flip alike; on a phone, a finger dragging
240px down the drawer moved the page 34px, the 700ms re-assert taking the
rest back as it went, and the last one took back all but 4px of that. A
downward scroll past the cap was already left alone (DRIFT); an upward one
never was.

THE FIX (lib/drawerdetent.js): as the opening's re-asserts are called off
once the person acts (revealPanelEnd), a wheel, a touch, a press or a key
anywhere while the growth's are due calls them off. Moves no person made, the
drift a glide overshoots and the browser's anchoring, are still taken back.
Pad and Flip: shared, one lib.

TESTS. verify_musicmore, in its kind part, on the Pad and Flip: the drawer
open and past the opening's own re-asserts, a song lands, and a person
scrolls up while the growth's are still due, by a finger on the owner's phone
(a touch drag on the drawer's tabs, held still before it lets go, so there is
no fling), a wheel on a desk and Page Up on a desk; read on every frame until
the last re-assert is past, the page stays where they put it.

CALIBRATION, each in a copy of the lib served to the browser, the file on
disk untouched: the fix taken out, red on all six rows, both editors; the
wheel left out of what calls the hold off, red on the wheel's two rows only;
the finger left out (its touch and its press), the finger's two rows only;
the key left out, Page Up's two rows only; the same file served unchanged,
green.

## After v329 -- The loop's ends: a tab at each foot; zoomed in, the start stays and the beat follows

Two of the owner's from the phone, mocked together and picked together ("All
yes"). Zoomed in on where a song begins, a tempo tapped and Snap to the beat
on: "how do I tell it where the beginning is? When I take it to the beginning
it just snaps to a different spot (under a beat?)". It did: a start let go
settled on the nearest tapped beat at 16x as at 1x, and a tapped beat is
rarely on the music to the hundredth. On the mock's song, tapped 45ms late, a
start let go on the note moved 45ms (48px on a phone at 16x, 93 on a desk)
and left the note's first 45ms outside the loop. Then, of the handle: "the
little handle in the middle of the line kind of gets in the way of seeing
where the wave starts for the beat. it sits right over the middle." On a soft
start it covered 59% of what was painted within 14px of the line, on a loud
one 32%, and on a phone the finger held it there too. Of the grip as a tab at
its foot, beside the line outside the loop, or slipping into the line while
held, the pick was the tab; of the start kept with the beat moved to it, kept
with the marks left where the taps put them, or found on the note's attack,
the pick was the first; and the switch says so. Asked then whether the snaps
after that count from a start set that way: they do.

A TAB AT EACH END'S FOOT (styles.css): the grip is 22 by 18px and half under
the song's edge, as the Restart view's dot sits at its foot, its arrows drawn
to fit (the template's viewBox), the tap band reaching down to it, 3px clear
of the whole song's line. It covers nothing beside the line on a soft start
and 2% on a loud one (the tips of the loudest bars). Its edge reads as the
grip's did, 3.6:1 on light and 3.1:1 on dark over the song, and 3.9 to 4.1:1
below it.

ZOOMED IN, THE START STAYS AND THE BEAT FOLLOWS (lib/musicdrawer.js snap):
the timeline says whether it is magnified as it lets go, and magnified, with
Snap to the beat on, a start let go stays where it is and a beat falls there:
the tempo keeps its beats a minute and its phase becomes the start. The end
follows on whole bars from it, as before. Every snap after counts from the
new beat (a start at 1x, a slid loop, the Restart view, a bar in Each
press); the new beat is kept with the song in the drafts; tapped again, the
beat is the taps' own. At 1x nothing changes. THE MARKS GLIDE to the new beat
(lib/musictimeline.js beatTo) with the view's own ease and the shorter way
round, so the settle, the reframing after it and the marks read as one; a
new tempo, or none, is there at once, and so is all of it under Reduce
Motion.

WORDS. The switch says "The start you drag lands on a beat, and the loop on
whole bars. Zoomed in, it stays where you put it, and the beat follows." The

TESTS. verify_musictimeline, its grip part, on a phone and a desk: beside

## After v329 -- Skribl's ears: a new song's loop starts on a bar, whole bars long, on the beat it heard

Step 3 of the music plan, "the part that loops best, on the beat". The owner
asked why it had not been done ("why havent you done The music plan's step 3
(looping on the beat) yet?"): each round the owner's newer asks came first,
and it needed ears, which needed a mock. The mock was the real drawer with the
ears wired in and songs to hear, each restart today's beside the one with ears
(today's restarted into the song's opening silence and intro, the drums
stopping for 2.5 to 4.2 seconds every time round). The owner: "all yes" to
whole bars nearest the drawing on the Pad, the first place the loop comes
round smoothly, the beat heard used straight away, and the words.

LIB/MUSICEARS.JS listens to a new song's first two minutes, a few
milliseconds at a time so the page never stalls (0.4 to 0.8 seconds in all
for a 70-second song in this box's Chromium; a phone is slower, not tested
here). A spectral flux and its low part, per step twelve bands and twelve
pitch classes; the tempo is the flux's strongest repeat between 40 and 240
leaning to 120, refined to a thousandth of a beat a minute; where the beat
falls is where the flux gathers round the beat's circle, less the flux's own
lead on a sound (a fifth of its window and a little more, measured on clicks
at 8 to 48 kHz, every rate within a millisecond after); a bar is where kicks
and chord changes gather. A steady beat needs two things: the flux gathering
round the circle (`sure`: songs with drums 5.7 to 15.9, clicks 23 to 32, slow
chords about 2, against 3.5) and a sound starting across the spectrum on most
beats (`hits`, at least half, at least eight: at a beat 100 to 490 of 511
bins grew at once, a sweep crossing from bin to bin 2 to 9). Each guard alone
was fooled by a test song the other catches: a steady tone's one start and a
sweep's even drift gather round any circle (sure 4 to 45) and land on no
beats; sounds starting at random, as rain does, land on most beats (24 of 31)
and gather round none (2.3). So every song the other music suites load (steady
tones, sweeps) is heard as no beat; the one with a beat, verify_musicbeat's
pulse, now runs with the ears off, since its rows are a person tapping from
nothing.

THE PICK. Of 4, 8, 16 and 32 beats the count nearest the length wanted (the
drawing on the Pad, else the most that fit the 20s); starting on a bar; where
the song after the loop's end goes on as it does after its start, or came to
its start as it comes to the end; of joins within 0.03 of the best, the
earliest. Each stretch of the song is heard again on its own (a band speeds
up), and the loop's length is its end laid over its start to the half
millisecond. Two parts were built, measured and taken out because no song
could tell them apart from their absence: moving the start onto its own sound
(3ms better on one song, 4ms worse on another) and a rule against quiet
stretches (the join already keeps intros and fades out, and the rule would
have skipped a soft verse).

THE DRAWER (lib/musicdrawer.js, both editors). A new song starts on today's
pick at once, and the beat line says "Listening for the beat…". Heard, if
nothing changed meanwhile, the loop glides to the pick with ears and the beat
heard is set, marked heard (`heard: true`, kept with the song in the drafts,
and by Snap to the beat's switch), its marks fading in on the timeline over
200ms (lib/musictimeline.js; at once under Reduce Motion, and the first
tapped beat fades in too). A loop moved or a beat tapped meanwhile is left as
it is. Back to Skribl's pick goes to the heard pick and beat, and its Undo
brings back the beat that was there as well as the loop. The beat line says
"124 beats a minute, heard by Skribl · tap to change it", or "Skribl didn't
hear a steady beat. Tap along with the music to count one."; a tapped beat
keeps "tap again to change it". A song a draft brings back keeps its loop and
is not listened to. The Pad's "Loop set to your drawing length" toast waits
for the ears (a new `fitted` hook): with a beat the loop becomes whole bars,
which that would not be, and with none it shows once Skribl has listened. The
help's Skribl's pick, Loop ends, Tap the beat and Snap to the beat say so.

THE INSTRUMENT is verify_musicears: songs made in the page whose every beat
and bar is known (steady at 124 with an intro, swung at 88, a band speeding
up from 100 to 102 with every hit up to 8ms off, slow chords, a tone, a sweep,
rain), every row held to the song's own beats, on the Pad and on Flip.

CALIBRATION, each part broken in a copy served to the browser, the files on
disk untouched, each red on its own rows on both editors: the bar ignored
(the swung and band rows; the steady song's first beat is a bar, so it cannot
tell); the length not fitted (the band row); the circle not asked (the rain's
row); the hits not asked (the tone's and the sweep's); a hit not needing the
spectrum (the sweep's); the three sets of words; a moved loop changed anyway;
a tapped beat replaced; the Undo leaving the beat; the loop jumping; the
marks appearing at once; the marks fading under Reduce Motion; heard not kept,
or dropped by the switch (the switch's and the reload's rows); a restored song
listened to; the Pad's drawing not setting the count. The same files served
unchanged: all green.

Pad and Flip: shared. One module and one drawer; of each editor's own code,
only the Pad's toast hook (the Pad picks before its song is decoded, and the
drawer starts the ears once it is).

## After v329 -- Skribl's ears hear a rock beat's whole count, its kicks, and the same at 48 kHz

The owner, after twelve real recordings were run through the ears, before
Match the beat: "yes, fix the ears first". Two fixes were proposed and one
went. The beat sits 4 to 13ms after the hits on the real recordings, but
that does not clip the restart: the smooth restart plays the song's own
next downbeat (lib/audioloop.js folds the loop's tail over its head), so
the loop comes round whole either way.

HALF THE COUNT. A rock beat at 120, kicks on 1 and 3 and snares on 2 and 4,
was heard at 60, on its snares. The flux sums what grows across 511 bins: a
snare grows nearly all of them, a kick a few, so the flux's strongest repeat
was snare to snare, stronger than the lean to 120. Made rock beats with an
808's kicks (no beater click) were heard at half at 112, 120, 132 and 140;
with a click, at their own count up to 140, and at half at 150. Now a beat
heard slower than 85 a minute (where twice it is nearer 120) with a sound
starting halfway between most of its beats is twice as fast; the doubled
beat must hold as steady, or the beat heard stays. And a kick counts as a
hit: the low part growing half as much as the song's own strong kicks do,
and twenty times its loudness at least (the test songs' strong kicks grew
670 to 1300 times it, songs with no bass under 35). Without that, an 808's
kicks between the snares leave nothing halfway that a hit can hear.

THE SAME AT 48 KHZ. A song is decoded at the device's rate: 44.1 kHz in this
box's Chromium, where every suite runs, and usually 48 on phones and Windows
(no phone here). The ears halved whatever came, so 44.1 became 22.05 but 48
became 24, a different window and step, and the same song was heard
differently: the suite's swung song at 176 instead of 88, a person reading
aloud (a LibriSpeech clip) as a steady beat at 98. Every rate is now brought
to 22.05 kHz, each step the mean of the samples it spans; at 44.1 that is
what it was, sample for sample. On a click track and a snare's, rates from
32 to 96 kHz now put the beat within 0.2ms of where 44.1 does (32 kHz was up
to 0.8 off).

MEASURED, old ears against new. The twelve real recordings (kept in scratch,
not here: one is licensed non-commercial) hear the same at 44.1; at 48 the
speech is no longer a beat. Choice (drums and bass) stays at 68: a sound

## After v329 -- Match the beat: Flip's Beat speed, a round of the pages in whole bars

The mock played today's Flip beside a matched one, both to a song: at 12
pages a second the pages slide off the song's beat a little more each time
round. The owner chose A, Beat as a fourth speed (6 · 12 · 24 · Beat), and
"all yes" to the rest: a round of a quarter, a half, one or two bars, the
one nearest the speed there was to start; Beat only once the song has a
beat, heard or tapped; a page added or taken away keeps the round and
changes the speed; Play from the page you are on, the song joining in step;
and Choice stays at 68.

A ROUND is what plays before the pages start again: all of them, each at its
length by the timing lib's plan (lib/holdtiming.js), or a stretch that loops
forever, the pages before it playing once. Still pages share the round by
their holds, a page held twice taking two shares; a page that draws itself
keeps the time it took to draw, and the still pages share the rest. The
speed comes from a few passes over the plan, to within half a millisecond of
the round, any number from 1 to 60 a second; a round over 60 is not offered.
Speed's hint says "on the song's beat" and the line under the round what it
makes ("12 pages in ½ bar · 12.4 a second"). A number turns Beat off at that
speed; the song taken away puts Beat aside and the speed stays. Saved and
posted as `beat: {bars}` beside `fps`; the server takes that one key and
those four values (validation.py, held to flip.js's own reading by
verify_sharedrules). The players read `fps` and leave `beat` alone.

THE PAGES KEEP TO THE SONG'S CLOCK. Flip's page timer is a chain of waits,
and the chain drifts against the audio clock: the same pages slid 179ms off
the beat in sixteen seconds. With Beat, at a watching speed of 1x with the
song playing, each page is due where the song says, by the loop's own clock
as heard (less the speaker's delay), and a page the song has already passed
is skipped rather than flashed by. Each round's first page then came up
within 23ms of its beat in every run here. Slower or faster than 1x, the
pages go at that speed and the song at its own, as they do without Beat.

PLAY FROM ANY PAGE starts the song as far into its round as that page is, so
the page is up for its own time. With the song started from its top, the
clock did the rest, but page 8 stood still for 0.7 seconds while the song
came round to it.

POSTED. The link page times a Flip by its frame clock against one start, and
starts the song where the drawing is, so a posted Beat Flip stays on the
beat there: sixteen rounds, each 3 to 47ms ahead of the sound, with no drift
(the lead is the speaker's delay, which the link page has never allowed
for). A post's box (inlineplayer.js: the feed, the Gallery, the
Library) drifts, about 12ms a second: each pass starts again from zero on
the frame that notices, losing what that frame came late by, while the song
plays on; and it starts its song from the top after decoding it or after a
pause. A bug for every post with music, plain to hear with Beat; fixed on
its own, next.

NOT KEPT: a hook that refit Beat whenever the tempo changed. Every change of
the tempo comes with a save, and a save refits; with the hook gone its break
stayed green.

THE INSTRUMENT is verify_flipbeat, on a phone, to a click track at 124 the
ears hear: Beat's showing (no song, a steady tone, a beat heard, a beat
tapped); the round, its line and its choices' glide (at once under Reduce
Motion); each round's length; holds, drawing pages, a page added, a stretch
looping forever, a round that cannot be made; a number turning Beat off; the
song taken away; a reload; the post; and on the beat, playing for sixteen
seconds, from page 8, and across a pause, each round's first page read on
every frame against the song as heard: each within 45ms (about where a
person starts to notice the sound before the picture) and the middle one
within 20ms. Its first version counted the page already up when it began
listening as a round, which measured how long the listening took to begin
(+39ms once); it counts only pages that come up while it listens.

CALIBRATION, each break served in place of flip.js, flip.css or styles.css,
the files on disk untouched, red on its own rows: Beat always shown; the
round always a quarter bar; no refit on a change; a number leaving Beat on;
holds not counted; an unfit round offered; a forever stretch counted with the
pages before it; Beat kept with no beat; a drawing page counted as a still
one; no glide; the round not saved, not loaded, not posted; the pages on
their own timer (all three timing rows: -61 to +234ms); the song from its
top (the page 8 row: up 710ms against 127). The Reduce Motion row went red
only with flip.css's rule and styles.css's two global ones all gone: each
alone keeps it still. As built: 23 of 23.

CONTRAST. verify_contrast reads Flip's Tune with Beat on, light and dark,
phone and desk, beside Tune as it was. Every new word wears the token of
Speed's words in its role: lit 8.64:1 light and 8.03:1 dark, unlit 9.35:1
and 8.59:1, the lines under them 8.33:1 and 9.69:1.

How it works says it (the fps tip, Set the timing), and Ask finds it under
beat, tempo, rhythm and in time.

Pad and Flip: Flip only. The Pad has no pages, and its speed is a way of
watching, not the drawing itself.

## After v329 -- A post's box keeps its song in step

Found building Match the beat, and a bug for every post with music: a post's
box (inlineplayer.js: the feed, the Gallery, the Library) slid off its song.

EACH PASS LOST A FRAME. At the end of a pass the box started its clock again
from zero, on whichever frame noticed the end, so each pass lost what that
frame came late by, while the song looped on its own: a Beat Flip in the
feed slid 190ms off its beat in sixteen seconds, about 12ms a second. Each
pass now carries on from what its frame came late by, as a stretch looping
forever already did, and the passes' time is kept (`lap`), so the song's
place is always the drawing's: lap + elapsed into its loop.

THE SONG STARTED FROM ITS TOP whenever the box started it: after decoding it
(70ms into the first play here, so the pages ran ahead from the start), after
a pause, after a new speed. It starts where the drawing is now, the link
page's rule (paStartAtElapsed); a scrub, a seek or a return to the start puts
the drawing somewhere rather than playing it there, and the song follows it
there.

THE INSTRUMENT is verify_flipbeat's posted part: a Beat Flip posted with
each page a colour of its own, the canvas's middle read on every frame
against the song as heard, through a hook on the audio source's start (a
player's own variables are its own). On the link page and in the box, every
round within 60ms of its beat and the last four where the first four were,
within 25ms; a pause 2.3 seconds into a fresh play in the box (a third of a
round into a pass) carries the song on from where it was. Both players run
about 20ms ahead of the sound: neither allows for the speaker's delay (42ms
here), which the editor does.

CALIBRATION, each break served in place of the real file: the box as it was
(its row slid -119 to +116ms; after the pause -322ms); the pass from zero
alone (a slide of 214ms; the pause row too); the song from its top alone
(-110ms throughout; -342ms after the pause); and the link page's clock run

## After v329 -- The loop's start lands where the music begins

The owner, of a song with dead air before the music: "how do I move the start
to the start of sound? It snaps back to empty space (no sound)"; of the mock
(today, the edge fixed, and three places it could land, on a phone and a
desk, light and dark): "All yes".

TWO THINGS PUT THE START IN THE SILENCE. On a phone at 1x the song's start
sits inside the timeline's edge zone, where an end held near the edge widens
the view so the loop can grow past what is on screen. With nothing past that
edge to show, the view kept widening and the start ran off to 0:00 under the
finger (lib/musictimeline.js widen). The view now widens only while there is
more song past the edge. Then Snap to the beat put the start on the nearest
beat, and a song's first sound is often a lead-in, between two beats: the
nearest beat was in the dead air.

WHERE IT LANDS NOW (lib/musicdrawer.js soundAt), at 1x with Snap to the beat
on: let go in the silence before the music and nearer it than the next beat,
or with the nearest beat in the silence, or up to half a beat into the
music, the start lands where the music begins, to the sample. The beat stays
where it was and the loop on whole bars, so it still comes round on the beat.
Music that begins within an eighth of a beat of one lands on that beat, so
music on the beat settles as it did. Past half a beat into the music, in a
gap too short to be a silence (under 0.15s), and in the quiet between two
drums on beats, the start lands on the nearest beat, as before. A silence is
a hundredth of the song's loudest (-40dB) or less on every channel, read off
the samples: the timeline's levels are blocks of 128 samples that reach past
a silence's edge, so at 44.1kHz a beat where the music stops read as sound
(found on songs built for it, before the browser rows).

ZOOMED IN, the start still stays where it is let go, and the beat moves to it
only when it is within an eighth of a beat of one: a tapped beat a little off
the music still lines up with the start, and a lead-in no longer pulls every
beat mark off its drum.

THE MOCK'S WORDS AND THE NEAREST BEAT. The mock said the music catches a
start let go "in the silence before the sound". Between drums on every beat
with nothing between them, that would take a start let go just after one
drum on to the next, a beat from the finger. There the nearer beat is kept.

THE INSTRUMENTS. verify_musictimeline: held near the edge that already shows
the song's start, the view holds still and the start stays under the finger
(main's timeline: the view moved 5.75s on the Pad and 5.51s on Flip, and the
start ran to 0.000). verify_musicbeat's new part, on four songs made for it
(a lead-in, the music on the beat, a break, drums alone): nine starts let go
on each editor. Its drag, tl_drag, now knows the view stops widening where it
shows the song's start or end.

CALIBRATION, each break served in place of lib/musicdrawer.js: main's drawer
(the start in the silence at 0.000, on the first drum at 0.667 for a start
let go just before or just after the lead-in, at the break's 2.000, and
zoomed in the beat moved to 0.399) turns 12 of the 20 red, every row but the
three "as before" rows and the page errors; then each part taken out alone
turns only its own rows red: the music nearer than the beat; half a beat
into the music; the beat in a silence (the music on the beat, the break);
the eighth of a beat (the same two, 0.1ms off the beat); the nearer beat
between two drums (4.000 for 3.000); a gap too short to be a silence (1.150
for 1.333); a whole beat into the music for half (0.400 for 0.667); and,
zoomed in, the beat moving whatever the distance. As built: 20 of 20.

The switch says it too: "The start you drag lands on a beat, or where the
music starts, and the loop on whole bars." (asked whether to add the words
after "All yes": "I said all yes"). The same words in the same token, so the
same contrast; no new colours. How it works says it (Loop ends, Magnify the
timeline, Snap to the beat).

Pad and Flip: shared. One drawer and one timeline for both editors.

## After v329 -- Beats: how many beats the loop is, 4 · 8 · 16 · 32

The owner, after Skribl's pick started a song mid-way and "It actually
works": "There should be ways to have skribl pick 4 or 8 16 32 64 etc.. like
other skribl picks?"; of the mock (A, a row of counts under the one line,
beside B, cards like Fit my drawing, on a phone and a desk, light and dark):
"All yes if it's intuitive".

WHAT IT IS. Under the one line, once there is a beat, heard or tapped:
Beats, 4 · 8 · 16 · 32, the counts the song and the 20s cap have room for,
the loop's own lit, none while the loop is not whole bars. 64 beats is past
20 seconds below 192 a minute, so it is not offered. It is Each press's row,
one seg; with nothing lit it says so (data-free, the free state verify_a11y
exempts, which the loop view's focus once had as data-role="focus").

INTUITIVE MEANT WHERE THE LOOP IS. The mock said a tap has Skribl pick again
at that length. Picked from the whole song, the steady test song's best 8
beats were at 23.5s while the loop sat at 4.2s: a tap on 8 would have thrown
the loop 19 seconds down the song. So on Skribl's pick (the tag), with ears,
a tap is Skribl's pick for that many beats where the loop is: the smoothest
stretch inside it when shorter, around it when longer, starting on a bar; of
joins as good, the one nearest the loop's start, and the start itself when
that is the same beat (lib/musicears.js pick's new from, to and near). A band
that speeds up has its bars a little apart in each stretch heard, 47ms on
the test band's, and the start "kept" moved by that much until the same beat
kept it exactly. The loop is still Skribl's pick after (the tag stays), and
Back to Skribl's pick goes to the pick for the drawing, as before. On a loop
of the person's own, or a tapped beat, the start stays where it is and the
loop is that many beats from it, moved back by whole beats only where the
song ends first.

KIND. The loop glides there, the count lit from the tap and the tag kept all
the way: the drawer reads where a glide will land (loopNow) for the tag, the
lit count and a tap made while it glides, so nothing changes its mind on the
way, and a second tap counts from where the first lands. Each tap offers
Undo for eight seconds, and Back to Skribl's pick waits while it does (they
share a place). Beats opens out as the beat lands, what is under it gliding
down; at once under Reduce Motion.

THE INSTRUMENTS. verify_musicbeat's Beats part (ears off, a person's own
loop): shown, offered and lit; none lit at 8.24 beats; the start kept; near
the song's end; Undo; two taps 60ms apart; the glide and the opening, and
Reduce Motion. verify_musicears' Beats part (ears on, songs whose every bar is
known): from the steady song's 32, 8 inside it, on a bar and 8 of its beats;
the tag and no way back on every frame of the glide; Undo; 16 around the 8,
its start kept; Undo of that, still the pick; the band's start kept to the
millisecond from 4 to 32; a loop of the person's own keeps its start.
verify_contrast reads the drawer with a beat ("Music, with a beat"), and
verify_musicbeat's words row reads Beats' name and a count.

CALIBRATION, each break served in place of the real file, turned red only
rows that guard it: the glide's landing not read (the second tap counted
from 4.58, mid-glide; the lit count none, then 8, on the way; the tag off
and the way back on, mid-glide); every tap a re-pick (a person's own start a
beat past the bar moved to the bar); no move back near the end; every count

THE PAGE STAYS STILL. As a beat landed, Beats opening grew the drawer, and

## After v329 -- Main red after #645: the copy's own Reduce Motion rule, in the player

Main's full run after the timeline's copy (#645) was red in two suites, on
both databases: verify_player_isolation (the player's CSS 40,992 B against its
40,906 B ratchet) and verify_jsstrip (the same bytes served, against its
40,925 B target). None of the copy's rules match on a player page, so
cssgraph left them out, all but one: `harness/tools/cssgraph.py` holds every
prefers-reduced-motion block as KEEP (a rule live only under a media query
nobody exercised is not evidence of anything), so the copy's own Reduce
Motion rule went to `player.css`, 92 B served, the whole overrun.

It is gone, and the ratchet stays. styles.css's two global Reduce Motion
rules (every transition none or near nothing, `!important`) keep the copy
still, as #645's calibration showed: with them there, taking the copy's own
rule out changed nothing, and verify_musicmore's Reduce Motion rows are green
without it. #645's entry says it stays, as Tune's and the name card's do;
it does not now. The served size is back to 40,900 B, the number the
ratchet's last raise measured.

The miss was the battery's: the copy's rules reached the player through a
media query, so the two suites that weigh the player's CSS were not named as
affected. WORKING-AGREEMENTS now says it: a re-emit that changes `player.css`
runs both.

720px column and never showed a drawing past 1:1, because a bitmap made at
the drawing's own size softens every line when it is stretched. It showed
three: today, B (a bigger canvas, drawn again at the size it shows) and A (B
in full screen, the button at the dock's end). The owner said "All yes" to
building B, then A, as two pull requests. This is B.

THE ROW REACHES PAST THE COLUMN. lib/chromefit.js span() gives the row the
canvas sits in (the Pad's .canvas-area, Flip's .flip-stage) negative margins
of half the difference between the page and the column, measured, so on a
window wider than 720px it spans the page's own box (inside the scrollbar
gutters the root keeps, so it never runs under a scrollbar). The header, the
dock and the drawers stay in the column. While it reaches, the page wears
one surface (body.canvas-wide): the column's surface and its glow at the
column's own size, from edge to edge, the column itself transparent. The
row starts to reach exactly where there are no sides to see, so nothing
jumps on the way. Each editor's fit calls span() before it measures.

THE BITMAP GROWS WITH THE DRAWING. Neither editor caps the display at 1:1
any more. The Pad: canvasRatio() is the bitmap's own pixels per drawing
unit, the screen's ratio times canvasGrowth, stored when the bitmap is made
(establishEditorCanvas); getCanvasLogicalSize, the stroke layers, the
compositor, the artwork stage and the colour pick all read it. Flip: RS is
the pad's own ratio; the pad and the four layers it is painted through
(onion skin, temp, frame and artwork) are made at it, while DPR stays the
drawing's own. A new size clears a canvas, so the bitmap is made again
once the page is still: the size on screen follows the window at once, and
the drawing is painted again from what describes it (the Pad's base plus
paintStrokesStatic, the identity every replay's end and every undo rests on;
Flip's render(), which paints from the pages). It waits while a stroke, a
replay, a pinch, a photo drag, a smudge or blur, a selection or a colour
pick is under way, any of which holds pixels of its own, and 150ms for the
window to stop changing size, so a dragged window edge repaints once, at the
end. Ink the Pad's strokes cannot rebuild (drawn outside a take) is carried
over as pixels, and so is a drawing whose base picture has not decoded yet.

A CEILING. The Pad's bitmap never holds more than 3x the drawing, what a
phone at 3x already carries; Flip's never more than 2x, what it already draws
at on a 2x screen, because a smudged page pays for every pixel on every
repaint. Past that the canvas still shows bigger, a little softer: on a 5K
screen at 2x the Pad stretches its 3x bitmap by 1.2.

WHAT LEAVES THE CANVAS STAYS THE DRAWING'S OWN SIZE. The PNG, the GIF, the
video files, the post card, a draft's base and thumbnail, a new take's base:
all at the drawing's size times the screen's ratio (the Pad's
drawingPixelSize() and drawingPixels(), the canvas itself whenever it is
that size, so nothing that left it before changes by a pixel). Flip's
paintFrame() goes through the frame layer at its target's resolution, the
grown one for the pad and its caches, one at DPR for files and tiles, so an
export of a long Flip does not pay for the grown canvas. Flip's fill reads
the pad through a copy at DPR once it has grown, so the same tap on the
same drawing makes the same runs on any screen (measured: 162 points, 81
runs, grown or not).

A NEW DRAWING STARTS IN THE SHAPE IT ALWAYS DID. The first build picked the
starting shape against the wider row, and on a desk that turned 1:1 into
4:3 (the preset that shows largest at 1:1 in the band). That is the drawing
changing, which B promised it would not, and it rippled into the fixtures of
three suites (verify_player_isolation's bead and phone rows drew a 4:3 where
they had drawn a 1:1). The pick is made against the column again
(chromefit's columnWidth()), and B changes only how big a drawing shows.

FOUND ON THE WAY: A ZOOM MOVED EVERY STROKE. getCanvasLogicalSize read the
screen's ratio live, so a browser zoom or a window moved to another screen
changed the drawing space under a bitmap made at the old ratio, and every
stroke landed away from the pen until a reload (at 1.25x, by a fifth). The
ratio is now the bitmap's own, and a matchMedia watch on the resolution
makes the bitmap again at the new ratio even when nothing resizes. Flip
always held its DPR as a constant, so only the Pad had this.

verify_player_isolation compared the player's drawing with the editor's
canvas, which on its 1280x900 fixture now grows a little past 1:1. Its
editor half is drawn at 1280x700, where the canvas has not grown, and read
through drawingPixels(): the ink count counts every pixel any ink touches,
and a canvas shrunk to the drawing's size spreads each edge over more of
them (16% more, measured), so the two counts would have been of two
different pictures. 0.04% apart as built.

PIXEL FOR PIXEL. The branch's full run went red in verify_framecache: its
fixture asks a 400x300 page shown at 1:1 on a 1000px window, and the canvas
grows there now. Measured grown, the cache itself was a pixel off: it
captured at CW*RS rounded (559 for a pad of 558) and laid the copy back
through the transform, so a page played from the cache was not the page
painted. It captures at the pad's real size and lays the copy back on the
pad's own pixels; the fixture shows grown and asks for the capture one for
one.

That led to measuring what reaches the screen, a 1px line put into each
bitmap and read off a screenshot, and the bigger canvas was not yet sharp to
the pixel. Flip's pad wears a frame (a 2px border) and the drawing shows
inside it, but the layers grew to the frame's outside: 692 pixels squeezed
into 688, so a 1px line came out two pixels at half. That squeeze predates
B, at 1:1 too; grown, the layers grow to the frame's inside now, and at 1:1
and on a phone it is as it was. Grown, each canvas takes its bitmap's own
size, up to the page's 1/64px, and is laid out again once the bitmap is
made: rounded on their own, the size shown and the bitmap were a pixel apart
at 1.25x and 2x. And Flip laid every page, and its live layers while a
stroke is under way, through the transform: grown, CW*RS is rarely a whole
number of pixels, and where it ran half a pixel or more past them the layer
was stretched by that fraction and every line softened. A layer the size of
the pad is laid on it pixel for pixel (layOn), and every layer's side is
whole pixels counted with a hair of slack (layerPx), since a canvas told
557.99999 is 557. At 1x the screen shows the bitmap one for one on both
editors. At 1.25x and 2x the size is exact, but where the canvas lands on
the screen is the browser's: half a pixel off a whole one, it blends, so
those are measured by size.

Found on the way, not fixed here: Flip maps the pointer through its frame's
outside, so near the canvas's edges a stroke lands up to 2px from the pen
(none in the middle). It predates B.

Pad and Flip: shared where they can be: the row's reach and the page's one
surface are one module and one rule for both; the growth is each editor's
own, because the Pad paints a canvas that holds its pixels and Flip paints
from its pages every time, and the two need different things to make a
bitmap again. Not tested here: Windows, Edge, Safari, and Segoe UI or SF; a
real 4K or 5K screen.

## After v329 -- A posted song that stalls keeps the pages with it

The owner said yes to fixing the link page and a post's box the editor's way:
the pages follow the song's clock. Measured first, on main: a Beat Flip
posted, its song's audio clock held for 0.3s three seconds in (the context
suspended, then resumed, which a busy phone or a Bluetooth hiccup does by
itself), and every round after it came 0.34s early on the link page and 0.31s
early in the box in the feed, for good: both players counted the wall's time
alone, and the song had fallen behind it. The editor's Flip was already fine
(it waits on the song's clock with Beat as the speed, flip.js runPlayTimer).

WHILE A SONG PLAYS IN STEP, THE PLAYER KEEPS TO IT, AS HEARD. lib/holdtiming.js
songClock(): began(ctx, ms, rate) when a source starts where the drawing is
ms, ended() when it stops, at(wall) the time to show. The song's time is the
audio context's from where the source began, less the time the sound takes
to reach the ear (baseLatency and outputLatency, as the editor allows for).
The link page (app.js) begins it where the song starts in step (musicRate()
is the drawing's rate) and ends it in paStop(), so a scrub, a new speed, a
pause and a restart each begin it again from where the song starts; its
frame() takes the time from it. A post's box (inlineplayer.js) does the same,
counted in lap plus elapsed as its song is. With no song, or one at its own
rate under a faster replay, both count the wall's time as before.

THE DRAWING KEEPS THE WALL'S PACE, AND THE SONG ONLY SAYS WHEN TO WAIT. The
first build read the drawing's time straight off the audio clock, and a
browser moves that clock a callback at a time: measured here, 9 to 20ms a
frame against the screen's 16.7, and 40ms on a phone's Bluetooth is likely.
A replay that should glide stepped (verify_glide, with a song and the clock in
40ms steps: the nib moved on 42% of frames). So the drawing goes at the wall's
pace and waits: from each start until the song is heard (the speaker's
delay), and whenever the song falls more than 50ms behind it, until the song
comes past it; it never steps back. 50ms is past the audio clock's own steps,
so a song that is playing is never waited for. A context that has not run
yet (an unlock on its way) is not the clock; once it runs, the drawing waits
for the song to catch up. AND IT EASES ONTO THE SONG: the two clocks drift
(2ms a second here, so a round slid 25ms in sixteen seconds), and a hiccup
under 50ms is not waited for, so the drawing eases instead, by a tenth of how
far it is from the song each frame and never more than a tenth of the frame:
at most a tenth faster or slower while it does. How far is the least it has
been lately, which leaves the audio clock's own steps out.

IT WAITS A SECOND AT MOST. A clock that waited without end froze the drawing
whenever the song's context stopped and nothing here started it again: on a
phone a call or the lock screen, until someone tapped. Past a second of
waiting (two of the drawing's seconds at twice the speed) the drawing goes on
at the wall's pace, and when the song comes back it goes on from where it is
at the song's pace, waiting for the next stall again; the beat is off by
however long the song was gone, until the song starts again (a pause and
Play, or a new speed). And THE LINK PAGE'S SONG STARTS WHERE THE DRAWING IS
WHEN ITS UNLOCK LANDS. An iPhone's first Play unlocks the sound late; the
song started where Play was pressed, and its clock then took the drawing
back to meet it (three pages, with the unlock held 0.25s). paStartAtElapsed()
reads the drawing's place again once the context runs. A post's box starts
its song at once, and its clock waits for the unlock, a second at most.

The players now allow for the speaker's delay too (42ms here), as the
editor does: verify_flipbeat's own words said they did not.

verify_flipbeat's posted part: a 0.3s stall on the link page and in the box,
every round after it within 60ms of its beat (red on main: -338 to -344, -297
to -325); a song gone for 2.5s, which holds the link page's drawing a second
at most; its song's unlock held 0.25s, after which the drawing never goes
back a page and every round is within 60ms of its beat; a speed the song does
not follow (4x) picked mid-play, which the drawing takes (without ended() the
song's clock kept it at 1x); the song a bed there, which does not hold the
drawing when it stalls; and the clock on its own, a context made up and its
time set by hand: begun at 1000ms, half a second on, less the speaker's 40ms,
at twice the speed, is 1920ms; held, it waits and never steps back; a context
that has not run is not the clock; ended, the wall's time again; a song gone
is waited for a second, then the drawing goes on, and follows the song from
there once it is back; with the song's clock in 40ms steps the drawing moves
on every frame, 16.7ms give or take a tenth, and keeps within 10ms of the
song as it really plays; a 45ms hiccup is eased out, never more than a tenth
slower; and a song's clock 1% fast is never more than 20ms ahead of the
drawing. verify_glide: with its song and the clock in 40ms steps, the nib
moves on nearly every frame. Twenty-five breaks, each served in place of
the real file, turned red only the rows that guard them: the players' wiring
(the link page's follow, its clock begun and ended, the in-step rule, the
song started where Play was pressed; the box's follow and its clock begun),
and in the clock the wall's time, the speaker's delay, the never stepping
back, a context that has not run, the end, the second's wait (without it,
without the time it counts, at the drawing's speed, at a tenth), the drawing
read straight off the audio clock, the start's wait, the wait for a song
fallen behind (gone, and at 400ms), the song followed again once back, the
ease (gone, uncapped, and without the least lead), and the release onto the
song. verify_glide's song row, with the drawing read off the audio clock: the
nib moved on 42% of frames. And the posted part's watcher reads the song
BEFORE the canvas now: reading the canvas back waits on the GPU, longer the
busier the box, and the song read after it was that much late (a round came
"79ms late" beside other suites; alone, never).

## After v329 -- Draw in full screen, on a desk (the owner's A)

The owner asked for "a full screen button so it opens over everything else to
full screen", and said "All yes" to the mock: B first (the canvas uses the
window, #648), then A, a button at the dock's end after Magnify, on a desk
only, with the drawers opening where they do today, under the dock.

THE PAGE ITSELF GOES FULL SCREEN, the header and the dock with it, and the
canvas takes the room through B's own fit: a full screen is a bigger window.
On a 1920x1080 screen the Pad's cat shows at 1197x898 (B's 1017x763 in a
1920x945 window) and Flip's card at 930x699 (the mock said 932: the fit keeps
the drawing at 4:3 inside the frame's 2px line, and the mock put the frame at
4:3). One module for both editors, lib/drawfull.js; going full screen is
lib/immersive.js.

THE REAL THING OR NOTHING. lib/immersive.js's stand-in (an element pinned over
the page, for the iPhone) means nothing for a page that already fills the
window, so where the browser cannot take the page full screen the button is
not shown: no API, or fullscreenEnabled false though requestFullscreen is
there, which is how a frame that does not allow it answers. And on a desk
only: a mouse and a window wider than the page's 720px column, where the
canvas grows past it too. The mock said over 640px, the dock's desk tier, but
at 641 the Pad's dock ran 26px past its edge (verify_layout caught it); it
needs about 667 with this box's fonts, and 720 leaves room for wider ones.
Asked as a positive media query, because harness/tools/cssgraph.py keeps
every touch-only block whole in the player's sheet and this one has nothing
for the player.

ON WEARS THE DOCK'S ON TILE, as Magnify and Media do, at Magnify's 26px and
1.8px line. Its words say how out: "Leave full screen (Esc)"; lib/tooltip.js
moves a title to data-tip for its own bubble, so that is where they are read
back. ONE RHYTHM AT THE RIGHT END: 34.2px between the drawn icons, Media to
Magnify and Magnify to this. That takes 7.5px before it where Magnify has 10,
because Media's glyph is 32px wide in its 44px button and the other two are
26. The four corners are the watch button's and the link page's. How it works
has a tip for it, claimed by verify_drawfull.

FOUND ON THE WAY: every full screen on a page fires the same
fullscreenchange, and lib/immersive.js reported each one to every attached
element as its own. The editors' watch heard the page itself leave full
screen as its own leaving and, with nothing focused, handed focus to its
button. It reports a change of its own now, and nothing else, which also
said what its "not ours to report" guard for the stand-in said (on() is
already true there, and was said), so the guard went: +2 B on the link page,
which loads it for its own full screen, inside that budget's line.

Not tested here: Escape (headless Chrome does not hand the browser's key over)
and a real full screen's size (headless Chrome keeps the window's), so the
sizes are asked of a window the screen's size; Windows, Edge, Safari and a
real big monitor.

## After v329 -- Magnify to 512x: close in, the wave itself

The owner, zoomed in on a loop's start: "We need to magnify by enough to see
where it crosses the middle line", then "Like 512x?". At 64x a phone's view
of a 15-second loop was 0.89ms a point, 39 samples, and the song was
loudness bars, the same above and below the middle, so nothing could cross
it. Mocked on the real drawer (Today beside Proposed; the middle line Quiet
or Stronger; an end let go zoomed in Stays, or Snaps to the nearest place the
wave crosses), the answer was "All yes": 128x, 256x and 512x, the wave
itself, the stronger line, and Stays.

THE LADDER goes on to 512x (lib/musictimeline.js MAGS). There a phone's view
of the same loop is 0.11ms a point, 4.9 samples, and a desk's at 1280px
0.06ms, 2.6 samples. The rung's words take the widest rung's room, in
whatever face draws them, so - and + stay where they are as it steps: the
readout was 34px and "128x" is 36.2px in this box's face, so - moved 2.2px
at 128x. The widest rung is written by the timeline and reserved by the
sheet, hidden, so it is neither painted nor read out.

CLOSE IN, THE WAVE ITSELF. While a point holds 64 samples or more the song
is loudness, as it was; under 64 it is the wave, both channels as one (their
mean), each point the least and most of its samples, through a middle line
at its zero; under 8, the samples themselves, joined, each a dot once they
are 6px apart. Past the loop it is dimmed, as the bars are. The line is the
timeline's guide ink at 65%: 3.3:1 to 4.4:1 against the song's ground,
inside the loop and past it, light and dark (the quiet line mocked beside it
was 1.8:1 to 2.0:1). The wave itself reads 3.1:1 dark and 3.6:1 light inside
the loop, and 1.4:1 and 1.5:1 dimmed past it.

LET GO STAYS AS IT IS. Snaps, an end let go zoomed in gliding to the nearest
crossing within 25ms, was mocked and not chosen: zoomed in is for exact
control. The join is already clean where it is heard: a smooth restart's
equal-power fade, or Cut on silence (lib/audioloop.js), which moves both ends
together to the nearest place they match. Advice pasted in from elsewhere (a
zero-crossing search, matching the slope, a 5ms fade at the join) was read
against that: the restart already does what it asks, and what it points at
is Play, Stop and the sound switch, which start and stop the sound at full
level. That is the next change, a bug fix.

Pad and Flip: shared, lib/musictimeline.js and the CSS; neither editor
changed.

TESTS. verify_musictimeline, a new part (wave), on both editors, light and
dark, on the owner's phone, over a 55Hz tone at 44.1kHz whose every zero is
known, asked of what is painted: loudness at 8x (82 samples a point), the
same above and below the line; the wave at 16x (41), which crosses it; the
line at the wave's zero, halfway between its crests and troughs, at 16x and
128x; the wave crossing the line where the tone crosses zero, within a pixel
at 32x and 128x (0.67px and 0.43px at most); the line 3:1 and up inside the
loop and past it; the wave dimmed past the loop; the samples joined at 128x
and the wave still at 64x. The magnify part steps to 512x and asks - and +
to stay put on every rung. verify_helpclaims reads the tip's new words.

CALIBRATION, each break served to the browser in place of the real file,
the files on disk untouched: the ladder stopping at 64x (the ladder's row,
and the buttons', which then have seven rungs to ask); no wave (every row
about it: the wave's, the line's, the crossings', the contrast, the dimming
and the samples'); the line 2px low (the line's row, 2px from the wave's
middle, and the crossings', 1.9px off at 128x); the quiet line (the
contrast row, 1.8:1); the wave 20 samples late, 0.45ms (the crossings' row:
1.13px at 32x, 3.83px at 128x); no dimming (the dim row); no samples (the
samples' row); and the widest rung not written, or not reserved, as
today's sheet (the buttons' row: 2.2px). Each red on both editors, on its
own rows, and the same files served unchanged green. The calibration found
two mistakes in the instrument: with no line to read, the contrast row
raised instead of going red; and it looked for the line where the stage's
middle is, so a line drawn 2px low read as ink and four rows could not read
the wave at all. It finds the line by its paint now, the rows inked across
nine columns in ten.

FOUND ON THE WAY: verify_musicbeat's row for the beat's dots against the
song's lane went red here on the Pad in light, alone and beside others, and
the picture said why: it was of the strip below the timeline. The row scrolls
the timeline into view and takes its picture 300ms later, and the drawer's
hold (lib/drawerdetent.js) can still put the page back where it glided to,
up to 1.2s after it grew; a person's own scroll stands the hold down, a
script's does not. On main the same scroll came a moment after the picture,
so it passed by its timing. The row now reads where the stage is before and
after its picture and takes it again until the two agree: green as built on
both editors, light and dark, and red on all four with the dots painted out.

## After v329 -- No click where the sound starts or stops

Advice pasted in from elsewhere (search for a zero crossing, match the slope,
a 5ms fade) was read against the code: the loop's own join already has all
three in effect, a smooth restart's fold or Cut on silence. What it pointed
at was Play, Stop and the sound switch, which began and ended the sound at
full level, mid-wave: measured on a real song, a Stop at a random moment
jumped by more than a tenth of the peak in one sample more than half the
time. The owner: "All yes" to a 5 ms fade on Play, Stop and the sound
switch, a bug fix.

EACH EDGE GLIDES OVER 5MS (lib/audioloop.js glide, fadeIn, fadeOut): a
source begins from silence through a gain of its own and stops at silence,
let go once it has ended; a sound switch glides its gain. The editors' loop
engine (Hear the loop, Play with my drawing, a tapped pause, on the Pad and
Flip) and the link page use the same three; a post's box, which loads
neither lib/audioloop.js nor app.js, carries the same block word for word,
and verify_soundfade compares the two.

WHERE A GLIDE BEGINS IS WORKED OUT, NOT READ. An AudioParam's value lags the
sound by up to a block, so a glide begun from it in the middle of another
jumps. And cancelAndHoldAtTime, the API made for this, does not do it in
Chrome: after a finished ramp, the next ramp starts from that ramp's end,
long ago, so it is all but over before it begins. Measured on a bare page:
the sound switch dropped 98% in one sample with it, and glided over 4.49ms
with the start set where the last glide says it is. A glide cut short by
another goes on from where it had got to: the first's ramp is cut at the
second's start, at the value it has reached there. Cancelled instead, it
would leave the gain where it was until the second began, then jump.

AND A MOMENT AHEAD. The audio is made ahead of the page's clock, a few
blocks at a time (here the clock moves 384 to 512 samples a step), so a
change scheduled for "now" can land on audio already made, a glide begun
there part done: now and then a start came in at 58% of the level, 3ms of
its 5 gone, and once more with the glide begun 10ms on. Most of all just
after a context wakes, which is every first Play (the engine wakes it in
the gesture and starts once it runs): on a bare page, begun "now", 3 first
starts in 52 jumped the whole level, and none in 40 begun 10ms or 30ms on.
So each glide begins 30ms on, and a source starts as its glide begins and
that much further into its clip, so it is where it would have been: the
music keeps its time with the drawing, to the sample, and no clock had to
change.

TESTS. verify_soundfade, new, on what reaches the speakers: every connection
to a context's output is led through a bus, and an AudioWorklet on it keeps
every block with the audio thread's own frame count (a ScriptProcessorNode's
blocks are the page's to deliver, its times jitter by a block, and a busy
page can lose one unseen, which first read a glide here as a jump). The song
is a steady level, so an unfaded edge steps the whole level in one sample.
Each edge's biggest one-sample step is a fiftieth of the level at most, and
the sound reaches the level or leaves it in 2 to 8ms: on the Pad and Flip,
Hear the loop, its Stop, and pressed again and again; on the link page,
Play, the sound switch both ways and pressed twice in a moment, and Pause;
in a post's box the same. And what pressing rarely reaches: the box's copy
is lib/audioloop.js's word for word; a glide cut short 2ms in by another
goes on from where it had got to (the page clock moves 9 to 12ms a step
here, so two presses rarely land inside one glide); and 80 first starts,
each on a context of its own just after it wakes, none jumps. As built,
every edge steps 0.00227 at most (the glide's own: half of full scale over
220 samples) and takes 4.49ms. The worklet loads from a blob, which the
page's script-src refuses, so the suite's pages bypass the CSP; verify_csp
pins the policy.

CALIBRATION, each part broken alone in a copy served to the browser, the
files on disk untouched; a break of the shared block is made in both copies,
so that only the rows about what it does go red. As built, every row green,
in eight runs as the suite grew, the last two with every row as it stands.
On main's files, 17 rows red: every edge (0.49998, the whole level), the
copies row (no block to compare), the cut-short probe and the first starts
(nothing to call); green, the page errors, the post, and the two
pressed-twice rows, since two presses in one moment cancel there. Each break
went red on its own rows only: the editors' engine begun or stopped unfaded
(the Pad's and Flip's Hear the loop and pressed again and again, or their
Stop); the link page's Play, Pause or sound switch unfaded (its row, or the
switch both ways); a post's box the same; cancelAndHoldAtTime in place of
the start worked out (17 rows: every edge on every surface, all but over
before it begins, and 77 first starts of 77); the start read from the gain's
own value (the cut-short probe in two runs in two, with a press-again row or
two, which ones varying with where the presses land); a glide cut short left
flat until the next (the cut-short probe alone); no lead (the 80 first
starts: 27 of 76 read jumped the whole level, with another suite running
beside it, and Flip's first Hear the loop with them); the box's copy
changed, doing the same (the copies row alone). The lead's row came out of
its own calibration: until it existed, no row went red without the lead, in
three runs, because every row presses on a context already awake.

COST, in the bytes a viewer downloads (parsed, before gzip): the link page
+1,181 B (lib/audioloop.js +1,032: the three and where a glide begins, 902
B, and their use in the engine and their names; app.js +149), a post's box
+762 B (its copy). Spent first: the stops' fallbacks for a source with no
gain of its own, which cannot happen (the two are made together), and the
try around a disconnect, which cannot throw. Both ratchets move with it,
and verify_jsstrip's line.

AND THE PLAYER'S TARGET IS PASSED, the third time, in writing. The link
page's JavaScript is 154,537 B, 737 B over the 153,800 line verify_jsstrip
asserts, and nothing on the page can be spent against it: the fade replaces
only the stops it rewrote. As for the smart fade, the line moves to the
spent value and 25 B (154,562), and the debt is named, not yet tied to a
carve. The first candidate: lib/audioloop.js's WAV writers

holds it is seen as late as the box held it, however on time it was drawn.

since their last look, and each row sets aside one round seen 50ms or more
after the look before, the furthest off, and names it in its detail. One at

## After v329 -- Main red after #656: How it works' rise, a frame the box held

Main's full run after #656 went red on one row, in sqlite's sixth shard and
not postgres's: verify_helpdemos, "Flip: ...and the sheet travels up from the
foot, no frame jumping 40% of the way", with the sheet read at 844, 844, 844,
733, 390: 45% of the way in one frame. #656 changed only the tool cards.

THE SHEET WAS NOT JUMPY. It rises by a transform the compositor moves, so a
person sees it glide whatever the page is doing. The row reads where it is
once a frame, from the page; the places it reads are the transition's own,
frame by frame (733, 631, 539, 459, 390, the same on every run), and a frame
held longer reads a stretch of the glide at once. Holding the page 70ms just
after the sheet first moves gives CI's reading here to the frame (844, 844,
844, 733, 390, 332, 284, 244), and main's row goes red on it.

THE ROW READS EACH FRAME ON ITS OWN CLOCK now (`document.timeline`, the time
the sheet's place is worked out for; `performance.now()` at the read can
come after a hold in the same frame). The ease's fastest stretch is about 15%
of the way a frame, so a frame under 50ms cannot cover 40%: one step of 40%
or more across a frame of 50ms or more is set aside, the biggest, named in
the detail. It still has to be one way and to be seen at three places on the
way at least, so a snap is red.

CALIBRATION, in a trimmed copy (the fixture and section 8, both editors): as
built green; held 70ms once, main's row red on CI's reading and the new one
green, setting aside 343px across a 67ms frame (Flip) and 401px across 83ms
(Pad); with the transition taken away (a snap), red.

Noted, not changed: while the sheet rises, the page spends most of each frame
drawing it (a profile here: about 175ms of 300 in the browser's own work, the
inline replays a few ms), which is why a busy box holds a frame there.

## After v329 -- The click and the beat lit as heard

Step 4 of the music drawer's eight (FUTURE.md 6s, the owner's "All yes"): a
soft click on each beat while Hear the loop plays, at the end of Hear's own
pill, and each beat's dot on the timeline lit as it is heard. The pill is the
menu card Hear was, Hear its first part and a metronome its end, parted by
the card's line (a third button in the pair pushed "Play with my drawing" out
of its own on a phone, which the mock found). Off at first, there once the
song has a beat; pressed, it wears the chosen choice's tint. Its icon reads
8.0 to 8.7:1 against its ground, off and on, light and dark, on both editors.

ON THE LOOP'S OWN CLOCK. lib/musicdrawer.js sets each tick to the sample on
the audio clock the loop plays on: every 30ms, the beats due in the next
160ms of what plays, a short sine (higher on the first beat of a bar, every
four from the loop's start as the timeline draws them), straight to the
speakers and never into a post or a file. Three things the first draft got
wrong, each found by a row before it went up:

  * THE FIRST BEAT. The engine starts 30ms ahead of its sound
    (lib/audioloop.js LEAD), and the loop's first beat falls in those 30ms:
    the draft never ticked it (the click began on beat two), and ticked at
    once it came 30ms before the music. It waits for the music's start now,
    which the drawer works out (the loop's top by its clock, where the start
    began in the clip, and LEAD) and keeps on the click for the harness. And
    a rule that let it through once let it through every 30ms from two
    seconds in, when the memory of beats set forgets them: the click rattled
    until the timing row caught it.
  * WHAT IS SET AHEAD. A tick set 160ms ahead sounded after Stop, after the
    click went off, and, when an end moved while it played, for the old
    loop's next time round beside the new loop's first beat. Each is called
    off now: its gain let go of, before it sounds.
  * A RESTART'S TIMER RUNS LATE. The loop starts again from a timer due 10ms
    before it comes round; a busy page fires it after, when the old loop has
    already ticked its top, and the new loop ticked the same beat again 30ms
    later. No beat is set within a tenth of a second of the last now. The
    row holds the page busy across the moment to make the timer late.

THE LIGHT AS HEARD. A beat's dot lights when the beat reaches the ear, timed
from the context's own record of what its speakers play (getOutputTimestamp),
else the clock plus the output's latency, and asked again as it comes due:
a first guess made as the sound began was once 59ms early. Read against that
record, lights came from half a millisecond before their beats to 13ms after
here. Web Animations, so
Reduce Motion fades it without the swell and the player's sheet carries no
keyframes.

TURNED ON WHILE IT PLAYS, the click starts on the very next beat: a beat
already set ahead, lit and not yet ticked, ticks too. Without that it began
on the beat after, half a second late at 120 a minute.

THUMB REACH (6s, from Wavebox): on the owner's phone, as the drawer opens
with a song, Hear and the click sit in the screen's lower half (their middle
at 720 of 874), whole on it.

Rows (verify_musicbeat, the click; MUSICBEAT_PART=click): the pill; the
thumb's reach; off at first, there once there is a beat; ticks on the beats
to the millisecond, the bar's higher, the first as the music starts; straight
to the speakers; a tick set ahead never sounding once the click goes off or
Hear stops; one tick at the join when an end moves while it plays, the timer
on time and held late; the lights as heard, at their dots, the bar's bigger,
click on or off; the swell, and only a fade under Reduce Motion. Calibrated
with the page's files served from broken copies (the files on disk

## After v329 -- The loop's end sets the tempo

Step 5 of the whole-drawer mock (FUTURE.md 6s; from the Wizard's "click the
end of the first bar"; the owner: "All yes"). Zoomed in, an end let go within
an eighth of a beat of 4, 8, 16 or 32 beats stays exactly where it was let
go, and the beat becomes the one that makes the loop exactly that many:
counted from the loop's start (where a beat falls is the start) and heard to
where the loop comes round, a smooth restart's length before the handle.
Tapped, a tempo is whole beats a minute; this one is to the thousandth, so a
live band or an old record between whole tempos can be matched. It is
by: 'end', no longer the one heard, kept with the song in the drafts
(tempoFrom keeps it), and Flip's Match the beat refits a round of pages to it
as it does to taps. Further off than an eighth, or at 1x, or in the Restart
view, an end settles as before. The eighth is the start's own reach; over 4
beats it moves the tempo by a 32nd at most.

THE COUNT IS THE ONE WITHIN AN EIGHTH, not the nearest the song has room
for: the loop stays as it is, so its room is already there. The nearest
that fits, as an end settling uses, would have dropped to 4 an 8-beat loop
let go at the song's very end.

A NOTE SAYS SO, with Undo: "The beat fits your loop now: 118.8 a minute, 8
beats." The Pad's toast and Flip's chip, seven seconds as every Undo offer.
Undo puts the beat back as it was, heard, tapped or an end's, unless it has

THE PAD'S STROKES, EACH IN ITS OWN INK. editor_music.js gives each stroke's
mark the ink of its first point as the replay draws it (lib/recolorplay.js
gives a recoloured line the colour it was drawn in), an eraser's none, and
lib/musictimeline.js paints it so. An ink that does not read 3:1 against
the lane (--menu-card) keeps its hue and is made darker on the light lane
and lighter on the dark, as the lane's words are, a fiftieth at a time
until it does, and no further; worked out once for each ink on each lane.
Skribl purple and a near-black are as drawn on the light lane; a coral
(2.80:1 there) goes two fiftieths darker, and a pale yellow (1.12:1) a dark
gold, 26. On the dark lane the near-black (1.08:1) goes a slate, 17
lighter. Mixed toward the lane's words instead (the mock's rule), the
yellows went olive. An eraser's stroke is the lane's accent.

FLIP'S PAGES, EACH ITS OWN LITTLE PICTURE. flip.js hands the timeline each
page's picture: the strip's thumbnail as the strip keeps it (_thumbCache,
repainted only when the page changes), or past the cache's budget the
strip's own tile, so a lane painted on every frame of a glide never paints a
page itself (8MB holds about 42 pages at 3x). Its own shape is kept. A page
as long as its picture or longer is the picture at the lane's height, one
centred on the page's time and the rest either side, clipped to the page's
slot, so a page held long is its picture again and again. A shorter page is
the whole picture, smaller, centred in the lane, as the mock had each page
whole in its slot; cropped to its middle instead, a ball crossing eight
pages showed only on the middle ones, and squashed to the lane's height it
was not its own shape. Each picture is framed in the lane's purple
(--accent-ink, 8:1 and up against the lane), on whole device pixels as the
loop's edges are, so a short page's small picture still shows; the card's
own line was 1.3:1. The number sits on a small badge (--accent-fill,
white, 10px) in the picture's corner, so it reads over any drawing, on a
page shown as its picture at the lane's height; a smaller picture has none.
In the first photos a badge on every page with room hid the ball on the
short ones. The mock's numbers were dark purple straight on its pictures.
The turns after the first are the pictures
at 45%, as the marks were. A stroke on Flip's canvas is a tap away from the
drawer, which closes it, so the lane shows a page's new picture as the
drawer opens again.

FLIP'S LANE TALLER FOR THEM. The lane's height is the editor's
(laneHeight(box, base)): Flip's is 34px over the box at its own height and

Pad's stays 26px: a stroke reads as a line.

lib/musicdrawer.js hands both hooks through to the timeline. The new

## After v329 -- Songs in three

Step 8 of the whole-drawer mock (FUTURE.md 6s; the owner: "All yes", of the
mock's songs in three: the Length row in beats, 3 · 6 · 12 · 24 for a waltz,
and a small choice of 4 or 3 beats a bar in Beat for when the ears hear it

song in fours, and its picks on four made waltzes started 0.35 to 0.65s off a
bar.

THE EARS HEAR THREES (lib/musicears.js meterOf). Each beat is scored as barOf
scored it, its kick against the stretch's own and how far the chord moved
from the beat before, and the song is read a stretch at a time, 16 seconds
on that stretch's own beat, as the pick reads it: how plainly one beat in
every three stands out of the others, and one in four, and one in six. In
three when the threes gather plainly (0.6 of the scores' own spread) and
twice as plainly as the fours; in four otherwise, as every song was before.
Sixes far plainer than threes (half again) are a waltz heard at its eighths,
and the beat is halved: a slow waltz at 84 with its eighths played was heard
at 168, one at 76 with soft hats between at 152, and at those speeds their
threes are half bars and gather too. Measured on 17 songs made in the page
(harness/songsynth.py): in four, the threes gathered 0.07 to 0.31 and the
fours 1.39 to 2.01; in three, the threes 1.93 to 2.10 and the fours 0.15 to
0.46. Every song in four is heard as it was, the same beat and the same pick
to the last digit; the songs the ears suite makes are made byte for byte as they
were. The six songs in three now start on a bar, 0.5 to 12.9ms off it (the
band in three plays 8ms off the beat on purpose). Reading the bar adds 15
to 26ms on this box to the ears' last step for a two-minute song (that step
took 27 to 111ms), in one go rather than sliced: on a phone perhaps four
times that, which measuring the ears at a phone's pace (FUTURE.md 6t, next)
is for, with a Web Worker if it shows. A rule that kept a slow waltz's beat
from doubling was tried, and changed no song's result once the sixes were

THE DRAWER COUNTS IN THE BAR (lib/musicdrawer.js). The tempo carries bar: 3
for a song in three and barBy: 'you' when Beats in a bar set it, both kept

BEATS IN A BAR, under Snap to the beat in the Beat door once there is a
