speed counts the song's bar, its rounds 1 or 2 bars in three.

Not tested here: an iPhone's WebKit, SF and Segoe UI, a real waltz.

## After v329 -- The owner's list: the drawing's strip in its box, Flip's time beside Play

The owner, looking at the live drawer: "screenshot 1 shows the things not
fitting in the container. is that meant to be that way?", and of Flip:
"when you draw on in slide 1 in flip the time does not show accurately, it
just flickers". Neither was meant. Bug fixes, in the PR with steps 7 and 8.

THE DRAWING'S STRIP IN ITS BOX (lib/musictimeline.js). Two things. Every
stroke's mark is drawn at least 60ms wide so a dot can be seen, and a dot at
the drawing's very end was drawn past the strip's end; a mark that would end
past it now moves back to end on it. And the strip is laid out in the
song's time from the loop's start, so zoomed in it runs past the timeline's
edge, and it was cut flat there by the canvas while the song's box under it
ends rounded; its box is now as much of it as is in view, ending at the
timeline's edge rounded as the song's does, its marks clipped inside it.
Rows (verify_musiclane, the strip part): a drawing that ends on a dot has
nothing of its ink past the strip's end, the dot inside and every mark
ending on the drawing's end or before, a phone in light and a desk in dark;
zoomed in past where the drawing ends, the box's corners at the edge
unpainted as the song box's are, on the Pad and Flip; a stroke running past
the edge cut by the box's rounded corner. Each red on main and against a
break of its own: no clip, no moving back, the box not kept to the view.
verify_musictimeline's row for where the lane's marks sit had its last
stroke as one dot at the drawing's very end, and the run found it still
wanting that dot at its time, past the end; it wants it ending on the end
now, and is red on main's timeline, against marks laid from 0:00 and
against no moving back.

FLIP'S TIME BESIDE PLAY (flip.js). It counted pages over fps, as if every
page were one frame: a page that draws itself lasts as long as its strokes
took, so with one the pass read 0.3s and, playing, the badge wrapped about
four times a second. It is one pass as it plays now (lib/holdtiming.js
plan, as the music drawer counts it), and while playing it reads the page
on screen: where that page starts in the pass and how long it has been up,
at the watching speed, no further than its end. So it keeps with the pages
from the page Play starts on, through a pause, a new speed, a scrub or a
page the song's beat skips, and waits at a page's end for a late one.
Found on the way: the page timer takes off what the next page's paint will
cost, and for a page that draws itself it counted every point, when it
paints a few a frame, so Play from the page before one cut that page to
about half its time on the first pass; a drawing page's first paint counts
as nothing now. Rows (verify_hold, THE LENGTH BESIDE PLAY): the length at
rest; every frame for 4s, forward but where the pages go round, once a
pass; every frame between the start and end of the page on screen; Play
from page 3 at its place; that page up for its own time; a late page (its
timer 40ms late) waited for; a pause, a new speed and a scrub each carried
on. Each red on main and against a break of its own: the old total, a
clock of its own, no wait at a page's end, the pause, the speed and the
scrub each not carried on, no reading off the page, a drawing page's paint
counted in full.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: the strip is the shared timeline's, both editors; the
time beside Play is Flip's own (the Pad counts its replay's time, which
had no pages to miscount).

Not tested here: an iPhone's WebKit, SF and Segoe UI.

## After v329 -- Snap by the wave, the nearest beat, the zoom inside the song

The owner, after trying the live drawer: Snap to the beat "is in beat. do
you think it is hidden down in there - it took me a minute to find it. I
was trying to change the first and last beat, but the toggle was on and it
kept snapping"; and of Magnify, "when it is at the very beginning it's a
little strange that it slides the wave over to the middle". Mocked as Now
beside the options (the Snap, zoom and Repeat page), "all yes", then "i do
like the magnet having it's own button. is there a way to have its own
button if there's room, but merge them if there's not enough room?", and
its C2.

THE MAGNET BY THE ZOOM (the template's SNAP TO THE BEAT). Snap to the beat
is a magnet in the timeline's top row, between the zoom and the taller
button, lit when it is on (the chosen choice's purple, as the taller button
wears it), so an end that jumps shows why and one tap turns it off. It is
there from the first, unlit and out of reach until there is a beat; its
words are its tooltip. The switch and its row are gone from the Beat door,
which is shorter by them, and the page-still follow has one row fewer to
leave out (lib/drawerdetent.js).

ITS OWN BOX WHEN THERE'S ROOM (lib/musictimeline.js fitHead). The magnet
has a box of its own while the name beside it keeps its one line; where it
would not, its box and the taller button's close up into one, the two cells
2px apart as the zoom's are. Room is measured, not guessed: the name's
width on one line in the face it is drawn in, against what the row leaves
it beside the magnet's own box, so it holds in SF and Segoe as here. On
this box's faces "Your drawing · 3s" keeps its own box from a 390px phone
up and on every desk. A later change (the name growing as the drawing
does) glides, the gap closing over frames; at once under Reduce Motion.
The magnet keeps its side of the zoom: C1, its own box before the zoom,
would have hopped across it. Not tested here: SF and Segoe UI, whose
widths decide where it closes up.

THE NEAREST BEAT (lib/musicdrawer.js beatsFor). With the magnet on, an end
let go settles on the nearest beat, not on 4, 8, 16 or 32 beats: from 23
beats whole bars went back to 16, from 13 on to 16; now each stays, and
none moves more than half a beat, so the first and last beat are the
person's to set. The start still lands on the nearest beat (or where the
music begins), and the end follows to whole beats. Zoomed in, an end let go
within an eighth of a beat of whole bars still makes the beat fit the loop
exactly; further off, the nearest beat. Whole bars are a tap in Beats, and
Skribl's pick is whole bars, as before.

ZOOMED IN, THE BOX STAYS INSIDE THE SONG (lib/musictimeline.js target).
Each zoom keeps the end touched last in the middle, unless that would show
time before 0:00 or after the song's end; there the end sits off the
middle, 12px (TAB_ROOM) left for its tab. At 2x with the loop at 0:00 half
the box had been before the song. A slide or a held end still carries the
view as it goes, and lets go into the box inside the song. 1x is as it was.

ROWS. verify_musicbeat: the nearest beat (an end let go at 10.6 and 12.8
beats to 11 and 13, where whole bars took them to 8 and 16; a start let go
off the beat to it, the end following to whole beats; a start off the beat
kept; the beats the song or the 20s cap have room for; Reduce Motion at once)
and the magnet by the zoom (there from the first, out of reach and unlit
before a tempo, lit as painted, its words, a new song's magnet unlit and out
of reach). verify_musictempo's 7-beat end zoomed in; verify_musicthree's 10.8
beats to 11. verify_musictimeline: zoomed in, inside the song (at 0:00 the
tab's 12px before it, at the song's end 12px past it, mid-song the end in the
middle, phone and desk), and the magnet's own box (exactly when the name
keeps one line beside it, at 402, 390, 375, 360 and a desk; closing up over
frames as the name grows; at once under Reduce Motion). Each shown red
against a broken copy of its own, 14 breaks: whole bars, the magnet always in
reach (a new song's too), never lit, its words never changing, its purple
gone; no clamp zoomed in, no room for the tab; no fit, always joined, the
name measured in a stand-in face, the boxes not closed up, no glide, the old
name ("1:05s"); and every Reduce Motion rule out. The magnet's own Reduce

The affected suites, side by side, found the magnet's box wearing the taller

The owner, of the Pad's replay: "i wasn't talking about the music looping -

mocked on the Snap, zoom and Repeat page (Now beside Repeat on and off, the

REPEAT (editor_draw.js). On a desk beside the speed: in the pill beside Play,
and in the line under the drawing while it plays, between the speed and full
screen; on a phone at the end of the bar (below). The posts' own arrows, bare while off and lit in the chosen choice's
purple while on, a 44px tap, its words its tooltip. Off to start and

stopped: at the drawing's end app.js asks editor_draw.js replayAgain, which

mid-round, that round is the last; Stop stops it at once and leaves it on.

full screen the band tones it as glass (lib/watchfull.js), the speed's while
off and a pressed full screen's while on, in rules of its own so the link
page's sheet carries none of it.

ON A PHONE, AT THE BAR'S END (found by the affected suites before the PR went

way in reads what is drawn before it now, the speed on a phone and Repeat on
a desk: it read the line's Repeat on both and went red (74/76).

THE MUSIC ENDS BY THE DRAWING'S CLOCK (editor_music.js drawingAt), found

## After v329 -- The loop's own Undo and Redo, the bin's Undo, and the ends' reach

THE OWNER, of the music timeline: "sometimes when I go to drag something I
move the whole waveform. shouldn't there be an undo button on the editor
(just to go back to what it was before) and maybe a redo button too?" Of the
Undo, reach and Repeat page, "All yes" to calls 2 to 4 (call 1, Repeat at the
bar's end on a phone, went in with #663).

THE PAIR (call 2, A). Undo and Redo sit at the end of the one line under the
timeline, in a box like the zoom's, each a 28px cell, greyed while there is
nothing to take back or again, as the zoom's minus is at 1x; their names are
"Undo a change to the loop" and "Redo a change to the loop", their tooltips
the same. On a phone the line is two rows tall with or without a drawing to
say it is shorter or longer than, the pair in the middle of them, so nothing
under it moves as the words change; on a desk one row. They take the place of
the Length door's eight-second Undo, which is gone.

EVERY CHANGE TO THE LOOP IS A STEP, and only those: an end dragged, the song
slid, a tap on the whole song's line, a Length card, Skribl's pick as the way
back, a count in Beats, Beats in a bar, Smooth restart and its length, Cut on
silence, a nudge, a typed time, Tap the beat. A drag is one step however far it goes, a held slider one however often it
moves; an end let go and settled on the beat is one step with its glide, and
a change made while a settle still glides is a step of its own, from where
the settle was going. Not steps: the zoom, the taller box, the magnet and
Lock the length, which are how a person looks and works (a step put back
leaves them as they are now), and what Skribl does on its own (its pick for a
new song, what it does once it has listened). A new song starts a new
history; a change after an Undo clears what Redo held; a hundred steps are
kept. lib/musicdrawer.js holds it: every change goes through four setters
that note the loop as it was at its first touch, and a step is kept when the
change is over (a finger lifted, a glide landed).

THE BIN'S UNDO (call 3). The person's own tap on the bin offers an Undo in the
note it shows ("Song removed"), which puts the song back as it was: its
bytes, its loop, its beat, its restart, and the loop's own Undo and Redo. It
says "Song restored", with a Redo that takes it away again. On the Pad the
draft has it again (its bytes back in the draft's store, the draft naming
it); on Flip the next save writes it. A script's click (New Skribl's clear
goes through the Pad's bin) offers none: New Skribl has its own Undo.

THE REACH (call 4). An end takes a press 32px either side of its line and 26px
below its tab (it was 22 and 12), over the row of tabs and the whole song's
line; the whole song's line takes a press on its own row only, 4px above it
(it was 14, up into the tabs), so a near miss beside a tab moves nothing.
Where the two ends' reach meets, the nearer end takes the press
(lib/musictimeline.js), and an end taken by a press beside its line keeps its
distance from the finger instead of jumping to it.

FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT, AND FIXED HERE:
  * Two quick taps on Beats came out as one step: the second landed while the
    first one's glide was still on its way. A glide's step is closed where it
    was going when anything else starts, and Undo and Redo land a glide first.
  * Flip closed its music drawer when an end dragged in it was let go past
    the drawer's edge (a mouse overshoots; on main too): the tap-away read
    where the click landed, which was outside. It reads where the press
    began now, for a click a press made.
  * Flip closed the drawer when the note's Undo was pressed: the note wrote
    itself again ("Song restored"), taking away the button that was pressed,
    and a click on something no longer in the page read as a tap away.
  * A press beside an end's line made the end jump to the finger.
  * The drawer's own nudge helper was shadowed by the new step helper of the
    same name (stepNow, now loopStep), which the new suite's first run found.

CHECKS. verify_musicundo (new) reads all of it on the Pad and on Flip with
real presses, drags and keys: the pair (where it is, painted, named, greyed;
the line's rows on a phone and a desk; one Undo); every kind of change as a
step, each undone and done again as soon as it is made, then Undo all the way
down and Redo all the way up; one step per drag and per held slider; a settle
with its glide; a change made mid-glide; what is not a step; a new song's
history; a change after an Undo; the keyboard's place moving to the other of
the pair as one runs out; the bin's Undo and Redo, the Pad's draft store and
Flip's next save; the reach, read where a press lands on a phone and a desk,
then real presses; the arrows at 3:1 or more on their cell, light and dark,
phone and desk. verify_musicbeat, verify_musicdoors, verify_musicears and
verify_sheetswipe moved off the Length door's Undo onto the pair;
verify_musicears asks that what Skribl does once it has listened is not a
step; verify_helpclaims claims the help's new words.

EACH ROW WAS SHOWN RED BY A BREAK OF ITS OWN (the page's files served from
broken copies, the files on disk untouched), 41 breaks. The steps: none kept;
each setter bypassed in turn (an end's, the slide's, Skribl's pick's, the
whole song's, Fit's, the bar's, the restart's, the cut's, the tapped beat's);
a glide's step never begun; the restart's length not noted before it moves; a
held finger not held; a glide's step left open when the next change starts
(red in verify_musicbeat's two quick taps too); a new song's pick a step; a new
song keeping the old history; a step put back taking the magnet with it; Redo
keeping what it held after a new change; the keyboard's place not moved. The
bin: no note; the song back without its history; the Pad's bytes not put back;
a script's click offering the note; Flip's save not written; Flip's drawer
closing on the note's Undo; and in verify_musicears, what Skribl does once it
has listened made a step. The reach: the old reach of an end and of the whole
song's line, each read where a press lands and by real presses; no nearer
end; the end jumping to the finger; Flip's drawer closing after a drag let go
past it. The pair: no gap, the phone's line one row, faint arrows, greyed at
60% rather than as the zoom's minus, the names, the Length door's Undo back,
the pair out of the line.

The first run ran every change in the chain before undoing any, so a break
took every row after its own red with it; each change is undone and done
again as it is made now, and the fourteen breaks re-run on that red their own
rows. Three first came back green, and each was the instrument: the pair's
names and the pair out of the line served their broken page at a path the
suite does not open (the Pad is at /), and the magnet's row put back a nudge,
which never touches the beat, so a step that took the magnet back could not
show; it puts back a step that changed the bar now. The nearer end: the
suite's song is short, so at 1x its ends are never within reach of each other
(at least 26% of the timeline apart); that row widens the reach in the page
under test until they meet, as a loop of a few beats on a long song does by
itself.

TWO OLDER ROWS, TAUGHT THE NEW DRAWER. The affected suites side by side
(40, beside two others each) found two rows that still asked for the drawer
before this: verify_musictimeline's grip row asked that a tap under a tab
reach the whole song's line, where an end's reach runs now, so it asks that
the tab keeps clear of the line and that a tap under it, on the line, takes
the end (red on the old reach on both editors, phone and desk, green as
built); and verify_helpclaims' census of named controls did not know the
pair's names, so it maps them to the help's own words for them (red on both
editors when the help does not say them). verify_musicundo is weighed at 250
seconds in harness/shard.py, from its 5.1 minutes beside two others here,
until CI measures it.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared. One drawer and one timeline, so all of it is
both editors'; the bin's way back has a part of its own in each (the Pad's
draft store, Flip's save), each read by its own rows.

Not tested here: an iPhone's WebKit, SF and Segoe UI.

## After v329 -- No style rule searches the whole page

Item 1 of the polish list (Phase 1 found it, measured; the owner: "all yes").

WHAT WAS SLOW. At phone pace (Chromium with the CPU 4x slower, 4G, 402 x 874
at 3x) Pad answered a tap only after about 3.7 s and Flip after about 7 s, and
a trace put most of it in style work, not script: UpdateLayoutTree 2.0 + 0.95 s
on Pad and 2.4 + 2.2 s on Flip, against 0.3 s and 0.7 s of script. Chrome's
selector statistics named the cause: five rules that began at the top of the
page, `html:has(...)` and `body:has(...)`. An editor makes about 235 small
style passes while it opens, the root is restyled in most of them, and each
root :has() walks the whole page. A copy of styles.css without just those five
(1,987 of 1,992 rules; every element's computed style identical at rest, 15
properties read) opened with style work 2.9 s -> 0.16 s on Pad and
4.3 s -> 0.23 s on Flip.

WHAT CHANGED. The page says what is open, once, as classes on <html>.
lib/opensurfaces.js (new: Pad, Flip, the gallery, the Library) watches the
hidden attribute and the class of the drawers, sheets, menus and cards, and
sets `skribl-covered` (the Saved pill and its x step away), `skribl-carded`
(the pill under a button's card) and `skribl-sheet` (no pull to refresh);
lib/immersive.js sets `skribl-fullscreen` on fullscreenchange (the scrollbar
gutter). The rules key on those classes, and the lists of surfaces live in the
module, with the reasons that were in the rules. Three more root :has() rules
went the same way: pagemenu.css's and the gallery's own (pull to refresh under
the page menu and the report sheet), and player.css's copy of the full-screen
rule, re-emitted, its live selector renamed in harness/tools/css_live.json so
the player keeps it.

MEASURED AS BUILT, the same pace, median of 3. Pad: style work 3,111 -> 158 ms,
blocked 4,251 -> 394 ms, the longest task 1,989 -> 326 ms, the page still
from 5.3 s -> 1.7 s after it was asked for. Flip: 4,550 -> 207 ms,
5,290 -> 905 ms, 3,237 -> 784 ms, 6.2 s -> 2.0 s.

THE GUARD. verify_pagewide.py, source only, on the PR gate: no selector puts
:has() on html, body or :root (red on main's tree, 29 selectors); every
`html.skribl-*` class a rule keys on is set by a module (red with a state
renamed); and every page whose styles read an open-surface class loads
lib/opensurfaces.js (red with the script tag gone from Flip or the gallery).
That last row first came back green on Flip's break: it read the module's name
in the comment beside the tag, so it reads the tag now. The behaviour stays
pinned where it was: verify_pillfit, verify_sheetswipe, verify_player_isolation.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared. One stylesheet and one module, both editors, and
Flip gains the most.

Not tested here: WebKit (Safari builds :has() differently, so the gain on an
iPhone is unmeasured), SF and Segoe UI.

## After v329 -- A Repeat turn reuses its layers

MAIN WENT RED after #668 (run 40906948983, PostgreSQL 3/6) on verify_padrepeat's
"no frame held at a turn": the first of three turns held 208 ms, the other two
23 and 22, a frame 17. #668 moved only the shards' weights, and the row had
passed on the run before; the turn was always close to its limit.

WHAT A TURN DID. The Pad's Repeat (editor_draw.js replayAgain) made a new stroke
compositor every round: two canvases the drawing's size and a copy of the
canvas into one, in the frame the round turns on. At phone pace (Chromium, the
CPU 4x slower) that was 20 to 29 ms of a 23 to 39 ms turn, and once 89 ms of a
turn held 216 ms, the music's restart taking 91 of it. Traced, the garbage
collector took a few ms near a turn at most, so the time was the turn's own.

WHAT CHANGED. A turn reseeds the two layers Play made, with the compositor's
reseed (which a recolour's moment in a replay already uses), instead of making
two more. The canvas keeps its bitmap while a replay is under way
(canvasBusy), so they still fit. Pad's own file only; the link page's
JavaScript is unchanged. Traced, 24 turns each at that pace: a turn held 40 ms
at the median and 56 at most, against 53 and 109. What a turn still does is
restart the music and copy the base into the layer.

THE ROWS, in verify_padrepeat's round. From the first turn on no canvas is made
(six over three turns with the old turn). And each round starts from the bare
canvas, two frames in, which is what reusing the layers could break: red with
them reused and not reseeded, when the next round opened on the finished
drawing. The count holds on every box; the time held only on a fast one.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: not for Flip. Its Play goes round through its pages and
makes no canvas at a turn (none in four seconds of rounds, counted). The link
page's loop does make a compositor each lap (app.js play(), from the start):
the same reuse there needs a size check and costs bytes under the player's
ratchet, which has 34 B of headroom, so it is named here and not done.

## After v329 -- A tip steps aside when something opens; three names and the first Tab

Items 3 and 5 on the polish list, found in Phase 1 by reading what a press
lands on (elementFromPoint) and what a screen reader is given (the
accessibility tree).

A TIP STEPS ASIDE. On a first visit Flip's intro ("New here?") hangs about 12 s
under the header, and Tune opens in the page rather than as a sheet, so the
toast sat on top of Tune's Speed buttons: on a phone a tap on 6, 12 or 24
opened the help instead, and on a desk a tap on 24. lib/hints.js now hears
lib/opensurfaces.js's classes on <html>: a tip that was up when a drawer, sheet
or menu opens goes, since whatever just opened is what the person is looking
at. A tip shown while one is open stays, because it is about that surface, and
so does one shown in the same moment a drawer opens, in either order (the
classes arrive a moment after, and must not read as the drawer opening over
it). On the way: a tip put away before its first frame used to fade in anyway,
its timer already cleared, and stay until tapped; it now fades in only if it
is still the current tip.

THREE NAMES AND THE FIRST TAB.
- The Shape button had no name of its own, on Pad and on Flip (where it comes
  onto the shelf once Shape is picked). lib/tooltip.js names a button from its
  tooltip only when it has no words, and Shape's word is in the button but
  hidden at a phone's width, so in a narrow window with a mouse it had no name,
  and on a phone it read the whole tooltip. It says "Shape" now, first, as Pen
  and Eraser do, in both editors.
- The Caption's count sat inside its label, so the field was named
  "Caption optional 0 / 300". The count is the field's description now, and its
  name is "Caption optional".
- Flip's first Tab went to page 1 in the strip and its header came last.
  Chromium moves where Tab starts on scrollIntoView, and Flip scrolled its strip
  that way as it opened. The opening scroll moves the strip's own row to the
  same centre instead, and the first Tab lands in the header, as on Pad.

THE ROWS, each shown red against its own break. verify_tips: Flip at 390 and
1280, the intro up, Tune opens and every Speed button takes the press; on Pad
a tip steps aside for Tune and for the menu, stays when shown with Tune open,
stays when shown in the same moment Tune opens (either order), and a tip put
away before its first frame is not left on screen. verify_a11y: the tools on
each editor's shelf are named by their word, Shape among them, in a narrow
window with a mouse and on a phone; the Caption's name and description; the
first Tab lands in the header on Pad and on Flip.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared. One tips module, one Post sheet and the same
Shape button serve both editors; the intro and the first Tab were Flip's to
fix.

## After v329 -- Undo on a long drawing, from a kept copy

Item 2 on the polish list, its first half: the Pad's Undo. The opening and the
link page's first paint are the second half, a PR of their own.

THE COST. A history state is the stroke list and a reference to its base, never
pixels: a full canvas copy per stroke once pinned half a gigabyte
(makeHistoryState, app.js). So every Undo painted the whole drawing again, and
on a two-hour piece (145,200 points, 6,600 strokes) that was 1.6 to 1.9 s at
this box's own pace, every press. Painting those points faster with the same
ink was tried first and is not on offer: pressure changes a stroke's width on
94% of its segments, so they cannot be joined into one path, and setting each
brush value only when it changes saved nothing measurable. One filled shape
per stroke halved the calls (0.9 s against 1.6 to 1.8) but drew slower in all
(3.2 to 3.4 s) and changed the ink.

WHAT CHANGED. As each stroke is laid (editor_draw.js commitStrokeWithMirrors and
commitActiveStroke), while the canvas holds exactly the drawing, padUndoKeep
copies it into one of three canvases kept for the purpose, the oldest first:
three, reused, never one per stroke. Undo and Redo (editor_menu.js) ask
padUndoRestore before they repaint. A state whose points are the very objects a
copy was taken of, in order, on the same base, canvas size and stroke layers, is
put back with one drawImage: the canvas as it was when that drawing was last on
it. Identity is enough because the editor never changes a point a state holds
(the select move and the recolour copy a point before they change it, and say
why). Anything else repaints as before. Pad's own files only: app.js and the
link page are unchanged.

MEASURED, the two-hour piece at this box's pace: the first and second Undo after
drawing held the page 92 and 154 ms against 1,799 and 1,868, with no repaint;
traced, the Undo is one 18 ms task on the main thread (the rest of the frame is
this box's software GPU compositing a large canvas). The third Undo, past the
copies, repaints as before (1.5 s).

THE ROWS, verify_undofast.py, each red against its own break: no fast path in
Undo or Redo (4 rows), copies never kept (6), no size check (the grown window),
a count-only match (an edit with as many points, other ones), no base or no
stroke-layers check (asked of padUndoRestore directly, with its own drawing as
the control), one copy instead of three (4), a new canvas per copy (2).

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: Flip next. Its Undo works on one page (flip.js undoStroke)
and repaints that page and its thumbnail: a page of 20,000 points held 253 ms at
this box's pace (861 at the CPU 4x slower) and one of 60,000 held 441, the time
in render and refreshThumb. The same kept copy applies per page; it is on the
list as its own PR.

## After v329 -- Flip's Undo on a busy page, from a kept copy; the tiles follow the photo

Item 2 on the polish list, Flip's half (the Pad's is the entry above). And a
bug in the strip, found while keeping the tiles: it goes with them.

THE COST. An Undo on Flip painted the page from its strokes, then its tile,
then, on page 2 and after, the onion skin's ghost of the page before: at this
box's pace a page of 20,000 points held 160 to 230 ms (720 to 980 with the CPU
4x slower, about half of it the tile), 250 to 280 over a busy page 1 in the
onion (1,130 to 1,440), and one of 60,000 points 460 to 610.

WHAT CHANGED (flip.js, UNDO WITHOUT PAINTING THE PAGE AGAIN). A busy page, from
4,000 points (KEEP_MIN_POINTS), keeps up to three copies of its ink, the one
used longest ago going first. The frame layer is tagged with the ink's
signature each time it has just been painted with the page at rest: by
render() when no stroke, smudge or blur is under way, and by a stroke's start,
which paints the ink under it. A stroke, a fill, a stamp, an Undo and a Redo
keep the tagged layer; an Undo or a Redo back to ink a copy holds lays the copy
where render() would have painted the strokes, and paints the backdrop, the
page underneath, the onion and the guides as before. A light page keeps
nothing: it repaints in a few milliseconds and a copy is 8 MB on a phone.
- BY CONTENT, NOT BY OBJECT. The Pad knows its copies by the point objects,
  because its edits make new points. Flip's tools move, recolour and liquify
  points where they lie, so a copy is known by every value its painting reads,
  hashed twice (_inkSig): positions and widths to a 65,536th of a pixel,
  colour, eraser, stroke starts, and the stroke-layers setting. Written flat,
  it is 1 ms for 20,000 points at this box's pace, 5 with the CPU 4x slower.
- THE TILE keeps a busy page's last three pictures (_thumbBack), known by the
  same signature as the cached tile.
- THE ONION. A busy page's ghost is no longer painted again while it is
  unchanged: the nearest stays on the onion layer, known by its signature, and
  with the onion two or three pages deep the farther ones keep a canvas each.
  That also takes the ghost out of every repaint on page 2 of a busy
  animation, the start of every stroke among them.
- A new canvas size, or the layers grown with the window, drop every copy and
  ghost.

MEASURED, before and after taken in turn on this box (a page built in the
document, one real stroke through the pointer, then Undo, Redo, Undo; the
press itself, its tile included):

                                  before            after
  20,000 points                   157 / 157 ms      11 / 6 ms
    the CPU 4x slower             719 / 739         37 / 29
  page 2 over a busy page 1       252 / 257         18 / 10
    the CPU 4x slower           1,441 / 1,150       68 / 37
  60,000 points                   556 / 607         24 / 11
    the CPU 4x slower           2,372 / 2,372       58 / 54

(Undo / Redo. What is left is the signature, the backdrop and the onion
painted again, and the copy laid on.)

ALSO FOUND: THE TILES DID NOT FOLLOW THE PHOTO. The cached tile was known by
its strokes, the ground colour and whether there was a photo at all, so a
second photo, the photo's strength, blur or framing, the photo switched off,
or a new canvas size left every tile showing the old one until its own page
was drawn on again: after each, the tiles were read against tiles painted
afresh beside them, on main's tree, and differed. The tile now knows
everything drawBackdrop reads and the canvas size (_backdropSig); a photo by
the Image it was loaded into, never its data URL. A strength, blur or zoom
slider now paints the page at each step and the tiles once it rests (150 ms
after the last step): with the tiles following the photo, each step painted
all of them, 66 ms on 31 pages at this box's pace and 284 with the CPU 4x
slower.

THE ROWS, each shown red against its own break on a served copy of this tree:
22 breaks, one component each (the four Undo and Redo branches; the signature
by count alone, and blind to the stroke layers; both drops; the settled test
always true, and without the smudge; the eraser's tag and the tile's; the
tile's pictures not looked in, and not kept; the near ghost and the far; the
keep at a stroke's end, its start, a fill and a stamp; the tile's backdrop as
it was; the slider painting every tile each step).
verify_undofast, Flip on a phone: Undo twice and Redo put back every pixel of
the pad and the tile with no ink painted, and show what a full repaint shows,
from a copy holding exactly the painted layer; past the copies, one paint;
three copies and three pictures, reused; nothing painted over a busy page in
the onion, one and two pages deep; the first Undo on a page just opened (the
stroke's start kept it) and the Redo straight after (its end kept that); a
fill and a stamp undone and redone; a light page keeps nothing; an edit in
place told apart by content; the stroke layers switched off; a new canvas
size and grown layers drop the copies; the frame layer never taken
mid-stroke, mid-erase, mid-smudge, or after a tile was painted through it.
verify_pages: a second photo, the strength (and the tiles once the slider
rests, not at each step), the photo switched off, and a new canvas size, each
tile against one painted afresh.

WHAT IT DOES TO THE PAD: the Pad's half came first (the entry above). The tile
fix is Flip's own: the Pad has no page strip.

  "Posted!" and the line that is true then (the Pad's "Anyone with the link can
  watch it draw itself.", Flip's "...watch it play."). Blooby jumps once, his

  ground in the in-post player (inlineplayer.js, which the editors do not load,
  asked for as the post starts going), from the payload just sent: the Pad's
  once, in about three seconds, resting on the finished drawing; a Flip twice
  round, resting on its first page. Under it the title, the caption in full,
  and whether it is in the gallery or shared by its link only. The player
  starts 400 ms in, once the glide is done, since its work on the page would
  hold the height's frames; the picture is the card if it has not started by
  1.5 s. The player's box waits in an inert <template> until the first post:
  an editor's page has no second canvas before then (verify_drafts took the
  first canvas on the page and found the card's).
- WHERE TO GO NEXT: Watch, Copy link and Share as before; then Make another,
  always (New Skribl and its Undo, which brings this drawing back: the Pad's
  clearAllWithUndo, Flip's newSkriblWithUndo), and Back to the site when the
  site has named its home. Focus goes to Watch. Watch on the Home Screen app
  opens the link page in place, since a new tab there is Safari; in a browser
  tab, a new tab as before. The toast and Flip's chip that said "Posted!"
  above the sheet are gone: the band says it.
- THE HOST NAMES ITS HOME once: create_blueprint(home_url=, home_label=), and
  app.py from SKRIBL_HOME_URL and SKRIBL_HOME_LABEL. Refused at startup unless
  it is an http(s) address or a path on the site, with no space or backslash
  in it (a browser reads "/\x" as "//x"). An address is called by its host
  unless it is named; a path must be named. Standalone, there is no button.

  and the card is the picture. Decided in the script, not by a media query:

THE REASON, when a post does not go: a card in the sheet's own ink with the
danger's mark, right above Try again (the button and what follows it are
ordered after it), and the sheet scrolls Try again into view with it. While it

THE WORDS AT THE MENU'S SIZES: the field labels 11 to 13 and bold, the speed
hint and the lines under the gallery tick and the delete key 11 to 13, the

the reason 14. Nothing painted in the sheet is under 12px. With the taller

FLIP'S WORDS: every failure in its own word, "Your animation is still here".

## After v329 -- A long drawing's first look: its own picture at once, the ink without a freeze

PR E of the posting mock the owner answered "all yes": 2b, B, "the picture at
once, then sharp". Measured on the two-hour stand-in (145,200 points, 6,600
strokes) before this: the link page stood blank until the payload had come and
been painted, 1.5 s on a desk and 1.7 s on a phone at this box's pace, 4.1 and
6.8 s with the CPU 4x slower, and the paint was one task of up to 5.7 s in which
nothing on the page could be touched. A real phone also waits for the payload
itself, 9.6 MB for that piece.

THE PAGE AT ONCE. A Pad post's size is a column (canvas_w/canvas_h, the tile's
reason), its line's numbers are too (line_json, the in-post player's reason),
and its title and caption are already read for the Open Graph tags, so the
route hands the page all of them (routes.py, pre) and the shell renders the
words. app.js lays the box out before it asks for the payload (initPlayer
playerPre), from the same fit it always used, with the track at the
scrubber's height and the line under it in the post's own numbers (the real
ones replace it), so the box the picture stands in is the box the drawing
gets (the first cut did not: the shell grew 59 px when the drawing came and
the box shrank under the picture), and a phone turned while the drawing comes
re-fits the box then. The post's own picture stands where the canvas is:
/s/<id>/poster, the card made when it was posted, cropped back to the
drawing. The crop is lib/sharecard.js drawingRect() with the plate's corner
and edge clipped off, the arithmetic inlineplayer.js fitPoster() does for the
feed's box. THE FRAME'S SHADE: the canvas has the frame's vignette over its
ground and under its ink, and a flat picture can only have it over all of it.
Bare, the picture's edge was lighter than the ink's by 14.5 of 255; with the
shade at full strength, darker by 9; at 0.6 it reads the same (within 1). The
transport is laid out but unseen until the drawing can play, so nothing
moves when it comes up, and it comes up over 0.3 s.

THE INK WITHOUT A FREEZE. paintStrokesStatic lays its runs in slices when
asked, the same runs in the same order, so the canvas ends exactly as one
call leaves it, and the link page asks for it under the picture. TWO THINGS
THE FIRST CUT GOT WRONG, both traced: a slice's ink is turned into pixels
after it, when the canvas is flushed, and that takes several times longer
than laying it (10 ms slices made frames of 40 to 110 ms; a flush left to
pile up made one of 400 ms with the CPU 4x slower). So each slice is shown
(the flush lands in the frame that laid it) and the last frame's length
steers the next slice toward a frame of about 34 ms, starting small. When
the ink is whole the picture fades over 0.3 s (at once under Reduce Motion,
which needs no rule of its own here: the page's every-element rule stills the
fade and the rise). A Play or a seek before then takes the canvas
(restoreSeq) and the picture goes. Unasked, the function is the one call it
always was: the editors are unchanged. An empty drawing has nothing to paint,
so its picture is let go at once.

AFTER, on the same piece, the box loaded as the battery loads it: the
picture is on screen in 0.3 s, before any of the data; the box stands to the
pixel where it stood, phone and desk; at this box's pace the one long task is
the data's own arrival (107 to 123 ms), and with the CPU 4x slower the
arrival's is 233 to 380 ms and the frames after it 50 to 150 ms, where there
was one task of 5.7 s. The ink is whole 1.9 to 2.4 s after the data comes at
this pace, behind the picture.

NOT FOR A FLIP, AND TIMED. A Flip's card is its first inked page, which need
not be the page its link page rests on, and its first paint is one page, not
the lot. Timed on a long Flip (60 pages of 2,400
points, 144,000 in all, a 20 MB payload): its first page is on screen 0.2 s
after its data has come (0.7 to 0.8 s with the CPU 4x slower), and the one long
task in that is 59 to 83 ms (247 to 265 ms). The wait is the payload's own
size, not a paint, so a Flip's page stays as it is; the picture first for a
Flip, where its card is the page it rests on, is FUTURE.md 6x.

THE ROWS. verify_firstlook.py (new, 35 rows): with the post's data held
back by the browser, the picture painted where the canvas is and cropped to
the drawing (read by hue), the words said, the transport unseen; the box
standing still, short and long, phone and desk, and a phone turned while it
waits; the swap cell by cell and at the edge's ring; the fade, Reduce Motion;
the slices' ink against one call's; with the CPU 4x slower, many frames, the
ink shown as it goes, and no task a third of the one call (THE INSTRUMENT'S
FIRST DRAFT left the data's arrival out of what it measured, and the arrival's
task is where the old freeze lived, so it could not have seen the freeze it
guards against); Play while it paints; a short drawing, an empty one, no
picture, a refused payload, a Flip, a missing post. Each red against its own
break on a served copy of this tree, 24 of 24, one component each: the route's
size, its line, the template's picture, the server's title; the early
scrubber height, the early line; the picture shown before inkWhole exists
(the first cut's own bug: a cached picture never showed); no fade (script and
sheet); Reduce Motion's page-wide rules; the paint unsliced; the slices
deaf to restoreSeq; no slice shown; the slice fixed at 10 ms (a 243 ms task);
the transport not hidden, not rising, never made ready; no crop; the shade
gone and at full strength; the empty drawing never let go; playerPre never
called; a slice that skips a point; no re-fit on a turn. TWO BREAKS FIRST
STAYED GREEN, and both times the tree was at fault, not the row: the picture's
own Reduce Motion rule was one the page already made (gone), and the shade
over the picture made its edge darker than the canvas's by 9 of 255 (now at
0.6, and a row that reads the edge both ways).

THE COST. The link page's script +2,268 B (156,801), its style +571 B
(42,316) and its HTML +94 B (13,953), raised in writing in
verify_player_isolation and verify_jsstrip; each Pad post's page also fetches
its 66 KB card. Spent first: the picture's own error handler and clip, the
line's pick, the four transport rows named three times over, and the
redundant Reduce Motion rule.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared, the title and caption said by the server on
every link page, a Flip's included, so its words are there before its data
too. Not for Flip, the picture and the slices, for the reasons timed above;
Flip next, the picture first where its card is the page it rests on
(FUTURE.md 6x). The editors draw as they did.

## After v329 -- A long word stays inside, wherever a post's words show

A bug fix, from the owner's own phone: a caption of long runs of letters
("vivuvuvjvjfux...", nowhere to break) ran off both edges of the link page,
the first and last letters of each line out of sight. The words on the link
page (.player-meta) could break only at a space, so the box took the longest
run as its narrowest width: 460px, its max-width, centred on a 402px phone,
and the run past even that.

THE FIX. overflow-wrap: anywhere on the link page's words (the title and the
caption inherit it from .player-meta; the Pad's own player wears the same
rules) and on the Library stage's title, the two places a post's words could
not break. The gallery's card, the Library's caption and the Posted! card
already broke a long word; the Library's rows and the feed's title line cut
theirs with an ellipsis, on purpose, and still do. A word breaks only where
it would otherwise leave its line; ordinary words wrap at their spaces as
before.

THE ROWS, verify_captions.py LONG WORDS (new): a post whose title is one
78-letter word and whose caption is the owner's, on a phone and a desk: the
link page, its gallery card, the Library's stage and row, and, through the
Pad's own sheet, the Posted! card. Each reads the laid-out words (a Range's
rects) against their own box and the page's width, so a word cut off at a
card's edge is caught as surely as one off the screen, and asks that the page
never scrolls sideways; a line cut with an ellipsis on purpose is asked only
to keep its box on the page. Each part shown red against its own break on a
served copy of this tree, 8 of 8: the link page's words, the Library stage's
title and its caption, the gallery card's title and its caption, the Posted!
card's title and its caption, and, for the instrument, a row's caption no

THE COST. The link page's styles +25 B (42,341), raised in writing in

## After v329 -- The link page: two lines of a long caption, and your own post's way back

The owner, from a phone, on the link page of a post with a long title and
caption: the drawing was a third smaller than on one with a short caption
(the page fits the drawing to what the words leave), and "Make your own
should be back to pad, cuz that's what it does, and should". Offered two
lines and a "more" so words never shrink the drawing, and Back to Pad on a
post of your own; the owner: "all yes, skip the mock and just build it".

TWO LINES AND A MORE. The caption shows two lines at rest and a "more" where
it runs on, as the gallery's cards do; "more" glides the rest open in place
and "less" back (Reduce Motion: it just changes). The box is laid out for the
two lines and the "more" before the drawing is asked for (initPlayer
playerPre), so it is the box the drawing keeps; it is laid out again only
when the answer changes with the width (a phone turned). Opened, the rest
pushes the page longer and the drawing keeps its size. The two lines, the
"more", its glide and its question (the words' own height against two of
their lines, at the width they are set at) were gallery.js's alone; they are
lib/capmore.js now, which the gallery, the link page and (next) the Posted!
card share, the way the full-screen bar is one module.

YOUR OWN POST'S WAY BACK. On a post this browser made (its posted list; a
post kept only on this device is its own), the button says Back to Pad, or
Back to Flip on a Flip, and goes there: a step back in history when the
editor is the page just left (Watch in place, the Home Screen app's way), so
the editor comes back as it was, its drawing on it; else the editor itself,
whose draft brings the drawing back. Anyone else's post still asks them to
make their own.

THE ROWS, verify_linkpage.py (a new section, 22 rows; 56 in all): a long
caption at two lines and a painted "more", 44px, its state and its word in

frames, none more than 40% of the way, and the drawing's own move gliding
with it; "less" gliding back; Reduce Motion with no frame between; a

standing still while the data is held back; Back to Pad, Back to Flip, and

"more" in a grey (2), never yours (3), always yours (1), a Flip taken for

## After v329 -- The Posted! card: the drawing in its own shape, two lines of the caption

The owner, from a phone, of the Posted! card with a long caption: "comment
chokes out canvas". The card's drawing sat in a fixed band, 200px tall on a
phone and 250 on a desk, letterboxed on its own ground, and the caption ran
in full under it, so the longer the caption, the more of the card was words.
Offered the drawing in its own shape, up to about half the screen, and the
caption at two lines with a "more"; the owner: "all yes, skip the mock and
just build it".

THE DRAWING IN ITS OWN SHAPE. The card's box is the drawing's shape (the
editor's own ratio, the one the Post sheet's preview already used), matted
on the card at the words' inset with the preview's corner and line, as the
gallery's cards mat theirs ("canvas borders hit card border and it's weird
looking"), and centred. It is as wide as the words until it would stand
taller than its room. The room is about half the screen, and never more
than the sheet has once everything else in it is laid out, so Watch and the
rest stay on the screen without scrolling; on a window too short for all of
it the drawing keeps 160px (the Post sheet preview's floor) and the sheet
scrolls. It is fitted when the card comes up, with the caption at its two
lines, and again when the window changes. Measured on a phone (402x874) with
a delete-key row: a tall drawing 142x252 (it was 112x200 in the band), a
square one 252x252 (was 200x200); on a desk a tall one 169x300 (was 141x250).
A 16:9 drawing is 348x196, about the 356x200 it was: the mat costs it a
little width, and a wide drawing has no height to gain.

TWO LINES AND A MORE. The caption shows two lines and a "more" where it runs
on, lib/capmore.js, the gallery's and the link page's own; "more" glides the
rest open in place and the sheet scrolls to it, the drawing keeping its size
(a window change while it is open measures the caption shut). Each post
starts shut. Flip's sheet loads the module too.

A PRESS INSIDE THE SHEET NEVER CLOSES IT. The sheet closed on the first
press of "more": lib/labels.js keeps a button's word in a span, the press
landed on that span, and "more" becoming "less" took the span out of the
page before the press bubbled to the overlay, whose outside-press check
asked the span where it was and heard nowhere. The check reads the path the
press took (composedPath) instead, so no button that rewrites its own words
can close the sheet it is in. The menu's, Export's and Flip's sheets ask the
same question the old way; none of them has such a button today.

## After v329 -- The Pad opens a long drawing without a freeze

The posting mock's 2b, which the owner answered "all yes": "Opening a long
drawing in Pad stops freezing too." The link page's half shipped as "A long
drawing's first look"; this is the editor's. Opening a long drawing (the
suite's is 60,000 points, about two hours of drawing) held the Pad for its
paint, and on a desk a second time a moment later: the canvas grew to the
screen and painted the whole drawing again.

ONE PAINT. growBeforePaint (editor_draft.js) gives the bitmap the growth its
new size asks for before anything is laid on it, where the growth's timer
grew it a moment after the paint and painted everything again. The canvas
is still empty then, so growing costs nothing. Both ways a drawing opens
take it: a file (loadSkribl) and a reload's autosave (restoreAutosave).

IN SLICES. Past 20,000 points the Pad lays the paint a slice a frame
(padPaint, through the sliced paint the link page already uses, each slice
shown); under that the paint is the one call it always was. The first press
or key anywhere on the page before the ink is whole lays the rest at once,
in that press and before anything it does, so a new take's base, the post's
card, an export, an undo all meet the whole drawing, never half of it. For
that the sliced paint now hands back a way to finish it at once.

MEASURED on this box, main beside this tree, the same 60,000-point file
opened through the Pad's own input, the tasks over 50 ms from the pick until
the page settles: on a phone (402x874) one of 587 ms became a longest of 103;
with the CPU 4x slower, 2,560 became 418. On a desk (1280x900) two, 348 and
296 ms (the paint and the growth's), became one paint and a longest of 96;
4x slower, 1,757 and 1,495 became 357. What is left of the longest is the
file's own arrival (reading it and taking it in), not the paint.

THE PAD'S OWN PLAYER (#skribl=, the post kept on this device) is as it was:
it paints a long drawing three times, on main as here (once on load and
twice as its canvas grows), all whole. Two things keep it from slicing: its
paint runs while app.js loads, before editor_draft.js and padPaint exist,
and padPaint paints in one call in player mode. The three paints are the
player's own and not this change's.

THE ROWS. verify_padopen.py (new, 25 rows): the long drawing painted once
on opening, on a desk on a canvas grown to its screen first; the slices'
ink pixel for pixel one call's, see-through ink and all, phone and desk;
with the CPU 4x slower, phone and desk, many frames, the ink shown as it
goes, and no task from the pick to the ink whole (the file's arrival and its
autosave included) a third of the one call on the same page; a stroke drawn
while it is being laid finds the ink whole when its press reaches the page
and lands on the whole drawing, and a key finds it whole too; a reload's
autosave laid the same way, painted once, the same ink; a short drawing the
one call it was; the Pad's own player never in slices; no page errors.

Each red against its own break on a served copy, one component each (15
runs, 13 of them red): no growth before a file's paint (the desk's one-paint row), nor
before a reload's (2 rows); never sliced (10); a press that does not finish
it (1), a key that does not (1), a finish that does not lay the rest (1);
a short drawing sliced (1); no slice shown (2); the slices without the
stroke layers (3); an error at the paint's end (6, and a long task); the end
painting the drawing again (7); the autosave never written (4, the case's
own row first). The Pad's own player row takes two breaks together: its
paint running after the editor's scripts and padPaint without its
player-mode case; each alone stays green, which is the two guards holding.

THE BREAKS FOUND TWO FAULTS IN THE INSTRUMENT FIRST. Its drawing had one
stroke in five of see-through ink, which put the whole paint over the
stroke layers' budget (24), so no slice ever went through the layers and the
two breaks of them stayed green; one stroke in 64 is see-through now (about
21) and the same-ink rows say the layers were used. And the player row's
first draft asked for one paint, which main does not do either; it now asks
what this change governs, whole paints and no slices.

THE COST. The link page's script +223 B (160,593 with the two-line caption's
+3,569 merged under it), all app.js: the sliced paint's way to finish at
once, and loadSkribl asking the editor's paint and growth when the page has
them. Spent first: a flag of its own for the sliced paint's end, where
`whole` serves. Raised in writing in verify_player_isolation and
verify_jsstrip. padPaint and growBeforePaint are the editor's own
(editor_draft.js), which the link page does not load.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: Flip next, named and on the list. Flip's editor
opening a long Flip (60 pages of 2,400 points, 144,000 in all, a 10.6 MB
file) holds the page in one task of 0.9 s on a desk and 1.1 s on a phone
(3.8 s and 6.0 s with the CPU 4x slower). Timed by step on the desk, the
page strip is 651 ms of the load's 739: every page's picture painted at
once. The strip a few pictures a frame, the ones in view first, is FUTURE.md
6y. The Pad's slicing is not Flip's to share: a Flip's page is one page,
already a paint of its own size.

## After v329 -- Main red after #687: the click drops no beat when the page is held

Main's full run after #687 failed one row, on postgres 6/6 only:
verify_musicclick, the Pad's click ("ticks on each beat of what plays ... to
the millisecond"), 21/22. The first tick was on time; a later beat had none.
The drawer sets each beat's tick ahead on the loop's audio clock, every 30ms,
and never sets one whose time has passed (a late tick is off the beat). It set
them only 160ms ahead, so a page held past a beat, as a busy box holds one,
dropped that beat. Run beside two heavy suites here it stayed green (6 ticks,
each on its beat): the hold is the box's, the gap in the click is the
drawer's.

Now each beat is set half a second ahead (lib/musicdrawer.js BEAT_AHEAD),
which rides out the longest holds seen on CI, about 350ms. Everything set
ahead is still called off when the click goes off, Hear stops or an end
moves, so a longer reach changes nothing heard. Shared by the Pad and Flip.

THE ROW. verify_musicclick.py, a new part "held" (MUSICCLICK_PART=held): the
page held busy for 300ms from 250ms before the loop's third beat, so no timer
runs between; that beat ticks once, on time, every gap after the first half a
second. Red on main's drawer on the Pad and Flip, twice each (that beat with
no tick, a 1s gap); green with the fix, twice each. Its first draft missed
twice in the instrument, not the tree: it took the beat from the sound's start
rather than the loop's clock, which starts LEAD (30ms) before it, and it
counted the first tick's gap, which LEAD shortens.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP AND THE PAD: one module, both editors, the same fix.

AND THE HARNESS'S PLAYWRIGHT MOVED, in this seal's own pull request. The cloud
container now ships Chromium build 1243 (Chrome 153), Playwright 1.56 asks
for 1194, and the old build cannot be fetched here, so no browser suite could
launch. harness/requirements.txt pins 1.63, the release that drives 1243, by
its own rule; CI installs the browser for whatever version resolves. Its full
run on the branch, dispatched before the seal began, is the first evidence of
the harness on 1.63; this seal is the second.

THAT RUN FOUND TWO THINGS, and the first seal start was stopped in its first
batch to put them right:

- FIREFOX 155'S MP4 EXPORT MADE A BROKEN FILE (a real bug, found by the new
  browser). The export asked first for H.264 High; Firefox 155's encoder
  answers High with B-frames, frames sent out of the order they show in, and
  the vendored mp4-muxer cannot take them. It threw "Timestamps must be
  monotonically increasing" inside the encoder's own callback, where nothing
  caught it, and the export finished a file of 29 frames out of 83
  (firefox_smoke, "no page threw"). lib/mp4export.js now asks for Constrained
  Baseline at level 4.0 first (avc1.42e028, the reach High had), which has no
  B-frames; and a frame that comes back out of order stops the export as an
  error, which both editors already answer with a WebM. verify_muxer, MP4
  VIDEO: Baseline asked first; an encoder that answers out of order on a later
  tick, as a real one does, stops the export and throws nothing uncaught; in
  order, the file is made. Red on main's mp4export.js with Firefox's own words
  ("DTS went from 66667 to 33333"), green with the fix. Shared by the Pad and
  Flip (one module).
- HEADLESS CHROMIUM NOW ENCODES H.264. Build 1243 has the encoder 1194 lacked,
  so the Pad's Video button took the MP4 route where verify_videoexport's two
  WebM rows for the Pad expected a WebM, and read the MP4 as nothing (red on
  main's code too: the instrument, not the tree). Those rows now ask for the
  WebM route by name (NO_MP4, the MP4 path declined, as NO_AAC already does
  for the music row). And verify_mp4 no longer skips here: it ran 24/24 in
  this container's Chromium, so the seal reports it locally and the real-Chrome
  attestation is extra evidence rather than the only evidence. START-HERE's
  MP4 section, release_run.mp4_attestation()'s note and the CI skip guard's
  comment said it skipped wherever Chromium was the browser; they say why it
  used to, and what reads the attestation now. The second seal start was
  stopped in its second batch for this, so the sealed primer and the sealed
  record agree.

THE FULL BATTERY ON CHROME 153 FOUND FOUR MORE (CI's run on the branch, six
of twelve shards red, each red on both databases; the third seal start was
stopped at its seventh batch for them). One was the app, three the checks:

- A LONG DRAWING'S FILE ARRIVED AS ONE TASK TOO LONG (verify_padopen, the
  app). With the CPU 4x slower, a 60,000-point file's arrival was one task of
  about 600 ms on a desk, where the "Pad opens a long drawing" entry measured
  357 under Chrome 141, and the row's line is a third of painting the drawing
  in one call (about 1,500 ms): red in CI twice and here once in three. The
  paint's slices were about 100; the arrival had grown. Profiled: reading the
  file's words a quarter of it, normalising its points a quarter, and the
  Pad's loadSkribl hook normalising the whole document a second time to read
  its media, a tenth. The Pad's file open moves from app.js, the link page's
  script, to editor_draft.js (the link page has no #draftInput), and reads the
  words in one task and takes the drawing in the next; the hook reads the
  media through currentFrameMedia, as app.js says every reader should. The
  longest task is now 188 to 297 ms, phone and desk, three runs of three. The
  link page's script is smaller by the handler.
- CHROME 153 WILL NOT RESIZE A WINDOW IN FULL SCREEN ("restore it to normal
  state first"), and verify_drawfull died where it made the window the
  screen's size inside full screen. It does so before the press now; the page
  ends at the same size in full screen. Calibrated: with the window left at
  the desk's height, the canvas rows go red (1017x763 and 752x564).
- CHROME 153'S EMULATED ZOOM TELLS NO MEDIA QUERY (verify_bigcanvas). Under
  Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride the ratio changes and every resolution
  query reads the new answer, but no `change` fires, in the headless shell
  and in full Chrome alike, with frames running. The Pad hears a ratio change
  the standard way, a `change` on such a query, so the check keeps the
  page's resolution queries as they are made and tells each whose answer
  changed, as the browser tells it. Calibrated: with the Pad's listener
  removed, red (the bitmap 763 where 954 is wanted). What a real move to
  another screen does under Chrome 153 is not tested here.
- CHROME 153 COUNTS AN ANCESTOR'S ROUNDED CLIP when it says what is under a
  point (verify_book): 2px in from a Flip tray card's clip corner now reads
  the card's stage, whose 12px rounded edge is the clip's corners by design
  ("Every tool in Flip's tray has its card"). Nothing painted changed. The
  corner points stand in by the rounding of whichever box clips the clip at
  its corner, as they already did for the clip's own. Calibrated: main's
  suite red on the same two rows; a clip pushed 10px past its stage still
  red.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP AND THE PAD: the file open is the Pad's (Flip's is its
own, flip.js loadDraftFile, and its long-Flip open is FUTURE.md 6y); the
three checks read both editors as before.

## After v330 -- How it works' rise: a start the box held, told from a skip

The next step the entry above names. The seal's fourth start went red on
verify_helpdemos' rise row, Flip: 844 four times, then 540, 40% of the way
in a frame the page's clock put under 50ms. Green on CI and in ten runs here.

THE BROWSER CAN START A TRANSITION LATE AND DATE ITS START BACK. The glide's
own clock (the transform transition's currentTime) then reads, at the first
frame the sheet moves, the time since it was asked for, so that frame is a
stretch of the way in while the page's clock saw one frame pass. A start the
box held: the cousin of the frame the box held (After v329, #656), and the
row set aside only that one.

THE GLIDE'S CLOCK ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH. A glide pushed on (its currentTime
moved forward) passes 50ms of its clock in a frame too, and forgiving that
forgives a skip. So the row reads a third clock, the wall clock since the tap
(performance.now()), and a step counts as held on the glide's clock only
while the glide is no further on than the wall clock, a frame's grace (20ms)
allowed: a late start never gets ahead of real time, and a skip does. Still
one step at most is set aside, the biggest, named in the detail with both
clocks; still one way, and seen at three places on the way at least. When
the row is red, its detail lists by frame how far the glide's clock ran
ahead of the wall clock.

CALIBRATION, in a trimmed copy (the fixture and section 8, both editors),
main's row, then the glide's-clock-only version tried during the seal and
not committed, then this one:

- as built: green, green, green;
- a snap (the transition taken away): red, red, red;
- a jump (the sheet shifted 45% of the way for two frames mid-glide): red,
  red, red;
- a skip (the glide pushed 150ms on at its second frame): red; GREEN, the
  skip forgiven (658px set aside on 167ms of the glide's clock); red, the
  glide's clock 105 to 135ms ahead of the wall clock;
- a held start (the glide held at 0 for four frames, then given the time
  since it began, as the browser dates it): red, the seal's red; green;
  green (478px set aside on 90ms of the glide's clock on the Pad, 585px on
  127ms on Flip).

As built, five more runs of the trimmed copy: green, nothing set aside. The
first try at the jump moved the box by margin-top, and the sheet's
translateY(100%), a share of its own height, took most of it back (51px of
342): green on all three, an instrument that could not go red. The jump is a
translate now, which nothing takes back.

WHAT IT DOES TO THE APP: nothing; the row is the instrument. Pad and Flip:
the same row on both.

## After v330 -- Main red after #695: the Pad's line ended before its third face

Main's full run after #695, which changed only documents, went red on one
row, in sqlite's fourth shard and not postgres's: verify_replayspeed,
"[320] the Pad's line while it plays: its end speeds as far from the pill's
edge as two speeds are apart, in each face", with "its own face: ok;
Liberation Sans: ok; FreeSans: no pill".

THE PILL WAS GONE, NOT WRONG. The row draws two short lines, plays them,
opens the speeds and reads the pill in each face in turn. The line goes with
the scrubber when the replay ends (editor_draw.js), and this drawing replays
in about a second, so on a slow runner the replay ended before the third
face was read, and there was no pill to read.

THE REPLAY IS PAUSED BEFORE THE FACES ARE READ (pausePlayback(), as
verify_recolorplay pauses it), so the line stays, however long the faces
take. The desk pill at 1280 stays after a replay ends and was never at risk;
it is paused too, in the same loop.

CALIBRATION, in a trimmed copy (the fixture and the first loop of THE PILL'S
ENDS): with a slow runner made by waiting 1.5s before the faces are read,
main's row red at 320 and 402 with "no pill" in every face (CI's red, whole),
and the desk pill green; paused, all three green; as built, both green. The
whole suite: 168/168 (3.7 min, on its own server).

WHAT IT DOES TO THE APP: nothing; the row is the instrument. It reads the
Pad's line only; Flip's speeds are not in this row.

## After v330 -- Recolor's lens: hold still to aim; a mouse lights the line; Redo

The owner: "the recolor should have the same magnifier as color picker, but
just so you can pick the stroke". Mocked on the real Pad with the cat from
How it works, whose whiskers are 0.6px lines about 11px apart on the owner's
iPhone, all three under one fingertip. The eyedropper's own lens, dropped in
unchanged, showed why it could not be the same: its 10x grid is for one
pixel's colour, and a whisker there is one row of dark cells, which whisker
unknowable. Then "Mock up the good ideas", and "All yes, build the lens
first and add a redo next to undo in recolor mode".

BUILT, in lib/recolor.js, one module for both editors:

- A FINGER HELD STILL (330ms within the 8px a press may wander) brings up a
  lens just above it: the eyedropper's body and split ring, showing the
  drawing at 3x from the same composited picture the colour's run draws
  from, the line under the finger lit (a glow and a white rim round it, and
  the line itself over them as the screen shows it, so a part rubbed out
  stays rubbed out). The ring says before and after: the line's colour now
  above, the pen's below. Sliding chooses another line; letting go gives the
  lit line the colour, one step of undo; a second finger or a cancel
  changes nothing. Near the top of the screen the lens stands beside the
  finger. A quick tap and a drag that moves at once are what they were.
- A MOUSE, or a pen that hovers, has nothing in its way, so no lens: the
  line it would catch lights up as it moves, and a click takes it. It goes
  by what is pointing, not the device.
- THE BAR HAS REDO BESIDE UNDO, each pressing the editor's own and off when
  it is. On a touch screen the bar says "Tap a line, or hold to aim", in two
  balanced lines; with Redo the words had 65px at 320 and ran to four lines
  out of the bar, so under 360px the bar is closer and the words 13px.
- Recolor's help card gains a row for each way (Hold on a touch screen,
  Point on a desk: lib/learncard.js now takes desk rows for a card that
  works one way under a finger and another under a mouse), and How it
  works' Recolor entry says the hold, the pointing and Redo.

THE LIGHT IS ONE PATH A LINE. Drawn segment by segment in a see-through
colour, every joint where two segments overlap showed as a bead, and the
first lens, which scaled the drawing's light up 3x, showed a blob; the light
is now one path a group at its widest, and the lens draws its own at its
own size. Only the line's opaque footprint goes segment by segment.

CALIBRATION, in a trimmed copy (the fixture and the AIMING section),
lib/recolor.js served in place of the file, each break red on its own rows,
on the Pad and Flip alike:

- main's module: the lens, the light and Redo rows (taps, clicks and the
  bar's layout stay green, as they should);
- no hold: the hold rows (the lens, above, the ring, sliding, letting go,
  a second finger, near the top);
- the lens at once (a hold of 0): "not at once" and the quick tap. A tap
  read at 60ms could not show this on Flip, whose press keeps the page busy
  past 60ms, so the tap is read at 150ms, still a quick tap;
- the lens over the finger: above, and near the top;
- no rule for the top: near the top;
- letting go takes the first point: letting go;
- a second finger ignored: the second finger;
- no hover: the desk's light;
- Redo not pressing the editor's: Redo;
- styles.css without the narrow rule: the two 320 rows.

As built, 26 of 26. The first version of the tap, the second finger and
Redo rows went red after an earlier row's failure had recoloured their
lines; each now reads its own gesture against the drawing just before it,
on a line of its own.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared; Flip's Recolor has the lens, the light and
Redo in the same change (its editor passes its own Redo). Flip's Select bar
keeps its way of recolouring many lines at once.

Not tested here: a real finger and Safari's long press (touch is CDP touch
events; no WebKit here); how long the hold should feel, 330ms to start and

## After v330 -- A finger's sideways drag on Pen: the browser took it

Filming the Size help card's example ("Quicker: Drag sideways on Pen") under
touch, a 140px drag on the Pen button moved the size 5 to 8, where a mouse
moves it 5 to 28. The button said nothing about touch, so a finger's drag
was the browser's to pan: Chrome took it after about four moves and sent
pointercancel, and lib/penswoosh.js's scrub ended with it. On a phone, the
quick way to change size barely worked, on both editors (Flip's buttons say
`manipulation`, which allows the same pan).

THE FIX is one rule in styles.css, `#penToolBtn { touch-action: none }`:
the button keeps the whole drag. An id outweighs Flip's `.flip-app button`
rule. A tap, the hold that opens the Pen card, and the mouse's drag are
unchanged; a vertical swipe that starts on the Pen button no longer pans,
and nothing there scrolled. The player's CSS is unchanged (re-emitted).

verify_helpclaims gains probe:pen_finger beside probe:pen_swoosh (which
drags with a mouse, which a browser never pans): a CDP finger drag of 60px
moves the size 10 with no pointercancel, on the Pad and Flip. Calibrated in
a trimmed copy with styles.css served in place of the file: without the rule
both editors red ("5 -> 8", "7 -> 10", a pointercancel each); the rule on
the Pad's dock only, Flip red and the Pad green; as built, both green. The
first Pad-only run read green on both because the route's pattern missed the
stylesheet's path and served the real file; a check of the computed
touch-action caught it before it was believed.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared; one rule, both editors.

Not tested here: a real finger and Safari (CDP touch in Chromium; no WebKit
here). Safari honours `touch-action: none` and fires pointercancel when it
starts a pan, so the bug and the fix should be the same there.

## After v330 -- Done in purple, a breathing dot, and the first take says so once

The owner, about Pad's recording header: "It's not noticeable. I had to look
around to find it and wasn't sure I was even recording." Measured, the
quiet glass Done (DONE, NOT STOP: the crimson Stop before it "feels
punitive... warning, failure vibes") was 1.15:1 against the light header and
1.18:1 against the dark: its words were plain, the button was not there. The
mock showed Now beside three options on the real Pad, phone and desk, light
and dark; the owner: "Yes to all and breathing dot is yes".

- DONE WEARS THE ACTION'S PURPLE, as Post does (same role, same token; Post
  is hidden while a take records): 4.4:1 against the light header, 3.4:1
  against the dark, its words and square white at 5.3:1, Post's weight and
  text shadow. It still recedes while the pen is down and comes back as you
  lift. Red stays out.
- THE FIRST TAKE SAYS SO, ONCE: the first time a stroke ends in a take,
  "You're recording. Tap Done when you're finished." (Click, with a mouse)
  hangs 12px under Done, its caret on Done's middle. It is a lib/hints.js
  hint, so it shows once ever and the tips switch turns it off; the take
  ending puts it away. lib/hints.js gains opts.under for it: the toast is
  measured at its containing block's own edge, which on a desk with classic
  scrollbars is a gutter in from the screen's (styles.css,
  `scrollbar-gutter: stable both-edges`: 10px here; the first build's caret
  was 10px off Done there, and the toast, measured while parked at 50%, ran
  past a phone's right margin). Automation never meets it unless it asks
  (window.__skriblTakeHintForce), as with the hello and the help cards.
- THE DOT BREATHES: its halo swells from a 3px ring at 0.16 to a 7px ring at
  0.30 and back every 2.4s, while a take records; under Reduce Motion it is
  the still 4px ring it always was. The halo is the dot's ::before and the
  dot its ::after, so the halo never tints it, moved by Web Animations from
  editor_bar.js. The first build used a CSS @keyframes, and the player's
  stylesheet went 228 bytes over its budget: every @keyframes and every
  Reduce Motion block ships to the player, which never records. The motion
  and the line live in editor_bar.js because app.js is every player's
  download too.

How it works' Auto-record tip says the dot and Done; verify_helpclaims
holds it to the new checks.

verify_ux gains DONE, THE DOT AND THE FIRST LINE (Done's fill and words off
the pixels, the line's place and its once, Done putting it away, automation
not meeting it, the halo's scale on every frame, Reduce Motion), and READOUT
ALIGNMENT reads Done's words against Done's own fill: against the header's
ground a filled pill measured the pill's middle, not the words.

CALIBRATION
CALIBRATION, in a trimmed copy of verify_ux (the fixture, the new section and
READOUT ALIGNMENT), each file served in place of the real one; each break red
on its own rows:

- Done back to the glass pill: DONE STANDS OUT alone (1.15:1);
- no breath: the breath's row alone (a still 0.727);
- the breath running under Reduce Motion: the Reduce Motion row alone;
- no line: the line's row, and Done putting it away (nothing went up);
- no automation guard: the "never meets it" part alone;
- the take's end not putting it away: the "gone after Done" part alone;
- a fresh key each stroke: "once", and the putting away (the take's end
  hides 'take-done', no longer its name);
- no gutter correction: the line's row, on the desk alone (its caret 10.1px
  off Done's middle; on the phone, -0.5);
- the toast measured where it was parked: the line's row, and DONE STANDS
  OUT too (its offsets read from the default 50% left and 84px top, it
  landed on Done);
- no caret: the line's row;
- Done's words 2px low in the pill: READOUT ALIGNMENT (2.5px); main's
  instrument, which read against the header, green on the same break.

As built, 8 of 8. The "once" row first went red on the built code: the
first line stays six seconds and was still up at the second stroke. It now
puts the first away before asking.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: not for Flip; Flip has no take to record, its pages are
the drawing, saved as you go. lib/hints.js's opts.under is shared, for Flip
when it wants it.

Not tested here: Safari (no WebKit here). Where a browser cannot animate a
::before with Web Animations (KeyframeEffect.pseudoElement), the dot keeps
its still ring rather than breathing. SF and Segoe UI are not on this box;
Done's words are the same weight and shadow as Post's.

## After v330 -- The Post sheet: a tick box you can see, a caption that fits, and its grip

The owner, with screenshots of the Post sheet: "The little box is almost
invisible until checked. Also maybe a way to expand box in lower right?" The
mock (the tick box, the caption, the music toggles; Now beside options, on
the real Pad, light and dark): "I like your ideas" to A1 and B3.

- THE GALLERY BOX'S EDGE is the sheet's secondary ink, 2px. Unticked it was
  the card's own faint line, 1.40:1 against the light sheet and 1.38:1
  against the dark; it is 8.3:1 and 9.7:1, on both editors (one sheet).
  Ticked, it fills with the accent as before. A2, the app's switch, was not
  picked: its off track is 1.5:1 against the sheet, like every switch's.
- THE CAPTION FITS ITS WORDS (lib/postsheet.js): it eases to the height of
  what is written (0.18s; at once on opening and under Reduce Motion), where
  three lines and a scroll had cut a five-line caption's top line in half.
- ITS CORNER IS YOURS: a grip drawn in the lower-right corner sets the height
  by hand, down for room and up for less, never under the three lines it
  starts with. A drag stops the fitting until the sheet opens again, and
  swallows the click that would put the caret in the box (the grip sits in
  the field's label). A phone's text box has no resize corner of its own, so
  the grip is ours: touch-action none, a 44px band.
- EVERY MEASURE IS TAKEN WITH THE EASE OFF. The first build read the words'
  height by setting the box to 0 with the ease on, and the box eased from
  there: read on every frame, it dipped to its padding (20px) for a frame
  before growing. Under Reduce Motion the easing is the script's, not a CSS
  block's: every Reduce Motion block ships to the player's stylesheet.

## After v330 -- Off switches: a lilac groove, the knob lifted

The owner, of the app's on/off switches when off. A firmer grey and edges
were mocked first, a loud 1px edge (7.4 to 8.8:1) and a quiet one (3.2 to
4:1): "Is the outline to contrasting? Seems loud?", then "I don't really
like those either. If you are going to change it, I want subtle
sophistication, simple and elegant and kind." Three quiet options followed
(a grey groove, a flat lilac, both) beside Now, light and dark, phone and
desk: "Yes" to D3, both, and to the gallery tick box keeping its firm edge.

- OFF IS THE ON COLOUR AT A FRACTION, PRESSED IN. The track was the wash at
  0.16, a flat grey. It is --ui-active at 16% in light and, in dark, the
  same colour a third lighter at a fifth (the #a792ff lilac the dark
  sheets' lines already use), with a soft shadow along its top inside
  edge. The knob trades its tight dark shadow (0 1px 3px at 0.4) for a
  soft, wide one (0 2px 6px at 0.20, over a 1px contact shadow). Made from
  the on colour, so the two cannot drift if the --ui-* dial turns. The two
  values live on .layer-toggle, with light's beside them: they are one
  control's, not the ramp's.
- IT READS BY ITS DEPTH, AND THE NUMBERS SAY SO. Against the row behind it
