## After v330 -- The letter sheet: the owner's own font, drawn on the Pad

The owner asked for text on the Pad, then "Can't we have our own font", and
said "All yes" to the letter sheet's mock: one letter at a time with guide
lines and a faint model, Redo, Back, Next, Finish later, a line along the
bottom that fills in, 92 boxes (a second try at e t a o i n s r h), and the
set reaching Cal as a post (FUTURE.md 6ab). Built at /skribl-pad?letters=1,
linked from nowhere: it is the owner's, for the Text tool's own hand.

WHY THE REAL PAD. The Text tool will write words at the pace they were drawn,
so a letter has to be a performance: each point with its time and its width
(pressure is folded into the width). The sheet is the Pad's own canvas and
pen with its chrome put away (visibility, so the canvas keeps its size and
nothing lays out again under the pen); skribl/static/editor_letters.js runs
it and letters.css dresses it, both on that page only. A letter is kept in
localStorage (skribl.letters.v1) after every stroke, so Finish later only
leaves, and a browser that will not keep it says so once.

WHAT IT LEAVES ALONE. The Pad's draft: editor_draft.js keeps no draft there,
as compose keeps none (PAD_DRAFT_OFF), or the slot would have been written
over by each letter in turn. The Pad's settings: the sheet draws with the
plain pen at size 6 in Skribl purple, unmirrored, by shadowing the brush and
mirror on their module objects for the page's life; setBrush and setMode
SAVE a choice, and the owner's Pad would have come back plain.

WHERE IT GOES ON FROM THE MOCK, each for a reason:
- THE X-HEIGHT LINE sits at 0.70 of the cap height (0.334 of the box, not
  the mock's 0.44): the mock's faint a stood far above its own line. The
  model is now sized from the face's own measurements, lowercase to the
  x-height and capitals to the cap height, so it fits its lines in SF, Segoe
  or anything else (measured here: the a 4px from its line on a 713px cap,
  the A 4px). A letter keeps the lines it was drawn to.
- THE LINE ALONG THE BOTTOM is the pangram while the letters are drawn, then
  each later group's own: the figures, the marks, the five accented letters
  (each accent sitting on the owner's own base letter), and each second try
  beside its first. The pangram alone would have stood still for 40 boxes.
- AN ACCENT is drawn over the owner's own base letter, faint, with the
  model's accent alone (its letter knocked out of it), so it sits where it
  will sit.
- AT THE END the canvas shows the whole set as it will post, the line writes
  itself over a faint copy in about four seconds, Redo and Finish later go,
  and Post your letters takes Next's room.
- KINDNESS: Redo's toast brings the letter back (and a new stroke takes the
  offer away); on a desk Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y take back and put back a stroke;
  the arrows move between letters. The Pad's letter keys (the eraser, the
  pen's size) do nothing here.

HOW THE SET REACHES CAL. Post your letters lays every letter out on the
canvas, one cell each in a grid as big as the canvas allows, scaled by its
cap height, on its cell's baseline, centred on its own ink, its width drawn
five times its scale so the set reads at that size, one after another at its
own pace and 300ms apart; and posts it as "My letters". harness/tools/
letterfont.py reads it back from the post's link by the same rule. Which
strokes are whose is not written anywhere: strokeGroups stay per stroke
(bending them per letter would change what undo and the readers take them
to mean), and the reader splits the strokes in order, the split that puts
every stroke's middle nearest its cell winning (a dynamic programme, so one
stroke drawn wide of its box cannot shift every letter after it).

verify_letters (57 rows) holds it: the bars painted and the Pad's chrome
hidden (and nothing of the header beside the desk's panel); the box clear of
both bars; a letter kept with its time from its first point, its pause, the
plain pen; four lines, under the ink, painted on screen, and the model fitted
to them in light and dark; Next, Back and a stroke added later landing after
the letter's last; Redo, its Undo, and the offer taken away; the line writing
itself read on every frame, still under Reduce Motion, and the end's whole
line over its faint copy; the Pad's draft byte for byte and the brush and
mirror as they were; Finish later and coming back; the set posted and read
back through the server, 92 letters with their own strokes (R's first stroke
starting left of its box, W wider than its cell, the dots), to a thousandth
of a cap height (measured 0.00012), widths to 0.00002, times exact, letters
300ms apart; Back from the end; every word on the bars 4.5:1 and up (the sub
line the lowest, 8.3 light and 9.7 dark; Next 5.3), every button 44px; the
keys.

CALIBRATION, the part alone, the file served changed: 31 breaks, each red at
its own row and nowhere it should not be: the chrome shown, the box under the
foot bar, Next always lit, the time not from the first point, the pause lost,
the model sized by the cap height, the guides over the ink, no time shift
for a letter taken up again, the offer left standing, Undo not putting the
letter back, the line not writing, writing under Reduce Motion, no faint
copy, the draft slot on, the brush and the mirror unshadowed, Finish later
staying, no coming back to a half-drawn letter, the width's gain, the cell's
width, letters centred on their box rather than their ink, no gap, a pen on
the finished set, no title, the set not finished, Back stuck at the end, a
faint sub line (2.1:1), 40px buttons, the Pad's keys let through, undo
blocked, the arrows gone. Three breaks first did nothing, each the break's
fault: one renamed only the last of a list of hidden things; one took away
one of the mirror's three shadows (count and reflect still made no copies),
so the mirror break takes the three; and Finish later reloading made the
suite stop on a timeout instead of saying so, so that row now waits, then
says where it went. The plain Pad's probe reads all five things on the sheet
and none on the Pad.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: not for Flip. The sheet records performances to make
a font, which is the Pad's job; the font will serve the Text tool on both
editors (one module, the next pull request).

THE FOUR: powerful (every letter a performance, posted and read back exactly);
playful (the line writes itself in your hand, and at the end the whole set);
simple (three moves and one way out); kind (nothing is lost: every stroke is
kept as it is drawn, Redo can be undone, Finish later picks up where you
stopped, and your Pad and its settings are left as they were).

Not tested here: WebKit (the owner's iPhone), and SF and Segoe UI for the
model's fit (it is fitted from the face's own measurements, so it does not
depend on this box's fonts); the live site (not reachable from this
session).

## After v330 -- Your hand: every person's own letters, theirs to change

The owner drew the letter sheet on their phone and posted it ("My letters",
92 letters, 136 strokes; every one read back from the post), said "I might
want to redo that, I did it fast", then asked "Every user should have their
own font, right? That they can edit?" and said "Yes to all" to five calls:
every person their own hand, kept on their device and editable; 30 letters
to start; a copy to keep; the owner's hand offered to everyone as the style
Skribl; mock first. The mock (the Text mock, v3) put seven more; "Yes" to all
seven. This is the first of the two pull requests; the Text tool is the
second. FUTURE.md 6ab has the plan.

WHAT A PERSON MEETS (editor_letters.js, letters.css, still /skribl-pad
?letters=1 until the Text sheet's door comes with the Text tool):
- THE START, for someone with no letters: what happens, how long it takes,
  Skribl's own "hello" writing itself, Start with a, Open a copy.
- THE FIRST 30 (a to z, then . , ! ?), then READY, once: Add the rest, or
  Done. The rest come in the order they are posted (capitals, numbers, the
  other marks, accents, second tries); Next goes to the next letter not yet
  drawn.
- THE TILES (Your hand): every letter in its group with its count, drawn
  ones in the person's hand, the rest faint in the page's face with a +.
  Tapping one draws it again with the old one faint behind it; the old one
  is kept until Done (a reload in the middle leaves it as it was), Cancel
  keeps it, Redo clears only the new strokes. Tapping a + adds the letter.
  The last letter drawn in order ends here, the whole line writing itself.
- ALONG THE BOTTOM: Save a copy (a plain download, my-hand.skriblhand, as
  the Pad's own Save as a file is, so Safari saves it rather than showing
  JSON), Open a copy (every letter checked, Undo), Start over (Undo), Post
  your letters (whatever is drawn).

THE POSTED ORDER DID NOT CHANGE. Letters are drawn in a new order but
posted in the 92-cell order the owner's post already uses, so letterfont.py
reads it and every set after it the same way. A set posted before every
letter is drawn leaves those cells empty; the reader's split now allows a
letter no strokes (each stroke's letter never before the one before it), and
reads the owner's post back exactly as before. A store from the letter sheet
is read as it stands and placed again: the owner's 92 open on the tiles.

What changed from the letter sheet, as built yesterday: the end screen (the
whole set on the canvas, Back, Post your letters) became the tiles; Back
from the end went with it; the sheet's progress counts to 30, then to 92.

verify_letters (69 rows, 13 parts) holds it: the start for someone new; the
sheet's bars painted and the Pad's chrome hidden; a letter a performance; the
guides and the model; Next, Back, Redo; the line, and the last letter ending
on the tiles with the line writing itself; the Pad untouched; Finish later
and coming back; the set posted from the tiles and read back (all 92, and a
hand of 30 with the other 62 empty); every word 4.5:1 and up on the bars and
all three pages, phone and desk, light and dark (the lowest 5.3:1, the purple
buttons), every button 44px; the keys; the first 30 and Ready, once; the
tiles, drawing again and adding; a copy, Start over and Undo, and a file that
is not a hand changing nothing.

CALIBRATION, the part alone, the file served changed: 42 breaks, each red at
its own row: the 30 old ones that still apply, and the start skipped, the
order not starting with the 30, Ready never, Ready twice, Add the rest from
a, no letter faint behind, a letter drawn again kept before Done, Done
ignored, no +, a copy with one letter, Start over's Undo doing nothing, any
file opened, a set of 30 posted packed together, the tiles not coming back
after the post sheet. Three did not go red first time, and each said
something: GAP 0 met a server error, three runs posting to one test
database at once, and went red run alone; Ready never and the faint letter
gone made the suite stop on a wait, and one read showed why the second

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared once the Text tool comes (one hand, one door

THE FOUR: powerful (anyone's own hand, any letter changed later); playful

## After v330 -- Main red after #715: a /* in a string read as a comment

Main's full run after #715 went red in both shard 4s, sqlite and postgres,
at one row of verify_music: "both editors load lib/musicdrawer.js and wire
their drawer through it" read the Pad's wiring as missing. Not a flake: the
row reads the Pad's code as text, app.js and every editor_*.js joined, with
one regex taking out /* ... */ comments, and Your hand's file types for Open
a copy ('.skriblhand,...,text/plain,text/*') put a /* inside a string. The
regex took it for a comment and took everything up to the next */, in a
later file, with it: the music drawer's SkriblMusicDrawer.wire( among it. The
app was right. The rows below it that check for ABSENCE (no editor keeps its
own copy of a drawer control) would have passed over the same missing code.

verify_music reads each file on its own through the server's tokeniser
(skribl/jsstrip.py, which knows a string), so a comment can neither start in
a string nor run on into the next file. Measured on the tree: the old read
misses the wiring (CI's red), the new one finds it; with the wiring really
taken out of editor_music.js the new read misses it; before #715 both found
it. The suite, 37 of 37. No other suite reads the editors joined and
stripped (verify_surfaces' census strips nothing; its regex is for CSS).

#715's own run of affected suites did not include verify_music: a new
editor_*.js changes what every reader of the Pad's whole source reads, and
those suites (verify_music, verify_surfaces) belong among the affected ones.

## After v330 -- Main red after #717: the gallery's search read before it answered

Main's full run after #717 went red in one job, sqlite shard 4, where
verify_captions stopped with KeyError 'long': the card with the long caption
was not on the gallery when its glide was read. postgres' shard 4, the same
suites on the same tree, was green.

The suite opens the gallery, types its word in the search box and waits for
its four cards, then reads them. Typing waits 350ms for more words before
the search goes (gallery.js), and on a server whose only public posts are
the suite's four, the listing from BEFORE the search already showed exactly
those four: the wait passed on it, the search then cleared the list to load
its answer, and the read 700ms later fell in the gap. It had never had a
server like that: #715 gave verify_letters its weight, which moved the suites
between the shards, and this one now runs before any suite that posts to
the gallery.

Reproduced here as it would happen: a fresh server, the suite's four the only
public posts, the search's answer held back 900ms (slowq, scratch): the
glide rows stop with KeyError 'long', as on CI. Fixed by searching as a
person presses Search (Enter), which clears the list at once, so the wait can
only see the search's answer; under the same conditions the rows pass, 10 of
10, and the whole suite 76 of 76. The suite's second search (the long words'
card) waited the same way and searches the same way now. verify_hot's
searches wait for the request itself and are untouched.

## After v330 -- Text: words that write themselves, on the Pad and Flip

The second of the two pull requests (FUTURE.md 6ab). The owner said yes to the
Text mock (Text in Shape's picker; S, M, L in the pen's colour and thickness;
the words moved while a preview, then ink with honest timing; Undo whole; the
Eraser rubs it; Mirror leaves it alone; our own font; a Speed slider), then to
the Your hand mock's style row and its one door, and said "Next".

WHAT A PERSON MEETS. Text is Shape's fifth kind, on both editors. Picking it
puts the picker away (it has no knobs); a press on the canvas says where the
words go, and the typing sheet rises. Nothing is ink and no take is armed
until Write it. The sheet: the words (16px), Style (four cards, each written
in itself: Yours, or + Make yours with no hand yet; Skribl; Print; Script),
under it "Your hand, N of 92 letters" and Edit your hand, or "Make your own
hand in about 10 minutes."; Size, Small, Medium or Large (the one pill; the
letters' cap height as a share of the drawing's shorter side, 4.5, 6.5 and
9.5%, chosen so "Happy birthday, Jo!" fits one line on a phone at Medium; in
words, not the mock's S, M, L, because verify_a11y holds every option to a
word: the outside review's rule that renamed the grid's S / M / L, which a
person could take for a line's width or the canvas's size); Speed, the app's slider
with - and +, nine stops from 1/4x to 4x, 1x in the middle, beside it how long
the words take ("1x · 6 s"), and under the word Speed what 1x means for the
style chosen; Write it. The words show where the press was, in a dashed box
with Drag to move, never under the sheet; a drag moves them, a press elsewhere
on the canvas moves them there. Write it: the sheet sinks, the box goes in the
same frame, and the words write themselves on the canvas, a stroke at a time.

INK, NOT TYPE. Each letter becomes ordinary stroke points through the step the
pen and Shape use, so the replay, a posted link and every export write the
words out with code they already had; the player never learns text exists,
and a viewer never needs the font. Written in real time on the editor's own
clock: each point's t is the clock when the words began plus the time the
plan gave it, forward only, so the take records what the person watched.
Anything done while they write (a press anywhere, a key) finishes them first,
each stroke keeping the time it was due, and the Pad's clock is moved on by
what was left, so the next line comes after them. One history state (Pad) or
one 'fill' entry, the one a stamp leaves (Flip), so one Undo takes the line
back and Redo puts it back. commitStrokeWithMirrors takes `plain` for Text;
Flip's hooks push the points themselves, so neither mirrors words.

THE STYLES (skribl/static/fonts, harness/tools/make_textfonts.py). Print and
Script are EMS Readability and EMS Allure, single-line fonts made for pen
plotters (from Source Sans Pro Light and Allura), under the SIL Open Font
License, which travels with them (fonts/OFL.txt); 160 characters each:
letters, numbers, punctuation, the Latin accents; no emoji. Their baselines
and cap heights are read from the letters (a single-line font is the middle
of a drawn outline, so its baseline sits half a stroke up), timed as a steady
hand that eases in and out of each line. Skribl is the owner's 92 as posted
(Oct 31), each point at the time it was drawn; Yours is the person's, read
from Your hand's store each time. A hand's letter keeps its pace, a pause
inside it held to a quarter second (as Your hand's own line holds it), and
spaced by its ink as Your hand spaces it; a second try ("e2") takes every
other turn; an accent it drew sits over its own letter (raised over a
capital); a letter it has not drawn comes in Print. 16.5, 24.1 and 58.6 KB,
4.6, 6.6 and 13.3 KB gzipped, fetched the first time the sheet opens.

THE DOOR. Make yours and Edit your hand go to Your hand with `back=pad` or
`back=flip`; Close, Done, Finish later and Ready's new Write with it (it was
Done) come back to that editor with `text=1`, and Text is chosen there with
"Tap where your words go"; the address loses the flag. Opened any other way,
Your hand leaves to the Pad as before.

ONE MODULE. lib/textwrite.js is the tool (the sheet, the lettering, layout,
timing, the preview and its drag, writing in time); editor_text.js and a
block in flip.js hand it the canvas, the pen, the clock and Undo. The sheet
is one partial (_skribl_text.html) and one block of styles.css; the Saved
pill steps aside while it is up (lib/opensurfaces.js). Its rise and sink are
Web Animations, Reduce Motion asked there, so player.css is unchanged. On a
desk a T rides by the pointer, as each shape's badge does.

HELP. How it works has a Text tip (on Flip: the page shows the words as it
plays, and a page set to Draw on writes them again); Shape's tip names it;
Shape's card says "Straight lines, rectangles, ovals, polygons, and words
that write themselves." verify_helpclaims claims the tip with verify_text's
checks.

verify_text (73 rows, 14 parts) holds it: the lettering (each style's
characters, baseline and cap height read from the files, the owner's 92 with
their times running forward, the license, all three served); the picker on
both editors; a press opens the sheet and draws nothing, arms no take, and
Close and Escape leave nothing; the words placed before ink (above the sheet,
in the pen's colour, moved by a drag exactly, never under the sheet, moved by
a second press without the sheet moving, following a colour chosen while it
is up); written in time (stroke by stroke over the plan, every point at its
planned time on the take's clock, where the preview showed it, the take
armed by Write it); one Undo and Redo on both editors; Mirror; finished
early (every stroke at its due time, the clock moved on, the next line after
the words); Speed (the label, 2x and 1/4x, the - and + and their ends);
styles and hands (Make yours a way there and not a choice, Skribl chosen with
no hand and Yours with one, each style in itself and in its own lettering, a
hand's pace with its pause held, Print for a letter not drawn); the door, both
ways, from both editors and from Ready; Flip's page (the page placed on, one
entry, the times kept, a Draw on page writing them); the sheet's words, 4.5:1
and up from its computed colours, light and dark, phone and desk (the lowest
5.3:1, Write it), every button 44px, the field 16px, the words above the
sheet; the rise read on every frame, Reduce Motion, and the dashed box gone
the frame the words start.

THE OTHER SUITES met four things, each the new sheet against an older rule:
verify_a11y the S, M, L above; verify_helpclaims the field's own name, "Your
words", which How it works now says ("tap where your words go");
verify_tray, which listed the picker's four kinds by hand; and
verify_contrast, whose reader met the Pad locked on the take its Post row had
just made, which refuses a tap as it refuses the pen (it presses Keep
drawing first now, as a person would; it reads the typing sheet on both
editors from its pixels).

CALIBRATION, each part alone, the file served changed (harness serve-run,
scratch): 49 breaks, every one red at its own row; part 1 against six changed
copies of the lettering (a letter gone from Print, Print's baseline raised,
Script's capitals cut short, a letter gone from Skribl, a time running
backwards, the license without Allure). Seven did not go red the first time,
and each was the instrument, not the tool: a missing Text button, a plan with
no ink and a way back that never chose Text stopped the suite on a wait
instead of failing a row (five breaks; they fail their rows now); the check
that the next line comes after words finished early drew that line with Text
still chosen, which opens the sheet rather than drawing; and one break called
the hook that starts the words without laying a stroke. All seven red since.
The sheet's contrast reader first read the chosen card's see-through tint as
if it were solid (2.6:1); it lays each see-through ground over the one under
it now. verify_contrast reads the typing sheet on both editors from its
pixels as well, as it reads every sheet.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared. One module, the same picker and sheet, one hand,
one door; the words go on the page they were placed on.

THE FOUR: powerful (words join the performance, in your own hand, at your own
speed); playful (the replay writing your words is a small delight, and so is
watching them write the first time); simple (one more kind in a picker you
know, one sheet, one button); kind (nothing is ink until Write it, they can
be moved until then, Undo takes them back whole, and a letter not drawn yet
still has a place, in Print).

Not tested here: WebKit (the owner's iPhone, its keyboard over the sheet),
SF and Segoe UI, the live site (not deployed until it merges).

## After v330 -- Holding selects nothing: the cards mark what they name

The owner, on the iPhone, with a screenshot: holding Tune's Watching speed
row opened its card, and the row's word "speed" was selected under it, with
Copy and Look Up. "The icons didn't, but the rows do."

Why: a card opens on a hold, and on a phone a hold on words also selects
them. The bar's buttons were kept from that by a list of ids written by hand
into styles.css (no selection, no system callout, no magnifier). Every card
that came after it was left out: Tune's rows on both editors, the draw
drawer's Eyedropper, Recolor and four tiles, and Flip's pages and x1 badge.
On the tree as it stood, 11 of the 33 things a card names on the Pad could
be selected, and 18 of 41 on Flip.

The fix: lib/learncard.js marks everything its cards name (data-lc-hold),
and the tag-only things whose hold keeps an old job, from the cards' own
list: once the page is whole, and as anything is added (a Flip page), so it
is marked before its first touch. styles.css's one [data-lc-hold] rule takes
selection, the system callout and the magnifier from what is marked. The
list of ids is gone; every id on it was already named by a card. The first
version wrote the rule from the script into a <style>, which verify_surfaces
bans (CSS in a string is CSS no audit reads, and copies of it drift); CI's
smoke job said so, and the rule went back into the stylesheet.

verify_learncard part 13 holds it on both editors: everything a card names
is marked and computes user-select none, a Flip page added since the start
among them, and the rule for what is marked carries -webkit-touch-callout:
none, which Chromium does not compute, so it is read from the stylesheet.
Chromium's own long press selects nothing here, so the owner's scenario
cannot be run; the check reads what WebKit obeys. Red on the tree before the
fix (both editors), and per part: nothing marked (17 of 33 on the Pad, the
bar's buttons with it now that the old list is gone), nothing marked as it
is added (the Pad's and Flip's late arrivals), the stylesheet's rule gone,
a list that leaves Tune's rows out, and the rule without the callout (that
row alone). player.css is unchanged.

Not tested here: WebKit itself (the owner's iPhone): one held row there says
whether it holds.

## After v330 -- Text on the phone: the sheet comes straight up, and sits on the keyboard

The owner tried Text on the iPhone the morning it went live. Picking Text
"just closes the menu": the picker stepped aside and waited for a tap on the
drawing, and nothing said so. The drawing was a finished take (Play and Post
showing), which refuses a press until Keep drawing, so the tap that was the
next step would have been refused too. After Keep drawing and a tap, the
sheet came up with the keyboard, and the bar over the keyboard covered the
field: the words could not be seen as they were typed. And the keyboard's
blue done key wrote the words at once (Enter was Write it), before they were
placed. The owner asked "How can I select and move text though?", and said
"Yes" to four calls:

1. CHOOSING TEXT OPENS THE SHEET (A), the words in the middle of the drawing
   that can be seen (lib/textwrite.js start), on both editors. A press with
   Text chosen opens the sheet there, or moves the words already in it. On
   the Pad that press now comes before the lock, as the eyedropper and
   Recolor do (it lays no ink); Write it carries a finished take on, as Keep
   drawing does (editor_text.js begin).
2. WHILE THE WORDS ARE TYPED ON A PHONE the sheet sits on the keyboard (the
   Post sheet's own way: iOS does not shrink the page for its keyboard, so
   the sheet is lifted to the bottom of the visual viewport) and is only the
   words and Write it (.typing), so the drawing shows above it with the words
   on it. Style, Size and Speed come back when the keyboard goes.
3. THE KEYBOARD'S DONE KEY PUTS IT AWAY. Writing is the Write it button; on
   a desk, with no keyboard to put away, Enter is still Write it.
4. A press on the drawing while the sheet is up moves the words there (it
   already did; it can be found now).

How to move written words was answered in words, as decided in the Text
mock: before Write it, drag the box or tap where they go; after, they are
ink: on Flip, Select moves them like any drawing; on the Pad, Undo takes the
line back whole to place again (the Pad has no Select, since moving recorded
ink makes the replay draw it in its new place at its old time).

Two things the first build got wrong, found by the suite: the typing view
came on whenever the field had focus, so with no keyboard up the x and the
Speed row were taken away; it comes on only with a keyboard up now. And words
were kept above the sheet where it was painted mid-rise, lower than where it
rests, so on a phone they could end under it; they are kept above where it
rests (its layout box, as lib/sheetswipe.js measures a sheet). Write it and
the x keep the field's focus until their click, so a sheet growing back as
the keyboard goes cannot move the x from under the press.

verify_text holds it: the sheet straight up from the picker on both editors,
the words in the drawing that shows (part 2); a press opens it again where
the press was (3); a finished take (15): the sheet opens, a press moves the
words with no refusal, Write it carries the take on, one Undo takes back only
the words; the keyboard (16), as iOS reports it (a visual viewport 336px
shorter than the page, which is all Chromium can be given): with no keyboard
the whole sheet shows while typing; with one, the sheet sits on it and is
only the words and Write it, the words above it; the done key puts it away
and writes nothing, the rest coming back; the x and Write it pressed with the
keyboard up do what they say; on a desk Enter writes.

CALIBRATION, each part alone, the file served changed: thirteen breaks, each
red at its own row: either picker not opening the sheet, the press opening it
in the middle instead of where it was, the lock first on a finished take,
Write it not carrying the take on, the sheet not lifted, the typing view in
the script or in the stylesheet gone, the typing view on focus alone, words
kept above the painted sheet, the field's focus let go on a press, the done
key writing, and a desk's Enter not writing. Four did not go red the first
time, each the instrument: a press in the drawing's middle could not tell
"where the press was" from "the middle"; a wait stopped the desk's row before
it could fail; nothing read the whole sheet with no keyboard; and the press
read with the keyboard up was Write it, at the sheet's foot, which does not
move when the sheet grows: the x, at its top, does.

BACK FROM YOUR HAND, IT IS YOURS. The same morning the owner asked "Where is
edit": the Text sheet in the Home Screen app showed + Make yours, though
they had made their hand in Safari. On the iPhone a Home Screen web app
keeps its own storage, apart from Safari's, so a hand made in one is not in

their letters, and Open a copy took it in. Then "I saved it, loaded it,
changed it, said done. It's still unchanged", most likely because Skribl,
the built-in lettering, was still the chosen style: it was made from the

never changes it. Their next picture had Yours chosen, the words written in

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared; Flip has no lock, and its picker opens the
sheet the same way.

THE FOUR: simple (one tap to start writing, nothing to discover); kind (the

Not tested here: the iPhone's own keyboard (WebKit), which is the point of

## After v330 -- Changing a letter: as ink, an eraser that cuts the line, and the font under it

The owner wanted to change a couple of Skribl's letters, which are their own
first 92. "Is there a way to have the original letters underlay?", then "Not
the drawings, but the letters that were under when I did it first time" (the
font under each box: system-ui at 300, on their iPhone SF; their posted set
came from a 3x screen), then "Maybe a button to put guide under it", "Also
maybe eraser? I have a couple that just need a tiny bit erased. I like all
your ideas if when I click redo it erased old letter but leaves underneath",
"Also a way to adjust eraser size", and "All yes" to the four calls of the
change-a-letter mock.

- A LETTER TAPPED ON THE TILES COMES UP AS INK, to change ("s · change it",
  the tile "Change s"): rubbed out with Eraser, added to with the pen, or
  Redo. It had been a faint picture to draw a new letter over, and a bit
  rubbed out needs the letter itself. Cancel keeps it as it was; Done keeps
  it as it stands, and with nothing changed writes nothing.
- THE ERASER WORKS ON THE LETTER'S POINTS, NOT ITS PIXELS. The ink inside
  its circle goes, a line it cuts carries on as lines, every point left keeps
  the time it was drawn at, and a crumb a cut would leave is let go, so what
  is left is a letter like any other, clean wherever Text writes it. The
  canvas is painted again from the points as it rubs, so what is seen is what
  Done keeps, and a line is cut where its ink (half its width past its middle)
  meets the circle, so nothing painted is left inside the ring. The ring is
  the real size, at the press, and over a desk's letter before one; the accent
  on a halo of the paper's lightness (3.9:1 light, 4.4:1 dark, measured in the
  mock). The Pad's own eraser cursor (white with a dark halo, app.js) would
  read about 2:1 on this light paper; this one is the mock's. A second finger
  is the pinch (lib/canvaszoom.js, on touch events): what the first finger
  rubbed out comes back, as a pinch unwinds a stroke.
- ITS SIZE, 6 to 48 px across at the drawing's fit and 22 to start, is a
  slider in the line's place while Eraser is on, so the bottom panel keeps
  its height (118 px either way) and nothing moves; kept on this device
  (skribl.letters.prefs, apart from the hand, so a copy never carries it);
  [ and ] on a desk, as they size the Pad's pen. At fit, because the Pad's
  eraser is sized in the drawing too: a pinch makes the ring grow with the
  letter, and the slider is how a bit gets smaller.
- GUIDE puts the font that was under the letter the first time back under
  it, gliding in over a fifth of a second, off to start and kept as left. An
  accent keeps its own base letter faint under it, Guide or not: that is
  where the accent goes, not the font.
- REDO clears the letter and leaves the guide, with the pen back (the
  owner's condition); its toast's Undo brings the letter back as it stood.
- Eraser and Guide take Finish later's place, which is empty while a letter
  is changed, on its card at its size; on is the app's on (the chosen tint,
  its ink, the 1px ring in --ui-hi).
- FITTED TO THIS SCREEN. A letter is put back fitted to the box this screen
  measures (its cap height, its baseline, its box's middle), in order and
  changed alike; the box it was drawn in gives it back as it was. The mock
  found the owner's hand, opened from the copy made for their phone, coming
  back as ink small in a corner: the faint picture had always been scaled,
  which hid it. Done with nothing changed keeps such a letter exactly as it
  came.

verify_letters 14 holds it (26 rows); 12 now taps a letter to change it (a
stroke added is kept with it; Redo and a stroke draw it again); 9 reads the
new words on and off (Eraser, Guide, the size and its value, the tint laid
over the bar it sits on) and their 44 px.

CALIBRATION, the file served changed, each part alone: 30 breaks, each red
at its own row: the letter not put back as ink (twice: the change part and
the tiles), the tools hidden, the font never under it, a jump instead of a
glide, a glide of 40 ms, Guide not kept, the line left beside the size, the
cut at the middle of the line instead of its ink, no repaint, the cut ends'
times lost, a ring twice the size, no unwinding at a pinch, the size not
kept, Redo bringing the old letter back, its Undo bringing nothing, the pen
not back after Redo, the eraser staying on from letter to letter, Cancel
writing, Done ignoring a change, Done writing an unchanged letter, no ring
before a press, no [ ], no fitting, the tools while drawing in order, an
accent's base letter only with Guide, the tile still saying "Draw g again",
Redo in the tiles keeping the old letter, the on ink of the old #b9a8ff,
buttons 36 px. Two did not go red the first time, each the instrument: the
settings were read by a parse that threw before the row could say red, and
the glide was read by counting frames, which four runs at once slowed into
false jumps. Read next by the time each step took, it was red once beside
three other suites and green alone (a frame read 10.1 ms after the last saw
a step of 0.153 against a bound of 0.151: the reader's clock is a callback's
jitter from the glide's own frame time). It is read now as a span: off to on
takes at least 120 ms, with something in between, which slow frames can only
lengthen. A jump and a 40 ms glide are each red at it; two controls with
nothing changed, run four at once, have no red row.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared. Your hand is one page; Flip's Text opens it.

THE FOUR: simple (tap a letter and it is there; what is seen is what is
kept); kind (Cancel and Undo; a tiny fix no longer means drawing the whole
letter again); powerful (a real eraser that cuts the line, sized exactly,
and the font when it helps); playful as before.

Not tested here: WebKit, so the iPhone's touch and its SF under the letter;
the owner's phone will say.

  with the y left unflipped (2.0 cap heights) and with the box's middle for

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared. Both editors write with the one lettering file.

## After v330 -- Main red after #723: a loop started again late ticked its first beat twice

Issue #724: main's full run on 0999b43 (#723, Skribl's letters, which
touched no music) was red in sqlite 6/6, one row of verify_musicclick, the
Pad: "the loop started again late, just after it came round (the page held
busy across it): its first beat still ticks once, as the old loop came
round", started again 43.2 ms after the old loop came round. Green alone
here, and in postgres 6/6 on the same tree.

MEASURED AT THE CPU 4x SLOWER first, as the entry after #692 asks of this
suite: the row red two runs in three, both the same: the first beat ticked
twice, as the old loop came round and again as the new loop's sound began,
0.10 to 0.11 s apart (the start 72 to 81 ms late). A DEFECT, NOT THE
INSTRUMENT: lib/musicdrawer.js kept a start's first beat from ticking twice
only by setting no beat within a tenth of a second of the last, which covers
a start up to about 70 ms late (the sound begins LEAD, 30 ms, after the
start). A slower box, or a page held longer, is heard as a stutter at the
loop's top.

- THE FIX: a start's first beat is not set when the last tick is closer than
  0.6 of a beat (0.3 s at the suite's 120): that tick was the old loop's top,
  ticked as it came round, and it was this beat. Every other beat keeps the
  tenth; a start before the loop came round still ticks its first beat as
  the music starts (the old top called off, the last tick a whole beat back).
- THE ROW: verify_musicclick's restart takes how long the page is held past
  the old loop coming round: 40 ms as before, and a new 160 ms, a start a
  fifth of a second late, red on the old drawer every time on both editors
  (the first beat at -189 ms and 0, 0.19 s apart), green on the new; the
  join counted from just before the old loop came round to just after the
  new sound began, so a second tick is counted however late the start.
  Twice green alone; at the CPU 4x, three runs, the restart rows green in
  all three.
- ALSO SEEN AT THE CPU 4x, once in three: the row the entry after #692
  watches ("the click turned on ... ticks from the very next beat"), Flip,
  its first tick 11.61 ms after the beat. Not this change; still watched,
  not touched, since CI has not shown it again.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared (lib/musicdrawer.js runs both editors' click).

## After v330 -- Main red after #733: the click read the clock twice

Issue #735: main's full run on 1f0565d (#733, Flip's music drawer saying
"flip", words only) was red in postgres 6/6, one row of verify_musicclick,
the Pad: "a page held for 300ms from just before a beat drops no tick",
with no tick on its beat, five in all, the gaps after the first 0.5116,
0.5 and 0.5. Green on the next run (#734), and the issue closed itself.

MEASURED AT THE CPU 4x SLOWER first, as this suite asks: the held row green
four runs in four on each editor, so not the hold and not the load alone.

THE NUMBERS SAID WHERE. The suite records the time the page asks a tick to
start at, and 11.61ms is one block of the audio clock (512 frames at
44.1kHz). Every tick after the first two sat on the true grid, so the grid
itself had moved: lib/musicdrawer.js beats() found the loop's top as the
audio clock less how far into the loop it was, and the loop's elapsed()
reads the clock again. A busy box can move the clock on a block between the
two reads; in the first call that sets the sound's start, the top came out a
block early, and with it the music's first tick, the next beat, and the
click's own record of the sound's start, which the row measures from. The
row then found nothing on its beat. The Flip blip the entry after #723 saw
at the CPU 4x (a first tick 11.61ms off) was this too. A DEFECT, small to the
ear (a tick a block early, once, at the start), and a flaky row with it.

- THE FIX: the clock read once. beats() reads the clock, asks elapsed(), and
  reads again until the clock stood still across it (at most three tries),
  so both are the same moment. In the drawer alone: lib/audioloop.js ships
  to the player, whose script is 3 bytes under its ratchet.
- THE ROW: verify_musicclick's new raced part moves the audio clock on one
  block, for good, at the moment the scheduler first asks elapsed() (found
  by the stack). The music's first tick at the sound's start and every tick
  after on its beat, by the loop's own top. Red without the fix on both
  editors, twice, the Pad's numbers main's (the first tick and the click's
  record 11.61ms early, the next beat 11.61ms off, the rest on time); green
  with it, three runs. Its own first try read the clock and elapsed() apart
  to find the top, and met the race it is about (half a block on the Pad);
  it reads them together now.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared (lib/musicdrawer.js runs both editors' click).

## After v330 -- While Skribl listens: the song shimmers, the dots dance, the beat it hears is kept

The owner, of a song whose beat the Pad found and Flip did not: "I've
loaded this beat many times. It finds a beat, just not in flip"; then
"Should we show a 'listening to sample' msg while skribl listens?", "a
little louder", "Maybe a pulsating wave and an ear icon?", Lucide's ear
pasted, "the wave needs to move and be separated", "Can't quite make it
out? Ideas?", and "Yes and yes" to C.

- THE BUG, both editors (one drawer): a beat Skribl heard was dropped when
  the loop had moved before it answered (heardIt set a beat only through
  Skribl's pick), so the magnet stayed grey and Beat said "Tap it"; and a
  song a draft brought back with no beat was never listened to again (sync
  listened again only to a song whose beat was heard). Now the beat heard
  is set beside the loop as it was put, quietly (not a step), and a song
  back with no beat is listened to again, its loop kept. A beat tapped is
  never listened over. verify_musicears' old KIND row, "no beat is set",
  reverses.
- LISTENING, SEEN (the owner's C): while Skribl listens a soft light sweeps
  the song on the timeline, the Beat tile's own four dots dance like a
  music meter (lines a hair long, round ends, the stroke not scaled, so a
  dot stretches into a bar and back), the magnet breathes, the tile says
  "Listening…" in the accent's ink and the line under the timeline
  "listening for the beat" ("listening…" under 350px). One clock; each
  fades in and out still moving, the magnet gliding to its new look;
  under Reduce Motion only the words. The browser's own animation
  (Element.animate): a first try with CSS keyframes went 305 bytes over
  the player stylesheet's budget, since keyframes and Reduce Motion rules
  always ship; player.css is unchanged.
- HOW IT GOT THERE: dots counting a bar (smooth in CSS, then stepped once
  the script kept the time, and the owner saw the difference); an ear with
  pulsing waves, then Lucide's ear (scaled 0.8 to the doors, as Fill and
  Stamps are on Flip); waves gliding in, apart. At 24px none of it could
  be made out, so the signal moved to things already big or already known:
  the song itself, and the Beat tile's own dots.
- HOW LONG SKRIBL LISTENS, measured: 0.4s for 30 seconds of song at full
  speed, 0.7s for a minute, about 1s for two; at a mid-range phone's pace
  (the CPU 4x slower) 3.7s for 30 seconds and 7s for a minute, 8 to 16s
  counting the song's opening.
- THE LINE KEEPS ITS HEIGHT: under 600px what the loop is against the
  drawing takes its own row (it did under 460px); the listening words
  wrapped the one row on a 460 to 544px screen, and the beat unwrapped it.
- THE ROWS, verify_musicears: KIND (the heard beat set; Undo brings back
  that loop and that beat), BACK (a song back with no beat heard again; a
  tapped one never), LISTENING (read on every frame from before the song
  until after the beat: the bars set off as dots, nothing hops, the light
  goes back to its start only out of sight, the end fades still moving,
  nothing runs after; Reduce Motion shows nothing that would move). Each
  calibrated by breaking its own piece alone on the Pad: the word's ink,
  the light on a clock of its own, the bars setting off already moving,
  the light going back in sight, everything stopped at once, the magnet
  snapping, motion under Reduce Motion, the heard beat dropped, a song
  back never heard again. How it works' Skribl's pick says it.
- Not tested here: Safari (no WebKit in this box).

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared (one drawer, the same on both).

THE FOUR: kind (you can see Skribl working, your loop is never moved, and
what it heard is never lost); playful (the song shimmers, the dots dance);
simple (no new buttons, the words say what Skribl is doing); powerful (the
magnet and the metronome ready the moment the beat is heard).

## After v330 -- The PRE-331 review: the first four fixes

The owner, of the outside review in FUTURE 6ad: "Get started cleaning up
those issues." Four of its fifteen, each confirmed in the code first and
each row shown red with its own fix undone. None changes what a person sees
when a save is fine.

- 1, A POINT'S TIME IS A NUMBER. `_validate_points` range-checked `t` only
  when it already was one, so "not-a-time", [], {} and true were stored,
  and a replay subtracting neighbouring times got NaN. Now a `t` that is
  there is a finite number in range; absent or null (what JSON.stringify
  writes for NaN) still posts. Rows in verify_apiedges. verify_mediameta's
  row of an object where a time goes expected the per-point size budget's
  words, and is refused first as a time now (still 400); it reads the
  time's words. The smoke job caught it on the first push: I had not
  named that suite among the affected ones.
- 11, A THUMBNAIL IS WHOLE. The draft check decoded the first 48 bytes, so
  the reviewer's PNG cut off at 26 was stored. Now the picture is decoded
  whole and ends as its kind ends: a PNG its IEND after an IHDR first, a
  JPEG its end-of-image marker, a WebP the length its RIFF header states.
  Rows in verify_clouddrafts (a PNG cut at 26 bytes, a PNG less its last
  byte, a JPEG with no end, a short WebP; a whole PNG saves). Each row
  deletes what a broken build saves, so the next row meets its own cause:
  the first calibration filled the cap of three and every later row read
  the cap.
- 10, THE BYTE BUDGET COUNTS THE PICTURE. A draft's thumbnail (up to
  200,000 characters) sat outside the budget it is stored under. Row in
  verify_hostseams: a 47 KB drawing with a 21 KB picture under 64 KB is
  refused, the same drawing alone saves.
- 2, ONE SAVE AT A TIME PER AUTHOR. A save read the author's count and
  bytes, then inserted, with nothing holding the two together; on
  PostgreSQL saves at once could each see room for one more. save_draft
  now takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed on the author after
  validating, as the post limiter does on the poster; on SQLite the one
  writer already serialises, so it returns at once. verify_postgres's new
  DRAFTS section signs the demo identity in (CSRF on) on a four-worker host
  and sends twelve saves at once. Without the lock the 64 KB budget that
  one 40 KB drawing fits stored two to four (red in five of six runs);
  with it 28/28, four runs. The cap row held at two even without the
  lock, so it was shown red by taking the count check out (five stored).
  The cluster ran here only for this, and was stopped before the other
  suites (a seal runs without it).

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared (one server path for both editors' drafts and
posts).

THE FOUR: kind (a save that fits is never refused, and the refusals say
why); simple (no new words on screen); powerful (what is stored replays
and counts as it should); playful (unchanged).

## After v330 -- The PRE-331 review: the second five

Four more findings from FUTURE 6ad and the review's high performance note,
each confirmed in the code first and each piece shown red on its own. A
person saving, posting or taking a drawing down sees nothing new unless
they are over the hourly budget, and then the words they already know.

- 7, TAKE-DOWNS AND VISIBILITY CHANGES SPEND THE ATTEMPTS BUDGET, after
  CSRF, as every other write does. Each is a lookup and a key check, and
  nothing bounded how many one connection could ask for. The budget is
  200 an hour by default and the clients send one per tap; a refusal
  shows each button's own words ("Could not delete — try again.", "Could
  not change it — try again.", "Could not take it down — try again.").
  Row in
  verify_hostseams (an id nobody has: 404, 404, 429 for each); red with
  either route's charge taken out alone.
- 4, NOTHING IS INFLATED FOR A REQUEST ITS ROUTE WILL REFUSE UNREAD. A
  client over its attempts made the server decompress, up to the request
  limit, before the 429. Every route that takes a body refuses a forged
  request, then one over budget, before it reads a byte, so the inflate
  hook now asks the same two questions first, charging nothing: a forged
  body is left compressed for its route's 403, and one over budget is
  answered 429 in the composer's words (only its post is sent gzipped).
  The budget is read by ratelimit._rate_over, a peek on either backend
  that refuses at the cap as the charge does. Rows tell the outcomes apart
  by a body inflating refuses, so a 429 or 403 where the inflate would
  have said 400: verify_delivery (memory), verify_review (the shared
  store, its own server), verify_hostseams (forged). Calibrated piece by
  piece: no peek turned both stores' rows red, no CSRF skip the forged
  row, the db branch alone its row, the memory branch alone its row.
- 13, GZIP BY ITS QUALITY. "gzip;q=0" refuses gzip and was sent it,
  because the word alone was read. Werkzeug's parse decides now, so a
  wildcard counts both ways ("*" is gzipped, "*;q=0" is not), and a
  quality that does not parse is no quality. Row in verify_delivery, a
  page and a busted asset; red with the word check.
- THE IDS STRING AND THE CURSORS ARE BOUNDED BEFORE THE WORK (the
  review's high performance note). /api/skribls/meta split its whole ids
  string, then kept fifty; it now reads fifty of the longest ids there
  can be (64 characters, a comma and a space each) and no further. A
  cursor over 120 characters is refused before it is base64-decoded (the
  longest this server writes is about 70). Rows in verify_apiedges, each
  shown by what reading past the bound would have done: a real id after
  the first 3,300 characters is not read; a cursor padded with zeros,
  which decodes to a usable one, is a 400 on New and on Hot while its
  unpadded twin pages. Each bound removed alone turned only its part red.
- 12, THE WORKER KEEPS WHAT THE SERVER VOUCHED FOR. sw.js kept any ?v=
  cache-first, while the server marks a static file immutable only for
  its real current hash, so a version nobody wrote pinned whatever it was
  answered with. Now a file is kept only when its answer says immutable;
  anything else is handed over as the network gave it. Row in
  verify_offline: app.js asked for by a made-up version is answered and
  not kept, beside its real version, which is. Red with the old rule. A
  proxy that strips Cache-Control would make files go unkept, which is
  the safe way to fail: not offline, never stale.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared (one server and one worker for both editors).

THE FOUR: kind (nobody is refused who was not before, and the refusals
are in the words people know); simple (nothing new on screen); powerful
(a flood costs the server less, and a phone keeps only true files);
playful (unchanged).

## After v330 -- The PRE-331 review: what a host's policy says, and a read-only database

Three more from FUTURE 6ad, each confirmed in the code first (15 reproduced:
a post read on a read-only SQLite answered 500 while the listing served),
each piece shown red on its own.

- 3, THE LISTING OBEYS THE POLICY. The feed filters by the visibility
  column and the host's feed_filter, in SQL; a host that installed a
  visibility policy and no matching filter listed the titles, captions,
  authors and ids of posts the policy refuses (the payload never). Under a
  policy each row is now asked visible_to too, and a page that loses rows
  is filled from the rows after them, a window at a time, eight at most;
  the cursor is taken only from a row the viewer was shown, since a cursor
  names its row's time and id. Where filter and policy agree nothing is
  dropped. The log says once what to install. The first version only
  dropped rows (short pages, a cursor that could name a refused row: the
  objection verify_integration's DECLARED row raised against "a Python
  filter over a paginated query"); its rows passed, and the row that
  caught it was that one. The DECLARED row asserted the leak, so it
  guarded outstanding work; it is inverted. verify_hostseams pages New
  and Hot three at a time: exactly what an app with no policy lists, less
  the refused, in order, once, full pages, no cursor naming a refused row.
  Its first form checked only the eight newest posts and passed a listing
  that stopped early; it compares the whole list now. Calibrated: no
  safety net, no filling, Hot's fill without its id tie-break, and the
  first version each turn their own rows red.
- 8, A POLICY DOES NOT MAKE UNLISTED MEDIA PUBLIC. Under a policy the
  media cache asked only whether an anonymous viewer may read the post,
  and an unlisted post is readable by whoever holds its link, so its
  media went out `public` behind any policy, where with none it stayed
  private. It asks what the share card asks now: public, and readable by
  anyone. Row in verify_mediaauthz (with a policy that has no opinion, as
  without one: private, no-store).
- 15, A READ SURVIVES A REFUSED COUNT. Counting a play writes; a database
  that will not take the write (read only, a replica) made the post read
  a 500. The count runs in one savepoint now and a refusal costs the count
  alone; the janitor that rides a new play has its own. Said once per app
  in the log. Rows in verify_hostseams on a read-only SQLite file (the URI
  mode=ro, which holds even for root): served twice, no play counted; the
  same read on the writable file counts one.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared (one server for both editors' posts).

THE FOUR: kind (a reader gets the drawing even when the count cannot be
kept, and a host's "no" is kept everywhere); simple (nothing new on
screen); powerful (a host's policy is the one word on what shows);
playful (unchanged).

## After v330 -- Hot holds still for one scroll-through; plays stay per connection

Two of the review's findings the owner decided (FUTURE 6ad), offered with
defaults and answered "all yes" on Nov 3.

- 6, HOT HOLDS STILL FOR ONE SCROLL-THROUGH. Hot ranks by plays in the last
  seven days, and plays arrive while somebody scrolls: a post that climbed
  past the cursor between two pages was never shown in that pass. Now the
  first page notes the moment it ranked at, its cursor carries that moment
  (microseconds since 1970, as a fourth part), and every later page counts
  plays up to it only, so the whole pass is one order. A refresh is a new
  first page and a new moment; a cursor from before (three parts) still
  pages, ranked as of now. The longest cursor this server writes grows to
  about 80 characters, under the 120 the bound allows. Rows in verify_hot:
  three posts nobody has played, a page of one, then two plays on the
  oldest; the next page still lists it where it stood, a fresh first page
  puts it on top. Red with the moment ignored (it was skipped, the
  review's scenario); the old-cursor row red with three parts refused.
- 9, PLAYS STAY ONE PER CONNECTION PER POST PER DAY. A classroom on one
  network counts as one play. Kept on purpose: it cannot be inflated by
  clearing cookies or opening private windows, and it stores nothing
  about a person (the viewer is a keyed hash of the connection). Counting
  per browser would need a cookie of its own. No code changed.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared (the Gallery's Hot lists both).

THE FOUR: kind (nothing jumps or vanishes mid-scroll); simple (no new
controls, a refresh is still how new plays arrive); powerful and playful
(unchanged).

## After v330 -- The demo signs in from a page, and out with a button

The review's 5 and 14 (FUTURE 6ad), the owner's "all yes" on Nov 3 to a
small sign-in page and Sign out as a button, and the look shown first.

- THE KEY IS POSTED, NEVER IN THE ADDRESS. /demo-login?key=... put the key
  in browser history, proxy and server logs and referrers. /demo-login is
  now a page: the Home Screen icon, the skribl signature, one field ("Your
  key", type password, so the browser can remember it) and a Sign in
  button that posts it. An old bookmark with ?key= in it lands on the page
  and signs nobody in. A wrong key is a 403 with "That key didn't match.
  Try again?"; guesses still spend the attempts budget (429 with its own
  kind words). Signed in, the page says "You're signed in as Mr. B." with
  Open Skribl Pad and Sign out.
- SIGNING OUT IS A BUTTON. /demo-logout was a link, so another site could
  sign the owner out (an earlier entry above judged that "not worth a form
  and a token"; the owner chose otherwise). It is the page's button now, a
  POST: the session cookie is SameSite=Lax, so another site's form arrives
  without it and signs nobody out, and a link to /demo-logout only shows
  the page. No token is needed for either form: signing somebody in needs
  the key, and signing them out needs their cookie.
- THE PAGE SAYS A SIGN-IN EXISTS, which the old 404 for a wrong key did
  not. The key (16+ characters, the attempts budget on every try) is what
  keeps it, as it always was.
- THE PAGE: the app's own tokens (the menu's lilac paper and white card,
  the ink, the purple fill), the stored theme read before first paint as
  _skribl_theme_boot.html does, its script carrying the CSP nonce the
  app-wide policy reads (an empty one blocked it at first). The key field
  is 17px. Measured in both themes: every word 5.3:1 or better (white on
  the purple button, the app's own pair), the rest 8.3:1 and up. Not tested
  here: Safari (no WebKit), Segoe UI.
- ROWS, verify_hostseams: an old bookmark shows the page and signs nobody
  in; a wrong key is a 403 that says so; the right key, posted, signs that
  browser in and lands on an address with no key; the signed-in page has
  Sign out as a posting form; a link to /demo-logout signs nobody out, the
  button does; guesses are 403, 403, 403, then 429; the key field is 16px
  or more. Calibrated: the address signing in again, a link signing out,
  a wrong key back to 404, and a 15px field each turn their rows red.
  verify_postgres's drafts section signs in by posting the key.

AFTER IT IS LIVE: set a new SKRIBL_DEMO_LOGIN_KEY on Render, since the old
one has travelled in addresses; that also signs every browser out.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: nothing (the demo's own page, beside both editors).

THE FOUR: kind (a wrong key says try again and locks nothing; signing out
says so); simple (one field, one button); playful (Blooby's icon and the
hand-drawn signature); powerful (the browser keeps the key like any
password).

## After v330 -- A file opened over a take ends the take first

FUTURE 6z's "seen while writing a check and not looked into", taken first
on the owner's "yes, start on the bug". A file opened on the Pad while a
take was still recording (a stroke on a blank Pad arms one; the ⋯ menu's
Open stays available during a take, unlike New Skribl) came up without
its Keep drawing pill. Reproduced: opening reset the drawing but not the
take, so `recording` stayed on; the opened drawing was neither locked nor
offered Keep drawing, the record readout ran on over it, and the next
stroke would have joined the old take's clock.

- THE FIX: the editor's loadSkribl wrapper (editor_draft.js) ends a take
  in progress the way Done ends it, before the load, so the drawing that
  opens comes up as every opened drawing does: a finished take, locked,
  its pill on the canvas. Only for a document the load will take (its own
  first test), so a file it refuses leaves the take as it was. Not in
  app.js: that is the link page's script too, under its byte ratchet.
- THE ROWS, verify_padopen's "take" part on a touch phone: the take ended
  and its readout gone; locked, the pill painted (the element at its
  middle is the pill); Keep drawing carries the opened drawing on; a
  refused file leaves the take recording. Red without the fix (no pill,
  unlocked, readout on) and with the refusal test dropped (the take ended
  on a refused file). The pill's click is skipped when it is missing, so
  a break shows as its row rather than a 30-second wait.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: not for Flip (Flip has no takes).

THE FOUR: kind (an opened drawing always offers the way to carry on);
simple (no new controls); powerful and playful (unchanged).

## After v330 -- Replays lay back only what changed

FUTURE 6z item 11, "trace first", on the owner's "do what needs to be done
in the best way": long replays dropped to 15 to 20 frames a second at a
phone's pace, the cat to 30, and nobody knew why.

- TRACED. A two-hour stand-in (145,200 points in about 6,600 strokes) on a
  402 x 874 touch phone at 3x, the CPU 4x slower, the Pad's Play: 11.7
  frames a second with the profiler on, and 94% of the time was the
  browser's own work, not our script. Turning stroke layers off took it to
  35; a 2,000-point drawing was no faster than the long one (11.7); a 2x
  phone was 19.9. A cost per frame that grew with the canvas's pixels and
  not the drawing: the stroke compositor's present() cleared the whole
  visible canvas and laid the whole dry layer back on every frame, 4.5
  million pixels on a 3x phone for the few segments a frame draws.
- THE FIX, in makeStrokeCompositor (app.js, so the link page, the Pad's
  Play, Repeat, scrubs, the static paint and the exports all gain): each
  stroke op marks the box it touched (its points, half its size and 2 for
  round caps and anti-aliasing), and present() lays the layers back held
  to that box. A bake changes nothing on screen and a reseed makes the dry
  layer the screen, so neither marks.
- THE FIRST VERSION WAS WRONG BY 1 OR 2 IN 255. Copying a source rectangle
  (drawImage's nine arguments) blends a see-through stroke a hair
  differently where it lies over ink. The new row caught it, and the old
  code passed the same row, so the instrument was right: the layers are
  now drawn whole as before, under a clip to the box, which is the old
  blend exactly.
- MEASURED, the profiler off, CPU 4x, layers on: a 3x phone, the two-hour
  stand-in 13.9 -> 41.3 frames a second and a 2,000-point drawing 15.1 ->
  41.8; a 2x phone, the stand-in 25.0 -> 46.7. Most frames now land on
  the 60 Hz cadence. Left per frame: a layout read and the scrub line's
  own paint, smaller, and a next pass only if a phone shows it.
- THE ROWS, verify_beading's new section, read against an independent
  reference: the compositor's own dry and wet layers, caught as it makes
  them and composed in full the old way. A replay driven step by step
  through the replay's own loop (opaque, see-through at one size and
  pressured, eraser strokes): the screen is that composite at every third
  frame, 148 checks; after a static paint (its runs as one path and as a
  baked run) the screen is its dry layer; a frame lays back 0.1% of the
  canvas. Calibrated: the old code passes both identity rows and fails the
  copy row (125% of the canvas a frame); the nine-argument version fails
  identity (102 of 148); a line's marks dropped fails both identity rows.
- THE PLAYER'S SCRIPT grows 120 B (160,713 measured), its ratchet raised in
  both places with the reason; spent first, the box's clamps to the canvas,
  which the clip holds. Its reachable lines (verify_seam, spans of the named
  functions the link page reaches, prose included) went 1838 on the first
  try; the explanation moved above the function, out of the span, and the
  box's helper joined onto two lines, 1818; the ceiling 1810 -> 1830 with the
  reason written beside it.
- verify_padrepeat was INTERMITTENT on the side-by-side run: 24/25 beside 16
  other suites (one Repeat turn held a 57 ms frame) and 25/25 alone. Load:
  the turn's work is unchanged by this (it reseeds as before), and the
  frames between turns are cheaper.
- Not tested here: Safari (no WebKit in this box), where the canvas's
  backing differs.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared where a Flip post plays through app.js (the
link page); Flip's editor paints its own pages and is unchanged. Not
changed: the in-post player's own compositor (inlineplayer.js), whose
canvases are a feed's small tiles; the same box would serve it if a phone
shows it there.

THE FOUR: powerful (an artist's two-hour piece plays smoothly on an
ordinary phone); kind (nothing on screen changes but the smoothness);
simple and playful (unchanged).

## After v330 -- Undo on a long drawing: a floor under the history

FUTURE 6z, "measured, not built": the Pad's Undo past its three copies on a
two-hour piece painted the whole drawing again. Next on the list after the
replays, on the owner's "do what needs to be done in the best way".

- TRACED, the two-hour stand-in (145,200 points) on a 402 x 874 touch phone
  at 3x, the CPU 4x slower, the canvas 2448 x 1836: the first two Undos came
  from the copies (82 and 60 ms of work in the press); the third and every
  one after it held the page 6.1 to 6.8 s (7.0 to 7.8 s to the frame that
  showed it), and each Redo past the copies the same. After a reload every
  Undo did, the first included (7.2 s): a draft comes back with thirty
  states and no copy.
- THE IDEA. Undo reaches thirty states down (the history's cap), so one copy
  of the canvas at or under the deepest of them serves every Undo and Redo:
  lay it, paint only the strokes above it. That is the FLOOR (editor_draw.js,
  A FLOOR UNDER UNDO): the canvas as it stood when a state was pushed (a
  stroke's start, a recolour's, a line of text's), so that state exactly;
  never under the select tool or a selection, whose outline is painted on
  the canvas. Once the history is full and its deepest state starts to move
  up, a NEXT is kept above it, which becomes the floor when the deepest
  state reaches it; so a press paints under sixty strokes, never the drawing.
- A FLOOR IS A SHORTCUT, NEVER ANOTHER PICTURE. The strokes above it are
  painted as the whole repaint paints them (padPaintAbove): the repaint lays
  see-through strokes in a layer of their own only while the whole drawing
  has 24 or fewer (lib/strokelayers.js), and the few above a floor would come
  in under that by themselves, so the whole drawing's count decides. Opaque
  ink paints the same with the stroke layers or without ("byte-identical",
  app.js), and without them nothing is set up, where the layers are two more
  canvases the size of this one: about 200 ms of a 260 ms Undo with the CPU
  4x slower. So strokes with no see-through ink are painted with the layers'
  switch off for that one call. The floor itself is the canvas as it was,
  like the copies: a see-through stroke drawn this session below it comes
  back as it was drawn, as it does from a copy.
- WITH NO FLOOR UNDER IT (a recolour or a move made new points under it, the
  canvas grew, the stroke layers were switched), padUndoRepaint paints from
  the base as before, in two parts laid as the whole would be, and takes the
  floor between them at the deepest state left: only that Undo pays. A draft
  back from a reload takes its floor the same way in its first paint
  (editor_draft.js renderPrefix), where its first part would be laid as the
  whole is; so its first Undo is quick too.
- MEASURED on the final tree, the same phone and drawing (work in the
  press; the frame that shows it lands 100 to 150 ms after):

                                          before          after
    Undo 3 to 6, after six strokes        6.1 - 6.8 s     41 - 48 ms
    Redo past the copies                  6.1 - 6.6 s     40 - 96 ms
    the first Undo after a reload         7.2 s           77 ms

  And after 56 strokes, thirty Undos in a row: 30 to 104 ms each, where each
  was a whole repaint. The keeping costs a stroke's start about 4 ms; twice
  in a session, when a floor's canvas is first made, up to 89 ms (the mean
  over 56 starts, those two in it, 7.1 ms). Whether a floor still fits the
  drawing is read from one point in sixteen at a push (it only chooses what
  to keep: reading them all was 16 ms) and from every point when it is laid.
- MEMORY. One canvas more for a busy drawing (PAD_KEEP_MIN_POINTS), two once
  the history is full: 18 MB each on a phone at 3x. A light drawing keeps
  none, and a cleared one lets them go, as the copies do.
- THE ROWS, verify_undofast: a hundred strokes, thirty Undos and ten Redos
  back, every pixel as it was drawn and fewer than sixty strokes painted a
  press; past the copies, the canvas from before; a reload's first Undos
  from the floor its paint took; the canvas grown, the repaint takes a floor
  of the new size and the next Undo paints one stroke; two see-through
  drawings, past the budget and under it, each Undo the whole repaint's
  picture; one just past it, its see-through ink on both sides of the floor,
  grown and reloaded, each picture the one-paint picture; no floor under the
  select tool's outline; a light drawing keeps none, a cleared one lets its
  canvas go. CALIBRATED, each shown red against its own break: no floors
  kept (4 rows), no NEXT (3), a floor matched by length (the edit's row), a
  reload painted in one go (2), the repaint taking no floor (2) or one at the
  drawing it painted (1), floors for a light drawing (2), canvases not let go
  (1), the strokes above a floor not painted (5); and the strokes above a
  floor layered by their own count (past the budget, 3 of the 4 Undos from a
  floor differ) or never layered (under it, the same), the repaint's first
  part laid by its own count (1), a draft's paint split where its parts are
  laid differently (1), no floor guard under the select tool (1). The
  layering rows first drew with the pen and caught neither of their breaks:
  a see-through stroke of one colour and one width is one path with the
  layers or without (lib/strokelayers.js uniformRun). They draw with the
  pencil, whose width follows speed, and read that it varies.
- FOUND, NOT CHANGED: a reload repaints the drawing from its draft, whose
  points are written to 0.01 px (lib/pointwrite.js), so its edges differ from
  the canvas before the reload (722 faint pixels on the row's drawing). The
  reload's rows read Undo against the whole repaint of the drawing as it came
  back, which is what every Undo painted before.
- Not tested here: Safari (no WebKit in this box), where a canvas's memory
  has its own ceiling.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: Flip next. Its Undo keeps three copies of a busy page
(flip.js, UNDO WITHOUT PAINTING THE PAGE AGAIN); past them it repaints the
page, as the Pad did. A floor per page would serve it the same way; on the
list.

THE FOUR: powerful (an artist's two-hour piece undoes thirty steps, each in a
blink); kind (nothing on screen changes but the wait, after a reload too);
simple and playful (unchanged).

## After v330 -- Flip on a busy page: a floor under Undo, the tile from the layer, a stroke's start

The owner's "All yes" (Nov 4) to "Give Flip the same Undo fix", after the
Pad's ("Undo on a long drawing: a floor under the history").

- TRACED, a phone 402 x 874 at 3x (Flip's layers at 2x, 1062 x 1888), the
  CPU 4x slower, one busy page with six strokes drawn on it. Past its three
  copies, an Undo or a Redo painted the whole page, and from the fourth Undo
  twice: the pad, then the page's tile, which is painted through the same
  frame layer.

                    Undo 3     Undo 4 to 6     Redo past the copies
    6,000 points    171 ms     0.33 - 0.50 s   222 ms
    20,000          447 ms     1.0 - 1.2 s     450 ms
    60,000          1.8 s      3.1 - 3.9 s     1.7 s

  And reading the code for it: every pen stroke's start on a busy page
  painted the page into the layer again (liveBegin), 55 to 262 ms on 6,000
  points and 0.48 to 0.91 s on 20,000, before the stroke's first point showed.
- ONE IDEA, THREE PLACES: the frame layer, tagged with the page's ink at
  rest (_fcvTag), is not painted again.
  1. THE TILE FROM THE LAYER (_frameHolds, beside drawThumb). A tile is
     painted through the frame layer itself while the canvas has not grown
     (frameLayerFor gives a tile fctx when RS is DPR): the ink at full size,
     then laid on the tile. When the layer holds the page's ink at rest, the
     tile is laid from it, as paintFrame would lay it after painting it again.
  2. A STROKE'S START (liveBegin) lays the tagged layer rather than painting
     the page into it. Checked after the page underneath is painted, which
     goes through the layer and untags it.
  3. A FLOOR UNDER A BUSY PAGE (beside repaintPage). Flip's Undo has no cap:
     it takes a page back to empty. So the floor is the page as it stood at a
     pen stroke's start, for the page being drawn on, known by the content of
     its first points (_inkSig with n), the layering it was painted with and
     the layer's size; a NEXT 30 strokes on (FLOOR_EVERY), which becomes the
     floor once the page is 60 past the old one. An Undo or a Redo past the
     copies lays the highest that fits and paints only the strokes above it,
     by the whole page's layering (paintStatic's third argument, as the live
     cache paints a page in two halves). With none that fits, the page is
     painted in two parts and a floor taken between them, 30 strokes under it.
- MEASURED after, the same phone and pages (work in the press):

                    Undo or Redo past the copies     a stroke's start
    6,000 points    31 - 44 ms                       3 - 8 ms
    20,000          40 - 55 ms                       12 - 27 ms
    60,000          88 - 128 ms

  (A session's first one or two starts on a busy page take 84 to 108 ms on
  20,000 points: the floor's canvas is made.)
- MEMORY: two copies of the frame layer for one busy page at a time, 16 MB on
  a phone 402 pixels wide; a light page keeps none; a new size drops them.
- THE ROWS, verify_undofast's Flip part: eight strokes on a busy page, none of
  whose starts paints the page; eight Undos and eight Redos, every pixel as it
  was and as render() paints, no press painting the page, each tile as one
  painted afresh with the layer untagged; a tile, and the page from a floor,
  never laid once the page has changed under them; seventy strokes and thirty
  Undos, the NEXT taking over, none painting sixty strokes; a page opened and
  undone before it is drawn on, painted in two parts with a floor between;
  see-through pencil strokes above a floor, past the layering budget and
  under it, each Undo what render() paints. The row past the copies now reads
  a floor and only the strokes above it; the stroke-layers row reads the whole
  page painted (in two parts) where it read one paint. CALIBRATED, each
  shown red against its own break: a stroke's start painting the page (1
  row), the tile painted again (7), the tile's check of the ink dropped (1),
  no floor kept (4), no NEXT (2), no two-part repaint (3), the strokes above a
  floor layered by their own count (past the budget) or never (under it),
  1 each, and a floor matched without the content of its points (2: the point
  moved under the floors, and the stroke-layers row, the setting being part
  of that content).
- Not tested here: Safari (no WebKit in this box).

WHAT IT DOES TO THE PAD: the Pad's floor came first; this is Flip's, by
content where the Pad's is by the very points (Flip's tools move points where
they lie). The Pad has no tiles, and paints a stroke's start live.

THE FOUR: powerful (a busy page draws and undoes without a hold); kind
(nothing on screen changes but the wait); simple and playful (unchanged).
