## After v330 -- An iPad held upright starts a new drawing square, in both editors

The owner's "All yes" to A in the tablet mock (FUTURE.md 6z item 10), after
asking whether there was any reason not to (a new drawing on an upright iPad
starts square rather than tall; the Canvas picker still has Tall); then, told
Flip still started tall on a 12.9-inch Pro: "Yes, do Flip on the 12.9 too."

- WHAT WAS WRONG: a new drawing's shape is picked once, from the room it gets,
  against a 720 px column in both editors. On an iPad Air or 11-inch Pro held
  upright the square needs 11 px more than the column gives (696 of its 707),
  so the Pad started tall, 562 px wide on the Air's 820 (69% of the width).
  Flip's stage is shorter than the Pad's band, so it started square there, but
  on a 12.9-inch Pro its stage is tall enough for 9:16 to win: tall, 554 px.
- ONE RULE FOR BOTH (lib/chromefit.js startShape; each editor measures its own
  room, the Pad's band with roomOf and Flip's stage with stageAvail): the
  preset that shows largest in the column (lib/canvassizes.js bestFor), as
  always, unless a touch screen is held upright (a coarse pointer, portrait)
  and the square fits at its own size in the whole row as it reaches to the
  screen's edges; then the square.
- OUT OF APP.JS, which the link player loads and never needs it from
  (resizeCanvas returns before it on the link page): the player's script is
  367 B smaller (160,346 measured), and its ratchet follows it down in
  verify_player_isolation and verify_jsstrip. Not in lib/canvassizes.js
  either: the in-post player loads that, under its own ratchet.
- THE REACH IS READ, NOT APPLIED (lib/chromefit.js reach, which span uses
  too). The first build applied it before measuring, and a row reaching while
  still empty grows taller (on a desk, 949 px where it lays out at 700): the
  desk's own choice tipped from square to tall. The existing row "Pad's
  default canvas is the best-fitting preset" caught it.
- MEASURED, every screen: the Pad as the mock's A (iPad mini 535 to 720 px
  wide, Air 562 to 796, 11-inch Pro 570 to 810, 12.9-inch Pro 666 to 1000; the
  9.7 and 10.2-inch already square at 744 and 786); Flip on the 12.9-inch Pro
  554 to 985, every other screen as it was. Unchanged in both: a phone, a desk,
  an iPad on its side.
- KIND: nothing already drawn changes shape; a draft brings its own canvas
  back (the Pad's editor_draft.js and app.js loadSkribl; Flip starts a shape
  only when nothing was restored).

THE CHECKS: verify_padcanvas, fourteen rows. The Pad: four iPads held upright
start square and fill the width; a phone, an iPad on its side, a desk window
an iPad Air's size and a big touch screen on its side start as the column
picks; a tall drawing on an upright iPad comes back tall after a reload. Flip:
the 12.9-inch Pro held upright starts square and fills the width; a phone, an
iPad on its side and a big touch screen on its side as its column picks; a
tall Flip comes back tall. CALIBRATED, each shown red against its own break:
the rule taken out (the Pad's four iPads and Flip's 12.9-inch); no finger
asked for (the desk window); no upright asked for (the big screen on its
side); the reach applied before measuring (the desk's existing row); Flip not
asking the rule (Flip's 12.9-inch); Flip shaping a restored Flip, and the
Pad's restore keeping the start shape (each tall drawing, back 707 x 707).

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared, one rule in one module.

THE FOUR: powerful (42% more canvas width on the iPads most people hold, and
78% more for a Flip on the biggest); simple (no new control; the Canvas
picker still offers every shape); kind (nothing already drawn changes shape);
playful (unchanged).

Not tested here: a real iPad (no WebKit in this box; the screens are
emulated), and Safari's own bars, which may leave less height: then the square
does not fit and the drawing starts as it did.

## After v330 -- Skribl's ears listen in a worker

The first of the speed fixes the owner said "all yes" to (Nov 4), FUTURE.md 6z
item 12: Skribl's ears never hold the page.

- TRACED, a phone 402 x 874 at 3x, the CPU 4x slower, a two-minute stereo
  song at 44.1 kHz with a beat, timed from the moment the file reaches the
  page (the test tool's own handing over of 21 MB held a slowed page 28 s,
  so the song is made in the page first). The ears held the page three
  ways: the mix-down to one channel at once (190 to 520 ms), the last sums
  (about 370 ms), and each pick (124 to 195 ms); and their 8 ms slices took
  10 to 12.6 s in all, each waiting behind the page's own drawing, where at
  full speed they take 1.1 s.
- THE EARS LISTEN IN A WORKER (lib/musicears.js). The file is also its own
  worker's script: the page hands it copies of the song's first two minutes
  and waits on none of it, and the worker hands back what it heard, the same
  code's numbers and arrays. Where a worker cannot start (a host's policy, an
  old browser) the ears listen on the page as before. The page's policy
  already allowed it (worker-src 'self').
- A PICK KEEPS THE STRETCHES IT HEARS (H.stretches): a pick hears the beat
  again in up to thirty stretches of the song, most of its time, and the same
  stretch is heard the same every time. The worker hears the usual ones first
  (every fourth second, 24 s long), so the first pick waits on almost none.
- MEASURED after, side by side with main on the same box, three runs each:

                        main                  this
    Pad   listening     12.0 - 12.6 s         1.1 - 1.5 s
          beat shown    13.8 - 14.1 s         2.7 - 3.0 s
          a pick        124 - 159 ms          41 - 84 ms
          over 200 ms   4 holds               1 - 2
    Flip  listening     9.7 - 11.7 s          1.5 - 1.8 s
          beat shown    12.5 - 14.4 s         3.7 - 3.8 s
          a pick        113 - 195 ms          52 - 130 ms
          over 200 ms   7 - 8 holds           5 - 7

- WHAT HOLDS THE PAGE NOW is not the ears, and is named here for the next
  pass (a Chrome trace, the same song): on the Pad the song read into its
  draft (346 ms); on Flip the song kept as 28 MB of text, read in (641 ms),
  a task with no script in it (970 ms, the text or the decode handed over),
  a paint once the song lands (496 ms), and the autosave writing it (275 and
  406 ms). Flip keeps a song as a data URL where the Pad keeps a file.
- TWO SMALLER, ON THE WAY: the timeline's waveform reads a new song a channel
  and a block at a time (lib/musictimeline.js peaksOf: the same loudest of
  each block, without a division and a channel loop on every sample); and
  Flip turns its song's text back into bytes with the browser's own reader
  where it has one (Uint8Array.fromBase64: Safari 18.2, this box's Chromium),
  the same bytes in about a third of the loop's time. TRIED AND TAKEN OUT:
  fetch() of the data URL, which the Pad uses for small ones; for a song's
  28 MB it cost a slowed page more than the loop did (Flip's holds 8 to 9
  became 10 to 12).

THE CHECKS: verify_musicears, the worker part, three rows on each editor: the
page's own thread spends next to nothing in the ears' listening while a song
is added (read with the page's profiler: 0 ms of the mix-down, the steps and
the last sums); what the worker heard is what the page hears, every number and
array, and eight picks the same, a steady song's and a band's speeding up, the
worker's stretches kept and the page's heard as asked; with no worker to be
had, the beat is heard on the page all the same. CALIBRATED, each shown red
against its own break: no worker (the off-the-page row: 302 ms of the
listening on the page's thread); a stretch kept by where it starts alone (the
same-results row, by the band's picks: the steady song's stretches are all 24
s, so that break was green until the band, whose 32 beats need 27.5 s, was
added); the worker hearing part of the song (the same-results row, and no beat
heard); no listening where no worker can start (the fallback row, and the
same-results row: the page never answered). With none broken, 4 of 4. FOUND
WHILE CALIBRATING: the same-results row waited on the ears with no limit and
hung a run for its 15 minutes; it gives them 20 s now, and the fallback row
says in red that a song was never heard.

FOUND BY THE AFFECTED SUITES, AND FIXED HERE: a stretch kept by where it is
alone answered at the wrong beat. Listening can change the beat after a
stretch is heard: a slow waltz heard at its eighths is heard again at half the
beat, and its meter counted again; the kept stretches still answered at the
old beat, so the waltzes at 84 and 76 were heard in four at 168 and 152
(verify_musicthree, 48 of 49, beside others and alone). The worker and the
page agreed, each wrong the same way, so the same-results row could not see
it; the suite that holds every song to its own known beat did. A stretch is
kept by the beat it is heard against as well now: 49 of 49.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared (one ears module, one music drawer); Flip's song
reader is Flip's own.

THE FOUR: kind (adding a song never freezes the page while Skribl listens,
and the beat shows in about 3 s on a slower phone, not 14); powerful (the
same ears, the same picks); simple and playful (unchanged).

Not tested here: a real phone (no phone in this box; the CPU 4x slower stands
in for one), and Safari (no WebKit here), whose workers are not throttled the
way this box's Chromium throttles its page.

## After v330 -- A page change on a long Flip moves the strip's mark

The third of the speed fixes the owner said "all yes" to (Nov 4), FUTURE 6y's
follow-up: "Still slow on a long Flip, measured and not built: a page change."

- TRACED, a long Flip opened (60 pages of 2,400 points), six taps on its page
  strip, each timed by its parts. go() made every tile again on each page
  change (buildStrip): the 60 pictures laid from the cache and every page's
  signature read. On a desk a change took 34 to 54 ms, the strip 19 to 43 of
  it; with the CPU 4x slower 122 to 260 ms, the strip 84 to 187. On a phone
  39 to 60 ms, 22 to 28 of it the strip; slower, 170 to 375, 104 to 197. The
  rest is the new page painted on the pad.
- BUILT: a page change moves the strip's mark (turnStrip). When the strip is
  the one made for these pages, in this order, and nothing on it follows the
  page you are on (a range of pages, the paste ghost after it, a delete
  armed), the mark moves, and the page bar, the length and the tools follow;
  else the strip is made again, as before. The page you leave is laid again
  from its ink as it is now, as making the strip again did; the page you
  come to is painted at once if its picture is still to come in slices, as
  the strip painted the page you are on. The tiles stay the elements they
  were, so the strip keeps where it is scrolled to, and a page's ⋯ opened
  from another page keeps its button.
- MEASURED after, the same Flip and taps: on a desk 11 to 28 ms a change (54
  to 101 slower), on a phone 15 to 35 (88 to 181 slower); the strip's part is
  3 to 5 ms at full speed and 12 to 32 slower. No change over 50 ms is left
  at full speed on either. What is left is the new page's own paint.

THE CHECKS: verify_flipopen, the turn part. On a phone and a desk: a tap on
another page moves the mark and makes no tile again (the same elements;
buildStrip not called); the strip is then, tile for tile, picture for picture
and with its page bar, what making it again gives (read, then made again and
read the same way); with the CPU 4x slower, the change's strip part (the
change less the new page's own paint) is under half of the strip made again
alone on the same page; the page you leave is laid from its ink as it is now.
On a desk, where the strip follows the page you are on, it is made again and
is what making it gives: after a range of pages, with a page copied (the
ghost follows), with a delete armed (the arm goes), with a range anchored
from a menu or an undo (drawn to the new page), and under a strip made for
the pages in another order. FOUND WHILE CALIBRATING: the strip read the
moment it is made still has its buttons' titles (lib/tooltip.js takes them
into data-tip from a MutationObserver), so each read waits a task; and three
rows read the ghost, the arm and the range after the check that makes the
strip again, where nothing can be wrong, so they read first. CALIBRATED, each
shown red against its own break: the strip always made again (the mark, the
time and the page-left rows, both screens); the page left not laid again
(that row, both); each condition taken out alone (a range shown, a range
anchored, a delete armed, the ghost, the pages' order: each its own row);
the page to come not painted at once (the tap row: a tile not yet painted is
painted when the tap is done). With none broken, 15 of 15.

WHAT IT DOES TO THE PAD: not for the Pad, which has no pages.

THE FOUR: kind (a page change on a long Flip no longer holds the page), simple
and powerful (the strip is the same strip), playful (unchanged).

Not tested here: a real phone (no phone in this box; the CPU 4x slower stands
in for one) and Safari (no WebKit here).

measured during #648 and not built till now. (The fourth, a long Flip's first
look, is mocked first, as 6x says; see the report.)

- MEASURED on a desk (1280 x 860), a phone (402 x 874 at 3x), and the desk
  zoomed to 200%. A pen put one screen pixel in from each edge of the
  drawing's own box (inside the canvas's 2px frame) landed 2.5 units further

  percent (a twentieth of a pixel on a 10 px ring); the photo's reposition (a
  share of the box, the same half percent of a drag); and where the rings and

  the drawing's units.

canvas's edges". A pen a pixel in from each edge of the drawing's box lands a

edge; artwork dragged moves as far as the pointer went; the replay's dot over

  is written for no-preference only, and styles.css's own reduce rule stops
  every transition on the page anyway. Either guard alone holds it.

  in one frame, since the cap is far wider than a button and the width
  arrived in the first frames. `interpolate-size: allow-keywords` lets the
  width itself glide from nothing to its own size; the cap stays as the
  fallback for a browser without it. The add row was rebuilt with the strip
  on every page change, so its buttons could never glide: buildStrip keeps
  it now. On a desk the add row was a grid, which cannot glide from four
  columns to two; there it is a flex row (a phone keeps its grid). And the
  glide waits two frames after Flip opens, so a Flip that opens on many
  pages does not glide its tools in.

disabled button would not) and not focusable; a second page glides them in,
each over many frames and no frame a sixth of its way; two pages paint all

Reduce Motion: at once. A phone keeps its four add buttons. A step is read
per frame's time: beside two other suites the browser dropped a frame, and
the step over it, two frames' travel, read 49.7 px against a limit of 48.
verify_icons photographed Tween and Smear on a one-page Flip and timed out
waiting for them; it adds a page first now. CALIBRATED, each

folded (seven), no groups (both group rows), no glide (both glide rows), the

## After v330 -- Flip keeps a song as a file, as the Pad does

The owner's yes (Nov 5, "yes do the Flip song fix"): the next step FUTURE 6z
item 12 named, "Flip keeping a file, as the Pad does, is next."

- TRACED on main, a phone 402 x 874 at 3x, the CPU 4x slower, a two-minute
  stereo song at 44.1 kHz (21.9 MB; 28 MB as text). Flip kept a song only as
  text, a data URL, and adding one held the page in long stretches: the text
  made and handed over (1.1 s), an <audio> element reading the song back out
  of the text (2.3 s, with no script in it), a paint of 2.5 s, and two
  autosaves writing all 28 MB again (0.3 and 0.9 s). Over two runs the
  longest hold was 3.0 to 4.1 s and the blocking 5.7 to 12.3 s in all. Every
  save after that took 258 to 485 ms of script, a stutter after each stroke;
  a reload brought the song back at 7.6 to 7.8 s.
- BUILT: the text stays, since the backup file, a saved draft and the post
  carry it and every "is there a song" check reads it. Beside it Flip keeps
  the song's bytes: the file picked, or for a song that came as text, made
  from the text once (and made again if the text is ever changed by any other
  way). The <audio> element plays the bytes' own address, the decode reads
  the bytes off the page, and the autosave keeps them once beside the draft
  ('flip:music', as the Pad's 'pad:music'), so the draft leaves the text out
  and each save writes the drawing. A reload reads the bytes and makes the
  text again for the draft's other readers. A save from before this is read
  as it was, and its next save moves the song beside the draft. Taking the
  song away takes its bytes out of the store, and the bin's Undo brings them
  back with it.
- MEASURED after, the same two runs each:

                                main             this
    adding    the longest hold  3.0 - 4.1 s      0.9 - 1.5 s
              blocking in all   5.7 - 12.3 s     1.9 - 3.6 s
              the beat shown    5.8 - 11.2 s     3.3 - 6.5 s
    a save                      258 - 485 ms     7 - 8 ms
    a reload  the song back     7.6 - 7.8 s      3.9 - 4.1 s

  What still holds the page while a song is added is what the Pad pays too:
  the song made into text for the post and the drafts (about 0.5 s at this
  pace) and its bytes written to the store once (0.4 s). The 2.5 s paint went
  with the <audio> element's text.

THE CHECKS: verify_flipdraft, DRAFT — Flip keeps a song as a file, six rows on

## After v330 -- A song's text and its bytes, made and kept off the page (both editors)

The owner (Nov 5, "do the song speed for both editors"): the next pass the
entry before this one named, for the Pad and Flip together.

- TRACED on main, a phone 402 x 874 at 3x, the CPU 4x slower, a two-minute
  stereo song at 44.1 kHz (21.9 MB; 29 MB as text), from the pick until its
  beat shows and the saves after it are done. Two of the holds were the
  song's own, and both editors had them: making its text (a data URL, which
  the post, a backup file and a saved draft carry), one stretch of 0.40 s on
  Flip and 0.31 s on the Pad; and writing its bytes into the draft store,
  where IndexedDB takes its copy of them on the page, 0.12 s on Flip and
  0.10 s on the Pad. A reload that brought the song back made its text
  again: 0.46 s on Flip, 0.31 s on the Pad.
- BUILT, one module each, both editors:
  - lib/songtext.js makes a song's text in a worker (FileReaderSync) and
    hands it back. SkriblSongText.of(blob) gives what FileReader's
    readAsDataURL gave, so the Pad's pick, Flip's pick and Flip's restore
    swapped one for the other and nothing after them changed. The file is
    its worker's script, as lib/musicears.js is.
  - lib/draftstore.js writes a record that holds a file from a worker
    running the same file: the bytes are read and handed to IndexedDB there,
    and the page waits for the answer. A plain record (a draft's text, the
    drafts' index) is written on the page, as it was.
  - NOTHING IS LOST FOR WANT OF A WORKER. Where one cannot be made, its
    script will not load, it cannot make the text, its store does not
    answer, or it does not answer at all (20 s for the text; the store's own
    deadlines for a write), it is given up and the page does the work, as
    before. A value the store refuses (a full disk, one that will not clone)
    is still that refusal. A page with no IndexedDB of its own writes nothing
    through a worker: what it could never read back is not written for it.
- MEASURED after, a Chrome trace of the same moment on each, main and this:

                                      main      this
    Flip  making the text             0.40 s    0.19 s, the text handed back
          writing the bytes           0.12 s    none on the page
          blocking in all             1.06 s    0.73 s
    Pad   making the text             0.31 s    0.10 s, the text handed back
          writing the bytes           0.10 s    none on the page
          blocking in all             0.94 s    0.56 s
    a reload, making the text   Flip  0.46 s    0.19 s
                                Pad   0.31 s    0.11 s

  Over two more runs each, read by the page's own long-task count: the Pad's
  blocking went from 0.82 - 0.91 s to 0.46 - 0.51 s and its longest hold from
  0.34 s to 0.15 - 0.17 s; Flip's from 0.84 - 0.88 s to 0.60 - 1.08 s, where in
  one run the decode's end alone took 0.92 s. That is what varies most, and
  it is Web Audio's own: it makes the song's 87 MB of samples on the page,
  0.2 to 0.9 s at this pace. The rest of what still holds the page while a
  song is added is the waveform's paint, the listening shimmer's frames (40
  to 75 ms each at this pace) and the text handed back (a copy of 29 MB). On
  a reload, reading the bytes back out of the store is still on the page,
  0.2 s: a worker could read them too, the next pass if a phone shows it.

THE CHECKS: verify_songoff (new), 17 rows, both editors, a song added
through the music drawer's own file input and a stroke drawn. The page's own
FileReader.readAsDataURL is never called and the text the editor keeps is the
file's own data URL; the page's own IDBObjectStore.put is never called for the
song's record and the record holds the same file (its name, size and SHA-256).
Then the page does both itself, the same text and the same file kept, where no
worker can be had, where a worker's script will not load, where a worker
cannot make the text and where its store does not answer; and on the Pad (the
module is one) where a worker never answers, after its 20 s.
CALIBRATED, each shown red against its own break: the text made on the page
again (both editors' rows), the Pad's pick reading it itself (its row), Flip's
(its row), the Pad's page not loading lib/songtext.js (its row; a server of
its own, since Flask caches templates), the bytes written on the page again
(both rows), no text where no worker can be had (both rows, and the bytes rows
with them: a song with no text is never kept), no bytes written there (both
rows), a broken worker's text lost (both rows, the bytes with them), a broken
writer never let go (both rows), a refusing worker's text lost (both rows, the
bytes with them), a store that did not answer taken as the last word (both
rows), and no deadline for a worker that never answers (its row). With none
broken, 17 of 17.

THE WAITS: waits.settle counted the page's file reads and IndexedDB writes as
work in flight, and those moved into workers, which nothing counted, so a
suite could read a page mid-save. QUIET_JS now holds settle for each message
posted to a worker until it is answered, and lets it go when the worker is
stopped or breaks. verify_waits, three rows: a worker answering 700 ms later,
and a worker stopped, and one broken, with a message unanswered. CALIBRATED,
each red against its own break: nothing counted (the first row), an answer not
counted (held to the window), a stop not counted, a break not counted. With
none broken, 20 of 20.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: the same as the Pad; one module each, both editors.

THE FOUR: kind (the song's own holds while it is added go from 0.4 - 0.5 s
to 0.1 - 0.2 s in either editor, the blocking in all down by a third or more,
and a song is never lost for want of a worker); simple, powerful and playful
unchanged.

Not tested here: a real phone and Safari (no WebKit here). FileReaderSync and
IndexedDB in a worker are in Safari 14 and every browser the editors run in;
where one is missing, the page does the work as before.

## After v330 -- The owner's desk test: a take undone to nothing, a blank base, a canvas that never grew back

The owner tested the checklist (the Skribl Test Checklist page, Nov 6) on a
Windows desk, the iPhone items included: 17 of 20 worked, and three were off.
"The biggest issues were with canvas resizing and timing and logistics
surrounding the text and recording and timing - as well as undo."

- UNDO ALL THE WAY THROUGH A TAKE ("i can undo all the way (even words), but
  it doesn't get to the home screen"). Reproduced: words or a stroke start a
  take on a blank canvas, and Undo back to nothing left the take running over
  the empty canvas, its clock counting and Done showing. Now a take with
  nothing in it, over an empty canvas, ends as if it never began
  (unwindEmptyTake, editor_draw.js): no take, the clock at rest, the empty
  canvas's hint, no Record button. The pinch's own unwinding of a phantom
  first stroke moved there from app.js (the player never records): it left a
  Record button standing over the blank canvas, fixed with it.
- THE WORDS THAT WERE NOT RECORDED ("it does not register the amount of time
  it took for the letters to write themselves ... I have to manually click
  record"). Reproduced, and it is the same take's doing: its saves kept the
  blank canvas the take began on as a base, and a reload read that base as
  ink left out of any take, so an empty canvas came back as one the Pad
  thought was drawn on. Words written there, and the strokes after them, were
  ink in no take (the auto-arm does not fire over such ink, by design), and
  Record stood over nothing. Saves keep a base only under lines now (the
  autosave and a file alike); a restore forgets a base saved before that has
  nothing on it, with nothing drawn since (forgetBlankBase, editor_draft.js),
  so the owner's own autosave from the test comes back fresh. A base with ink
  in it stays ink.
- RECOLOR "doesn't recolor after text and undo": lib/recolor.js works on the
  lines of a take, and those strokes were in none. With the two above it finds
  them. (On a desk it lights the line under the mouse and shows no lens, by the
  owner's choice of the hover-to-light mock; the lens is for a finger.)
- THE CANVAS THAT NEVER GREW BACK (a draft opened with the music drawer open
  "shrinks because of open drawer, then when closed drawer - it stays small";
  a new 4:3 Pad "just never goes back to be as big as it can be"). Measured on
  a 1536 x 864 desk: opening a drawer only scrolls the page and the canvas
  keeps its 682px, but a fit that ran while one was open gave the canvas only
  the room it left -- 423px with the music drawer, 345 with the draw drawer,
  331 with Tune, 204 x 363 of 378 x 672 on a phone with Tune -- and nothing
  fit it again when it closed. A fit runs when a draft or a New Skribl is laid
  out, the window is resized, or a phone's toolbar slides away. The Pad's fit
  now measures the room as it is with them shut (editor_bar.js, drawersAside):
  the drawers below the dock lifted out of the page's flow for the measuring
  and put back before anything paints, and Tune's height given back (lifting
  it took its 10px tuck under the header too). Flip had the same, 24px of it:
  its stage took off an open drawer's content but not the room under the
  drawer's last row that the container wears only while one is open
  (flip.css); it takes off all of it now, against the container as last seen
  with nothing open.

THE CHECKS: verify_emptytake (new), 12 rows: a stroke's and words' take
undone to nothing end, the next stroke starts a fresh take (its first point
at 1 to 3 ms, where the old take's clock was past 3 s), Redo brings the words
back to watch; a reload after it is fresh, words written then are recorded,
a stroke joins their take and Recolor finds it; a save of an empty canvas
keeps no base; an autosave and a file holding a blank base come back fresh,
and one with ink in its base comes back as ink; a second finger on a blank
canvas leaves no take and no Record button. verify_drawerfit (new), 7 rows:
the Pad's canvas through a draft opened, and a window resized, with the music
drawer, the draw drawer or Tune open (Tune on a phone too), and Flip's with
the music and draw drawers.
CALIBRATED, each shown red against its own break. verify_emptytake: no
unwinding on Undo (the four Undo rows), the base saved again (its row),
nothing forgotten on a restore (the autosave's and the file's rows), a
forgetting that drops any base (the ink row), the file's or the autosave's
forgetting left out (each its row), the pinch not unwinding (its row), the
unwinding leaving Record shown (the pinch row: the old pinch's own fault);
the old build's three together red ten of twelve, the reload, the words and
Recolor among them, "the stroke's colour None -> None". verify_drawerfit: no
drawers aside (five rows), the drawers not lifted (three), Tune's height not
given back (two), Flip's old subtraction (two). A row that a field in a drawer
keeps its focus through the fit could not be shown red here (Chromium gives
the focus back even to a field hidden and shown in one task) and was dropped.
With none broken, 12 of 12 and 7 of 7. The player's JavaScript went down 276
B (160,337 to 160,061) and its ratchet with it.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: the fit, the same rule in both editors. Flip has no
takes, so the first three are the Pad's alone.

THE FOUR: kind (Undo all the way is a fresh start, words and strokes are
always in the drawing's replay, and the canvas stays as big as the window
allows); simple, powerful and playful unchanged.

Not tested here: the owner's iPhone (the checklist's iPhone items were run on
a desk this time) and Safari (no WebKit here).

## After v330 -- The owner's all yes: a post's song keeps its own speed past 2x, and the same draft just opens

The owner answered the desk test's two questions "all yes" (Nov 6), and the
parts of each that needed no new look are built here. The looks (a Song choice
with the speeds, and one short question for a draft opened over a different
drawing) wait on their mock, "Text, Song and Drafts", with the Text sheet's
faster speeds.

- A POST'S SONG AT SPEED ("with music at high replay speed the music changes
  and just sounds like a weird constant noise"). The Pad's own replay and a
  link (app.js musicRate) already kept the song in step only between half and
  double and played it at its own speed outside them; a post's player
  (inlineplayer.js) pitched it with the drawing at every speed, 16x and a
  Fit's 94x included, which is the noise the owner heard. The rule is now
  one function, lib/replayline.js songRate, read by both players. Off the
  drawing's pace the song starts where it would be had it played from the
  start at its own speed, as the Pad's does, and the drawing no longer keeps
  the song's time there (the song clock is not started).
- THE SAME DRAFT, UNCHANGED, JUST OPENS ("it loads the file, but shows you the
  drafts menu over the draft you just picked"). A draft saved, then opened
  from the Library, landed on an editor whose autosave was that same drawing,
  and the drafts list opened over it, asking "Tap again -- this replaces what
  is on your canvas". lib/savedrafts.js now compares what the editor would
  save with the draft, less what is stamped at saving (the times, Flip's
  savedAt, and the name a Flip without one gets by the minute): the same, it
  opens with no question and the next Save updates it. Measured first: both
  editors serialise a reloaded draft to exactly what was saved, once its
  photo and song are back, and those come back about 0.1s after the page
  without either editor saying it is busy all that time (the Pad's "busy"
  drops between the store's read and the attach). So a different drawing is
  told at once, and the same drawing whose media is late is looked at again
  for 3s at most. And an account's draft comes back from the server with its
  keys sorted (Flask's JSON), so every object is compared in one order: the
  check's first run found that, the account's same draft still asking. Pad
  and Flip share it.

THE PLAYERS' BYTES, raised for the rule, each with its named cost: a link's
JavaScript +64 B (lib/replayline.js songRate; app.js's own copy went, -5 B),
160,125 measured; a post's embed +147 B (songRate and inlineplayer.js asking
it), 76,487 measured.

THE CHECKS: verify_inline, the song at speed (3 rows): the rule's table; a
post's song at 2x and 1x pitched with the drawing from where the drawing is;
at 8x and at 1/4x at its own speed, from where it would be. verify_clouddrafts
6b (5 rows): the account's Pad draft opened over itself opens with no question
and is adopted; changed (a new ground) it asks within 1.5s; this browser's
Pad and Flip drafts with a photo and a song open with no question; Flip
changed (a stroke) asks within 1.5s.
CALIBRATED, each shown red against its own break: a post's song pitched
with the drawing at every speed (the 8x and 1/4x row: rates 8 and 0.25); the
song at its own speed but started where the drawing is (the same row, 1.23s
into the clip where 0.18 was due); the old hand-off that always asks (the
three same-draft rows); one look with no waiting for the photo and the song
(the two media rows, Pad and Flip); a different drawing waited on as if only
its media were late (the two "at once" rows, 3.2s); keys left in the order
they came (the account's row). With nothing broken, 3 of 3 and
verify_clouddrafts 104 of 104.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: both shared. A Flip's post plays its song by the same
rule; Flip's editor has no watching speed. Flip's drafts open the same way.

THE FOUR: kind (no noise, and no question when nothing would be lost); simple
and powerful unchanged; playful (a time-lapse with its song).

3.4s, 9.5s and 17s). The mock "Text, Song and Drafts" offered A, the same
slider on up to 16x, and B, a slider of seconds instead; the owner said "all
yes", A.

So the Text sheet's Speed has four more stops past 4x: 6x, 8x, 12x and 16x,
a replay's own top speed (lib/textwrite.js SPEEDS, the slider's max 12). 1x
is still the hand's own pace and the sheet still says how long the words will
take: at 16x the note is 5s, the 200 letters 9s. A speed kept from before is
the same stop it was (the stops up to 4x did not move).

THE CHECKS: verify_text 9, two rows changed: 16x takes a sixteenth as long as
1x and a quarter of 4x, and the sheet says "16x · "; - and + stop at 16x and

ending at 4x (both rows), the slider's max left at 8 (both rows). With
nothing broken, TEXT 9 4 of 4.

## After v330 -- A draft from the Library over a different drawing asks in one line (the owner's all yes to A)

The owner, of opening a draft from the Library: "it loads the file, but shows
you the drafts menu over the draft you just picked". The same draft,
unchanged, already just opens (the entry above). For a different drawing on
the canvas the mock "Text, Song and Drafts" offered A, one short question
under the header, and B, the drafts list with the question on top; the owner
said "all yes", A.

So lib/savedrafts.js asks in one line, in the glass "Another drawing is
waiting" wears (lib/othertab.js, the owner's T1 and D2): "Open "Cat"? What's on
your canvas now goes to Drafts first." Open it keeps the drawing on the canvas
in Drafts first, as Save draft makes one, then opens the draft and says
"Opened "Cat". The drawing you had open is in Drafts." Keep drawing puts the
question away and changes nothing. The drafts list no longer opens over the
drawing to ask (armOnRender is gone); inside the editor, the list's own rows
still ask "Tap again" as before.

- NOTHING LOST. A photo or song still on its way back from the store when
  Open it is tapped is waited for (5s at most; each editor's new pending()
  says what is still coming), so it is kept with the drawing. Measured first
  on Flip, whose busy() never says so: kept without the wait, a photo-only
  autosave still loading was filed with no photo. If the drawing cannot be
  kept (Drafts full, the store not answering), nothing is replaced and the
  line says why.
- NO COPY OF A DRAFT THAT IS ALREADY ONE. The draft the canvas was opened as
  or last saved to is remembered across a reload (localStorage, per editor),
  and Open it compares the canvas with it: the same, nothing is saved again.
- "Draft restored" is not said on a page that arrives with ?draft=: that draft
  is what was asked for, and the question sat under its words on the Pad.

THE CHECKS: verify_clouddrafts 6 and 6b (5 rows new or changed): the Pad asks
in one line with no list; Keep drawing changes nothing; Open it keeps the
drawing in Drafts first, then opens the draft with its name; an unchanged
saved draft on the canvas is not copied; changed, it asks in one line at once.
verify_amber's Flip row: asks in one line over an autosave still loading, and
what Open it kept holds its photo. CALIBRATED, each shown red against its own
break: the list in place of the line (the line rows, Pad and Flip), keeping
nothing (the keep row, the no-copy row and the kept photo), copying a draft
that is already one (the no-copy row: refused at the account's limit, so not
opened), no wait for media still on its way (the kept photo), Keep drawing
opening the draft (its row). With nothing broken, verify_clouddrafts 107 of
107 and verify_amber's Flip block 4 of 4.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared; one module for both editors, each telling it
what media is still coming.

THE FOUR: kind (nothing lost, nothing to puzzle out), simple (one line, two
buttons), powerful (straight to what you picked), playful (out of the way of
the drawing).

## After v330 -- The Song choice with the speeds (the owner's all yes to A)

The owner, of a post's song at 8x: "just sounds like a weird constant noise",
and then "maybe should have the option of music replay speed too?". The rule
(an entry above) keeps a song with the drawing between half and double and at
its own speed past them; the mock "Text, Song and Drafts" offered A, a Song
choice that opens with the speeds, and B, the song's speed as a second button
in the line. The owner said "all yes", A.

quiet, then With the drawing and Normal speed (lib/replayline.js attach, its
new song, songPick and pickSong). The lit one says what the song is doing at
this speed, by the rule, until the viewer picks; a pick then holds at every
speed (songRate(r, pick): 'with' the drawing's rate, 'own' 1), restarts the
song at once from where it would be had it played from the start at that
speed, and closes the pill, as a speed does.

- EVERYWHERE THE SPEEDS ARE: the Pad's line under the drawing, its desk pill
  beside Play and Tune's Watching speed row (one pick, said in all three, and
  kept in this browser as the speed is: skribl_replay_song); a link page and

  visit, as their speed is; nothing of it is posted.
- WHERE IT SITS, as the mock had it: 14px from the speeds in a line (over them
  on the Pad and in a post, under them on a link) and 8px under them on a
  desk. On a phone under 400px wide the room between goes first and then the
  words shrink with the screen, so a 320px phone holds it whole, on one line,
  at 12.5px (Tune's at 12.8). The owner's 402px phone sees the mock's sizes.
- A POST KNOWS ITS SONG ONCE ITS DRAWING HAS COME: the line's summary on the
  page carries no song, so before the first Play its speeds open alone.
- Its label is --text-secondary on the pill, 8.2:1 light and 9.3:1 dark, as
  the mock measured (a post's, the quiet words' .62, 7.6:1); its choices are
  the speeds' own ink and lit fill. On short phones (375x667, 320x568) every

speeds open alone (the Pad, a link, a post); with one, the lit choice at 8x,

THE PLAYERS' BYTES: a link's JavaScript +807 B (lib/replayline.js +626, app.js

## After v330 -- verify_musicbeat's timeline drag aims, reads and corrects (main red after #773)

Main's run after #773 went red on one shard, SQLite 6 of 6, on a row #773 did
not touch: verify_musicbeat's "an end let go counts whole beats from the
start wherever it is". The app did the right thing: let go at 9.20 beats, the
end settled on 9 whole beats from the start, and the start stayed where it
was. The drag did not: it aimed at 8.8 beats and let go at 9.20, 0.2s later on
the song. The run after #774 was green on every shard, that row included
(issue #775).

The drag (tl_drag) works out where the finger goes from one reading of the
timeline's view and of where its stage is, then moves there. Anything that
moves after that reading, such as a view still widening on a busy runner or a
page that shifts, moves where the finger lands. Not reproduced here under 4x
and 6x CPU throttling (8 of 8, four times).

- FIXED, in the suite: after it moves, the drag reads where the handle says it
  is, as a finger watching the line does. When that is more than 0.02s from
  where it was sent, it reads the view again and moves again, four times at
  most.
- CALIBRATED with the condition forced, in a scratch copy only (the
  timeline's stage moved 30px after the drag read it): the old drag let go at
  2.836s where 3.15 was aimed (a row red); the new one landed every row, 8 of
  8. With nothing forced, the whole suite with the fix: 62 of 62.

Nothing in the app changed.

## After v330 -- The Song choice in a wide face, and the full screen's speeds (main red after #776)

Main's run after #776 went red on four shards, SQLite and PostgreSQL 2 and 4,
on two things #776 brought (issue #778):

- A POST'S SONG CHOICE AT 320px IN DEJAVU SANS. CI draws the feed page in
  system-ui, which on Linux is DejaVu Sans, wider than any face the app is
  drawn in where it is used; there the two choices were 20px too wide for the
  post's box at 320 and one spilled out of the pill (edge 18, inside false,
  exactly the numbers measured here once DejaVu was forced). This box draws
  in Inter, where it fits with room to spare, and so does every face THE
  PILL'S ENDS reads (Inter, Liberation Sans, FreeSans). Fixed for any face:
  the pill wraps a whole choice to a second row where a face cannot hold it
  on one, centred and 10px down so their taps never overlap; in the faces
  the app is drawn in it stays one row, as the mock had it. And the 320 rows

## After v330 -- The drafts list opens a draft in one tap, what is on the canvas kept first (the owner's yes)

The owner asked which made more sense: the list in the editors' Your drafts
sheet asking "Tap again -- this replaces what is on your canvas", where the
second tap replaced it and a drawing never saved was gone, or keeping what is
on the canvas in Drafts first. The recommendation was the second, as the
Library's one line already does ("Open it" keeps it first); the owner: "Yes".

- ONE TAP OPENS IT (lib/savedrafts.js openDraft, both editors: one module).
  What is on the canvas is kept first by the same keepFirst the Library's
  Open it uses: not again when it is the draft it was opened as, unchanged
  (compared, not assumed); its photo and song waited for, 5s at most. A blank
  canvas keeps nothing. A draft for the other editor still hands over to it,
  which asks over its own work in its one line.
- IT SAYS WHAT IT DID. The row's second line says "Keeping your drawing in
  Drafts..." while it keeps (a live region, as the row's Delete question is);
  the toast says 'Opened "Cat". The drawing you had open is in Drafts.', the
  Library's words. Nothing is asked, so there is nothing to tap twice.
- WHEN IT CANNOT KEEP IT (Drafts full, a photo or song still loading, a store
  not answering), NOTHING IS REPLACED and the row says why, in the store's
  own words then "Nothing was replaced."; if the sheet was closed while it
  waited, a toast says it instead.
- The row's lilac "armed" look went with the question (styles.css; the re-emit
  changed neither the player's CSS nor the band's). The sheet's one question
  left is Delete's, still one row at a time.
- A DOUBLE TAP KEEPS ONE COPY, AND A STUCK OPEN GIVES WAY. A second tap while
  the first keeps and opens does nothing; an open that never answers (a store
  that hangs) is given up after 20s and its late answer opens nothing, so the
  list never stops listening.

FLIP: shared. The sheet is the same module in both editors, so Flip opens in
one tap too; verify_clouddrafts 4c drives it in Flip, with room in Drafts and
with Drafts full.

THE CHECKS (verify_clouddrafts): one tap opens in the composer's Pad, the
drawing it replaced is the newest draft, the row and the toast say so; Flip
at the account's cap replaces nothing and the row says the server's words;
Flip with room keeps and opens; a Pad holding only a photo keeps it; a photo
still loading replaces nothing (on the row, and as a toast with the sheet
closed); a blank canvas keeps nothing; an unchanged draft is not copied; one
Delete asks at a time in the sheet; a double tap keeps one copy; an open
that never answers does not stop the list (the page's clock moved on 30s
rather than the suite waiting). How it works says it too ("keeps that work
in Your drafts first"), claimed by those rows (verify_helpclaims).

CALIBRATED in scratch copies of the tree, one break each. Main's
lib/savedrafts.js (the old Tap again): the composer's four one-tap rows red,
then the suite stops at Post, the take still recording. Opening without
keeping: six rows (the composer's keep, Flip at the cap and with room, the
photo, the photo still loading, the closed sheet). Keeping a blank canvas:
the blank row. Copying an unchanged draft: both no-copy rows (the Library's

## After v330 -- The live demo answers 8 requests at once (gunicorn threads)

The owner timed a first open of the post box at "over 5 seconds", and said yes
to the server fix ("all yes"). The live demo's gunicorn ran one sync worker
with one thread, so it answered one request at a time. An editor's first open
asks for about 120 files, and on the live site their first bytes came 25 to
40 ms apart: 5 to 9 s in all. Twelve requests sent together came back spread
over 0.3 s, one after another.

- **`gunicorn.conf.py`** (new, at the root) sets 8 threads a worker, or
  `GUNICORN_THREADS` if it is set. `gunicorn app:app` reads it by name from the
  folder it runs in, so neither the Procfile nor Render's dashboard start
  command changes. `WEB_CONCURRENCY` still sets the workers. Same instance, so
  no cost.
- **Safe with threads.** The app already runs threaded under every harness run
  (the dev server is threaded). The in-memory limiter takes a lock, and
  production's limiter is the database.
- **Measured here** with gunicorn itself, the one-thread run and the eight-thread
  run side by side. While a slow client downloaded flip.js at 20 KB/s, a small
  file took 2.35 s with one thread (the worker was busy) and 0.05 s with eight.
  Pad, Flip, the post box's Pad and the feed all booted under the threaded
  worker with no errors.
- **Shipped in the package.** `harness/package.py` now ships the file in the
  runtime package, since a package without it serves one request at a time.
- **verify_hostconfig asks gunicorn** (`--print-config`, run as the host runs
  it) and fails under 4 threads. Red without the file and red with
  `GUNICORN_THREADS=1`; green at 8.

The live site's before and after are to be measured once this deploys.
FUTURE 6af holds the rest of the speed work.

## After v330 -- The server stops redoing its work: its file caches hold every file

Part of the owner's slow first opens ("over 5 seconds"). The server strips
the comments out of each script and style and compresses it, once per file
version, and keeps the result. It kept 128 files and emptied all of them when
full. That cap dates from when an editor asked for 25 files. The Pad now asks
for 123 scripts and styles, Flip for 117, and the pages together for 146. So
opening the Pad and then Flip emptied the caches, and the next open did every
file again.

- **Measured** in-process on this box, each page's files in turn:

  | in turn                | cap 128 | cap 512 |
  |------------------------|---------|---------|
  | Pad, the first open    | 3.1 s   | 3.2 s   |
  | then Flip              | 2.4 s   | 1.1 s   |
  | then the Pad again     | 1.5 s   | 0.1 s   |
  | then the post box Flip | 3.2 s   | 0.1 s   |
  | then the post box Pad  | 2.9 s   | 0.1 s   |

  It is all CPU, so the threads (#796) could not help, and a slower server
  takes longer.
- **The fix:** both caps are 512. The caches keep only a file's real current
  version, so a running server holds at most one entry per file: 147 scripts
  and styles and 172 compressible files today. Everything kept is under 3 MB.
- **Still slow:** the very first open after each deploy. Each server process
  starts with empty caches, so its first visitor pays the 3 s above. The
  combined files (FUTURE 6af, step 2) can be built when the server starts.

Four rows in verify_assetcache, red at 128 and green at 512:

- every page's scripts and styles stay stripped together;
- every file sent compressed stays compressed;
- the Pad again, after every other page: not one of its files done twice;
- each cap sits above every file it could hold (a drawer's script fetched on
  demand is on no page, so the page rows alone would miss it).

## After v330 -- Each worker does the file work before its first visitor

#799 kept the server's stripped and compressed files once made. But each
server process starts with none of it done, so the first visitor after every
deploy paid for all of it: on the live demo the Pad's files took 8.8 s of
server work the first time. The owner usually opens the site soon after a
deploy, so that is the open they see.

- **`skribl.warm_assets(app, tick=None)`** asks the app for every script,
  style and other compressible file (172 today) at the URL a page builds,
  with gzip accepted, through the app's own test client. Going through the
  app's own route makes the kept keys and bytes exactly the ones a visitor's
  request looks for; a second copy of the strip-and-compress code would drift
  from it. It returns how many files it asked for, and 0 for anything that is
  not a Flask app with Skribl mounted.
- **`gunicorn.conf.py`** calls it in each worker's `post_worker_init`, after
  the app loads and before the worker takes a request. It ticks
  `worker.notify` after each file, so gunicorn's timeout never takes a long
  warm-up for a hung worker. A warm-up that fails is logged and the worker
  serves anyway, doing each file on its first request as before.
- **Measured** with gunicorn here, one worker and 8 threads: the warm-up took
  4.0 s at boot. A first open's files then took 0.22 s of server time against
  3.07 s cold, and Flip's 0.25 s against 1.15 s.
- **A host** calls it the same way (INTEGRATION.md, "The file work before the
  first visitor"; docs/SKRIBLS-NET.md, item 10).

New rows:

- verify_assetcache (4): it asks for every file either cache could hold; it
  ticks once per file; after it, serving every page's files adds and redoes
  nothing; a host without Skribl, or anything not a Flask app, warms nothing
  and does not fail.
- verify_hostconfig (1): gunicorn, started as the host starts it, logs every
  file warmed before its first visitor.

Calibrated in a scratch copy of the tree (verify_assetcache whole,
verify_hostconfig's new section alone):

- As it is: 20/20 and 1/1.
- The warm-up's requests without gzip, or its URLs without the bust: red on
  "adds and redoes nothing" only.
- No tick: red on the tick row only.
- Only the top folder warmed: red on "every file", "adds and redoes nothing"
  and the gunicorn row.
- No guard: red on the "warms nothing and does not fail" row only.
- gunicorn.conf.py without the hook, or with a warm-up that fails: red on
  the gunicorn row only.

The owner, after a week of the empty canvas's words writing themselves on
every open: "I want pad and flip to be the same. What would be best?

themselves is already starting to get annoying. I like the font though."

one. What showed every time was the words, writing themselves for 1.7 s
(1.9 s on the Pad) and un-writing at the first stroke. The box shows on a
slow open; part 2 takes it.

- **The words are already written.** The editors draw them into the page
  from lib/handwords.js's own recording (`skribl_hand_words`,
  skribl/__init__.py, read from the line between MARK:BEGIN and MARK:END),
  so they are there on the first frame with no script to wait for. The
  module takes that drawing over as it is: the page's path and the
  module's whole path are the same string, so not a pixel moves.
- **They write themselves once**, as a welcome: under the first-open hello,
  once it has gone. The hello comes once on a device, so after that the
  words are simply there, on an open, after Undo back to nothing, on a new
  Skribl. Under Reduce Motion they are whole, hello or not. The page's
  drawing waits unseen under the hello until the module blanks it to write
  it (`_skribl_hand_boot.html`; on its own at 9 s if the module never comes).
- **The first stroke fades them** with the line under them, in the hint's
  own 0.3 s fade, whole while they fade. They no longer un-write first.
- **The pen hops when you had to wait for it** (lib/penswoosh.js, which both
  editors carry): one tiny hop, 5 px up and 1 px under in 0.38 s, as the
  editor is ready, when that was more than a second after the page began.
  On an everyday open nothing moves. Not under Reduce Motion, not under the
  hello (the welcome there is the words), not once a stroke has begun.
  Automation meets it only when it asks (`window.__skriblHopForce`, as the
  hello and the snail), so no other suite catches the pen in the air.
- A page that does not draw the words (a template without the helper) still

## After v330 -- The calm open, part 2: the canvas in its place from the first frame

The rest of the owner's "Yes calm" (part 1 is the words and the pen's hop):
"I want pad and flip to be the same... it has to be subtle cuz it happens a
lot." On a slow open Flip showed a 300 x 150 box that jumped to full size
when its scripts were done, and its page row changed under it; the Pad's
canvas settled (a 9:16 guess 26 px too tall on a phone; on a desk a 4:3
guess that turned square).

- **The canvas is laid out before anything paints.** lib/canvassizes.js and
  lib/chromefit.js load in the head (`_skribl_fit_boot.html`): small, globals
  only, render-blocking beside the stylesheets. Right after each editor's
  column an inline script (`_skribl_fit_early.html`) does the editor's own
  sums with them: Flip's sizeStage() and fitPad() at rest and the shape a new
  drawing starts in; the Pad's resizeCanvas() and layoutEditorCanvas(). The
  editors' scripts then find nothing to change. Until it has run the canvas
  is unseen, so a slow line that paints the page in pieces never shows it at
  a size it will leave; should it never run, the canvas shows on its own at
  4 s (not under Reduce Motion, which turns every animation off), and each
  editor's boot shows it too.
- **Flip's page row starts in its first-page look**: the add row is in the
  template now (flip.js wires it once, and makes it only on a page without
  one), the size class is stamped as lib/sizeclass.js would stamp it (the
  page bar hides on a compact one-page Flip), body.one-page as flip.js marks
  it, and one page's tile in the strip, so the row is as tall as it will be.
- **A draft you come back to is in its own shape from the first frame.**
  Each editor notes its drawing's shape beside its draft (lib/chromefit.js
  note: the size, Flip's page count, whether there is ink) and drops the note
  with the draft. The page lays the canvas out in it, and the Pad starts in
  it (app.js, through lib/chromefit.js padShape): its restore is a later
  script (editor_draft.js), and at a slower phone's pace a frame was drawn
  between the two, a new drawing's tall shape between the draft's square and
  the square again. With ink on it, the words are not shown at all (they
  would only go when the drawing comes), and at once: hidden by their class
  alone, they faded out over the canvas for 0.3 s, a frame before having
  styled them unseen. A note left without its draft is dropped by the open
  that finds it. A draft an older page saved holds no size, and the note
  beside the slot may then be another drawing's (this page's last save,
  saved over): it goes on the shape this window chooses for a new drawing,
  as it always did (padShape's fresh), before holdStrokes looks.
  verify_drafts caught that one: its "an autosave with no size" row went
  red beside the other suites and alone (98/99) until the restore did so.
- **A site's post box and the letter sheet keep no draft**, so they start as
  a new drawing whatever is noted: the template's word in the early script
  (the page's own SKRIBL_COMPOSE comes after it) and noted()'s for the Pad's
  start, which also reads SKRIBL_LETTERS.

Pad and Flip: shared. One head partial, one early partial with a branch for
each editor's own sums, one note in lib/chromefit.js. The link player loads
neither library nor either partial, and app.js, which it does load, is 69 B

## After v330 -- Text's dials, and the recorder as it was found

The owner, on the Text sheet: "Shouldn't the editor shut the recorder off
once it's written the words? Also, shouldn't we have control of thickness on
text editor, and font size?" Cal answered with what happens now and two ways
for the recorder, and the owner said "all yes" to the defaults.

- **Size is a slider.** It was three buttons (Small, Medium, Large). The
  letters' height is still kept as a share of the drawing's shorter side, so
  one setting suits every shape, and the sheet says it in this drawing's px
  (Medium is 35px on a phone's 9:16 and 46px on the square). 2.5% to 20%
  of the shorter side; its - and + step it by half a percent. The three old
  sizes are stops on it, and a choice of one kept from before comes back as
  that stop.
- **Thickness is a slider, for the words alone.** It was out of sight: the
  words took the pen's size. Now it is the pen's size until it is moved;
  moved, it is the words' own, kept for next time, and the pen stays as it
  was (a real pen's line does not grow with the letters, and a caption
  should not change the pen that draws). In the pen's own px, 1 to 34.
- **The three dials line up** in one grid: Size, Thickness ("for the words
  only") and Speed, each the app's slider with its - and +, the numbers on
  the right.
- **Text leaves the recorder as it found it** (the Pad). A take Write it
  began, on a blank canvas or a finished take, ends when the words have
  written themselves out, as Done ends one ("Saved. Play to watch it, or
  Keep drawing to add more"). A take that was recording before goes on. So
  does one whose words a press or a key hurried along: that press is often
  the next stroke, and a finished take would refuse it.

Pad and Flip: shared, one sheet (lib/textwrite.js); the recorder is the
Pad's alone, Flip has none.

verify_text has two new parts (18, the dials, on both editors; 19, the
recorder) and one changed row (15: Write it on a finished take records the
words as a take of their own and leaves the recorder off); the contrast
census reads the two new numbers. How it works says it all, and
verify_helpclaims holds its three new sentences to their checks. Calibrated

- The Size slider not wired: Size's row and the kept row, both editors.
- The words not written at the Thickness: Thickness's row and the kept row,

- The dials not kept: the kept rows. A Large kept from before not coming

- The take Write it began never ended: the blank-canvas row and 15's.

## After v330 -- Text is a drawer

The owner, of Text's typing sheet (a card fixed over the foot of the
screen): "Shouldn't text be a drawer? Not a popup?" The mock showed it as one
of the drawers under the tools in four ways; the owner: "I like your idea of
only opening the drawer a little but you need to know it opens more right?",
which A3 compact answers (the sliders behind tiles that say what they hold,
the pen drawer's way), and then "Yes" to: Text becomes a drawer, A3 compact;
and while you drag your words, the drawer drops down and comes back when you
let go.

- Text's drawer sits with the others under the tools, on both editors, and
  is one of them (lib/drawers.js): one open at a time, so another drawer
  opening closes it and the words with it, and the page comes to it and goes
  home after, gliding. The Pad's drawer machine is made in app.js, which the
  link player loads too, so editor_text.js joins Text to it with a new add()
  and the player carries nothing for it. Another tool closes it, as does
  Escape, its grabber on a phone (a desk keeps the drawers' rule: no
  grabber), and Write it.
- In it: the words and Write it in one row; Style; and three tiles, Size,
  Thickness and Speed, each saying what it holds (35px, the pen's 5px, 1x)
  and opening its slider under it, joined to it, one at a time; on a phone
  the opened slider is brought on screen as the pen's is ('drawtile',
  lib/drawerdetent.js). Gone: the sheet's title and its x, and the bar it
  stepped aside to ("Text's sheet steps aside", above).
- WHILE THE WORDS ARE DRAGGED the drawer steps aside: unseen and untouched,
  its room kept so nothing jumps, while the page glides home with the words
  under the finger all the way, so they reach the top of the drawing (with
  the drawer up, a phone shows 57% of the Pad's drawing and 42% of a Flip's,
  the mock's numbers). Let go and it is back, the page gliding to show it no
  further than the words and Write it need: the words kept clear of the
  header, unless that would leave Write it off the screen, and then Write it
  wins (lib/drawerdetent.js revealPanelEnd, two new arguments: what to keep
  clear of the header, and the row that must show whatever).
- Typing on a phone, with the keyboard up, the drawer leaves the page and
  sits on the keyboard as the grabber, the words and Write it (#txSpacer
  keeps its room), and comes back into the page, on screen, when the
  keyboard goes.

FOUND ON THE WAY, each a bug fix:
- A drag begun within 1.2 s of the drawer opening had the drawer's own
  re-asserts of where it opened carry the page back down under the finger,
  260px in one frame. The step-aside now goes through revealTop (Play's "show
  the whole drawing"), which calls them off.
- A press on the drawing within 1.2 s of the drawer's return had its last
  re-assert carry the page to the drawer's end under the words just placed.
  A press is the person's own: lib/drawerdetent.js hush() calls the
  re-asserts off, as a press inside the drawer already did.
- On a phone the keyboard's bar kept the drawers' 240px: 150px of empty
  paper over the drawing. It is as tall as its row now.
- harness/tools/make_art.py's Text path still clicked the Small, Medium and
  Large buttons #807 made a slider; it sets the slider now.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP: shared. One template (_skribl_text.html, its drawer
in each editor's drawers), one module (lib/textwrite.js), and the drawer
joined to each editor's own machine. The one difference is each editor's
existing rule for any drawer: on the Pad, a press on the drawing with
another drawer open only closes it, and the next press brings Text; on Flip
the one press does both.

THE CHECKS: verify_text 2, 3, 4, 13, 14, 16 and 17 remade for the drawer,
21 new (the tiles); How it works' Text tip and verify_helpclaims' claims
follow; verify_contrast reads "Text's drawer" and "Text's drawer, Speed".
Calibrated in tree copies, each with its own server: 40 breaks, each red
on its own rows. 2: the Pad's or Flip's drawer not joined to its machine,
and the words started at the top of the drawing. 3: no grabber, no Escape,
a close that leaves the words, another tool that leaves it open, a close
the machine is not told of, and the Pad's drawer opened around its machine.
4: the words riding the page instead of the finger, a let-go that moves
them, no hush, and the box drawn over the drawer. 9: the Speed tile not
following. 13: the tiles' values dimmed. 14: the page jumping to the
drawer, gliding under Reduce Motion, and the tiles popping open, vanishing
shut, and moving under Reduce Motion. 16: the bar on the screen's floor,
the bar 240px tall, no room kept, no return on screen after the done key,

step-aside, one that gives up its room, one without the glide home, the old

Calibrating taught the rows four things. A drag to the top of the drawing
stays on the screen: one past its top reached the top with the step-aside
broken, and no finger can. A close is read by the page gliding home, not

## After v330 -- Text's tiles draw what they hold

The owner, of the Text drawer's first tile pictures (an Aa, three bars and a

The mock (https://claude.ai/artifact/R3g2VHexiErTWDr86pEN8R, version 1)

icons aren't great. Thickness is okay, but speed is not great." Version 2
kept A's line and offered Size as a small, the words' own and a large A, an
A with a height mark, or Aa; and Speed as a snail and a rabbit with a little
slider between them, a dial, or a rabbit alone. The owner: "All yes", the
picks: small, yours and large; the snail and the rabbit.

WHAT CHANGED. The three tiles' pictures are canvases drawn by
lib/textwrite.js (paintTiles), as the pen drawer's are by lib/drawtiles.js:

- Size: three A's in the words' own style, a small one and a large one at
  the ends, faint (the ink at 35% over the tile), and the words' own between
  them in the ink, as tall as the Size (9px at the smallest, 28 at the
  largest), its line the words' thickness against that height. Placed at a
  fifth, a half and four fifths, as the pen drawer's Size dots are; a wide
  hand (Script's A) would run one into the next there, so they close up as a
  group, smaller only if they must be.

  thicker past 30.
- Speed: Lucide's snail and rabbit in the tile's grey, and between them a
  little slider in the ink, its dot at the speed: a quarter by the snail,
  16x by the rabbit. Apple puts a tortoise and a hare at the ends of the

  Lucide's paths, scaled, under the ISC banner jsstrip keeps, as flip.js's
  Lucide glyphs are.

What holds a value is the ink at full strength (a see-through ink drawn in
short pieces beads where they meet); an ink too near the tile's ground, as
white is on the light theme, is drawn over a soft edge, as the pen drawer
draws one. The pictures repaint with the dials, the style, the pen, the
tiles' width and the theme (at the switch and again after the tile's .15s
fade); a closed drawer's canvases have no size and are drawn when it opens.

## After v330 -- Two reds on main, both the instruments

Main's runs after #810 and #811 each went red on one lane, in suites neither
change touched; the twin lanes and the next runs were green on the same rows.

VERIFY_JSSTRIP, THE GALLERY (after #810, sqlite 2/6 only). "Every element
computes the same style, stripped or raw": 25 of the gallery's 1,800
elements differed, and the row could say only the first one's opening custom
properties. It did not come back: not on the postgres twin, not on main's
next run, and not in thirteen loads here of a gallery filled as CI fills it
(thirty posts, verify_captions' long captions, the CPU slowed to 6x). A strip
that changes a style changes it on every load; the page's own settling does
not. So a pair that differs is loaded again, stripped and raw: a stylesheet
the strip changed differs in both pairs and stays red; a difference the
second pair does not repeat is said beside the pass. The row now names the
element and the properties that differ. Calibrated in tree copies with their
own servers: the strip made to drop font-weight is red on all four pages in
both pairs, naming it (DIV.brand: font-weight '400' vs '800'); one gallery
load given a stray margin passes on its second pair and says what the first
pair saw; the copy with nothing broken is green.

VERIFY_POSTGRES F3 (after #811, postgres 1/6 only). "The two concurrent
retries were handled by BOTH workers": one worker answered both,
['67879', '67879'], the contract rows green beside it. The cause was not the
timing of the two threads. gunicorn.conf.py gives every worker 8 threads
(#796), and F3's host starts from the repo root, so it read that file: one
process could answer both retries at once. Holding the first retry open
proved it here: with the threads, the pair still landed on one worker in 2
of 5 runs. F3's host now runs `--threads 1`, two sync workers, one request
each, which is what a claim about two processes needs; and the first retry
is held open (its headers and a byte of its body) while the second is sent,
so the second can only go to the other worker. It goes on its own thread: one
worker serving both would wait behind the held one, and the row says so
rather than the suite hanging. Six runs here on a local PostgreSQL 16, the
pair split every time, 28/28; with one worker, the setup row, the pair's row
and the cross-worker row went red, the suite done in 30 s. The local cluster
was stopped after (with it up, browser suites' frame pacing suffers).

## After v330 -- Every drawer shows what a tap opens

The owner: "is there any reason that all drawers shouldn't open all the way
(scroll to bottom) when a selection is made that shows below the screen? I
know this happens on several drawers (at least on desktop). Is there a way
to check that or do I need to be specific about all the affected drawers?"

A sweep pressed every tile and door in every drawer, 44 of them, on the Pad
and on Flip, on a 402x874 touch phone and a 1280x800 desk, and read where
what opened ended. Twenty ended below the screen. On a desk the pen
drawer's four tiles and Text's three opened their choices 21-241px below
the foot and the page did not move at all: lib/drawerdetent.js answered a
tile only where the detent's grabber shows, on a phone. The music drawer's
Restart door (phone and desk) and Length door (phone) moved the page, but
not far enough: Restart's choices ended up to 264px below. The phones' pen
and Text tiles, and the photo drawer, were fine. The owner's pick ("All
yes"): one rule for every drawer -- the page glides just far enough to show
all of what opened, without going past the top of the drawer; with Reduce
Motion it goes straight there; and the check stays in the suites, so a new
drawer cannot miss it.

THE RULE, ON A DESK. SkriblDrawerDetent.showOpened: the 'drawtile' event a
tile sends (lib/drawtiles.js, and Text's in lib/textwrite.js) now names what
opened, and where there is no detent the page glides until its end is 12px
above the foot of the screen. Its end is read as laid out (its top plus its
height): it unfolds from its top as a scale, so the box it is drawn in on
the first frame stops 8% short. Never past the top of the drawer -- the bar
right above it stays below the header, as every reveal in the module keeps
it -- and only ever down: a choice that already shows moves nothing.
A newer reveal, or a press on the drawing (hush), calls it off.

TEXT'S WORDS STAY IN VIEW. Their sliders change them while you watch, so
the words, when they are on screen, hold the page as the drawer's top does
(on a 560px desk the Pad's slider stops with the words at the top). Words
Text's own reveal has already let go above the screen (Flip, on a short
desk, where the drawer's first row wins) hold nothing: holding for them only
left the slider below the screen.

ONE TILE FOR ANOTHER, found on the way. The new tile's choices replace the
old ones at once, and a shorter set made the drawer shorter in the same
frame; scrolled to the drawer's end, where the page had just brought the
old choices, the browser clamped the page in one frame. Feel for Eraser
leapt 217px on the Pad's phone and 234px on Flip's (already, before this
change), and 93-118px on a desk (new with it). The swap is held and glided
(shrinkGently), as a close is and as the music drawer's doors swap: 7-15
frames, the most 20-62px in one. Under Reduce Motion it is simply done.
Text's swap is the same code; its choices differ by 11px, too little for a
row to tell a glide from a leap, so no row pins it.

THE MUSIC DRAWER'S DOORS are left as they were, and asked of the owner.
Restart's choices are taller than the room the drawer's top leaves on these
screens (the song and its timeline sit above the doors): kept below the
header, the bar above the drawer stops the page with Restart up to 264px
short on a phone and 212px on a desk, and Length up to 39px short on a
phone. That is the approved rule's own limit, and the check accepts it.
Showing all of it means the bar, the song and the timeline go up under the
header (on a desk, off the top), the tapped door's tile staying on screen.

WHAT IT DOES TO FLIP. Shared: one module, one event, both editors.

THE CHECK. verify_drawerreveal presses all 44 for real (a tap, a click) and

## After v330 -- A Skribls page on the host's site

The owner's pick A for a Skribls section ("All yes", after FUTURE 6ah and a
mock on skribls.net's saved stylesheet, Now beside A and B, phone and desk,
light and dark): every public skribl, from both doors, as a grid in the
site's own frame and colours; each tile says who drew it and links back to
the post it came from, or says it was made in the app.

BUILT IN THE REFERENCE HOST, for skribls.net to copy (docs/SKRIBLS-NET.md
item 12). examples/host_app gains a frame (templates/base.html: the head,
the colours, the header and two tabs, Feed and Skribls), a page for one post
(/posts/<id>, where "From a post" leads and each post's #id now links), and
the Skribls page (/skribls). The page is drawn in the browser from Skribl's
own listing, the way /feed's preview does it (feed.js): clone the
skribl_inline('__ID__') template, set its size and line, mount. So it pages,
sorts (New, Hot) and searches as the listing does, and shows only what the
listing shows: public skribls, through the host's feed filter.

TWO THINGS ONLY THE HOST KNOWS. Skribl has no user table and no post table.
The names come through author_resolver, which the example host had never
installed (so Skribl's own gallery called its people "Anonymous"). The way
back to the post is new: source_resolver(public_ids) -> {public_id: url},
called ONCE PER PAGE of the listing with every id on it, so the host's side
is one WHERE skribl_id IN (...) and not a query per tile (the authors' memo
cannot help: tiles share authors, but every tile is its own skribl). The
listing and GET /api/skribls/<id> then carry "source": {"url": ...}; a
skribl made in the app has none and its tile says "Made in Skribl Pad", or
"Made in Flip" for a Flip (the mock said Skribl Pad under a Flip too).
FUTURE 6ah had planned the post's address handed to create_post; a
resolver keeps no copy of an address that could go stale and needs no new
column. Only an http(s) address or a path on the site is passed on (the
URL parser's reading, no backslash, space or control character), because
the listing is public and every viewer sees it as a link; an answer that is
not a mapping says nothing. The page checks the link again before it uses
it.

A NARROW TILE SAYS ITS TIME. Two across on a phone (about 185px a tile), the
whole line took two rows and cut the title off; the mock said "I'd trim
each tile's line to just its time". inlineplayer.css makes the line a
container and, under 240px of its own width, keeps "Drawn in 15 sec" (a
Flip's "10 pages") and hides the speeds and the words before them. Its own
width, not the screen's: a post on a 320px phone keeps the whole line
(258px in the example host's feed). +164 B to every page that shows a post
(verify_inline's ratchet, 78,188 B measured).

THE CHECKS. verify_example 7: the listing names each author as the host
does and says where the ticked one was posted, nothing for one made in the
app, and the single read the same; the page shows the public ones from both
doors and not the one left off, each a mounted player, with its title,
@name and "From a post" to that post or the editor it was made in;
searching finds the ticked one by its gallery caption; "From a post" opens
that post with its drawing and no composer; Skribl's own gallery names the
site's people; on the desk every tile keeps the whole line, on a phone each
says its time, and a post on a 320px phone keeps the whole line.
verify_hostseams #6ah: one resolver call for a page of thirteen tiles; a
path and an https address passed on; a script, another site's //, a
backslash path, a space, a number and nothing not; the single read; a
non-mapping answer says nothing rather than a 500; app-local.

CALIBRATED in a tree copy, 15 breaks, each red on its own rows. In
verify_hostseams: a resolver call per tile (13 calls for 13 tiles); any
address passed on; the single read saying nothing; a non-mapping answer
trusted (a 500); one resolver for every app. In verify_example: the host
naming no post; the host naming nobody; the link going to the feed; a post's
own page keeping the composer; every tile saying Skribl Pad; the search
words never asked; the tiles never mounted; no narrow line; the screen's

## After v330 -- Main red after #817: verify_hold read a frame the runner never drew

Issue #819, main at fbbf8f0, postgresql 6/6 only (sqlite 6/6 and every
other shard green): verify_hold 73/74, "a new watching speed mid-page
carries the badge on from where it is, at the new speed", 505ms then 562.6ms
100ms into 2x, where about 200 on was asked. #817 did not touch Flip's badge.

THE PRODUCT IS RIGHT. Measured here, ten times at CPU 1x and ten at 4x: the
badge's own reading moves exactly twice the real time between two reads
(to within 1.5ms), setFlipRate takes 1 to 10ms even at 8x, and frames keep
coming at 4x. The row read the badge's PAINTED value, which is only as
fresh as the last frame: one frame old here (2 to 16ms), and on a runner
that drew no frame for about 70ms after the speed change, 70ms old.

THE ROW NOW READS THE BADGE AT THE MOMENT OF THE READ (flipBadgeShow, then
data-ms) and compares it with twice the real time between the reads, and
asks that the painted badge moved on too, so a badge whose frames stop at a
new speed is still caught. Calibrated in a tree copy with its own server:
green as built (74/74); red when a speed change does not move the badge's
start (a jump to 1234ms), when the badge ignores the speed (it went back),
and when its frames stop at the change (the painted badge stuck at 519ms).
With the page's frames held back 150ms after the change, the old row went
red as CI did (504ms then 526ms) and the new one stayed green.

## After v330 -- Main red after #825: a stalled glide catching up read as a leap (verify_drawerreveal)

clamp). The log keeps both on every frame. Calibrated: the CI trace's shape
