## After v330 -- The herky-jerky check's last gap: a beat leaving called its own glide off

The check above left one thing untested: the music drawer's hold through a
beat landing or leaving (lib/drawerdetent.js holdThrough). A landing never
moves the page (verify_musicbeat pins that). A leaving does: the drawer gets
shorter, so the page at its end is held and, 320ms later, glides up to
where the drawer now ends.

THE PROBE. Pad and Flip, a 402x874 phone at CPU 4x and a 402x664 one at 6x,
the Beat door open and the page at the drawer's end, the beat taken away
(the state an Undo or a new song leaves), with every frame and every write
to the page's scroll recorded with who made it. A new song as the trigger,
three Pad runs at 4x: clean.

THE JUMP: 3 runs of 18 on the 874px phone at 4x (Pad twice, Flip once), none
of 6 on the 664px one at 6x. The page sat a second under the hold, then
clamped 20px (Pad) or 7px (Flip). As the beat leaves, the tap's row takes
its line of words back in one frame while Beats in a bar folds away. The
growth follow (followGrowth) leaves Beats and Beats in a bar out of the
card's height, but not the tap's row, so the leaving armed it, and its 300ms
take-back, which waits for a still page (#823), found one in the instant
between holdThrough's glide being asked for and its first frame. It pulled
the page back 11px (Flip 24px: the dock under the header by that much at
the drawer's end), an instant write, which calls a smooth scroll off; the
hold's wait for its glide to land never ended, and its 900ms net let the page
go, which clamped the rest.

THE FIX: what grows while the page is held (the root's min-height, which
only holdThrough, shrinkGently and a closing drawer set) is part of that
change, and the follow leaves it to the hold. One shared module, so Pad and
Flip together. After: 12 runs of 12 at 4x glided, the hold's glide the only
write.

THE CHECK: verify_musicbeat, on a phone, both editors: the Beat door open,
a beat landed, the page at the drawer's end, the beat leaves; the page
glides to where the drawer now ends, with no clamp, and the hold's glide is
the only write. The follow armed was a second write in every run of the old
code, so the row does not wait for the race to land. Calibrated in a tree

## After v330 -- The skribls.net stand-in on the demo, at /host

The owner looked on the live demo's /feed for Add to post's gallery tick
(#818) and found none. /feed never asks, by design: it posts everything
publicly, so its list is the public gallery. The host that does ask
(examples/host_app, opening the Pad with compose=1&gallery=1) ran only on a
laptop. Shown the difference, the owner said "I want the stand-in", and then:
"make sure you do this so if someday skribl needs to be its own site (say the
skribls.net owner doesn't want to merge this) it can be". That is now a line
in WORKING-AGREEMENTS and in FUTURE 6ah.

- MOUNTED, NOT MERGED. app.py puts examples/host_app at /host with werkzeug's
  DispatcherMiddleware, in the same process. Skribl was built for two apps in
  one process: every seam init_skribl takes is the app's own. The stand-in has
  its own database (a SQLite file beside the demo's where that is SQLite, one
  per test server; in the temp directory where it is PostgreSQL, gone on a
  redeploy), a secret derived from the demo's, and its own cookies: its
  session `skribl_host_session` on /host (the demo keeps a Flask session for
  its demo identity, so a shared name would have overwritten it) and its CSRF
  cookie `skribl_host_csrf`. A stand-in that fails to start is logged and
  left out; SKRIBL_STAND_IN=0 leaves it out on purpose. Nothing in Skribl or
  the demo's own pages links to it or knows of it.
- WHAT ELSE WAS CHECKED BEFORE MOUNTING. Compose mode keeps no Pad draft, so
  the two Pads on one origin cannot restore each other's drawing; the demo's
  service worker answers only its own pages and /static/skribl files; the
  stand-in's media stays inline in its own database; gunicorn does not
  preload, so each worker opens its own connections; attach_to_metadata copies
  Skribl's tables, never moves them.
- THE CHECK: verify_standin, through the demo's own server: the stand-in at
  /host with its Skribl under /host/skribl; Add to post's tick and caption on
  a phone (the frame opens with compose=1&gallery=1); a post that lands in its
  own feed and Skribls page and not in the demo's public list; every cookie it
  sets named skribl_host_..., its session on /host. Calibrated in tree copies
  with their own server, one part at a time: left out (SKRIBL_STAND_IN=0),
  /host a 404 and the suite stops there; its cookies unnamed, a `session`
  cookie on / and the cookie row red; the demo's own database, the demo's
  list 0 then 1 and the posts row red; its composer without gallery=1, no tick
  and the asking row red. As built, 5/5.
- ITS FILES ARE DONE AFTER A START, BESIDE THE DEMO'S VISITORS. The
  stand-in's Skribl keeps caches of its own, so every start left them empty
  and the first open of its Pad paid what the demo's did before the warm-up
  (#801: 8.8 s of server work on the live demo). gunicorn.conf.py now warms
  each app mounted beside the demo once the demo's files are done, on a
  thread of its own that rests 0.1 s after each file. The rest is the point:
  Python runs one thread at a time, and unrested the stand-in's five seconds
  of work held the demo's own visitors. On the dev box, three runs each, the
  demo's Pad opened while the stand-in warmed (after one open thrown away) in
  0.22-0.23 s with no stand-in warm-up, 1.4-1.8 s unrested, 0.35-0.39 s
  rested; the stand-in's 172 files are done in about 22 s. The live demo is
  one Starter instance that does not sleep, so this runs once per deploy. The
  stand-in costs a worker about 10 MB in all: 68 MB without it, 69-71
  mounted, 77-80 with its files kept (which a first /host open did anyway).
  verify_hostconfig starts gunicorn as the host does and now also asks that
  the stand-in's line names every file, after the demo's, and that the demo's
  Pad opened while it warms takes at most 4x one opened after, plus 0.3 s.
  Calibrated in tree copies, the warm-up section alone, one part at a time:
  no stand-in warm-up, no line and the files row red; unrested, 1.85 s
  against 0.21 s and the not-held row red; warmed before the worker takes a
  visitor, the stand-in done before the demo could be opened and the not-held
  row red; as built, 3/3 (0.37 s while it warmed, 0.23 s after). The whole
  suite on the tree, 61/61.

## After v330 -- Main red after #830: the stand-in built a second host on import

Run 42830024763 (main after #830): every lane green but the PostgreSQL
shard 6/6, where verify_deletion_foundation's blast-radius row said "no
pragma listener is installed on postgresql" was false. Reproduced here on a
PostgreSQL 16 cluster in the scratch area (stopped after): red with the
stand-in mounted, 17/17 with SKRIBL_STAND_IN=0.

Two things, one of each kind.
- THE INSTRUMENT asked that no SQLite engine in the process carried Skribl's
  pragma listener. That was the property while Skribl was alone; since #830
  the stand-in brings a Skribl and a SQLite database of its own, which
  rightly enforce foreign keys. The row now asks the seam, of each engine's
  own connect listeners: the engine Skribl was given here has none, and
  every engine that has one is an engine some Skribl was given (the
  stand-in's, read through the mount).
- THE TREE: asked that way, a third engine carried one,
  examples/host_app/example.db. The host's module ended in
  `app = create_app()`, so app.py's import of it to mount the stand-in also
  built a second, unused host with its own Skribl in every worker. No app is
  built on import now: `flask --app app run` finds create_app() itself (as
  verify_example and verify_clouddrafts start it) and `python app.py` builds
  one in its __main__.

Calibrated on PostgreSQL in tree copies of the suite: a stray SQLite engine
handed the listener, red; the listener put on the demo's own engine, red;
the module still building its app on import, red (the example.db engine
named in the row); as built, 17/17. On SQLite, side by side:
verify_deletion_foundation 17/17, verify_standin 7/7, verify_example 59/59,
verify_hostconfig 61/61, verify_clouddrafts 116/116.

## After v330 -- The social site, laid out before it is built

The owner, after "all yes" on the look-over: "we are beginning to build the
social media site... This may be the beginning of a social media site that
will have millions of users... Let's lay this out well so we don't have to
later fix stuff... I hope we can just drop the pad/flip into skribls.net, but
we may have to go it alone." docs/SOCIAL-SITE.md is the layout, and FUTURE
6ai points to it: three layers (Skribl owns everything about a drawing, the
site owns everything about people, and the site is a host of Skribl through
the public seams only, as skribls.net would be); everything a social site
has against what Skribl has today; fifteen scale rules taken now because
they are cheap now; the phases, with the Gallery card (the owner's B) first;
and eight decisions with defaults. Asked "what answers do you need", then
shown the eight, the owner said "all yes": the site is its own app beside
Skribl and reaches it only through the public seams; the stand-in stays the
skribls.net stand-in; "Skribl" for now; passkeys with a link by email; 13 and
over; private messages later; B first, then the phases in order; no public
sign-ups before a lawyer has read the terms. Nothing in it is built yet.

## After v330 -- The Skribls tab is Skribl's own Gallery, in the host's frame (B)

The owner's B from the stand-in's look-over ("all yes", Nov 10; FUTURE 6ah,
docs/SOCIAL-SITE.md phase 0): the stand-in's Skribls tab stops drawing tiles
of its own and shows Skribl's own Gallery under the host's header and tabs.
One gallery, two doors: /gallery and a host's page hold the same section.

- ONE PARTIAL. `_skribl_gallery_section.html` holds what is the gallery: New
  and Hot, the search box, the list, the three states, Load more, the report
  sheet, the card's template and the live region. /gallery includes it inside
  its own page (the header, the heading, the foot); a host holds it with two
  macros, `skribl_gallery_assets()` in <head> and `skribl_gallery_section()`
  where the gallery goes. gallery.js finds its parts inside the section and
  its settings on the section's root (the listing, the player's address, the
  CSRF token), where they were on <body>, and builds the card's menu inside
  it.
- /GALLERY IS AS IT WAS. Its <style> is untouched but for one new rule
  (`.tfrom`, below), its scripts are the same in the same order, its ids are
  the same; the report sheet, the template and the live region now sit in the
  section inside <main>. Measured against the starting commit served beside
  it on the same database, the clocks held: /gallery the same pixel for pixel
  on a phone and a desk, dark and light, at rest, with a card's menu open and
  with the report sheet open (12 of 12).
- FROM A POST. A card whose listing item carries `source` (the host's
  source_resolver) says "From a post" at its foot, where the mock had it:
  small violet words in a 44px box, set in to where the caption starts.
  Skribl alone knows no posts, so /gallery shows none.
- LOAD MORE ASKS ONLY FOR A NEXT PAGE. Skribl's own had the second half of
  the stand-in's bug (#833): a press with no cursor fetched page one again.
- A HOST'S REPORT IS TAKEN. A host's page gets nothing from Skribl's context
  processors, so init_skribl adds two app-wide globals beside skribl_asset:
  `skribl_report` (the reasons and the note's limit) and `skribl_csrf()`,
  which on a page Skribl's own hooks never saw runs the CSRF `prepare`; an
  app-wide after_request then sets the cookie that token pairs with
  (security.page_csrf_token). The gallery view no longer passes the reasons.
- A STYLESHEET MADE FROM /GALLERY'S. `gallerysection.css` is written by the
  command that writes player.css and fullband.css (cssgraph.py --emit), from
  /gallery's own sheets in /gallery's order (fullband, fullbar, tooltip,
  labels, pagemenu's glass and grab bar, segslider, the page's <style>), every
  selector under `#skriblGallery`. The root starts from nothing and takes what
  /gallery's page gives the section (its body's type and ink, its <html>'s
  language); every part of it starts from the browser's defaults, but the
  player's box, which keeps inlineplayer.css, and an <svg> or a <canvas>,
  whose attributes a revert would undo; every custom property the section
  reads is defined on the root as /gallery defines it, or cut off there.
  Light follows `data-theme="light"` or, with no data-theme, the device. AN
  ID, NOT THE CLASS THE PLAN NAMED: a class-scoped rule ties a host's own
  class rule, and the later one wins; the stand-in's nav is `.tabs`, which New
  and Hot wear too, and in the approved mock (the host's CSS laid over
  /gallery) its margin had pushed the pill 10px above the search box.
- THE SCRIPTS KEEP TO THE SECTION. lib/tooltip.js takes a root; lib/labels.js
  and lib/segslider.js read `data-skribl-scope` off their own script tag.
  Without either, as on every Skribl page, they do what they did. Not loaded
  on a host's page: the page menu, the theme switch, opensurfaces, Report a
  problem, the marks; so under the report sheet the second belt against
  pull-to-refresh is the host's own (sheetswipe's first belt is there).
- WHAT IT DOES TO PAD AND FLIP: nothing in the editors. The three libraries
  are theirs too and behave as before without the new argument or attribute
  (verify_ux, verify_parity, verify_onepill and verify_tips below). The card
  is the one Pad's and Flip's skribls already had on /gallery.

THE CHECKS, each shown red first, one part at a time, the server bounced
after every template and Python change. A small runner ran the suite's own
section code on a fixture (a post through the host's form, no Pad), so a
calibration took a minute.

- SKRIBL'S FADE BETWEEN PAGES. The editors ask for a cross-document fade

- LIGHT AND DARK FOLLOW THE DEVICE. INTEGRATION.md documents no seam for

  chose light in the Pad on a dark phone sees the site dark.
- WHAT IT DOES TO PAD AND FLIP: nothing. Make opens them as they are, at

## After v330 -- Sign-in at /social: invite-only, passkeys (phase 1, piece 2)

docs/SOCIAL-SITE.md's build order, item 2, with the owner's answers ("all
yes", Nov 10): built on the demo's own address for invited people (their
passkeys are made again after the move to a domain, so nothing names a
host); passkeys alone, no email yet; invite-only until a lawyer has read the
terms. Built to the approved sign-in mock (A) without its email half.

- INVITE-ONLY, WITH PASSKEYS. Join from an invite link (a name, a handle,
  "I'm 13 or older", a passkey; signed in), Sign in with a passkey (nothing
  typed: the passkey says whose it is), Sign out and Sign out everywhere as
  buttons, You, Invites for admins, and a recovery link. py_webauthn checks
  every ceremony: discoverable credentials, user verification required both
  ways, the sign count stored and checked, a challenge for one browser, five
  minutes, used once, and the relying party and origin the request's own (a
  passkey keeps the address it was made on and signs in only there).
- A LINK'S CODE IS AFTER THE # (/social/join#<code>, /social/recover#<code>),
  NOT IN THE PATH THE BRIEF NAMED. A code in the path is in every access log,
  proxy log and Referer on the way (the dev server already logged each
  path), and a recovery link is the key to somebody's account for an hour. A
  browser keeps what follows the # to itself: the page posts it to
  /join/check, then options and verify, in the body. Only its SHA-256 is
  stored. A link that does not work (used, run out, revoked, never made) gets
  one kind card, and the server one answer, 404 {"error": "gone"}.
- THE FIRST PERSON. SKRIBL_SOCIAL_FIRST_INVITE (16 characters or more) works
  as a join link only while the site has nobody, compared in constant time,
  and makes that person an admin; spent, it is a used invite row with its
  hash, so two people racing for it cannot both win. `flask --app app social
  invite --base https://...` prints a join link from a shell, and `social
  recover HANDLE` a recovery link: the way back for an admin who lost every
  passkey, through Render's shell.
- YOU, AND SIGN IN IN ITS PLACE BEFORE. Once signed in, You is the bar's
  fourth place on a phone and the rail's foot on a desk (name over @handle);
  before, the place says Sign in, as the approved mock has it, and a phone's
  first screen says Sign in at its top right too. verify_social's two rows
  that pinned a bar of three now pin Sign in. You holds name and handle, the
  passkeys (add another; rename and remove in place, never the last), Sign
  out, Sign out everywhere and Delete my account. No profile page (piece 3).
- INVITES ARE AN ADMIN'S: a join link (once, 14 days) and a recovery link for
  a named person (once, an hour; it adds a passkey to their account, the
  stand-in for the emailed link), each shown once, since only its hash is
  kept; the unused ones listed with Revoke. To anybody else, signed in or
  not, the page and its forms are a 404 with the same status, words and
  headers as a page that is not there.
- ONE SKRIBL, SHARED. While somebody is signed in to the site, the Pad and
  Flip post as them (Skribl's user is their public id, "site:" and 26
  letters and digits, stable for ever) and the Gallery names them; while
  nobody is, the demo's own identity is asked as before. app.py composes
  both through the seams any host has (current_user_id and the author
  resolver), only where Skribl's CSRF is on: init_skribl refuses a cookie
  identity without it. THE LIVE DEMO RUNS WITH IT OFF (START-HERE: no
  SKRIBL_DEMO_* on Render), so there the site's people sign in and the Pad
  still posts as nobody until SKRIBL_CSRF_PROTECT=1 is set; the boot log
  says so as a warning wherever the app looks like a deployment. A demo
  identity beginning "site:" is refused at boot.
- TABLES OF ITS OWN, ON A CHAIN OF ITS OWN. social_people, social_passkeys,
  social_invites, social_challenges, social_rate_events: 64-bit keys that
  never leave the server (a person, a passkey and an invite each have a
  random public id for addresses and forms), every index written with its
  table. social/alembic.ini runs social/migrations into
  social_alembic_version; Skribl's chain and tables are untouched, in either
  order. RENDER DOES NOT READ THE PROCFILE (v270), so the chain is run by
  gunicorn.conf.py's on_starting, once per start in gunicorn's master,
  before any worker loads the app: Render's start command and the Procfile
  both start gunicorn, and neither changes. CAREFULLY: a chain that fails or
  takes over two minutes is logged with alembic's last lines (a database
  address in them blanked), the server starts anyway, and the site's
  sign-in answers a kind 503 ("resting") until its tables are there, while
  the Pad and the rest of the demo serve. `flask init-db` and the harness's
  fresh databases make the tables too (attach_to_metadata, as Skribl's).
- WHAT AN ATTACKER WAS GIVEN TO THINK ABOUT. CSRF: every state-changing
  request carries the site's token (HMAC of the browser's session id) and its
  own Origin (Sec-Fetch-Site where a browser sends none), the passkey
  ceremonies as JSON with the token in a header. Fixation: a new session id
  at every sign-in. Stolen cookies: the cookie is the site's own, signed,
  HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Secure over HTTPS (Render's X-Forwarded-Proto
  believed: a client claiming HTTPS only makes its own cookie stricter), 30
  days, path /; every request checks the person's sign-in generation, which
  Sign out everywhere moves on (a copy taken before Sign out alone stays good
  until then, as with any signed cookie). Guessing and flooding: codes are
  128 random bits, and the database counts sign-ins, joins and link checks
  per address (30, 20 and 60 an hour; one trusted proxy's address, IPv6 by
  its /64), tries per invite (12), links per admin (60 a day) and passkeys
  added per person (20). Replay: one challenge per browser and purpose, used
  once; the sign count. A copied key: refused when its count does not rise.
  Logs: no code, cookie or address reaches one. Enumeration: one answer for
  every link that does not work; a hidden page's 404 like any other. Spoofed
  names: a handle is ASCII letters, digits and underscores from a letter,
  with the site's own words kept; a name may not hide bidi or other invisible
  controls. Bodies: past 64 KiB a post to the site is refused by the
  length it says, or read no further, and whatever a body says is answered,
  never a 500. Scripts: none inline; the site's policy kept.
- DELETING IS REAL, WITH ONE GAP SAID ALOUD. Delete my account says first
  what goes and what stays, and needs the handle typed. It deletes the
  person, their passkeys, the invite links they made, the recovery links for
  them, the invite they came in by and ceremonies in progress. Their skribls
  and drafts stay: docs/INTEGRATION.md documents deleting one post by its id
  (delete_post) and no way for a host to take an author's drawings with them,
  and the site does not reach past the seams; the page says they stay, and
  to delete them in the Library first. A Skribl seam for it is the owner's
  call (anything the site needs from Skribl, every host gets).
- THE LOCK. webauthn 3.0.1 and its dependencies (cbor2, cffi, cryptography,
  pyasn1, pyasn1_modules, pycparser, pyOpenSSL) in constraints.txt, one hash
  each. cryptography's is its glibc 2.17 wheel, not the 2.34 one pip prefers
  here: a hashed install takes the wheel whose hash is listed (checked in a
  fresh venv: the whole lock installs, `pip check` clean), and it runs on any
  build image the lock already runs on. cbor2 ships a glibc 2.28 wheel only,
  greenlet's baseline already.

THE FOUR: kind (one card for every link that does not work, nobody blamed,

to sign in, nothing typed); powerful (passkeys, sign out everywhere, a
recovery link); playful (Blooby draws his card beside sign-in on a desk).

- 10, DELETE: what stays not said, red; any handle confirming, red; their

- 11, LIMITS: sign-ins, joins, link checks and an invite's tries each

- 14, THE CHAIN: the site stamping Skribl's alembic_version, red; a model

- 15, THE NEW SCREENS: the second ink made #a3aab7, red; the small buttons

- 16, NO ERRORS: an inline script on sign-in, red (the site's policy blocked

FIVE GREENS THAT COULD NOT HAVE BEEN RED, found by that calibration and fixed
in the instrument, not the site:

- The run-out link was made to run out before the admin's Invites page was
  read, and reading it deletes links that ran out unused: the row had been
  testing a deleted link (green with expiry unchecked). It runs out after
  now, and the row says the link is still there.
- With sign-out broken, the suite died waiting for the sign-in page instead
  of printing a red row. Every sign-out is pressed through a helper that
  lands wherever the site sends, and a missing element reads as no words.
- The forged cookie raised its own generation by hand, which the generation
  check refuses whatever the signature says. It names somebody else now,
  with their own current generation: only the signature can stop that.
- The 429's words: the page maps a 429 to them and the server names it
  "limited", so either alone keeps the scenario. Shown red by the words, and
  by both taken out together.
- The age: the page's own check and the server's say the same words, so the
  page's row was shown red with both out, and the server's row by its own.

FOUND BY THE SUITE, NOT BY A BREAK: a second link opened in the same tab
changes only what follows the #, so the page did not load again and a good
link read as gone. A link page now reloads on hashchange. FOUND READING THE
ROUTES AGAIN: a number for a name or a list for a handle raised inside the
field checks, and a verify with no credential raised inside py_webauthn:
both answered 500, both answer 400 now (the rows in section 12). And the
hidden Invites 404 carries the demo's missing-page policy on purpose (its
empty nonce is the console error piece 1 recorded on the demo's own 404), so
the page-error row navigates nowhere hidden.

## After v330 -- The owner's first sign-in on the live site, and what tripped it

Nov 10, evening (Mountain Time). After #844 the owner set the three settings on
Render and joined the site at /social as its first person and admin, with a
passkey on their iPhone, then posted a drawing from the Pad that the Gallery
showed under their name. One Skribl, shared, working on the live demo.

What tripped it, each a lesson for the words and the instructions:
- SETTINGS NEED A DEPLOY. Saved in Render's Environment, they did nothing until
  a Manual Deploy; read off the live pages (the Pad's SKRIBL_CSRF_TOKEN empty,
  no CSRF cookie) before and after.
- A VALUE THAT IS NOT EXACTLY 1. SKRIBL_CSRF_PROTECT stayed off after the first
  deploy (the app reads `== "1"`); right after a second, the Pad's token came.
- "PASSKEY" FOR TWO THINGS. The owner called the invite code Render held "my
  passkey" and went to Sign in, where the phone had nothing to offer ("No
  passkey was picked"). The words to put to the owner: the sign-in page's
  answer to a picked-nothing says "Haven't joined yet? Open your invite link",
  and every instruction calls the setting an invite code.
- CHROME ON AN IPHONE. A passkey Chrome keeps in the Google account is not on
  offer where the phone looks in iCloud Keychain unless Chrome is turned on
  under AutoFill & Passwords; Safari was the plain way through.
- THE JOIN LINK. Typed by hand, the address landed on Home (the path lost to
  autocomplete); written out in Notes and tapped, it opened "Welcome to
  Skribl".

START-HERE's "The live demo" now names the two new settings. The database is
Render's paid Postgres Basic, so the free-tier expiry warning given to the
owner that afternoon does not apply.

## After v330 -- Sign-in says where joining starts; the first invite code is an invite code

The owner's yes to both word fixes from the first evening, and a principle
with them: "Make it make sense. Simple and kind means intuitive and fun."
(WORKING-AGREEMENTS, "Powerful, playful, simple, and kind", and
docs/SOCIAL-SITE.md section 6 now carry it: simple is "would a person get it
without being told?", kind is "does it feel good to use?".)

- On the sign-in page, a passkey not picked now says "No passkey was picked.
  Haven't joined yet? Open the invite link you were sent." (a word of its
  own, `cancelled_signin`, in _passkey_words.html; passkey.js uses it only
  on sign-in, so joining, adding a passkey and recovery keep "Try again when
  you're ready.").
- SKRIBL_SOCIAL_FIRST_INVITE is called the first person's invite code, "not
  a passkey", in .env.example, docs/SOCIAL-SITE.md and the log line that
  warns of a short one.

verify_socialauth section 4: a fresh browser with no passkey presses Sign in
with a passkey and is told where joining starts. Red with passkey.js's
choice of words taken out (it said "No passkey was picked. Try again when
you're ready.", what the owner saw), green with it. Side by side:
verify_socialauth 60/60, verify_social 36/36, verify_docs 144/144.

## After v330 -- Profiles with drawn faces at /social (phase 1, piece 3)

docs/SOCIAL-SITE.md's build order, item 3, in the profile mock the owner
said "all yes" to (A) and "Faces that draw themselves: everyone's picture is
a skribl they draw of themselves; it draws itself once, in about four seconds
(at 4×), when someone opens their profile, and sits still everywhere else".
Built without what does not exist yet: no follower, following or play counts
(follows are phase 2, and a count is kept, never made up), no comments, and no
pinned skribl (next, below). Finished from a helper's unreviewed work, saved
as one commit after a container restart; what was kept and what changed is at
the end.

- A PROFILE at /social/@<handle>, any case of the handle: the face, big, in a
  circle on a ring of the card's paper, drawing itself once; the name,
  @handle and a few lines about them (plain text, 160 characters, 4 lines,
  nothing invisible or turned around, no links); Share; and their public
  skribls as Skribl's own Gallery section, newest first, New and Hot and
  search within them. Your own adds Edit profile, Draw your face (Redraw my
  face once there is one) and the gear to Settings. Nobody by that name,
  never made or deleted, is one kind 404 that says the handle back only when
  it could be one. A person sees on their own profile what their visitors see.
- YOU IS YOUR PROFILE. The bar's You and the rail's foot lead there and wear
  the face, still. Somebody else's profile marks no place in the bar. The
  account page of piece 2 is the gear's now, titled Settings; nothing else on
  it changed.
- DRAW YOUR FACE IN THE REAL PAD, over the profile, through lib/composehost.js
  (the frame's address set on the first press): the whole screen on a phone,
  gliding up and back down; a card on a desk, rising as it fades in; fading
  where it sits under Reduce Motion; the page behind inert, focus given back.
  "Use this face" sends the drawing to /social/you/face, which posts it
  through Skribl's create_post, UNLISTED, titled as their face, in the same
  transaction as the row that names it; a redraw deletes the old one through
  delete_post, and so does deleting the account. Its own limit per person
  (20 an hour), and a larger body for that one page (16 MB, a whole drawing
  and its share card; the site's 64 KiB stays everywhere else).
- NO STOCK SILHOUETTE. Before a face is drawn: on your own profile an empty
  circle that says "Draw your face" and opens the Pad; to anybody else an
  empty circle; in the bar's You a dashed empty circle. ON A GALLERY CARD THE
  INITIAL STAYS (the brief left others' views to me): a card is Skribl's, and
  its rule for any author without a picture is their initial on the tinted
  disc, skribls.net's own; an empty circle beside a name in a grid of drawings
  reads as a picture that failed to load. If the owner would rather see the
  empty circle there too, it is a small change to the card.
- THE CIRCLE'S GROUND IS THE PAD'S PAPER, as the mock has it in both themes,
  so in the dark a face draws itself from paper, not from black.

WHAT SKRIBL GAINED, FOR EVERY HOST (docs/INTEGRATION.md, "A face that draws
itself"; the site reaches none of it any other way, and verify_social section
8 holds that):

- THE FACE PLAYER: skribl_face() and skribl_face_assets() in
  skribl/_skribl_face.html, face.css, lib/face.js. Still: the face skribl's
  own poster, framed so the drawing's middle square fills the circle, by
  lib/sharecard.js drawingRect()'s sums, 3 card pixels in from the plate's
  hairline: one cached image, no script, no fetch, no play counted. Once: the
  in-post player's engine (SkriblInline.attach, ambient: it stops nothing and
  nothing stops it), at 4×, or quicker where that would take over five seconds
  ("about four", with room for a face drawn in twenty), from the empty
  circle, resting finished; under Reduce Motion finished from the first
  paint, nothing fetched; with no script at all, the still picture after a
  moment. A small piece of its own, not the in-post player with its controls
  hidden: the player's draft macro gives it the engine's parts and none of
  its chrome (skribl_inline_draft(chrome=false): no veil, no time chip), and
  the in-post player's assets and byte budget are untouched.
- THE PAD'S FACE MODE, compose=1&face=1: square from the first paint (the
  early fit, and lib/chromefit.js padShape reading SKRIBL_SHAPE); a face's
  words ("Draw your face" on the empty canvas; "Use this face", "Use" where
  the header is narrow, its title "Keep it as your face", and a press with
  nothing drawn saying "Draw your face first" through editor_compose.js's own
  status line; the sheet titled "Your face"; the × "back to your profile");
  a sheet that asks nothing a face does not use (no title, no Viewers start
  at, no gallery tick); no switch to Flip. It posts nothing, as compose mode
  never does.
- skribl_gallery_section(author=...), and the listing's visibility=public,
  which narrows an author's own listing to what anybody is shown and takes no
  other value (400).
- The author resolver's `face` ({"id", "w", "h"}), shown still in a Gallery
  card's circle, and its `url`, which the card already linked: the site's
  people's names link to their profiles, on Skribl's own Gallery too.

Not sealed since v330, and that is fine. Since the last "where things stand"
(the owner's first look at the live stand-in, the morning of Nov 10): the
stand-in's More fixed; B, Skribl's Gallery section, embeddable and used by
the stand-in's Skribls tab; the empty Gallery naming its door's tick; the
owner's choice to build Skribl's own social site rather than copy another
(docs/SOCIAL-SITE.md, the plan, with its phase 1 mocks: "all yes"); and
phase 1's first three pieces, each built, shown, merged on the owner's yes
and live on the demo: the frame at /social, sign-in by invite with passkeys
(the owner joined that evening as its first person and admin, and posted),
and profiles with drawn faces. And a principle, in the owner's words, kept
in WORKING-AGREEMENTS: "Make it make sense. Simple and kind means intuitive
and fun."

At writing (about 9 PM Mountain Time, the owner asleep: "tidy up when
you're done"), main was green through #846; #847's full run (profiles) was
still running; the live site answered the owner's profile with its empty
circle, their face not drawn yet. The branch matched main, with this entry's
pull request the only one open.

Still open, the owner's:
- Piece 4, posts (SOCIAL-SITE section 5): next, built from the approved
  mocks as piece 3 was, with pictures of anything beyond them for a yes.
- The domain: the owner picks a name (section 8, decision 3); passkeys are
  made again after the move (section 5, piece 2). Then Cloudflare in front
  (section 4).
- An email service for the emailed sign-in link: prices compared, asked
  first.
- Media to object storage (piece 6): its cost, asked first.
- Render stays (asked "Is it cheapest to keep Render?"; yes, section 4).

Found and not yet fixed, each a bug fix that merges on green:
- The site's limits count and then record (social/security.py), so tries
  landing at the same instant can each pass: a few extra at most.
- A passkey's address is the request's own; a list of the site's own
  addresses would be stricter, and the move to a domain wants one.
- The demo's pages that are neither Skribl's nor the site's (its 404) carry
  Skribl's policy with an empty nonce, a console error in Chrome on every
  load (recorded at piece 1, not changed).
- Deleting an account leaves its skribls, as its delete page says: it needs
  a seam that deletes an author's all, which Skribl does not have.
- A face deleted in the Library leaves its circle empty (piece 3's "not
  yet").

## After v330 -- Main red after #847: a still face's ink line stood on its own edge (verify_socialprofile)

Issue #849: main's full run on 0feb024 (#847, profiles) was red in sqlite
3/6, one row of verify_socialprofile, section 4, "elsewhere the face is a
picture, still". Its detail, read from the job's own log (the run's summary
keeps 300 characters of each failure, and had cut exactly the part that
said what failed): fetched 0; the same paint True; inked False.

NOT THE FACE. The pictures were the poster, still, with no player and no
fetch; the row also asks that something drawn shows in them, by counting
inked samples, and its line was 30. At this phone's one device pixel to a
CSS pixel the bar's 28px face and the card's 34px circle read 36 and 34
here: the line stood on the measurement's own edge, and CI read 30 or
fewer.

A FIRST GUESS, WRONG AND TAKEN BACK: that the first photo came before the
picture had (the same paint). Calibrated before it was believed, it could
not be: with the network held back a second and a half the old row stayed
green (both pictures are one poster address, loaded once with the page),
and a face made to move by an injected style never reached the paint. The
job's full log then said what had failed.

THE FIX, IN THE INSTRUMENT: the line is 10 (an empty or broken circle reads
0); both pictures must have loaded and decoded before they are read (the
card brought into view first, its picture being lazy), and whether they did
is part of the row; the detail leads with the numbers. Calibrated on
section 4 alone: as built green (card 34, You 36); the bar's still picture
hidden, red (You 0); its picture never coming, red (painted False, the
card's initial instead); the old line with the bar's face 4px smaller, red
in main's own words (the same paint True, inked False); the new line there,
green (You 24). The whole suite 35/35. Nothing of the site or Skribl
changed.

## After v330 -- A face from a skribl you made, placed in the circle (the owner's yes on mock A)

The owner, Nov 11, asking whether a skribl already made could be their face
("like the skeleton with the hat", posted before they joined and used in How
it works). Mock A shown (phone and desk, light and dark, "now" beside):
"Change my face" raising two doors, a picker, the circle. Their "all yes,
mock A", then "all yes, build A". The skull went to them first as a .skribl
file (skribl/static/help/demos/skull.json with a title), with today's way to
use it: Draw your face, then ... > Your drafts > Open a file... in the Pad's
face mode, run end to end here before it was told.

- YOUR FACE, ONE SHEET. Change my face (Add your face before there is one,
  and the empty circle) raises Make's own sheet: social.js's controller is
  window.SocialSheet now, one for every sheet the site raises, Make's
  behaviour unchanged. Two doors: Draw a new one (the Pad, as before; the
  sheet goes first, so the page the Pad makes inert is the page it hands
  back) and Use one you made, which leads on inside the sheet a step at a
  time. Whatever changes the sheet's height (a step, the list arriving, a
  line said) glides it there; under Reduce Motion the height is simply the
  new one, and only the fade remains.
- PICK: their skribls from Skribl's own listing, their user id asked for (so the
  link-only ones too), newest first, paged by its cursor; Pad drawings only
  (a face plays once, as a drawing does), never the face they have, never
  anybody else's; each tile the drawing cut from its own card by
  lib/sharecard.js's drawingRect, contained in the tile. Or Open a file...
  for a .skribl file, read in the page. The picker waits a moment for the
  list so its step arrives at its own height.
- PLACE: the drawing painted whole by the in-post player's engine under the
  circle (88% of the stage, the rest dimmed), starting on its middle square,
  the face a drawing has today. A drag (finger or pointer), the arrow keys
  (Shift for more), the slider and a pinch move and size it, from a quarter
  of the short side to the whole drawing inside the circle.
- USE THIS FACE: Skribl's new lib/faceframe.js (docs/INTEGRATION.md, "A
  face from a drawing you already have") makes the placed square a face of
  its own: a new 707 square drawing, every point moved and its size scaled,
  its time, colours, groups and recolours kept, its music left behind, its
  card painted by the player's engine and composed by lib/postedcard.js. It
  is kept by /you/face exactly as a drawn face is (unlisted, the old face
  deleted). The drawing it came from is never touched, so deleting or
  changing it never empties the circle. Skribl's face player, the bar's still
  You and a Gallery card's circle needed nothing new.
- NOT YET, SAID KINDLY where it was picked, the picker staying: a Flip ("That
  one's a Flip. Faces are drawings for now, so pick another."), a drawing
  with a picture under it ("... faces can't use those yet. Pick another, or
  draw a new one."). A face that moves (a Flip) and a face from a drawing
  with a photo are next, if wanted.

Pad and Flip: neither editor changed. Skribl gained lib/faceframe.js and two
macros in _skribl_face.html (skribl_face_maker_assets, skribl_face_maker),
documented for every host; the in-post player's assets and budget are
untouched.

FOUND IN THE PICTURES, NOT BY A ROW: the placing step's ring was first named
.face-ring, the profile's own circle's class, and its rule drew the
profile's face as an oval across the page. It is .face-place-ring, and a
row now reads the profile's circle itself (red with the old name: 353.8 by
769.1; green with the new: 112 by 112).

THE FOUR: kind (nothing of theirs is changed or lost; Back is always there;
what cannot be a face yet is said where it was picked); simple (two doors,
pick, place); playful (any drawing can be a face, and it still draws
itself); powerful (the exact size and place, by hand, keys or slider).

THE CHECKS. verify_socialprofile section 11, seven rows, every one shown red
by breaking one part and green as built (15 breaks): the sheet's opener not
bound (the first row); the step's height not glided (the second: a jump);
Flips not filtered, the listing without their id (the second); the start not

## After v330 -- Three small fixes: the site's limits, a passkey's address, the demo's own 404

The owner's "all yes" (Nov 11) to the docket's three small fixes: the two
follow-ups from sign-in's review (docs/SOCIAL-SITE.md, piece 2) and a
console error found while building profiles.

- THE LIMITS (social/security.py, over()). It counted the tries in the
  window and then wrote this one, so tries landing at the same instant could
  each count under the limit and all pass; and on SQLite a read-then-write
  transaction under a burst failed outright ("database is locked"), an error
  page for a person signing in. Now each try is written and committed first,
  then counted among every try already committed, and a try past the limit
  takes its own row back, one statement a transaction: no more than the
  limit are ever let through, on SQLite and PostgreSQL alike, with no lock of
  either's. In a burst it can refuse a try the limit had room for (tries
  count each other before the extra ones take theirs back); that errs toward
  the limit, and a try a moment later passes.
- A PASSKEY'S ADDRESS (social/passkeys.py, rp()). A passkey was made at, and
  asked for, each request's own address. SKRIBL_SOCIAL_HOSTS now names the
  site's own (comma-separated). With it set, a request at any other address
  begins no ceremony, and the page says "Passkeys work only at Skribl's own
  address. Open Skribl there and try again." Unset, nothing changes: a site
  reached by one name loses nothing. The demo is reached by one name, so it
  is not set there; the move to a domain sets it (SOCIAL-SITE.md, decision
  3), before anybody makes a passkey at the new name. A first draft also
  took Render's own name for the service (RENDER_EXTERNAL_HOSTNAME) when the
  list was unset. Render's docs could not be read from this box to confirm
  what Render puts there, and a wrong guess would have told the owner, at
  the site's own address, that it was not; so it came out.
- THE DEMO'S OWN 404 (skribl/security.py). Where a page had no nonce (the
  standalone app's own 404), the policy said script-src 'self' 'nonce-', and
  Chrome reported the empty nonce as an invalid source, a console error on
  every such page. _script_src() leaves it out when there is none, in the
  blueprint's headers and the standalone app's alike.

Pad and Flip: neither changed. Kind: a burst of sign-ins no longer ends in
an error page, and a passkey at another address is told where to go, never
blamed.

THE CHECKS, each shown red before it was believed.
- verify_socialauth section 17, one row: twelve tries released at once
  against a limit of five (each one's write held 50ms), then eight one at a
  time. Red on the old over(): tries failed with "database is locked". A
  first rewrite (count and take back in one transaction) was red the same
  way, SQLite's lock upgrade, hence one statement a transaction. Green: five
  let through, seven refused, five rows; the eight after, all refused.
- verify_socialauth section 18, one row: from elsewhere.test, 400
  "elsewhere" and no options; at localhost, options for localhost. Red with
  the check taken out (a ceremony began for elsewhere.test) and red with the
  list unset; green with both, beside section 4 (sign-in end to end with the
  list set), 7/7.
- verify_csp, "A page no blueprint answers", two rows: the 404's script-src
  names no empty nonce, and no console error. Red on the old security.py in
  Chrome's own words; green, 34/34.

Side by side, final tree: verify_socialauth 62/62, verify_social 36/36,
verify_csp 34/34, verify_integration 29/29; verify_docs 144/144 and
gen_docs.py --check current with this entry. The full battery was not run;
main's run after the merge is.

Not measured here: the limits on PostgreSQL (no PostgreSQL in this box, and
verify_socialauth runs on its own SQLite file in every lane). Each count
there runs after its own commit and sees every try committed before it.

## After v330 -- Trace a photo: a face's photo is a guide, and only the lines are kept

The owner asked (Nov 11) whether a person should be able to upload an image
for their avatar, "or better yet, maybe skribl could interpret an avatar and
generate a simple drawing of it". Cal's view: not a photo as a face (a face
that draws itself is the site's signature; a photo of a teenager's face is
the riskiest thing a site for 13 and over can hold, and every image needs
watching), and not a drawing made from one (its replay would be a
performance nobody gave, the one thing Skribl is about; a button that
decides; people's face photos sent to an outside service, at a cost per
face). Instead, Trace a photo: mocked through the real site and Pad (light
and dark, phone and desk; the photo a portrait of nobody, painted here),
and the owner's "all yes, build A" (the door and the guide; B was the guide
alone, in the Pad's drawer, with no door).

- THE DOOR (the site, profile.html and profile.js): Your face's third door,
  between Draw a new one and Use one you made, "Trace a photo: Draw over a
  photo. Only your lines are kept." It opens the device's own picker for
  one photo of the kinds the Pad takes (the Pad's frame cannot open one for
  the page); a file that is not one is said kindly where it was picked and
  the sheet stays; a photo puts the sheet away and opens the Pad with it.
- THE HANDOFF (Skribl): lib/composehost.js's guide(file) and a fifth
  compose message, skribl:compose:guide {file}, the face mode's alone
  (editor_compose.js); the Pad puts the file through its own photo drawer's
  input, as a photo picked there.
- THE GUIDE (Skribl, editor_face.js, loaded only in face mode): any photo
  there starts at 40%; the drawer's row says "A guide to trace" (the panel's
  data-guide, which lib/pendingcards.js reads) and a line under it "Only
  your lines are kept. The photo is never posted."; while there is a photo,
  the empty canvas says "Trace your face" and "Draw over your photo. Only
  your lines are kept.", and the face's own words come back when it goes.
- WHAT IS KEPT: editor_post.js leaves the photo out of a face's drawing
  (every frame and the legacy mirror) and paints its card without it, so it
  never leaves the browser; the site drops one sent anyway (profiles.py).
  This closed a side door: the face mode's photo drawer used to keep a
  photo under a face, with it.

ONE THING BEYOND THE MOCK, shown to the owner before merging: while there is
a photo, the empty canvas's two lines sit on one soft backing of the
canvas's own lightness, both in the hint's stronger ink. The mock said those
words read at 5.4:1 or better over the stand-in's face; that number was
wrong, because it took the words' colour without its see-through part. Read
off the paint with it, over a photo's dark middle at 40%, they read 3.5:1
(light, both lines) and 3.5:1 (dark, the quieter line); on the backing, 5.7
and 5.7 light, 5.9 and 5.7 dark.

Pad and Flip: the Pad's face mode only. Flip has no face mode; the image
drawer and lib/pendingcards.js are shared, and change only where the panel
carries data-guide, which only the face mode's does.

THE FOUR: kind (anyone can have a face that looks like them; the photo is
never posted; the words read as well over darker skin as over lighter);
simple (one door, a photo, trace, Use this face); playful (tracing paper,
and the face still draws itself); powerful (the guide's Opacity, Blur and
Fit, exactly).

THE CHECKS. verify_socialprofile section 12, five rows, and section 11's
first row (three doors). Thirteen breaks, each turning its own row red: the
door gone (the first; hiding it with the hidden attribute changed nothing,
since the doors' own display wins, so the door was taken out); any file
taken (the first); composehost sending no guide, editor_compose ignoring
it, the face flag gone (the second and the third); no 40% start,
the row's words, the drawer's line (the second); the words not swapped (the
second and third); no backing (the third: 3.54 and 3.49 light, 5.88 and 3.52
dark); the photo kept in the drawing, the photo on the card (the fourth); the
site keeping a photo (the fifth).

Side by side, final tree: verify_socialprofile 47/47, verify_social 36/36,
verify_compose 88/88, verify_example 59/59, verify_parity 434/434,
verify_contrast 628/628, verify_player_isolation 85/85, verify_review
292/292, verify_amber 111/111, verify_ux 487/487, verify_a11ypages
162/162, verify_inline 192/192, verify_clouddrafts 116/116; verify_docs

## After v330 -- "Use one you made" takes drawings made in the Pad

Found while building the face-fit mock (the owner, Nov 11: a traced face
"didn't fit in the circle"), on the live tree since #851: Your face's "Use
one you made" said "That one has a picture under it" to every drawing made
in the Pad, so it could only place drawings a script had posted. The Pad
keeps the canvas as it was when a drawing's first take began under the take
(its frame's baseSnapshot, app.js beginRecording and captureCurrentFrame),
and on a fresh Pad that canvas is empty: a see-through picture. A drawing
drawn in the real Pad on the mock server and posted signed in carried one
(531x944, every pixel's alpha 0, under 235 points), and the picker refused
it. lib/faceframe.js's check() called any base a picture; section 11's
drawings, posted through the API, had none, so no row could see it.

THE FIX, in lib/faceframe.js: inspect(payload), a Promise of check()'s
answer once each base has been looked at by the Pad's own rule for a blank
base (forgetBlankBase, editor_draft.js): any pixel painted, and it is a
picture; one that cannot be read is a picture too, so nothing is left out
unseen. check() still answers at once, a base counting as a picture until
inspect() has seen it blank, and place() takes a base only then, keyed by
the very bases, and leaves it out of the face. The site's picker asks
inspect() and answers only the latest pick (social/static/profile.js).
docs/INTEGRATION.md names inspect() for any host.

Pad and Flip: neither changes. What the Pad saves is as it was (a blank base
under a take is also how a restore tells a fresh Pad from a drawn one); the
face maker reads it. Flip drawings are not faces (check() says 'flip').

THE CHECK. verify_socialprofile section 11, an eighth row: a drawing posted with
the Pad's see-through base is placed, painted whole and kept as a face with
no base and all 60 points; one on a base with ink is still said kindly to
have a picture under it, and the picker stays. Four breaks, each red on that
row alone: the picker asking check() as before (the blank one refused); every
base read as blank (the inked one placed); check() never trusting a base
inspect() saw blank (the blank one refused); place() refusing any base (the
blank one placed, then no face kept).

## After v330 -- Your face fits the circle: the circle after the Pad, its Back, Edit this face

The owner, Nov 11, after tracing a photo for their own face: "when I traced an
image it didn't fit in the circle. there should be a way to adjust the size so
it fits in the circle. also, maybe you should be able to edit it after it's
done rather than have to redraw the whole thing." The mock (phone light and
dark, desk; Now beside it) asked three things, and the answer was "all yes":

1. THE CIRCLE AFTER THE PAD, EVERY TIME. Whatever the Pad's face mode hands
   back, drawn, traced or edited, goes to Your face's circle before it is
   kept, starting with ALL of the drawing inside the circle: Skribl's
   lib/faceframe.js fit(payload), the square whose circle holds every point
   (its size included) with 4% room, kept in range. Before, a face was the
   drawing's middle square, and a traced head and shoulders lost its
   shoulders to the circle without the person seeing it. Dragged, pinched
   and sized as a skribl you made is, then Use this face. A drawing the
   circle cannot take (a base with ink) is kept as it was drawn. Shown
   only when something would be cut off, and fitted with no step at all,
   were the other two options; both decide for the person.
2. EDIT THIS FACE, the first door once there is a face: the face fetched as
   its player fetches it and handed to the Pad (composehost setPayload), so
   it opens finished and locked, Keep drawing showing the way on; then the
   circle.
3. BACK FROM THE CIRCLE is the Pad again, the drawing it handed back still
   in it (composehost reloads it), and, if it was traced, the photo under it
   again: profile.js remembers the photo being traced and sends it again
   (composehost guide); a new drawing or the face you have opens without
   it. The mock showed the gap (the photo was gone after Back), and said so.

ONE THING FOUND BUILDING THE MOCK: the circle came up empty. The place step
lays the drawing out by the stage's width, and laid out while the sheet was
still closed the stage had none; it is laid out again once the sheet is
open. Read every frame now, the drawing is in the circle from the first
frame the sheet is seen, as it rises.

THE OVERLAY, MOVED. The Pad over the page is social.js's SocialPadOverlay,
the controller profile.js had inline, moved out for posts (piece 4, still on
the branch) and shipped here first because the face's circle uses it.

Pad and Flip: the Pad's face mode only; Flip has no faces. Skribl gains
fit() in lib/faceframe.js (docs/INTEGRATION.md), shared with any host.

THE FOUR: kind (nothing redrawn from scratch, and a face is never cut off
unseen; Back keeps the drawing and the photo); simple (one circle, the one
Use one you made already has); playful (drag and pinch your face into
place); powerful (exact size and place, and edit any time).

THE CHECKS. verify_socialprofile section 13, three rows, run through the real
Pad with a pen: (A) after the Pad, the circle glides up with the drawing laid
out in every frame it is seen and painted at once, and a head and shoulders
whose shoulders reach 114 units past the middle square's circle starts with
every line inside, and is kept so; (B) Back is the Pad with all of the
drawing (164 points) and the traced photo again at 40%, and Use brings the
circle back; (C) Edit this face is the first of four doors once there is a
face, and opens the face in the Pad, Keep drawing showing; a line added, the
kept face has both. keep_in_pad goes through the circle, as a person does.
Eight breaks, each red on its row: no circle (all three); the middle square
(A, and C, whose edited face is cut too); not laid out once the sheet is open
(A alone: the drawing 0 wide on every frame, the mock's empty circle);
fit() the middle square (A, C); Back to the picker (B); Back without the
photo (B: no photo, its slider at 100); no Edit door (C); Edit opening the
Pad without the face (C).

Side by side, the PR's tree: verify_socialprofile 51/51, verify_socialauth
62/62, verify_sharecard 32/32, verify_docs 144/144; verify_social 35/36
beside the others and 36/36 alone, INTERMITTENT: its red was Make's sheet's
Esc glide sampled at 6 positions with one 204px step of 304, frames dropped
under three suites at once. Load, not this change: social.js only gained
lines here (SocialPadOverlay), and nothing on the page Make's sheet is read
on calls them. The full battery was not run; main's run after the merge is.
Not tested here: Safari, and a pinch on a real iPhone.

## After v330 -- Your face first, and icons drawn in our pen

The owner, Nov 11, with a picture of Your face's four doors in dark and the
bar's Home and Explore: "do you think those icons represent skribl (or blooby
someday)? theyre good, but the 4 in a column look kinda weak. what do you
think?" Cal's answer: they were stock line icons any app has, four equal
solid tiles reading as a settings list, and the sheet about your face did
not show it. The mock (Now beside B, the same column with drawn icons, and
C, your face first; phone dark and light, desk) and the owner's "all yes":

1. YOUR FACE FIRST (C). The face you have leads Your face, the sheet's one
   big door, Edit this face; it draws itself again each time the sheet
   rises (a fresh copy of the template's lib/face.js once, started from the
   sheet's new onOpen; the still under Reduce Motion and before it plays).
   Before there is one, the empty circle leads, Draw your face. The other
   ways sit side by side under it as tiles, each still saying what it does
   to a screen reader (Trace a photo's "Only your lines are kept" among
   them; the Pad says it again once the photo is in).
2. ICONS DRAWN IN OUR PEN (_icons.html, _pen): the signature's rounded pen,
   one idea across the set, faint is what is already there (the empty
   circle, the photo, at the guide's 40%) and solid is your new line: a
   face with the pen still going, a line looping into the empty circle, a
   photo with your line over it, two drawings you made. In the small violet
   ink on the note's tint: 7.1:1 light, 6.83:1 dark against the tile, where
   the brand's own purple read 3.7:1 (enough for a graphic, dim in dark).
3. EACH DRAWS ITSELF ONCE as the sheet rises: every path one unit long
   (pathLength), drawn in by its dash, the tiles a little after each other;
   still under Reduce Motion.
4. THE BAR'S HOME AND EXPLORE in the same pen, Explore a star to follow
   (Blooby's star); the page you are on still fills its own.

## After v330 -- A frozen sample of the shape picker's fade is taken again

Main's run after #862 (Home holds every drawing) went red on one row, in one
shard of twelve: verify_motion, "the shape picker opens over several frames
-- 0 frames between". Nothing near the picker had changed, and the same row
passed in the PostgreSQL shard on the same tree. On this box it reads 7
frames between, every time. A 300 ms stall on the page's thread two frames
into the 0.18 s fade reads it red: the frozen sample the drawer glide met
after v322 ("A frozen sample read as a jump"), where the compositor carries
the fade on while the sampler, on the stalled thread, reads nothing.

- The shape picker's open and its close are taken again, at most twice, and
  only when a take failed with a frame longer than half the fade (90 ms). A
  real cut has no frames between however far apart its frames are, so a
  second look cannot turn one green.

  frame, so the next red says whether the picker froze, opened late or cut.
- The suite's other fades keep their one take until one is seen frozen.

the close, fails the old row and passes the new one ("taken again after
frames of [300] ms"); the open's @starting-style removed, or the close's

## After v330 -- A person signed in no longer looks signed out while SQLite is busy

Main's run after #864 went red on one row: verify_socialposts section 9, a
drawing's own page, where its own author's ⋯ offered "Report this post"
instead of "Delete post". The page had taken her for nobody. Side by side on
this box it failed one run in three, and the server's log said why: "database
is locked", then "the site could not read its people".

The site read who is signed in on a connection of its own. Skribl's SQLite
recipe begins a request's transaction at its first read, so a request that
has read anything holds the read lock to its end. A second connection's read
then queued behind a writer waiting to commit (here, another page's player
fetching its drawing), and that writer waited for the first request's lock:
each waited on the other for the 5 s busy timeout, the read failed, and the
page showed nobody signed in. The same was true of the author resolver,
which names the site's people on Skribl's own pages.

- security.read_aside: a read beside the request's own work goes through the
  request's session once that has begun (sharing the lock it holds), and on a
  connection of its own, closed at once, before (so it never begins the
  request's transaction, which a limit's commit would then wait on). Who is
  signed in and describe_author both read through it.

Pad and Flip: not affected (who is signed in, read on the site).

THE CHECKS, in verify_txcontract: with a request that has read and a writer
waiting to commit behind it, who is signed in and whose drawing this is are
read at once, the right person; the writer then commits; and before the
request has read, those reads leave its transaction unbegun. The old code
stalls both reads 5.0 s and fails them ("database is locked"); always reading
through the session leaves the transaction begun, red on the last row. The
section that went red ran six times side by side after: six green, no lock
in any server's log.

## After v330 -- Report and block at /social (piece 5, its first part)

The owner, Nov 12, "all yes on both" to the Safety mock and the comments
mock. Safety comes first, in three parts: report and block (this), your
Reports page with what a maker sees once something is taken down, and the
draft rules pages.

- REPORT ANYTHING. A profile's ⋯ (beside Share, never on your own) says
  Report @them and, signed in, Block @them. A person has their own reasons:
  spam or a fake account, abusive or hateful, pretending to be someone, under
  13, a child's safety, something else. A post's and a drawing's Report has
  the Gallery's reasons and a child's safety, and now goes to the site's own
  queue (social_reports, on the site's chain), not Skribl's: the site owns
  the moderation of people and words, and a person's report is the site's.
  A report is a row, never an action. Who sent it is kept for the admins'
  eyes only (reporter_id); one reporter makes one row for one thing (a keyed
  hash of the person, or for somebody signed out their address). Anybody who
  can see the thing can report it, signed in or not: a child's safety must
  never wait on an account, so a post's and a profile's pages carry their
  token for everybody now.
- SKRIBL'S OWN REPORT offers a child's safety too (REPORT_REASONS; the
  Gallery's sheet renders from it), and `takedown --reports` lists those
  first, with a word about the law (in the US, reporting to NCMEC; the
  owner's lawyer sets that up).
- BLOCK, BOTH WAYS AND QUIETLY. From a profile's ⋯ or a post's ⋯, asked once
  in its own words. While it stands neither sees the other's posts or
  drawings (Home, a post's page, a drawing's page, More from); to the one
  blocked the blocker's profile is "Nobody here by that name"; the blocker
  finds theirs saying so, with Unblock, and nothing they made; nobody is
  told. Settings lists the people you blocked, newest first, each with
  Unblock; only the blocker lifts a block. Deleting an account takes its
  blocks; a report that names it stays, naming nobody.
- A BLOCK REACHES SKRIBL'S PAGES through the two seams Skribl gives every
  host for a block list: a feed filter (Explore's gallery, a profile's
  skribls, Home's drawings) and a visibility policy (a drawing's link page,
  payload and card; the card falls back to its blank canvas, as it always
  has for a drawing somebody may not see). The host installs both, asking
  social.blocked_authors(viewer_id), as it installs the author resolver
  (app.py). The site reads it beside Skribl's own work through read_aside
  (the deadlock #865 fixed), never on a second connection once that work
  has read.

Pad and Flip: not affected (who sees whose drawings, and the reports' words).

THE FOUR: kind (nothing is taken down by a report alone, nobody is told of a
block, and a child's safety is one tap away for anybody); simple (⋯ on a
person, as on a post; Settings holds who you blocked); playful (nothing
here gets in the way of a drawing); powerful (both ways, everywhere a
drawing shows, Skribl's pages too).

THE CHECKS. verify_socialsafety, ten sections and twenty rows, its own
server: reporting somebody (the ⋯, a person's reasons in order, the queue's
row, once per reporter, signed out with no sender); a post and a drawing
into the site's queue, Skribl's untouched; the report guards and limit;
blocking from a profile and from Home, both ways on every page of the
site's; Skribl's listings, link page, payload and card both ways, the author
and anybody else unaffected, and no "install a feed filter" warning in the
server's log; Settings' list and Unblock, the blocker's alone; the block
guards and limit; deleting an account; Skribl's own sheet and queue; every
new screen's words, targets and fields, phone and desk, light and dark; no
page or console errors. Twenty-three breaks, each red on its row: a person's reasons out of order; who sent
a report not kept; Block offered signed out; the post's sheet sending a reason it was not given; a drawing
reported as a post; a hidden character let through; no limit on reports; the blocker's profile not saying
so; Home without the block; Home not saying it; no feed filter; no visibility policy; the policy hiding
everybody's from everybody else; Settings oldest first; either side lifting a block; blocking yourself; no
limit on blocks; neither the code nor the cascade taking an account's blocks; a report deleted with the
person it names; Skribl without a child's safety; its queue most-reported first only; no word about the
law; the blocked profile's words faint; safety.js throwing once loaded. Two were green or stopped first:
without the feed filter the listing still read right, because Skribl gives the policy the last word,
drops the rows it refuses and refills the page, saying so once in the log (the row now reads the log);
and a block lifted by the wrong side left no Unblock to press, which stopped the suite (now recorded).
verify_socialposts' ⋯ rows now say Block and the site's queue, and
verify_socialauth's chain eight tables.

## After v330 -- Your Reports at /social (piece 5, its second part)

The same "all yes on both" (Nov 12): the Safety mock's Reports page, and what
a maker sees once something is taken down.

- AN ADMIN'S PAGE, AND ONLY THEIRS. /social/reports, with Take it down and
  Keep it as forms (social/reports.py). Anybody else, signed in or not, meets
  the same 404 as a page that is not there, as Invites does. Settings tells an
  admin how many things wait.
- ONE QUEUE FROM TWO. The site's own reports and Skribl's (what people
  reported on Skribl's own pages: Explore's tiles, a drawing's link page) on
  the same cards, a post's drawing reported on Explore on the post's card.
  Skribl gains two seams for any host's own reports page,
  list_reports(limit) and close_reports(public_id) (skribl/moderation.py,
  docs/INTEGRATION.md "Your own reports page"): read the open reports a group
  per drawing, a child's safety first, naming nobody; close one drawing's,
  taking nothing down. takedown --reports reads the same groups.
- A CARD PER THING, a child's safety first, then the newest. Its card is
  ringed, its picture and words blurred until Open it, and Keep it and its
  page's link come only once it is opened: nobody should meet that picture by
  accident, and nobody should dismiss it unseen. It says what the law may ask
  (in the US, reporting to NCMEC; the owner's lawyer sets that up). Every card
  says what and whose, each reason and how many gave it, what reporters wrote
  and who they are (somebody signed out, somebody on Explore), seen only here.
- TAKE IT DOWN deletes nothing. A post is gone for everybody but its author,
  its drawing withheld in Skribl (set_post_visibility as an operator); a
  drawing is withheld; a person is nobody to everybody else, and all they
  made is hidden, on the site's pages and Skribl's (the host's hooks now ask
  social.hidden_authors, which the first part called blocked_authors: a
  block either way, and anybody taken down). A person taken down can still
  sign in, see their own with the note, and delete their account; nothing new
  is shared from it (taken_down, said kindly in the post box). Its maker sees
  "Taken down: it broke the rules. Only you can see it." Every report on it
  is closed, Skribl's too, saying who answered and when. KEEP IT closes them
  and hides nothing. taken_down_at on social_people and social_posts holds it
  (a migration on the site's chain). No undo on the page yet: nothing is
  deleted, so a takedown can be lifted by hand.

Pad and Flip: not affected (who sees whose drawings, and an admin's page).

THE FOUR: kind (a report is answered by a person, never a count; the maker
is told, in plain words, and loses nothing; a child's safety is looked at
first and never by accident); simple (two answers, one card per thing);
playful (nothing in the way of a drawing for anybody who keeps the rules);
powerful (one queue for the site and Skribl, and a takedown that reaches
every page a drawing shows on).

## After v330 -- Comments at /social (phase 2, comments)

The owner, Nov 12, "all yes on both" to the Safety mock and the comments
mock. Safety came first (piece 5); this is the comments mock, built in its
own classes, sizes and words (`social/comments.py`, `_comments.html`,
`comments.js`), in two parts: words, then drawing answers.

- THE SECTION. On a post's own page "Comments" and how many replace
  "Comments open soon". The box on top is Home's composer in the mock's size
  (.cm-box): your face, the words, Post. Comments come newest first, each its
  face, name, a short time ("40m", "2h", posts.js's own), its words (line
  breaks kept), Answer and ⋯; twenty a page, then Load more.
- ANSWERS, ONE LEVEL DEEP, oldest first under their comment. Answering an
  answer puts the new one under the same comment (parent_id is always a
  top-level comment's). Answer brings the box there, "Answer Theo…"; Answer
  again, Esc or Post sends it home.
- KIND, NEVER JUMPY. The comment keeps its place on the screen while the box
  moves (the page scrolls by what moved above it, the browser's own scroll
  anchoring held off for that one change so the two never both move it; an
  iPhone has none); the box fades in where it lands; a new comment fades in,
  a deleted one fades out. FOUND IN THE PICTURES, FIXED BEFORE THEY WERE
  SHOWN: under a long thread, Answer left the box below the fold, under the
  phone's bar, so a person would type into a field they cannot see. The page
  now glides down to it (scrollBy, smooth; put there at once under Reduce
  Motion).
- WHO MAY COMMENT: somebody signed in, not taken down, with no block either
  way with the post's author; answering, none with the comment's author
  either. The route refuses anybody else kindly (gone, signed_out,
  taken_down: each said in the box), and the box is not shown to them.
  Signed out, the comments are readable and "Sign in to answer" (the small
  violet words Sign in wears at the top of a phone) stands in the box's
  place, back to the post once signed in. Words are a post's (check_words:
  tidied, 500 at most, nothing hidden or turned around); a comment needs
  words (and, from the second part, or a drawing). 60 an hour a person.
- HIDDEN, NEITHER SHOWN NOR COUNTED: nothing by anybody a block either way
  or a takedown hides from the viewer, nor any answer under such a comment,
  on the post's page and on Home's card alike (comments.counts reads the same
  rules as the page). A comment taken down is its author's alone, with "Taken
  down: it broke the rules. Only you can see it."
- THE ⋯, as the post's: "Your comment", Delete comment; on your own post
  somebody else's, "Theo’s comment", Remove from my post and Report comment;
  anybody else's, Report comment (signed out too). Delete and Remove go at
  once, as the mock has them (the ⋯ is the asking), the comment fading out
  with its answers. Report rises as "Report this comment" with a post's
  reasons (REASONS['comment']; KINDS gains comment) into the site's own
  queue. Your Reports shows a comment's card: whose face, "Theo Lind @theo ·
  a comment", its first line, a link to it on its post's page; Take it down
  sets taken_down_at, deleting nothing; Keep it closes, hiding nothing.
- HOME'S CARD says how many beside the plays: the comment icon and the
  number, "3 comments", a link to the post's comments, 44px; nothing at none.
  On a desk the comments sit beside the drawing, under Share.
- DATA: social_comments on the site's chain (e4b8c2a91f37), indexed by
  address, a post's newest first, a comment's answers oldest first, a
  person's, a drawing's. DELETING IS SAID IN CODE: a comment with its answers
  (drop_comments), a post with its comments (drop_post), an account with its
  comments and every answer under them (delete_person). The schema's ON
  DELETE CASCADEs are a net, not the way. The brief said SQLite does not
  enforce them here; it does, in the demo: Skribl's pragma hook turns
  foreign keys on for the engine the site shares (measured: deleting a
  person's row took their posts). So the route-level rows cannot see a
  missing line of that code, and a probe runs the three deletions on a copy
  of the database with SKRIBL_SQLITE_FOREIGN_KEYS=0, the documented opt-out.
- COUNTED, NOT KEPT. docs/SOCIAL-SITE.md section 3's rule 3 keeps counts as
  stored numbers. A comment count that hides what a block hides is each
  viewer's own, so it is counted: one grouped query a page, on the post's
  own index. A kept count waits for a measurement that asks for one.
- A drawing shown outside a post (/social/b/<id>) has no comments: they are
  a post's, so its page lost the "open soon" note rather than keep a promise
  this does not keep.

Pad and Flip: not affected in this first part (words; the drawing answers of
the second part open them as they are).

THE FOUR: kind (a refusal says why in the box and blames nobody; nobody is
