## After v330 -- Comments on every drawing, and a card opens its post from its words and its time

The owner, Nov 12, yes to both. Comments shipped that morning (#872) on
posts only, the rows Home's box makes; but Home, profiles and More from also
show drawings shared outside a post (a skribl made in the Pad or Flip on
their own pages and shown in the gallery: `/social/b/<id>`, kind `s` in
posts.cards), and most of the owner's own drawings are that kind, since
Make's Draw and Flip post from the editors' own sheets. The two look the same
to people, so the owner opened several and found no comment box: "there was
comments on one of them though. weird?"

1. "Comments on every drawing, however it was made, so whatever you open has
   the comment box."
2. "Easier to open a post: tap its words, its name line or its time; the 💬
   shows even at zero."
3. Then, the same day, a plain yes to anywhere on a card opening its post:
   but the drawing, which plays and pauses and never opens the post; the
   face and the name, the person's page; ⋯ and Share, their own jobs; the
   💬, the comments; and a drag that selects words opens nothing.

- ON A DRAWING TOO. A drawing's own page has a post's comments: the box (Draw
  and Flip in it open the editors over the drawing's page), answers one level
  deep, drawing answers, the ⋯ (its maker removes, as a post's author does,
  in the words the drawing's ⋯ already uses: "Remove from my post"), Report
  into the site's queue, Load more, and the count on Home's card. Its own
  routes, `/social/b/<skribl_id>/comments` (POST a comment or an answer, GET
  the next page); `/social/c/<id>/delete` is both kinds'.
- ITS PAGE DECIDES, AND ITS COMMENTS FOLLOW IT. posts.bloob is the drawing
  page's rule, now one function the page and every comment route read
  (comments.on_drawing): Skribl describes it to the viewer (deleted, withheld
  or private to somebody else is absent, and so is what the host's visibility
  policy hides: a block, a person taken down); public, or withheld and
  theirs; its maker one of the site's people, not taken down unless it is
  them; no block either way. A post's drawing is its post's, and so are its
  comments. A block either way with its maker, the drawing taken down, its
  maker taken down, or the drawing deleted in the Library: its page is a kind
  404, and its comments are neither read (Load more), said, answered nor
  reported. Its maker still sees them on a drawing taken down, with the note
  and no box, as on a post. An answer is on what its comment is on: one
  naming a comment on another drawing, or on a post, is refused.
- THE DATA, the shape decided with the yes: social_comments.post_id nullable;
  drawing_id, the drawing's skribl public id (Skribl's: the site has no row
  of its own for a drawing); a CHECK that exactly one is set
  (ck_social_comments_on_one); owner_id, whose the post or the drawing is,
  ON DELETE CASCADE, so deleting an account and a block never ask Skribl
  whose a drawing was. POSTS CARRY IT TOO (the brief left it ours), for one
  code path: Remove reads it for both kinds, an account's comments on what it
  owned go by it, and the comments already there are filled from their
  posts' authors, then NOT NULL. Indexed for a drawing's comments newest
  first and by owner. One migration on the site's chain (ded60afbc86d); a
  comment whose post is not there (none can be) is deleted rather than stop
  the chain at NOT NULL. The downgrade deletes the comments on drawings,
  there being no post for them to be on; their drawing answers stay in
  Skribl, unlisted, since the site's chain never touches Skribl's tables.
  PostgreSQL: the DDL was rendered offline (alembic --sql) and read; not run
  here.
- DELETING, IN CODE. A drawing deleted through the site (its ⋯, Delete post)
  takes its comments and their drawing answers (comments.drop_drawing_comments),
  only after delete_post has said it was theirs: a refused delete still
  commits, so dropping first would let anybody's try empty a drawing's
  comments. An account takes every comment on what it owned
  (comments.drop_owner_comments, by owner_id) before its own and the answers
  under them.
- NOT DONE: a drawing deleted in the Library (Skribl's own page) takes its
  page, and so its comments, from everybody at once, but their rows stay
  until its maker's account goes, or each commenter's: Skribl tells a host
  nothing when a drawing is deleted on its own pages. A seam for that (or a
  sweep asking describe_posts as the maker, which sees anything of theirs
  that still exists) would let the site delete them then.
- EASY TO OPEN, on Home's cards (More from's tiles were whole links already;
  a profile shows Skribl's Gallery, not these cards). The words and the time
  are each a link to the card's own page, a post's or a drawing's; the 💬
  shows even at none, its icon alone, named "Comment", a 44px way to
  #comments, where the number would be. THE NAME LINE KEEPS GOING TO THE
  PERSON, the brief's call, said here because the owner's words were "tap
  its words, its name line or its time": the name and the @handle go to a
  profile everywhere on the site, and so do they here, and the face.
- ANYWHERE ON A CARD (3): a tap or a click on a card's own ground opens its
  page (posts.js: one that landed on nothing with a job of its own). The
  card is not one big link, which a screen reader would read as one: its
  words and its time stay its real links. The drawing plays and pauses and
  never opens the post; it is set apart three ways (the card's tap leaves
  .post-art alone, the player's box is a button by its role, and the player
  stops its own taps, which Skribl's player has done since v316 for hosts
  that make a whole post a link). The face, the name and the @handle, ⋯ and
  Share, and the 💬 keep their own. A press that moved more than a few
  pixels is a drag, and a click that ends a text selection opens nothing, a
  link's included. Ctrl or ⌘, or the middle button, opens a new tab, as a
  link's would. A keyboard's click is never read as a drag. On a desk the
  card shows a pointer (hover and a fine pointer only); a phone's card is
  unchanged.
- THE WORDS SELECT AS WORDS. Found by its row, red on the tree as first
  built: in Chromium a link's text cannot be selected by pressing and
  pulling (the link drags itself), and with only draggable="false" it still
  selects nothing while the press, let go on the same link, follows it. The
  words' link is draggable="false" with -webkit-user-drag: none and
  user-select: text, so they select; the click that ends the selection is
  then stopped. (Measured on a bare page first: each property alone, and
  each pair, before the card's.)
- NOTHING ON THE CARD MOVED, measured before and after on HEAD and this tree,
  four cards (a post with words and one without, a drawing with a title and
  one without) on four screens (phone and desk, light and dark): every
  painted word, the drawing and the footer at the same pixel, the 💬 at none
  the only new paint. The line had been one link, the name, @handle and time,
  the finger's 44px. Now the name's link lies under the @handle's line too
  (padding given back by a negative margin, from the two lines' own heights,
  so it holds in any face), and the @handle lets a tap through to it; the
  time's link lies over it, 44px wide at least and 44px tall by reaching
  down into the room under its line, toward the words, whose link goes where
  it goes. THE TIME ON A CARD WITH NO WORDS, a judgment call: its box reaches
  about 11px over the top edge of the drawing, and the drawing lies over
  that (its own stacking order), since the drawing never opens the post. So
  there the time's own tap is the 33px from its line to the drawing; the
  card's ground beside and above the drawing opens the post too, and so does
  its plays link (44px, the same page). Its box is still 44px by its rect,
  which is all verify_socialposts section 7's census reads; section 10 reads
  the paint, and there the time's lower corners land on the drawing. The
  other ways to a 44px time were moving it
  to the right of the header, or a taller header on a card with no words,
  both of which change the card; this was first built the other way round
  (the time over the drawing's edge), until the owner's addition said the
  drawing never opens the post. The words' link is the paragraph, 10px of
  padding above and below given back by margins, so a one-line post's is
  44px; the ⋯ stays over all of it. Focus rings: the name's around both
  lines as the line's was; the time's hugs the time. Measured again on the
  final tree: the same sixteen renderings at the same pixels.

Pad and Flip: not affected; a drawing answer on a drawing opens them over its
page in compose mode, as on a post (lib/composehost.js, the site's one
overlay). Neither editor changed.

THE FOUR: kind (whatever is opened has the box; a drawing gone, blocked or
taken down takes its comments with it and nobody is told; a refused delete
takes nothing; a drag that selects words is never taken for a tap); simple

## After v330 -- Activity at /social (phase 2, notifications)

The owner, Nov 12, "all yes" to the notifications mock made that day: A of
its three (a bell at the top right of a phone's Home and Explore, Activity in
a desk's rail; B was a fifth place in the bar, C a "New for you" card on
Home), the dot's colour, the Activity list as drawn, and one extra: a drawing
answer opened from Activity draws itself once when you land. Built in the
mock's own classes, sizes and words (`social/activity.py`, `activity.html`,
and comments.js for the landing).

- WHERE IT LIVES. Signed in, a bell drawn in our pen (the _pen set: 24
  units, the signature's round pen at 2.1, each line one unit long) at the
  top right of a phone's Home and Explore, where Sign in sits before you sign
  in: 44px, named "Activity", "Activity, something new" with its dot. On a
  desk, Activity in the rail after Explore, on every page; on its own page
  the rail's bell is filled, as Home's house is, with the pen's line under
  its name. THE BAR KEEPS ITS FOUR: Activity is not in it, and on Activity's
  own page a phone's top says "Activity" with the way back, as a post's says
  "Post"; the page's own heading is then a screen reader's (a desk shows it).
- THE DOT, a new token for a new job: --new-dot, Blooby's blush a shade
  deeper on light (#e64a78, 3.64:1 on the page, where his own blush reads
  2.58:1, under the 3:1 a mark needs) and his blush itself on dark
  (var(--blooby-blush), 7.34:1). Ringed in the page's own ground, so it stands
  clear of the line; each new row in the list wears it too. IT GOES AS YOU
  LOOK: a tap on the bell lets it fade while Activity opens (social.js), so a
  page the back button brings back whole has it gone too; on a desk's Activity
  page the rail's fades once the page is there. A fade, never a move, so
  Reduce Motion keeps it.
- THE LIST, AS DRAWN. New, then Earlier, a dot on each new row. A row is a
  comment or an answer, not yours: answering you ("Theo answered your
  comment", with a drawing "Juno answered with a drawing"), else on what you
  own, a post or a drawing shown outside a post ("Mira said something on your
  post", with a drawing "Juno drew something on your post"). Their face, when
  as comments say it, their words under it in quotes (two lines at most), the
  small picture (the drawing they answered with or drew, else the post's,
  cut from its poster as More from's tiles are), and one link to the comment
  on its page (#c-<id>, a post's or a drawing's).
- GROUPED SINCE YOU LAST LOOKED, as the words say: several on one post, or
  answering you in one conversation, are one row, the newest face in front
  and the next behind, the newest words, opening the newest ("Mira and 2
  others", "Mira and Theo" for two). A drawing keeps its own row. EARLIER
  KEEPS A ROW FOR EACH, a judgment call read off the approved pictures, whose
  Earlier shows the cottage's two comments as two rows: grouping is what was
  new since you looked, and history is said as it was said. So a group of
  three in New is three rows under Earlier next time.
- SEEN IS OPENING IT. The page reads the list, then keeps on your row the
  time it was opened (the time taken before the list is read, so a comment
  made meanwhile is still new next time). The rows that were new keep their
  dot while you are there; next time they sit under Earlier. Nothing to tick.
- NEVER IN IT: yourself; anybody a block either way or a takedown hides; a
  comment taken down; an answer under a comment you are not shown; anything on
  a post or a drawing whose page you cannot see (a block either way with its
  maker, it or its maker taken down, a drawing deleted in the Library or no
  longer public). comments.seen's rules, read for many comments at once, so
  every row lands on a comment that is there. The dot reads the same rules,
  so it never promises a row the list will not show.
- LANDING. The comment glows a moment in the note's tint, the comment alone
  and not the answers under it (its own height, set by comments.js), then the
  tint fades over a second and a half; nothing moves, so Reduce Motion keeps
  the fade. One on a later page of comments is brought in with Load more, a
  page at a time (ten at most), and the page glides to it; under Reduce
  Motion it is put there. THE DRAW-ONCE: a drawing answer opened this way
  draws itself once, sound off, never under Reduce Motion, and THE POST'S OWN
  WAITS, a judgment call: Skribl's player plays one post at a time, so both
  started would have the later stop the earlier, and the one you came for is
  the answer. Landing at words, the post's own plays as on any visit.
  posts.js asks comments.js (window.SocialPlayOwn) when the address names a
  comment; otherwise nothing about a post's page changed.
- NOTHING YET: Blooby as his Home Screen icon in small (the sign-in pages'
  own), "Nothing new yet", the mock's words, and "Make a skribl", which opens
  Make's sheet. The brief left the word to me ("Make something" or the
  mock's): "Make a skribl" is what the first visit's button says, and it
  opens the same sheet; same role, same words.
- WORKED OUT FROM THE COMMENTS, NOT KEPT, as the brief preferred: no table of
  notifications to keep in step with them, so a comment deleted, removed or
  hidden takes its row with it at once and nothing is ever swept. TWO THINGS
  ARE KEPT, on the site's chain (c276c1445bc1): social_people.activity_seen_at
  (nothing until you first look: then everything is new), and
  social_comments.to_person_id, WHOM AN ANSWER ANSWERS, a departure from the
  brief's "owner_id, parent_id, created_at", for a real reason: an answer to
  an answer sits under the same top-level comment, whoever wrote that, so
  parent_id cannot say whom it answered, and "answered your comment" would
  miss every answer to an answer, though the box said "Answer Nico…". The
  answers already there were filled from the comment they sit under (all an
  answer kept until now). It is set to nothing, in code, when that person's
  account goes (accounts.delete_person; ON DELETE SET NULL is the net).
  Answers to you in one conversation group by the comment they sit under.
- CHEAP, AS ASKED. Indexed newest first by whose (owner_id, created_at),
  which takes the place of the owner's own index (it starts with it, so
  deleting an account and the cascade still use it), and by whom
  (to_person_id, created_at). The dot is two searches, one on each index,
  since you last looked, twenty rows at most, and Skribl is asked only when
  every new one is on a drawing (whether its page is still there); asked once
  a request (the phone's bell and the desk's rail are the same page), by a
  page with the bell or the rail. SQLite's own plan for the code's own query
  says SEARCH on each index, no scan and no sort. The page reads the newest
  100 comments. A DESK'S RAIL HAS THE DOT ON EVERY PAGE (the mock's "on a
  desk the rail names it, always in view"), so every signed-in page with the
  rail asks it, not Home and Explore alone: the same two searches.
- PRIVACY says what is kept: "And when you last looked at Activity, so it
  can tell you what's new."

Pad and Flip: not affected. This is the site's chrome and its own page; a
drawing answer made in either shows its small picture the same way and,
opened from Activity, draws itself in the in-post player it always had.

THE FOUR: kind (one quiet dot, gone once you look, never a count shouting;
nobody hidden or blocked ever surfaces, and nothing is lost: what was new
sits under Earlier); simple (a bell at the top right is read without being
told; one tap from a row to the comment, which glows so you see which);
playful (a bell drawn in our pen, its dot Blooby's blush; a drawing answer
draws itself as you arrive); powerful (every answer in one list, grouped
since you looked, a tap from its comment; Load more brings an old one).

CONTRAST, measured on the built pages, as the mock quoted: the bell's line
17.47:1 light and 17.17:1 dark at the top, 7.36:1 and 10.49:1 in the rail;
the dot 3.64:1 and 7.34:1 (a mark's 3:1); a landed comment on the tint, its

and on the chrome with the bell, phone (touch) and desk, light and dark:

(part 2, with a marks seam of its own), and the comment box as an icon,

- THE HEART ON THE DRAWING'S LINE (way 3). A lilac pill, [♡ 4], at the start
  of the line under every drawing, before the scrubber, on Home's cards and on
  a post's page and a drawing's (`/social/b/<id>`) alike: the player's lead
  (below). Dressed as the loop button at the line's other end: 32px tall, its
  lilac and the line's ink, its hover and focus ring; a 44px tap area from the
  drawing's edge to 2px under the pill, 6px either side, clear of the 1×
  speed's (whose own reaches 10px up from the words). The scrubber gives it
  the room, 59px with one figure (the mock's 49px pill and 10px), 42px at
  none, and NOTHING ELSE MOVES: a card's foot (plays, comments, Share) and a
  page's time-and-plays line are what they were before likes, and a line with
  the heart is the height of one without. The old places (beside Share on the
  card, the end of the time-and-plays line) are gone. `aria-pressed`, named
  "Like" or "Liked" with how many ("Like, 4 likes"); hidden on anything taken
  down, its maker's view too.
- ITS COUNT inside it, none at zero (just the heart, a 32px circle). Its line
  is the line's ink until you like it; liked, Blooby's blush inside and round
  it a NEW TOKEN FOR A NEW JOB, --heart-line, the line a step deeper on light
  as way 3 said (#d11a32, the dots' third step), his blush itself on dark.
  --heart (#e64a78, the bell dot's) stays the liked line off the pill:
  Activity's small heart. A JUDGMENT CALL: THE HEART KEEPS ONE PLACE, 7px
  into the pill, with a count or without. The mock had 7px at none and 8px
  with a count, which a count that comes or goes would turn into a pixel's
  hop under your finger; the count's gap is 5px instead of 4, so the pill is
  the mock's to the pixel (49px with "4") and only the heart sits 1px further
  in. Being on the line, it shows when the line does, once the player has
  started it, and A SECOND JUDGMENT CALL, the player's own rule kept: while a
  drawing can't be shown (one deleted in the Library, or a dropped connection
  until a tap retries) the line steps away and the heart with it; the likes
  are kept, and it comes back with the line.
- LIKING, KIND AND NEVER JUMPY, as the mock drew it: the blush line draws
  itself round from the notch (0.36s), the blush fills in behind it and the
  line's ink fades under it; nothing grows, bounces or moves. TAKING IT BACK
  FADES (0.2s), nothing un-drawing (a class for each way, `.lk-anim` and
  `.lk-fade`: the mock's CSS alone would have snapped the line off and
  un-drawn it). A COUNT THAT COMES fades in as the pill grows round it, the
  heart never moving and the scrubber giving up its room a frame at a time
  (0.22s); one that goes fades first, then the pill closes round the heart.
  Under Reduce Motion it only fades, the pill taking its width at once.
- ONE LIKE A PERSON A THING, the same tap taking it back; you may like your
  own. The page changes at once and tells the site what it should now be (a
  yes or a no, never "toggle", so a retry cannot flip it twice), ONE REQUEST
  AT A TIME A HEART: quick taps end where the last one left them, and the
  site's answer is what stays. One that did not take goes back and the page
  says why, kindly ("That isn't here anymore. Reload the page to see what's
  new."). The heart sits inside the player's line, which keeps its clicks
  from a post that is a link, so likes.js reads them while capturing.
- HOW MANY is everyone's, COUNTED BY THE VIEWER as comment counts are: a like
  by anybody hidden from them (a block either way, or taken down) is neither
  shown nor counted, anywhere. Home asks once for all its cards: one grouped
  read a kind (posts, drawings).
- WHO MAY LIKE: signed in, not taken down, on what is open to them, read
  through the comments' own comments.On (there for everybody, no block either
  way with its maker; a post's own drawing is liked through its post, even
  when it is in the gallery too); the token and Origin first, then the
  limit, A JUDGMENT CALL: 120 an hour a person, likes and taking back alike
  (comments' is 60; a heart is lighter and gets tapped twice). Signed out,
  the heart is there all the same; a tap raises the mock's small sheet ("Like
  this drawing?", "Sign in, and a tap on the heart lets Mira know you like
  it.", Not now, Sign in), which comes back to the same page, where the heart
  waits: nothing pressed for them.
- EACH LIKE KEEPS ITS MOMENT, from day one, so the dots can come with
  nothing lost: at_ms, where the drawing's replay was when the heart was
  tapped while it played, ON THE DRAWING'S OWN REPLAY CLOCK (the same moment
  watched at a quarter or at sixteen times), nothing when it was still or
  paused (it counts all the same). The site keeps a whole number of ms from 0
  to a day, else nothing.
- "LIKED BY…", THE MAKER'S ALONE. On their own post's or drawing's page,
  under the time-and-plays line: the newest three faces and "Liked by Mira,
  Ada and 3 others" (every name up to three, else two and how many more; YOU
  FIRST when one is yours, a judgment call), newest first. It opens the sheet
  of who, Make's own sheet in its paper with the people on one card, newest
  first: face, name, @handle, when, and under when the moment their heart
  landed ("0:06") where one was kept, with a dot in --heart; each row their
  page; "Only you can see who liked it." It lists the newest 200; the count
  is exact. Nobody else is sent any of it, not in the page and not in its
  source. The maker's own like, given or taken back, answers with the line
  and the rows as they now stand, so the line never says "you" after they
  took theirs back; the line's room opens and closes.
- ACTIVITY: a like is a row like a comment's, its face wearing a small liked
  heart: "Mira liked your post", when, the post's small picture (a drawing's
  own, outside a post). Grouped since you last looked, the newest face in
  front ("Mira and 4 others liked your post"); a like says no words, so
  EARLIER KEEPS LIKES ONE ROW A POST too, as the mock said. A like row opens
  the post at "Liked by…" (#liked), which glows a moment in the note's tint
  and fades, as a landed comment does. LIKES NEVER LIGHT THE BELL'S DOT (the
  mock's recommendation, in the "all yes"): they wait under New, with their
  own dot. Never yourself, never anybody hidden. The heading's line and the
  empty page's words are the mock's.
- DELETING IS REAL, AND SAID IN CODE: a post goes with its likes
  (posts.drop_post), a drawing deleted through the site with its likes
  (posts.bloob_delete: a drawing's likes have no cascade under them at all),
  an account with its own likes and every like on what it made
  (accounts.delete_person). The ON DELETE CASCADEs are the net. Privacy and
  docs/LAWYER-NOTE.md say likes are kept: who liked what, when, and where in
  the replay.
- DATA, on the site's chain (a81c5c4dde3a, after c276c1445bc1): social_likes,
  shaped as social_comments is: on a post or a drawing, exactly one (a
  CHECK); owner_id, person_id, at_ms, created_at; unique on (person, post)
  and (person, drawing); indexed by the thing and when (counts, and who,
  newest first) and by whose and when (Activity, since you last looked and
  before, each one search).
- TWO SEAMS IN SKRIBL'S IN-POST PLAYER, both general, both documented in
  docs/INTEGRATION.md; Skribl never knows they are likes. WHERE THE PLAYHEAD
  IS: `player.playhead()` answers { ms, playing } from the clock the player
  already keeps (on the drawing's own clock, clamped to its length); it only
  reads. A CONTROL AT THE LINE'S START: `skribl_inline(..., lead=markup)`
  puts one control of a host's first in the line, before the scrubber, in
  the loop button's dress, with the 44px tap area; the scrubber gives it the
  room and nothing else on the line moves; it shows with the line; with
  line=False there is none; a click on the line stops at the line. Nothing
  of the player's names what a host puts there. EMBED_RATCHET raised by each
  cost, written beside it: +100 B (playhead(), inlineplayer.js) and +448 B
  (the lead, inlineplayer.css: its dress joins the loop's own rules for
  ground, ink, hover and focus ring instead of repeating them; 570 B down to
  448 with the focus ring added), 78,941 B measured.

Pad and Flip: SHARED, ONE PLAYER. Both seams are on the in-post player that
plays Pad drawings and Flips alike: a like on a Flip keeps its moment on its
pages' clock, and a Flip's line wears the heart as a drawing's does
(verify_inline lays out and presses the lead on both, and plays the
playhead on both). Nothing changes in either editor, and nothing is left for
Flip to catch up on.

THE FOUR: kind (no number at zero; who liked it is the maker's alone; a like
never pulls you back to the bell; a refused tap goes back gently and says
why; signing in presses nothing for you; the heart never hops under your
finger); simple (one heart in one place under every drawing, dressed as the
button beside it, so it reads as a button; the same tap takes it back);
playful (the line draws itself round in Blooby's blush, right where the
replay plays; a like row lands with "Liked by…" glowing); powerful (every
like keeps its moment, for the dots to come; the maker sees who and when in
the replay).

## After v330 -- Likes at /social, part 2: the dots and the rising hearts

The owner, Nov 13, on the likes mock: "I like d.", then "Just put a smaller
dot (same color as blooby blush) wherever someone likes it. If it doubles
someone it gets redder.", then "All yes, b". Part 1 kept each like's moment
from day one; this piece shows them, as the mock's "D, drawn your way" drew
it: the pink dots on the drawing's line and the hearts that rise from them
as the replay plays, on a general seam of Skribl's player. NOT IN THIS
PIECE, as briefed: the comment box as an icon, which is being decided
(post.html is untouched).

- ONE SMALL DOT A LIKE, AT ITS MOMENT: 5px on a phone and a desk alike, over
  the line under the drawing, in the middle of the 17px between the drawing
  and the scrubber. No bigger dots, no numbers. WHERE THE LINE ITSELF PUTS
  THAT MOMENT: the playhead's own mapping, so a piece played with its long
  pauses squeezed lines up as its playhead does (a five-second pause played
  in 50ms: each dot sits on the playhead at its moment, where the artist's
  clock would have put one 30% further on), and a Flip's pages each take
  their share of the line, as its playhead's do.
- DOUBLES GET REDDER: likes whose dots would overlap on this line (closer
  than their 5px) are one dot of the same size, at their middle, a step
  redder for two and redder still for three or more. A desk's longer line
  keeps apart what a phone's doubles, as the mock said.
- THE COLOURS, (b), the bell dot's pairing: on light #e64a78, #e33157,
  #d11a32; on dark his blush #ff6f91, then #ff4d78, #ff2d5f. One like's dot
  is --heart, the "Liked by" sheet's dot (same role, same token); two new
  tokens for the new job, --heart-2 and --heart-3. They reach Skribl's dots
  as its --mark tokens, set on the site's own .post-art, so the site never
  names a part of Skribl's.
- ON HOME'S CARDS TOO, on the same line, from the same grouped read as the
  count: Home still asks once a kind (posts, drawings) for a whole page.
- THE HEARTS THAT RISE: as the playhead reaches a dot in normal play, a
  small heart (the liked heart, 14px) rises from it about 30px and fades,
  gone in a second: it fades in as it starts and never pops, never grows,
  and the dot stays. It wears the deeper blush in both themes (a new token,
  --heart-paper, #e64a78): the paper it crosses is the drawing's, cream in
  both. A redder dot sends one heart.
- UNDER REDUCE MOTION nothing rises: the dot glows a moment, a 13px halo of
  its own colour fading in and out (at most 0.32, over 0.9s) where it sits;
  nothing moves.
- A LIKE WITH NO MOMENT GETS NO DOT. DOTS SAY WHERE, NEVER WHO: a page is
  sent each moment and how many landed there, nothing else, and a dot
  carries no words. Likes by anybody hidden from the viewer (a block either
  way, or taken down) have no dot, as they have no count: one query does
  both. Nothing taken down has dots, its maker's view included.
- YOUR OWN DOT FOLLOWS YOUR HEART (a judgment call, from the mock's "After
  your tap: the blush heart, 5, and your dot at 0:14"): liked while it
  plays, a dot fades in where you tapped; taken back, it fades out; a like
  the site refused goes back with the heart. Liked while it is still, no
  dot, as the like keeps no moment.

THE SEAM, Skribl's, general (docs/INTEGRATION.md, "Marks on the line";
Skribl never knows they are likes). `skribl_inline(..., marks=[{"ms": 6420,
"n": 1}])` writes a host's moments, on the drawing's own clock, onto the
box, only when there is a line; `player.marks(list)` changes them and
answers the list it holds (a copy). The player draws a 5px dot over the
scrubber for each, where its line puts the moment: through fracAt(), the
mapping frac() now gives the playhead, once the drawing is here; before it,
a replay's moment over the listing's `line.play` (the same number). One dot
stands for those that would overlap, carrying data-n 1, 2, or 3 for three or
more; coloured by the host's --mark, --mark-2 and --mark-3, each falling
back to --mark and that to --accent; taking no taps (the layer has no
pointer events, and the scrubber's own reach lies over it); a dot that comes
fades in (@starting-style), one that goes fades out, and one whose count
changes keeps its element, its colour gliding. As the playhead reaches a dot
in normal play the player sends `skribl:mark` from the dot, bubbling, its
detail { ms, n }: the middle of the moments it stands for, and how many.

WHO DRAWS THE HEART: the host, from that event and the dot's own box (the
event's target), as the brief preferred. Skribl stays generic: a mark may
mean anything to a host, and what it does when one is reached (a heart, a
glow, a sound, nothing) is its own. The site puts each heart in its own
.post-art, never inside Skribl's elements, so a resize that places the dots
again never cuts a heart short.

THE RULES CHOSEN (the brief's "decide well, and say what you decided"):
- A SCRUB, A SEEK OR A JUMP TELLS NOTHING. Only a frame of normal play
  tells, of the dots between the clock's last place and its new one. play()
  starts the count where the clock is, so a scrub, a seek or a press on the
  line (each pauses, moves the clock, and plays again) passes its dots
  silently and carries on from where it was let go: the next dot ahead
  tells. A frame that comes more than a quarter of a second after the last
  (a tab put away and back, a long stall) starts the count again without
  telling.
- A LOOP COMING ROUND tells again, once a pass, from its start (a forever
  loop's from its stretch's start). From the very start, a dot at 0 tells.
- CALM AT EVERY SPEED, the site's rule (likes.js): at most three hearts in
  the air, and each at least a third of a second after the one before; a dot
  reached meanwhile sends none. Nothing waits its turn: a heart held back
  would rise late, from a dot the playhead had left. The same rule holds the
  glows under Reduce Motion. A JUDGMENT CALL: the cap is the host's, not the
  seam's; the player tells every dot and a host decides how many to show.
  At 16x on a busy drawing (40 likes, 40 dots on a phone) the player told
  81 dots in 3.6 seconds and 10 hearts rose, never more than three at once,
  the closest 334ms apart, each starting at its dot within 1.7px of the
  playhead (the final run below).
- A FLIP'S DOTS WAIT FOR ITS PAGES (a judgment call). A Flip's line gives
  each page an equal share, so where a moment sits depends on its pages'
  lengths, which only the drawing carries, and a feed never fetches a
  drawing nobody asked for (inlineplayer.js, "NOTHING FETCHES UNTIL SOMEBODY
  ASKS"). So a Flip's dots come with its drawing, on the first tap or touch
  of its line, fading in; a Pad drawing's are there from the first paint.
  Keeping a Flip's page plan with its listing (a port of lib/holdtiming.js
  plan() to the server) would put them there at rest; that is not this
  piece.

DATA, no change to the chain: stats() reads by the thing and the moment, so
a card's count, whether one is yours, your moment and the dots' moments come
in the one grouped read a kind (its plan still a search on
ix_social_likes_post_created, with a temporary tree for the grouping). A
JUDGMENT CALL: past 200 distinct moments on one drawing (MARKS_MAX), the
others' moments within a two-hundredth of the latest are sent as one, at
their middle, standing for them all (a line shows far fewer dots than that;
it only keeps a very liked drawing's page small); the viewer's own is always
sent exactly, so taking it back can take its dot.

EMBED_RATCHET 78,944 -> 81,244, written beside it: +2,300 B, 81,241 B
measured. inlineplayer.js +1,831 (the moments read +266, placed +1,141,
told +424), inlineplayer.css +469 (the layer that takes no taps, the dot in
the host's tokens by how many, its fade in). Spent first, 2,807 B down to
2,300: the merge one pass left to right (a joined dot never moves left, so
it never needs a second pass: the same answer as the mock's repeated
pairwise merge), a dot's fade in by @starting-style with no script, its
colours through one custom property every level falls back to, the
playhead's frac() made the mapping both use rather than a second copy, no
aria-hidden on a layer of empty elements, and no test for a Flip before its
pages come (its line has no length to put a moment on).
gallerysection.css is the tool's output again (cssgraph.py --emit): it
resets the player's custom properties for the Gallery section, and now
names --mark, --mark-2, --mark-3 and --m.

Pad and Flip: SHARED, ONE PLAYER, the same day. The marks are the in-post
player's, which plays Pad drawings and Flips alike: a like on a Flip is a
dot on its line where its pages put it and sends up a heart as a drawing's
does (verify_inline places them, reads them against its playhead and plays
them on a drawing and a Flip). Nothing changes in either editor, and nothing
is left for Flip to catch up on: a Flip's dots coming with its drawing is
its own nature (its line is its pages, not a clock), not a gap.

THE FOUR: kind (a heart fades in and never pops; nothing jumps at any
speed; a scrub sends no burst; the dot stays; your own dot comes and goes
gently; Reduce Motion gets a glow, and nothing moves); simple (a dot where
people loved the drawing, redder where they agreed, no numbers, no names);
playful (hearts rise from the line as the replay reaches the moments people
loved, on Home as on a page); powerful (where a drawing was loved, at a
glance, at any speed from ¼× to 16× and Fit, and one seam any host can
use).

CONTRAST, READ OFF THE SCREEN. The mock's colour reader parsed only rgb()
and read the player's lilac (written color(srgb ...)) as grey; these are
read off the painted pixels instead: each dot's middle against the ground
5px above it, between the drawing and the line, on a post's page and Home's
card, a phone and a desk, light and dark, every step at 3:1 or more (the
final run's figures below). The rising heart at full strength: 3.35:1 on
the drawing's cream paper (light and dark alike, the paper being the
drawing's own), 3.64:1 and 5.20:1 on the page where it starts. No words were

## After v330 -- The comment box is an icon

The owner, Nov 13, looking at a post's page: "The comment needs to be an icon
not a card. It takes up too much room sitting there." The comment mock that
day offered three places for the icon (on the drawing's line beside the
heart, at the end of the Comments heading, or in the row with Share) and
recommended the heading; the owner answered "Yes to all": every default.
Built in the mock's own sizes, words and classes (`_comments.html`,
`comments.js`, `social.css`, the icon in `_icons.html`).

1. WHERE IT SITS, the mock's 2: a round 44px button at the right end of the
   "Comments 3" heading, in the chips' lilac and the small violet ink: the
   comment's bubble with a small plus, in the pen (`_icons.html`,
   comment_new()), named "Say something" (its tip too). The heading keeps
   its 29px line: the button reaches 7.5px above and below it into the room
   already there (font-independent: (44 - 20 x 1.45) / 2). The box is folded
   away until asked for, which takes its 136px off the page.
2. A PHONE: a tap raises Make's own sheet from the bottom with the one box on
   it (comments.js moves it there), its field focused and ready (the
   composer's 17px), titled "Say something to Mira", Draw, Flip and Post as
   before. It glides up in a third of a second while the page dims (Make's
   own sheet, social.js's SocialSheet). A tap on the dimmed page, a drag down
   or Esc puts it away, keeping the words.
3. A DESK: a click glides the box open under the heading (its room opening
   while it fades in, the comments under it sliding down), the field ready,
   and the icon lights (white on the action purple) while it is open. A
   second click, Esc or a press anywhere else folds it away, keeping the
   words; Esc gives focus back to the icon.
4. ANSWER on any comment opens the same box: on a phone the sheet titled
   "Answer Theo", Theo's words in a line under it (in quotes, one line, cut
   short with an ellipsis), the field saying "Answer Theo…"; on a desk under
   that conversation as before ("Answer Theo…"), the page gliding down to it
   when it opened below the screen. Answer again, Esc or a press elsewhere
   puts it away.
5. AFTER POSTING the box closes (the sheet glides down, or the fold folds
   away) and the new comment sits at the top of the list, fading in as its
   room opens, glowing a moment in Activity's landing tint (`.is-landed`,
   comments.js glow()), which then fades over a second and a half. ON A DESK
   THE TWO MOVE IN STEP: the fold closes in the same 0.32s, on the same curve,
   as the comment opens its room where the box was, so what is under them
   moves only by how much taller or shorter the comment is than the box. An
   answer glows under its comment, and the page glides to it when it landed
   below the screen.
6. PUT AWAY, IT KEEPS WHAT WAS TYPED for as long as the page is open: the one
   field keeps its words (and a drawing waiting in it) whichever way it was
   put away.
7. SIGNED OUT, the icon still shows; a tap raises a small sheet like the
   heart's "Like this drawing?": "Say something?", "Sign in, and you can
   answer Mira in words or with a drawing.", Not now and Sign in. Sign in
   comes back to the same page with the box open (its next names the page
   and #say; comments.js opens the box, focuses its field, and takes #say off
   the address so a reload is just the page). Nothing is posted until Post.
   On an iPhone the keyboard waits for a tap in the field (Safari raises it
   only for a tap). The old "Sign in to answer" line is gone.
8. WITH NO COMMENTS YET, "Say the first thing" stands where they will be: the
   small violet words "Sign in to answer" wore (16px, 600, --accent-ink),
   44px tall, opening the box as the icon does (for nobody signed in, the
   same small sheet).

The same on a drawing's own page (/social/b/<id>), which is this template.
Home's cards are as they were: their own box for a new post, and the 💬
count that takes you to a post's comments.

JUDGMENT CALLS, said so they can be changed:
- THE ICON LIGHTS FOR THE BOX IT OPENED. Answer marks its own Answer as
  open, as before, and the heading's icon stays unlit then (the mock's phone
  picture of Answer showed it lit under the dimmed page). Signed out it
  stays unlit while "Say something?" is up, as the mock's picture had it:
  no box is open (found in the pictures, where that sheet's own
  aria-expanded lit it).
- ON YOUR OWN POST the sheet says "Say something", not "Say something to"
  your own name.
- POSTING SAYS "Posting…" ON POST ITSELF (dimmed, as a button at work is),
  and the box's line says it to a screen reader only. FOUND IN THE FRAMES:
  the line appearing for the round trip and going as the box went made
  everything under the box jump twice (31.75px each way); now nothing under
  it moves until it goes. What goes wrong is still said in the box, which
  stays open.
- THE BOX EMPTIES ONCE IT HAS GONE. Found in the frames too: emptying the
  field at once shrank a two-line box by a line (23.6px) as it began to go,
  and a drawing taken out would have shrunk it more. It keeps what was sent
  while it goes, and empties when it is away.
- A NEW COMMENT NUDGES NOTHING. It lands right under the icon that was
  pressed; an answer, which can land at the end of a long conversation below
  the screen, is glided to once in place. (A first build glided the page
  5px to show the last of a new comment's height above a phone's bar: a
  small late move, found by section 33, gone.)
- ONE BOX, ONE SET OF WORDS: words typed for an answer are there when the
  icon opens it for a new comment (the box says whom it is for each time).
- OPEN IN ONE PLACE AND ASKED FOR IN ANOTHER (a desk), it folds away there
  first and then opens, both glides, rather than jumping across the page.
- "ELSEWHERE" IS A PRESS, NOT A CLICK, so selecting words in the field and
  letting go outside it does not fold the box; and the editor over the page
  (Draw or Flip opened from the box) and a sheet are not elsewhere: a press
  beside the Pad puts the Pad away and leaves the box open.
- "SAY THE FIRST THING" FOLDS IN STEP with the box on a desk (one room
  closing as the other opens), goes when the first comment comes, and comes
  back, fading in as its room opens, when the last one is deleted.
- PHONE OR DESK FOLLOWS THE SITE'S OWN DESK WIDTH (900px); a window that
  crosses it puts the box away, keeping the words.
- A FOLDED BOX IS NOT LAID OUT AT ALL. Found by the first side-by-side run:
  verify_sociallikes' census of a post's page (a desk, a post with nothing
  under the heading) read the folded box's Draw, Flip and Post at 1.00:1.
  The box had kept its layout, unseen at opacity 0, and that census takes a
  word for shown when the point at its middle hits any of its ancestors
  (here the section). Folded, the box's inside is hidden now, not laid out,
  and laid out again just before it glides open: the glide is unchanged, a
  drawing waiting in it comes back at its size, and the field's
  grow-to-fit never takes a height off a field that is not laid out. "Say
  the first thing" folds the same way. Section 29 asks it, and a break that
  lays the box out again turns both section 29 and that census red.
- THE EDITOR OVER THE PAGE GIVES BACK ONLY THE INERTNESS IT SET (social.js,
  SocialPadOverlay): opened from the phone's sheet, the Pad used to un-inert
  the page behind the sheet when it went. A general fix in the site's
  chrome, the one change outside the post page's files.
- ON A PHONE'S KEYBOARD THE SHEET RIDES ABOVE IT: comments.js reads the
  keyboard off the visual viewport (what it lost at the bottom of the layout
  viewport the sheet is fixed to, at a zoom of 1 only, so a pinch is no
  keyboard) and the sheet glides up by that much (`--cm-kb`). This box has
  no phone keyboard: see Not tested.

Pad and Flip: NOT AFFECTED, and nothing for Flip to catch up on. The comment
box is the site's; Draw and Flip in it open the editors over the page as
before (lib/composehost.js through SocialPadOverlay), from the phone's sheet
too, where the Pad opens over the sheet and the sheet is still there when it
goes. Neither editor changed.

THE FOUR: kind (the box only when you want it; put it away any way and
nothing is lost; every move glides, and posting no longer makes anything
jump; signed out, an invitation, not a wall); simple (it sits on the word
"Comments", so nobody needs telling; "Say the first thing" where a list
would be; Answer says whom, and shows what); playful (a small lilac bubble,
the heart pill's colour; your comment glows as it lands); powerful (on a
desk it opens right where you are; a phone's sheet keeps the drawing you are
answering in view above it).

CONTRAST, from the tokens and off the painted pixels: the icon's line on its

anti-aliasing, 6.88 and 8.65; a mark needs 3:1); lit, white on the action

NOTHING ELSE MOVED, measured against main itself (its own server, the same

KIND, NEVER JUMPY, READ ON EVERY FRAME (a glide is three frames or more

The owner, Nov 13, on the follow mock: "Yes to all": B (yours alone) and
every default. Built in the mock's own classes, sizes and words
(`social/follows.py`, `_follow.html`, `follows.js`, the FOLLOWING block of
`social.css`), with one general seam on Skribl's listing.

- B, YOURS ALONE. On somebody else's page there is only Follow, or
  Following: no line, no count and no list, for anybody, not in the page and
  not in its source. Your own page says who under its buttons, the twin of
  "Liked by…" (its own classes): "Followed by Mira, Theo and 2 others" with
  their drawn faces, every name up to three, else two and how many more,
  newest first; before anybody follows you "You follow Mira and Juno"; with
  nobody either way no line at all, so nothing ever says zero. The line opens
  Make's own sheet (--menu-paper) with the one pill, Followers | Following,
  each newest first with when, "Only you can see who follows you, and who you
  follow."; a row opens their page. Counted by the viewer: anybody a block
  either way or a takedown hides is in no line, no count and no list.
- THE BUTTON. First in the row on somebody's page, before Share and ⋯ (on a
  desk the same row beside their face, as the profile already lays it), in
  the action's purple with a plus drawn in the pen; once tapped "Following",
  the quiet button, its check drawing itself. Both words sit in one grid cell,
  so it is as wide as "Following" in any font: on a touch phone 135.31px at
  81.34px from the left, Share at 224.66px and ⋯ at 276.66px, both times, the
  mock's own figures to the hundredth. The motion fades and draws, never moves;
  under Reduce Motion it only fades.
- UNFOLLOWING ASKS ONCE: "Unfollow Theo?", "You'll still see Theo's drawings
  under Everyone. They aren't told.", Unfollow the big button (the action),
  Keep following beside it with the focus. Nobody is told.
- HOME'S PILL, Following | Everyone, under the composer: the Gallery's New /
  Hot value for value (44px, the card's ground and line, 12px round, the
  tint rgba(124, 92, 255, 0.22) gliding under the chosen option over 0.42s,
  13px words at 600, the Gallery's inks). The site cannot name Skribl's
  classes, so it is the site's own control with the Gallery's values, under
  three new tokens for the role (--pill-on-fill, --pill-on-ink,
  --pill-off-ink): the same values, not new ones. Home opens on Following
  once you follow somebody and on Everyone before that; a tap keeps your pick
  on the account (social_people.home_feed), so it holds on every device. The
  switch: the pill glides, the posts fade, change while unseen, fade back; the
  page doesn't scroll (held at its place and height while the posts change).
- FOLLOWING NEVER RUNS OUT. The people you follow and you, posts and drawings
  alike, newest first, nothing ranked; then "You're caught up with the people
  you follow." with a check in the pen, then Fresh from everyone (a heading)
  and everybody else's, so nothing shows twice; Load more carries on through
  both. Somebody who follows nobody sees the kind card, "You're not following
  anyone yet", how, and Look around (Explore), then everyone's.
- ACTIVITY: "Mira followed you", the face wearing a small Follow disc (the
  action's purple, a white plus), no picture; grouped since you last looked
  ("Mira and 2 others followed you", "Mira and Theo followed you"); one person
  opens their page, several open who follows you (your page, #followers, the
  sheet rising on Followers). The heading and the empty page say follows, in
  the mock's words. A FOLLOW NEVER LIGHTS THE BELL'S DOT.
- SIGNED OUT: Follow raises the heart's small sheet: "Follow Theo?", "Sign in,
  and Theo's new drawings show first on your Home.", Not now, Sign in, which
  comes back to Theo's page; nothing is pressed for them.
- NEVER: Follow on a card, "Follow back", "Follows you".
- BLOCKS: a block ends a follow both ways (the rows go) and none can begin
  while it stands; lifting it restores nothing. Somebody taken down drops out
  of every list and every Following.
- Following again doesn't ping twice; 60 an hour; you can't follow yourself;
  deleting an account takes its follows both ways, in code; Privacy and
  docs/LAWYER-NOTE.md say follows are kept. Later, not now: pings for new
  posts, private accounts, suggestions.

DATA, on the site's chain (1757a4385be8, after a81c5c4dde3a): social_follows,
follower_id and followed_id (both to social_people, ON DELETE CASCADE),
created_at (when they first followed), ended_at (when they unfollowed, or
nothing while they follow); unique on the pair (ix_social_follows_pair);
never yourself (ck_social_follows_not_self); indexed newest first both ways,
(follower_id, created_at) and (followed_id, created_at). And
social_people.home_feed, Home's pick. Offline, the PostgreSQL DDL is plain:
CREATE TABLE with its CHECK and two foreign keys, three CREATE INDEX and one
ADD COLUMN; the downgrade the reverse.

JUDGMENT CALLS, said so the list reads true:
- AN UNFOLLOW KEEPS ITS ROW (ended_at), the one way "following again doesn't
  ping twice" can hold: Activity reads the follow's first time, so a second
  follow has nothing new to say, and a follow taken back has no row. A block
  deletes the rows instead (a clean break, which is what "lifting it doesn't
  restore it" asks). Privacy says the first: "if you unfollow someone, we keep
  that you once did, so following them again doesn't tell them twice."
- COUNTED WHEN READ, BY THE VIEWER, not kept as a number as the mock's "What
  it takes" line said: under B the only count anybody sees is their own, in
  names, and "by the viewer" leaves out anybody hidden, which a kept number
  cannot. It is an indexed count on your own page alone.
- SKRIBL'S LISTING TAKES `authors` (the mock said "nothing in Skribl"):
  drawings shown outside a post are Home's cards too, so Following must hold
  them, and without it the choices were a read per person followed or a scan
  of everyone's. It is general (any host's feed of the people somebody
  follows), documented in docs/INTEGRATION.md, any number of authors (asked
  in pieces of 500 inside, one query a piece, the newest of all kept). The
  site's layering rule holds: it imports only the documented name.
- 60 AN HOUR, follows and unfollows alike: comments' and blocks' number, not
  likes' 120 ("A rate limit, as likes have"), for the mock's reason, "nobody
  can follow everyone at once to be noticed".
- UNDER EARLIER A DAY'S FOLLOWS are those within 24 hours of the newest of
  them: the site keeps no time zone of a person's, so a calendar date would
  be UTC's, the owner's evening split in two.
- THE BUTTON'S NAME FOLLOWS ITS WORD ("Follow Theo Lind", then "Following Theo
  Lind"; a tap on Following says it raises a dialog), not aria-pressed under a
  fixed name: the name always holds the word on the button (WCAG's label in
  name), and a status line says "You're following Theo Lind." to a screen
  reader.
- THE LISTS show the newest 200 each, as "Liked by" does; the line's count is
  exact. An empty one (only reachable when the other has somebody) says so
  kindly, in new words: "When someone follows you, they'll show here." and
  "Tap Follow on someone's page, and they'll show here."
- WHEN THE PEOPLE YOU FOLLOW END PART-WAY DOWN A PAGE, at least five of
  everybody else's follow on it, and a page of everybody else's reads at most
  four of Everyone's pages looking for one that isn't all the people you
  follow. Following nobody, Following is everyone's, your own among them (the
  mock's own page did so).
- ONE WAY TO SAY A TIME, MOVED: window.SocialWhen now lives in social.js
  (loaded on every page) instead of posts.js, so your own page's lists can
  say "8m" in your own time: posts.js cannot load on a profile, where it
  would take Skribl's Gallery's own #reportSheet for the site's. posts.js
  calls it as before, so nothing a post's page or Home says changed.
  comments.js's own comment still says posts.js (not touched: the comment
  icon's helper is in that file).
- Home's pick is a short string the route checks, not a CHECK in the table,
  so SQLite never rebuilds social_people to add it.

Pad and Flip: nothing changes in either editor. Home's cards play Pad drawings
and Flips in the one player they share, so Following shows both alike. The one
change on Skribl's side is the listing's general `authors`, which is no
editor's; nothing is left for Flip to catch up on.

THE FOUR: kind (no scoreboard on anybody: who follows you is yours, as who
liked your drawing is; nothing says zero; unfollowing asks once and tells
nobody; a follow never pulls you back to the bell; nothing jumps); simple
(one button, first in the row, as wide as its longest word so nothing beside
it moves; your page says who in plain words); playful (their drawn faces in
the line, a check that draws itself in the pen); powerful (Home shows the
people you follow first and never runs out, and the next drawing of the
artists you love comes to the top, where it plays at the artist's own speed).

MOTION JUDGED FAIRLY. Every motion row reads its thing on every animation
frame, and a step is judged over the display frames it spans (60 a second),
so a frame the browser drops on a busy machine is not read as a jump; a snap
cannot hide in a long frame, because each change must also show over several
frames of its own (a 30ms fade is red). The thresholds are the mock's:
nothing moves; a fill or a word no more than 35% of its change a frame; a
check drawn over six frames or more; a pill no more than 30% of its way a
frame over eight or more; posts changed only at 0.05 or less, after the pill
started; nothing scrolled. Read as built: the button's fill at most 15% a
frame over 15, its check 11% over 18; Home's pill 11% over 20, its posts' fade
26%, the posts changed at 0, the page 0px moved; the lists' pill 11% over 20,
one list gone before the other comes.

## After v330 -- The comment box keeps to its column

Main's full run after #883 (the comment box as an icon) went red in one row
on GitHub's machines, on both databases, and again on Following's branch
run: verify_socialcomments section 12, "the box opens right under the
heading, as wide as the column", read the desk box 350 wide in a 340 column.
Here it read 340.

THE CAUSE, a defect and not the instrument. This box's sans is Inter
(fontconfig maps system-ui and sans-serif to it); GitHub's ubuntu-latest has
DejaVu Sans, which is wider. In DejaVu, Draw, Flip and Post need 320 of the
310 the box's line has. The fold that opens the box is a grid whose one
column was auto, and an auto column grows to the min-content of what is in
it once the fold is still (overflow visible), so the box grew to 350 and its
right edge left the column. The same happened here, in Inter, once the
counter showed ("5 left", from a hundred characters left): 360 in 340, and
Post slid 20px right while the person typed. So it was never only GitHub's
font: anybody typing a long comment on a desk would have seen the box spill
past its column.

Reproduced here by standing in for GitHub's font: a fonts.conf that maps
system-ui and sans-serif to DejaVu Sans, handed to the suite as
FONTCONFIG_FILE (Chromium reads it), read the same 350 in 340 to the pixel.
That is a way to see what CI's fonts do without waiting for CI.

THE FIX, in social.css (the fold's block and the comments' block):
- The fold's column is minmax(0, 1fr), and the fold min-width 0, so nothing
  in it can widen it.
- The box's line wraps. Draw, Flip and Post share it while they fit; when
  they don't (a wide font, larger text), Post keeps to the right on the next.
- The counter reads on its own line under Post, at its right edge, and makes
  no line at all while it is empty. Post never moves while someone types.
- Post is as wide as its longer word, as Following's button is. The first
  cut of this fix let the line wrap, and then "Posting…" (11px wider than
  Post in this box's font) pushed Post onto a second line just as the comment
  went: the box grew 50px while it folded away, and the comment no longer
  opened in step (section 33, red alone as well as beside the others).
  "Posting…" is now measured under "Post" in a row with no height (the
  page's own word, set on the button as data-busy by comments.js), and
  Post's sides are 12px, so both words still fit the 96px it always was.
In this box's font, and in the mock, the box looks exactly as before until
the counter shows; the counter now sits under Post instead of beside it.
Home's composer is unchanged: its line has room for the counter.

THE CHECK: a new row in section 12 asks it of the box whatever is in it: the
chips' words spread (6px letter-spacing, standing in for a wider font or
larger text), something 600px wide put in the box, typing to the last
hundred characters, and the same in an answer's box. The box stays as wide
as its column, the chips and Post inside it, Post at its right edge, no gap
under Post while there is no counter, the counter painted under Post at its
right edge, and Post where it was; Post is as wide saying "Posting…" (and
with a longer stand-in word, so the rule holds in a wider font than this
box's), is named Post all the same, and has 12px sides. Shown red on the old
CSS here (the counter: 360 in 340, Post moved 20px). Each of the fix's nine
parts removed alone (the fold's column, the wrap, Post's right margin, the
counter's own line, its :empty, the measured word, Post's grid, its sides,
comments.js setting the word) turned the row red, and the unbroken control
stayed green. Section 33's posting row, red with the first cut, is green
again. Sections 12 and 33 are green in this box's font and in DejaVu.

Pad and Flip: not touched; the box is the site's. The four: kind (Post stays
under your finger while you type, and nothing spills off the column), simple
(one line while it fits), playful and powerful (unchanged: a comment to its
last character).

It rides on Following's PR (#884), which was waiting on main going green.

## After v330 -- Every card opens its post

The owner, Nov 13, with screenshots from the phone: "Show me where you click
or touch to go to post view? It's not clear. I thought on card?" The rule
said yes to on Nov 12: "anywhere on the card should open the post and
clicking on the player should make it play", with the face, the name and the
@handle opening the person's page, ⋯, Share and 💬 keeping their jobs, and
every other control its own. Home's posts.js already did this; Cal's tap map
(every point of real cards on a touch phone, coloured by what a tap does)
found where it did not.

THE MAP BEFORE, measured on main (3a9d1f75): an exact tap on every part of
each card's ground, followed to where it went.
- HOME'S CARD: three parts did nothing, all inside .post-art, which posts.js
  counted as a job of its own: the line under the drawing ("Drawn in 16 sec
  · watching at": its words take no taps, so a tap lands on the line, which
  keeps its clicks from bubbling), the gaps in the line's row between the
  heart, the scrubber and the loop, and the drawing's edge (the 10px under it
  and its round corners).
- EXPLORE'S AND A PROFILE'S SKRIBLS CARDS (Skribl's own Gallery cards): the
  title, the caption, the time, the plays, the head's empty space and the
  card's margins all did nothing. A tap only played the drawing, and ⋯ → Open
  went to Skribl's player page (/s/<id>, not /p/<id> as the brief had it) in a
  new tab: from Explore or a profile there was no way to a drawing's page on
  the site, its comments or its heart.

THE MAP AFTER: no part does nothing, light and dark, on Home, Explore and a
profile. Its pictures, measured the same way before and after, went with
this change, beside Cal's map.

HOME (posts.js, inside its card-open block): .post-art is no longer a job of
its own (the drawing's box is role="button" in its own markup, so it plays,
script or not); a group of controls (the speed's choices, role="group") keeps
its taps, so a near miss between two speeds opens nothing; and since the
player and its line keep their clicks from bubbling (docs/INTEGRATION.md,
the lead: a host whose whole post is a link must not navigate on a scrub), a
click inside .post-art (the site's own class; it names nothing of the
player's) is heard on the way down. The speed, the heart, the scrubber, the
loop and the drawing keep theirs.

THE SEAM, Skribl's, general (docs/INTEGRATION.md, "Where a Gallery card
opens (`card_url`)"; Skribl never knows the site): init_skribl(...,
card_url=fn) or skribl.set_card_url(fn, app=app). fn() is asked in the
request, once a page that holds the Gallery section, and answers None or an
address with __ID__ for the drawing's id (a path on the site or an http(s)
address). The section writes it on its root (data-skribl-open, through the
template global skribl_card_url()), and gallery.js then opens it from the
card's own ground by Home's rules (a drag is not a tap, a click that ends a
selection opens nothing, Ctrl, ⌘ or Shift or the middle button a new tab),
makes the title a real link to it (a keyboard's and a screen reader's way
in; the card is not one big link), and sends ⋯ → Open there, Copy link and
Share… giving it. Unsaid, the Gallery is Skribl's own byte for byte: /gallery
and the skribls.net stand-in are unchanged. A wrong answer raises on the
first page that asks, as a brand's does. Two rules in /gallery's own sheet,
met only by a card with an address (the title link without an underline and
selectable as words; a pointer over the card on a desk), re-emitted into
gallerysection.css. Explore's and the profile's templates are untouched.

THE SITE (app.py, _site_cards, beside _site_brand) sets it for its own pages
(the site's blueprint: Explore, a profile's Skribls, and the first visit's
newest under Blooby's card): /social/b/<id>. ONE ADDRESS FOR EVERY CARD, so
that page learned two things (social/posts.py, bloob_page):
- A post's drawing goes on to the post (302 to /social/p/<public id>) for
  anybody who may see the post, signed in or not, by the post's own page's
  rule (comments.on_post); to anybody it is hidden from (a block either way,
  a takedown not theirs) it is the kind 404, and the answer names no post.
  It used to redirect everybody, naming the post in the Location before the
  post's page said it was gone.
- A JUDGMENT CALL: a public drawing by somebody not on the site (made on
  Skribl's own Pad; Explore lists every public skribl) goes to Skribl's own
  page for it (/s/<id>), the one page it has and the one its ⋯ → Open gave
  before. Section 9 pinned a kind 404 there, from when nothing on screen
  led to that address; its row now pins this. Unlisted, gone or none: a
  kind 404, as before.

THE OTHER JUDGMENT CALLS: ⋯ → Open goes in the same tab, as a tap on the
card does (the address is the site's own page; Skribl's player page still
opens in a new tab where nothing is said); Copy link and Share… give the
card's address, so one card has one address; "Anonymous" names nobody, so
on its card it is ground and opens the card; the first visit's Home holds
the same section and opens the same way.

A FINDING, NOT CHANGED: a phone moves a tap that lands near a control onto
it. Chromium does here, whatever the touch's radius and with
--disable-touch-adjustment: a finger in a card's 16px padding beside the
drawing plays it, and one in the head's band under the name opens the
person, where an exact click opens the post. That targeting is the
browser's, not the page's, and Safari's (the owner's iPhone) is its own,
not seen here. So the map's rows tap every part of the ground EXACTLY (a
click at the point, in the touch phone's context), and a finger (a real
touch) the drawing, the name and the spots a person aims for ("watching
at", the time).

Pad and Flip: SHARED. The Gallery shows Pad drawings and Flips alike, and
Home's card is one card for both; section 12 maps a Flip post's card on Home
and on Explore beside a drawing's, under the same rules. Nothing changes in
either editor, and nothing is left for Flip.

THE FOUR: kind (no dead ends on a card; a near miss between speeds, a drag
or a selection never takes you away); simple ("I thought on card?": the card
is the way in, as expected, on every card the site shows); playful (the
drawing still plays where it is; the card around it opens its page, with
its comments and hearts); powerful (Ctrl, ⌘ and the middle button open a
new tab, the title is a keyboard's link, and one seam serves any host).

CONTRAST: no words, colours or tokens changed; the title link keeps the
title's ink. verify_contrast ran (/gallery's sheet gained two rules).

POST'S WIDTH, HELD BY THE SCRIPT, NOT THE STYLESHEET. Laid on Following and
the comment box's fix, verify_socialposts went red in its console row in
every full run (five of five, alone and beside others): Chrome dropped the
page's cross-fade from Explore to a drawing's own page (/s/<id>, where a
card for somebody not on the site now goes), "Transition was aborted
because of invalid state. ViewTransition opt-in disabled". Bisected by
whole runs: the card fix on the comment icon alone was green, on Following
without the box's fix green, and with the box's fix minus its two Post rules
green. Those rules (Post as an inline grid, and "Posting…" measured under it
through ::after with content: attr(data-busy)) match nothing on Explore or on
Skribl's page, so this is Chrome's, and not understood beyond that. The width
is now held by comments.js: it measures "Posting…" once the box is laid out
and sets it as Post's least width (through the style object, which the
page's policy allows); Post's sides stay 12px. Same result for the person,
in any font. Section 12's row asks that comments.js set it (red with the
call removed, green with it); sections 12 and 33 are green in this box's font
and in DejaVu, and verify_socialposts 42/42 alone.
